                        FAMILY HISTORIES

GOTTLIEB and EMMA ADAM

Christian Burrer was born in Russia in 1855, Elizabeth Albrecht, in 1860. They
married in 1881 and immigrated to the United States in 1884. Emma Burrer was
born to the couple December 9, 1900, six miles west of Long Lake, SD, one of
ten children, all the rest of whom are deceased.

Gottlieb Adam was born August 1, 1896, about 16 miles north of Hosmer, to Fred
Adam and Eva Maier Adam. Fred and Eva were both born in Neudorf, South Russia,
and had immigrated to America in April 1893 with four sons. Eventually seven
boys and one girl were born to this family and all are now
deceased.

Gottlieb, served in the Army during World War I and August 23, 1921, he married
Emma Burrer. They farmed near Hosmer until they moved to Leola in October 1957.

Their children are: Elmer, married to Regina Heupel, has four children and
lives in Bosie, ID. Helmuth, married to Margaret Pfeifle, has four children,
and died August 1982. Esther, married to Herbert Gienger, had three children,
two deceased, and lives in Aberdeen. Milbert, married Phyllis Whisenant, lives
in Rapid City. Raymond died in the Vietnam War, 1964. Milton, married to Doris
Mohr, has three children, and lives in Rapid City. Harry, never married, lives
in Diamondville, WY.

        Emma & Gottlieb Adam.

Emma and Gottlieb celebrated their Golden Wedding Anniversary in 1971 in Leola.
Gottlieb died in January 1978. Emma still resides in Leola and is a member of
St. James Lutheran Church and is a Gold Star Mother.

EDWARD and ANNA ALBRECHT

Anna Job, was born to Ludwig and Rosina Kranzler Job, who immigrated from
Russia and lived north of Hosmer. Later they moved to a farm 14 miles west of
Leola, now owned by Art Fischer. Anna grew up there attending country school
and the Reformed Church. She married Edward Albrecht, son of John and Fredricka
Wisze Albrecht, and they lived on the parents' farm for several years before
moving to Wetonka. Their 12 children attended school in Wetonka and the family
attended the Lutheran Church. Edward did carpenter work for many years until
stricken by a stroke in 1954. Anna and Edward moved to Leola in 1956, where
they attended St. Paul's Lutheran Church. After being bedridden for ten years,
Edward passed away in 1964.

        Anna & Edward Albrecht.

Their children are: Milbert, married to Velma Muehlbeier and lives in Lead, SD.
Herbert, married to Delphi Becker and lives in Deadwood, SD. Gertruth, married
to Clem Knittle. She is deceased. Alice, married to Richard C. Wilson and lives
in Aberdeen, SD. Albert, who lives in Aberdeen. Melvin, married to Evangie
Jahraus and lives in Lead, SD. Martha, married to Milbert Jerke and lives in
Aberdeen, SD. Paul, married to Helen Clovested and lives in California. Allen,
who is deceased. Anna, married to Harold Bauer and lives in Gettysburg, SD.
Marcella, married to Wesley Bonnet and lives in Tempe, AZ. Thomas, married to
Shirley Kaaz and lives in Finley, ND.

In 1979, Anna Job Albrecht, married Christ Schock and they are members of St.
James Lutheran Church. Christ has two sons: Elmer, married to Norma Guthmiller
and lives on a farm near Leola. LeRoy, married to Eileen Albrecht and lives on
a farm near Long Lake, SD.

EMIL J. and LAVINA ALBRECHT

Emil J. Albrecht, son of John & Carolina Kranzler Albrecht was born on July 13,
1914. At 14 years of age, Emil started working out as a hired hand on other
farms. On October 6, 1940, he was united in marriage to Lavina Rueb, daughter
of Jacob and Magdalena Lechner Rueb. They made their home 12 miles west of
Leola on Lavina's parents' farm until 1947, when they moved six miles southwest
of Leola. In 1955, they moved to Leola. Emil was employed by his brother,
Edward for a time. He then went to work for Wesley Rueb for 11 years. And the
last 14 years he worked for the Leola Equity Oil Exchange until partial
retirement in 1982.

Lavina was employed at the Leola Community Hospital for two years until its
closing. Then she was employed at Presentation College for 14 years until
health reasons forced her to retire.

        The Emil J. Albrecht family. Back: Wallace, Eileen, Dianne, Pamela
        and Stanley. Front: Lavina and Emil.

They were blessed with five children: Eileen, born June 2, 1942, married to
LeRoy Schock. They live on a farm near Long Lake, SD. Stanley, born November
11, 1945, married to Lavonne Beaver. They have two sons, Ryan and Scott and
live in rural Aberdeen, SD. Dianne, born May 5, 1947, married to Robert
Benzley. They have one daughter, Brianne and live in Aurora, CO. Wallace, born
February 20, 1951, married to Fran Rappe. They live in rural Aberdeen, SD.
Pamela, born September 16, 1952, married to Curtis Walz. They have one son,
Brian and one daughter, Becky and live in Leola, SD.

Emil and Lavina are members of the First Baptist Church in Leola

JOHN J. and CAROLINA ALBRECHT

John J. Albrecht, son of Johann Albrecht and Fredricka (Weisz) Albrecht was
born July 19, 1891, near Hosmer, SD. His parents came to the United States from
near Bergdorf, South Russia in 1884. John married Carolina Kranzler on February
4, 1913. She was born October 15, 1888, near Hosmer, SD. After their marriage,
they farmed near Hosmer until 1930 when they moved to a farm three miles north
where they lived until 1941. John and his son Edmund rented a farm until 1943
and then purchased a farm four miles south of Leola. They lived here until 1949
when they moved to Leola. John continued to farm with his son and also worked
for a son Ed in his produce store. After his death on April 15, 1955, his wife
Carolina lived in an apartment at the Huber Hotel, owned by her daughter,
Loretta and husband. Carolina passed away on April 3, 1969. They were blessed
with six children: Emil was born July 13, 1914 and lives in Leola. He is
semi-retired and his wife
Lavina is also retired.

        The John J. Albrecht family.

Loretta Huber was born January 7, 1916. She lives in Aberdeen and is employed
in the housekeeping department at Presentation College. Her husband Jacob is
retired.

Edward was born October 2, 1918. He lived in Loveland, CO where he was killed
in a car-train accident on November 10, 1969. His wife Estella still resides in
Loveland.

Edmund was born on June 13, 1920. He is semiretired, his wife Florence is also
retired. They live in Eureka.

Vivian Rueb, born April 30, 1923, lives in Leola where she operates a beauty
shop. Her husband Walter passed away November 5, 1981.

Lucille Mettler was born on September 8, 1926. She lives in Aberdeen and she is
manager of the World of Fabric store at Super City. Her husband Reinie passed
away August 30, 1981.

HENRY and ETHEL ARTZ

Henry John Artz was born August 4, 1894, to Marie and John Artz (Dutch descent)
who had immigrated from Germany. On February 11, 1918, Henry married Ethel May
Schafer, born February 12, 1897 to Clara and Theodore
Schafer of Webster, SD.

        Henry, Ethel & Delores Artz.

The young couple made their home in Aberdeen, where Henry was employed by the
Dakota Farmer. Later he was foreman of the composing room of the Watertown
Public Opinion. His dreams of publishing his own newspaper eventually
materialized when he purchased the McPherson County Herald at Leola in 1929
from former editor, W. C. Peer. Both he and his wife worked at this venture
until for health reasons she was unable to continue. Almeda Krambeal and Madge
Schubert (Henry's half-sister) then assisted him. Later he also owned the
newspaper at New Effington, operating it and the Herald simultaneously.

In World War II Henry served in the Seabees.

Their only child, Delores, was born April 15, 1923 at Watertown. She attended
school at Leola, graduating from L.H.S. in 1941. During World War II she joined
the WAVES. While in the service she met Richard Moore, who was serving in the
Coast Guard. They were married August 4, 1944. He is a partner in the Civil
Engineering Surveying Firm. The Moores have two sons, Derek and Dennis. Henry
was a member of the Masonic Lodge and Ethel of the Eastern Star. Both were
members of the United Methodist Church. Henry died April 11, 1953 and Ethel
died May 28, 1982

HENRY and JESSIE ATKINSON

Henry Atkinson was born June 18, 1899, at Helena, MT, to Charles and Minnie
Knudtson Atkinson. At a young age he moved with his mother and brothers to
Forbes, ND. He attended grade school and high school in Forbes and attended
college for awhile in Ellendale, ND.

        The Henry Atkinson family. Back: Abner, Genaveve and Vernon. Front:
        Jessie and Henry.

Jessie Hart was born November 4, 1908, to Abner and Mollie Haberman Hart. She
married Henry Atkinson February 27, 1928 in Aberdeen. Henry worked at the
William Haberman farm for many years before starting to farm on his own. He and
Jessie bought a farm near Leola in 1946 where they lived until Henry's health
forced him to retire. They moved to Aberdeen in 1963, where Jessie was employed
at St. Luke's Hospital for nine years. She has spent ten years caring for two
ladies and is still employed there. She is a member of the First Methodist
Church in Aberdeen.

Their children are: Vernon, born 1929 and married Loretta Nelson, they have six
children and live in Billings, MT; Genaveve Atkinson Kolb; Abner, born 1933 and
married Arlene Edelman, they have two children. Abner died in 1978.

FRED (FREDERICK) and VIRGINIA BAIN

Fred Bain, born December 27, 1865, at LaCrosse, WI, was united in marriage to
Virginia Vera Pourrier. They lived in Minnesota until 1889, when Fred, his wife
and sons Fred C. and George Wm., moved to Elkton SD, where they lived in a sod
shanty.

Fred and Virginia were the parents of four children: Fred Charles, born August
3, 1887; George Wm., September 24, 1888; Henry Arthur, April 10, 1890 and
Jennie Vera (Heagley), December 13, 1891. Their mother Virginia, passed away in
1892.

        Frederick & Anna Theresia Bain.

Six months later, Fred was united in marriage to Anna Theresia Ulbert. Children
born to this marriage were: Anna Gertrude (Jensky) May 23, 1894; Edwin Rudolph,
December 11, 1896; Arthur Walter, July 26, 1900.

Fred, Anna and family moved to the Conde, SD area, in 1904. They lived there
until 1917, when they bought land in Section 35, of Carl Township, in McPherson
County. There they built a two-story house, barn, granary and chicken house.
These buildings are still in use today. Alvin Kallas is the owner of the farm,
Otto Kolb lives on it.

Fred passed away in 1922, Anna continued to live on the farm in Carl Township
for a couple of years and then went to work as a housekeeper for others.

She retired and lived in a small home in Leola, next to her daughter Anna and
son-in-law Richard Jensky. When Richard and his wife moved to Aberdeen, SD,
Anna Bain, went to live with them. Anna passed away in 1942.

FRED and LOUISE BAIN

Fred Charles Bain was born August 3, 1887, in Nicollet County, St. Peter, MN.
He was the son of Fred (Frederick) Bain and Virginia (Pourrier) his wife. Fred
C. Bain and Louise Kurtz, were married September 15, 1909. Louise, the daughter
of Gustav and Louise (Fogel) Kurtz, was born July 22, 1889, in Gunns, Austria.
The family moved to Elkton, SD, when Louise was about four years old. Louise
taught school for several years.

Fred and Louise moved to McPherson County in March 1928. They lived where Alvin
Kallas is now residing.

Fred C. Bain died March 11, 1930. His brothers, George and Henry, are both
deceased. His sister, Mrs. Jennie Heagley, is in the Aberdeen Nursing Center.

Louise moved to Leola in August 1933. She was head cook at the Leola Dormitory
from 1934-35. In the summer she was head of the N.Y.A. girls and taught sewing,
canning and was in charge of distribution of food to the needy.

In May 1941, Zona, Earl and Louise, moved to Brookings to take care of her
father, Gustav Kurtz. After the death of her father, Louise moved back to Leola
to live near her children. She lived in an apartment in the Zulk (a/k/a
Shaeffer) Hotel. She resided there until she broke her hip in October 1973. She
then resided at the Americana Nursing Center for more than seven years. She
died in the Ellendale Nursing Home May 24, 1981, having lived there three
months. She was nearly 92 years old.

To this union nine children were born: Louise Meyer, Mina, SD; Laura Harrison,
Ellendale, ND; Vera Kindelspire Nelson, La Moure, ND; Ada Bundschuh, Litchfield
Park, AZ; Elta Lapka, Leola, SD; Iva Habeck, Ipswich, SD; Fred E. Bain,
Webster, SD; Zona Pittenger Clark, Bristow, OK and Earl Bain, Wisconsin Rapids,
WI. Vera, Ada, Elta, Iva and Fred all attended Leola High School .

GEORGE WM. and MARY ANN BAIN

George Wm., the son of Fred C. and Virginia (Pourrier) Bain, was born September
24, 1888, at Ottawa, MN. He attended country school through the eighth grade.
He spent his early life farming in the Elkton area.

On December 31, 1908, at Elkton, George was married to Mary Ann Lynch. They
moved to Verdon, SD, where George operated a dray line with wagon and horses.
In the fall of 1909, the family moved eight miles east and three-fourths mile
north of Leola, here they built up their farm. There were no roads or fences.

Three sons were born to this union: Francis, born September 28, 1909 married
Janette Little at Mellette, SD, March 12, 1936. They had six children. Francis
died October 10, 1969, in Oregon. Lloyd . . . (see Lloyd Bain, history); Fred
"Fritz," was born April 2, 1915, married Meta Stickel October 16, 1940. Two
sons were born to this union: Frank and Lee of Aberdeen, SD.

Mary Ann passed away August 18, 1920.

George married Blanche Rude at Leola, SD on March 4, 1923. Blanche was born
April 14, 1901, to Al and Mina Rude at Elkhart, IN. They had six children:
Freeman, born December 1, 1923, drowned in the Elm Dam, August 31, 1940; Mrs.
Robert (Edna) Mesmer of Detroit Lakes, MN, born May 14, 1926; Bill of Kansas
City, MO, born October 18, 1928; Mrs. Jerald (Helen) Andersen, born January 13,
1932, at Elkton, SD; Mrs. Glyde (Virginia) Knutson, born May 13, 1934, lives in
Lake Benton, MN; Charles born March 11, 1938, lives at Owatonna, MN.

        George Wm. & Blanche Bain.

In the summer of 1925, George bought three new tractors and a threshing
machine. He shipped several carloads of his horses to Michigan. He continued
farming and ran a threshing rig every fall possible. They experienced drought
and were hailed out many times.

In December 1947, George and his family returned to a farm near Elkton, where
Blanche died March 21, 1950.

George married Isabella Watts, on April 8, 1951. She was from Miles City, MT, a
widow who had ten grown children. George died February 13, 1977. Isabella
returned to Montana to be near her children. She died June 4. 1978.

LLOYD E. and DELORIS BAIN

Lloyd was born July 31, 1913, to George and Mary Ann (Lynch) Bain, where the
family had homesteaded; eight miles east and three-fourths mile north of Leola.
He started school in Willow I with his brothers. His mother passed away August
18, 1920. They spent two winters at the home of their grandparents, Mr. and
Mrs. John Lynch, at Brookings, SD where they also attended school, returning in
the spring to help with farming and chores. Lloyd completed the eighth grade at
Willow 1.

During the depression and drought, work was hard to find. In the fall of 1933,
Lloyd went to North Dakota to pick potatoes. Later he rode the freight train
into Minnesota and continued to pick potatoes for three cents a bushel. The
next fall he hauled baled hay, straw and feed from the Red River Valley, in
North Dakota, for $1.00 a day wages.

Lloyd joined the C.C.C.'s and was stationed at Camp Narrows, BlueBell, SD,
about 15 miles southeast of Custer, for a nine-month period. He returned home
in time to help with the threshing in 1935.

On August 8, 1938, Lloyd was united in marriage to Deloris, the daughter of
George and Laura (Mills) Kindelspire. Deloris was born May 17, 1921, on the
Matt Kindelspire ranch, south of Leola. After their marriage Lloyd and Deloris
moved to the Mitchell Farm, owned by Floy Hickman, located 12 miles northeast
of
Leola. The first crop was put in with horses. They later bought the farm.

It was on this homestead that their two children were born: Duane, born
February 11, 1940, married Patricia Marshall at Strongville, OH, March 11,
1961. He is a lineman instructor at VO-TECH in Mitchell, SD. They are the
parents of five children: Ronda, born December 31, 1961, married Bruce Geffre
May 30, 1981. James was born December 20, 1962; David, September 29, 1967;
John, September 27, 1972; Brenda, July 4, 1975.

Darlis was born February 15, 1941, she married Lyle Weishaar at Leola, on
October 6, 1963. Darlis is secretary of Good Shepherd Lutheran Church, of
Aberdeen. Lyle is employed at Dakota Midland Hospital. They have two sons:
Scott, born May 28, 1966; Boyd, March 27, 1968.

Lloyd continued farming in partnership with the Kindelspires until 1956 when he
and Ted Liedle bought the store, feed and cream station from Ed Albrecht. The
farm was sold to Clinton Kindelspire; the Lee Kindelspire family live there at
present.

Bain and Liedle took over the new business July 1, 1956, known as B and L
Market. In 1959 they received the prize for the most beautiful float in the
75th Anniversary Parade.

Lloyd bought Ted Liedle's share of the business in 1960. They continued to buy
cream and eggs, the store business was leased to Bernard Mack. In 1971 the
business was sold to Vincent Geffre.

        Deloris & Lloyd Bain.

Lloyd was employed with the city of Leola from 1970-76. Lloyd was custodian at
the Leola school for 2 1/2 years. He also was a Standard bulk truck driver for
Elmer Hoffman until 1981, when the business was sold to Walter Hoffman where
Lloyd is presently employed.

Deloris has been employed as a kitchen helper at the Leola school since 1972.
She is a member of the Star Extension Club; U.M.W. and Eve Circle of the
church. Lloyd and Deloris are members of the Methodist Church.

LUKAS E. and EVA BALLIET

Lukas E. Balliet, came to South Dakota from Russia in 1902, at the age of ten.
He grew up in Eureka, attended local schools and Eureka College. In 1915, he
married Eva Gross. In 1927 he was elected to the office of Clerk of Courts of
McPherson County and moved his family to Leola, the County Seat. He held that
office for 30 years. In 1957, he left Leola and spent his remaining years in
Lodi, CA.

There are five Balliet children, all of whom graduated from Leola High School,
and now all reside in California. Harold lives in Huntington Beach, CA, has two
daughters and a granddaughter. He served in the Army in World War II and saw
action in the Pacific area. Wally lives in Rocklin, CA, is semi-retired. He
also served in World War II in North Africa and Italy. He has no children.

Ella Palmer lives in San Clemente, CA, with her husband, who is a general
contractor. They have two sons and one grandson.

Wilma Canady is a registered nurse and lives and works in Temple City, CA. She
has three children and four grandchildren .

Marcie Gaither of Long Beach, CA, is a medical transcriber in a hospital in
Long Beach. She has two children and two grandchildren.

ARNOLD and CAROL BECKER

On June 28, 1970, at Leola, Carol Schaible was married to Arnold Becker of
Ashley, ND.

Carol, the daughter of Adolph and Olivia Schaible, was born on April 12, 1946,
at Aberdeen, SD. She attended school in Leola, graduated from high school in
1964.

After attending Northern State College in Aberdeen, she returned to Leola to
find employment. Carol continues to work part time in the Office of Register of
Deeds, at the courthouse.

Arnold Becker, the son of Peter and Mathilda (Morlock) Becker, was born on a
farm northeast of Ashley, ND, on May 12, 1938. He attended school near Ashley,
graduated from Ashley High School in 1958. After serving in the United States
Army, he returned to farming, near Ashley.

Following their marriage, Arnold and Carol purchased the Adolph Schaible farm,
which is historically known as the "Dively Place."

        James, Carol, Jeffrey, Arnold and Jessica Becker.

They are the parents of three children: Jeffrey, born in December 1979; James,
in January 1981; Jessica, in March 1982.

Besides being busy with their family, they find time to participate in church
and community activities. They are members of St. James Lutheran Church, where
Arnold has served on the Church Council and as Sunday School teacher. Carol is
a member of the ALCW and American Legion Auxiliary. They are active members of
the Town and Country Twirlers Square Dancers.

JACOB P. and CAROLINA BECKER

Jacob P. Becker, born September 21, 1877, to Philip and Sophie nee Bischke
Becker in Kassel, South Russia, migrated at the age of 12 with his family to a
homestead near Eureka. In November 1898, he married Carolina Kuszmaul, who was
born to John and Magdalena nee Weil Kuszmaul in Bergdorf, South Russia, on
January 24, 1876, and migrated to a homestead near Eureka at the age of 19 The
young couple homesteaded northwest of Leola and later moved to the farm which
is the present Elmer Ketterling farm west of Leola and became the parents of
seven children.

        The Jacob P. Becker family. Back: Caroline, Emil, Lydia, Jacob J. and
        Theresa. Front: Martha, Jacob P., Carolina and John.

Active in community and church affairs, Mr. Becker served on his township,
school and church boards. The Becker home was a stopping place for those coming
to Leola from the west, with one well-traveled trail leading directly through
their land. In the 1940's they moved to Leola, where Jacob died in May 1953,
followed closely by his wife in January 1954.

Surviving children include Martha Chewakin, living on a farm near Pollock with
her son Donald and family; Jacob J., retired in Anaconda, MT; and John J.,
retired in Lodi, CA.

JACOB J. and GERTRUD BECKER

Jacob J. and Gertrud L. Becker became a part of Leola's business community in
1946 when Emil and Jacob bought out E. D. Berridge and Son and started Becker
Implement, later known as Becker's. Case implements, electric appliances,
radio and TV sales and repair, heavy hardware and REA wiring and plumbing
contracting were all handled by the business, of which Jacob became the sole
owner in 1950. Emil served as assistant city marshall and water superintendent
for the city.

Jacob was born on September 2, 1910, to Jacob P. and Caroline Becker at the
family farm west of Leola. On July 17, 1941, he married Gertrud Dierenfeldt of
Eureka, born there on April 24, 1919. They farmed west of Leola for five years
before moving back to Leola. Their four children are Carol Metz, owner and
manager of Connections Graphics in Minneapolis; Steve, counselor with the drug
and alcohol unit at the VA Hospital in Hot Springs; Terry, nurse-anesthesist at
St. Luke's Hospital in Duluth, MN; and Randy, chef at the Madison Club and
part-time art student at the U. of Wisconsin in Madison, WI. Carol and Steve
grew up in Leola and attended high school there.

        Gertrud & Jacob J. Becker.

Jacob started his public service as a Triple A (now known as ASCS) field man,
later serving as county chairman and also War Board chairman during WWII. While
in business, he also served as county auditor and county director of
equalization before joining the South Dakota Department of Legislative Audits
as an examiner. After the sale of the business, the building was used as
headquarters for the 75th anniversary of Leola and was later torn down.

Besides working in the family business, Gertrud taught school in Spring
Township for one year and then in Leola High School for ten years, after which
she worked for the McPherson County Abstracting Company for a year. Active in
community affairs, both served in various offices in their church, civic
organizations, clubs, Eastern Star and Masons. Jacob helped to organize the FEM
rural electric organization.

Selling their business in 1958, they moved to Huron in 1962, where Jake
continued his auditing work and Gertrud served as head of the English
department at Huron Senior High School for 19 years. Upon Jake's retirement in
December 1975, he continued as an independent public accountant and auditor.
They retired to their present home at 1919 Tammany, Anaconda, MT in 1982.

MATHEIS and ALMA BECKER

Matheis Becker, son of Phillip Becker and Sophia nee Pischke, was born
September 26, 1883, in Kassel, South Russia. On January 26, 1906, he was united
in marriage to Alma Steiger at Menno, SD. Alma, the daughter of Gottlieb
Steiger and Sophia Berreth, was born May 18, 1889, in Menno, SD.

The family lived on farms in the Leola and Long Lake vicinity until the spring
of 1942 when Matheis retired from the farm and moved to Leola. He was employed
by the State Highway Department until 1956 when he retired. They were members
of St. James Lutheran Church.

This union was blessed with four sons and six daughters: Clara, deceased;
Bertha, married Henry Zumbaum, lives in Aberdeen; Lenora, married Albert Hinz,
is deceased; Albert, married Anna Schumacher, lives in Spokane, WA; Rueben,
married Matilda Weisz, lives in Spokane, WA; Edna, married Dan Lechner, lives
in Leola; Raymond, married Bertha Schaible, deceased; Gertrude, married Albert
Schaible, lives in Leola; Edmund, married Ella Muhlbeier, lives in Clearfield,
IA; and Delphy, married Herbert Albrecht, lives in Deadwood, SD.

Mr. Becker passed away June 26, 1959, at Leola, SD. Mrs. Becker passed away
December 12, 1977, in Aberdeen, SD Both are buried at Green Mound Cemetery in
Leola,

PHILLIP and HELENA BECKER

Phillip Becker was born in Cass County, ND in 1882. His wife, Helena Brosz was
born in Martell, SD in 1894. They were married in 1912 at the German Lutheran
Church in Leola with Rev. Taubert officiating, and with her sister Frederika
and his brother, Edward as attendants.

Phillip was a blacksmith who had his own shop in Leola by 1908; he continued
this work until his retirement in Bristol, SD in 1955.

        Helena & Phillip Becker.

Children of the Becker's living today are Elmer of Spring Valley, CA; Robert,
of Pekin, IL; Adeline (Mrs. Kenneth Traphagen) and Phyllis (Mrs. Harold
Vaughan) of Aberdeen; Betty Jean (Mrs. Ernest Smith) of Hot Springs Village,
AR; Margaret of Santa Barbara, CA; Louise (Mrs. Paul Logan) of Agar, SD. A
daughter, Ruth Schwartz died in 1983.

The Beckers have 18 grandchildren and 12 great-grandchildren.

Phillip died in 1968; Helena died in 1969. Both are buried in Bristol, SD.

WILL and MARY BECKER

William (Will) Becker was born June 21, 1876 and Mary was born July 20, 1883.
Mary and Will were married February 14, 1900. They lived on a farm four miles
west, 1 1/2 miles south of Leola. When they retired, they moved to Leola where
they lived the rest of their lives.

Will and Mary had three daughters. Alvina, Marbell, Mable and two sons, Arnold
and Harold.

        Mary & William (Will) Becker.

Alvina and Marbell married brothers, Alvina to Alex Schumack and Marbell to
Morris Schumack. Alvina and Alex had two daughters, Marbell and Morris had
three sons and one daughter. Mable married and had one son and one daughter.
Arnold married and did not have children. Harold married and had five sons and
five daughters.

Will and Mary were members of St. Paul's Lutheran Church in Leola. Will passed
away in October of 1957.

ALBERT and MELINDA BENDER

Albert, son of Frederick and Katherine (Guthmiller) Bender was born in 1921 on
a farm near Long Lake. SD.

        Albert & Melinda Bender

In 1944 he married Malinda Zenker, born in 1924 to Fred and Caroline (Rath)
Zenker of Leola, who had been teaching in Highland Township. At first they made
their home with his parents, but in 1945 purchased the Marion Hummel Ranch. In
1974 they sold the ranch to Earl and Sylvia Rott, and moved to Aberdeen. Albert
is presently employed by Mohr's Custom Fencing and Malinda is a Walter's
Nutritional Products distributor.

The Benders have two children. Leon (born 1947) married Sue Shantz and they
have two children. Leon is the owner operator of Eastside Service in Aberdeen,
and his wife works in the dietary department of St. Luke's Hospital. The
Benders' daughter Kathleen (born 1949) married William DeYoung, and has two
children. She is a legal secretary for Siegel, Barnett and Schutz, and her
husband works for Frontier Kaps at Ipswich, and does some commercial
photography. They live at Mina Lake.

ALBERT and LENORE BENDER

Albert was born to Jacob and Emelia (Pfieffle) Bender October 1, 1906 at
Yankton County, SD. His parents moved to McPherson County, SD. Albert joined a
family of four brothers, Edmund, William, Richard and August, and five sisters,
Olga, Mada, Mary, Martha and Bertha.

Albert married Lenore Diede on December 12, 1929 at her home near Barnard, SD.
Lenore was born June 9, 1909 at Lesterville, SD. Her parents were Christian
Michael and Anna Marie (Schatz) Diede. Lenore's paternal grandparents
immigrated to America from South Russia. They sailed from Hamburg, Germany on
the vessel, Westphalia and landed in New York July 23, 1873. The 1880 census
shows them living in Yankton County in the Dakota Territory. Lenore moved with
her family to a farm about six miles west of Barnard, SD in 1918. Lenore's
brothers and sisters are: Hugo, Edmund, Edwin, Olinda, Edna, Rueben and
Rubrecht.

        The Albert Bender family. Back: John, Arlene, Jerold and Milbert.
        Front: Lenore and Albert.

Albert and Lenore moved to a farm north of Leola after they married. Later they
moved to Minnesota where they lived for three years. They came back in 1941 and
started farming 4 1/2 miles west of Wetonka. They remained on that farm until
they retired in October of 1978. Albert and Lenore have four children: Milbert,
married to Darlene Schwartz. They have two daughters and live on a farm
southeast of Leola; Arlene, married to Marvin Rall. They have four children and
live in Worthington, MN; John, married to Carol Beilke. They have five children
and live in Aberdeen, SD; and Jerold, married to Lea Erickson. They live in
Gettysburg, SD with their three children.

The Benders celebrated their Golden Wedding Anniversary December 1979, at
Leola. Albert passed away April 2, 1981. Lenore still lives in Leola.

Lenore is a member of the Leola Reformed Church.

        Melvin, Olga, Fred M. and Marvin Bender.

Fred M. and Olga farmed until they moved to Leola where they still reside.

ALBERT NORRIS and MARY BELL

Albert Norris (A. N.) Bell, the son of W. G. and Margaret (Edgar) Bell, was
born December 25, 1873, in Iowa.

On February 8, 1899 he was married to Mary Boehmer, at Moville, IA. Mary was
the daughter of Antone and Lena (Baier) Boehmer, of Jackson County, IA. She was
born September 20, 1879, at Iowa.

        Albert Norris (A. N.) & Mary Bell.

The Bell family came to South Dakota in 1903 and settled on a homestead in
Edmunds County. They lost their homestead due to a fire set by hot coals from
the Milwaukee train. The Bells then moved to Roscoe, SD. Four years later the
family moved to Leola, where they operated a restaurant that was adjacent to
the Brosz Store, on the east side of Sherman Street. The first home in Leola
for the Bells was the one-story square green house on the west side of what is
now Route 45. (Still standing, Mrs. Rochus Geffre home.)

Mr. Bell left the restaurant to work for rancher S.D. Frost, breaking sod.

In 1918-'19-'20 Mr. Bell operated the municipal light plant and also was the
town's marshal.

During the flu epidemic of 1918, Albert spent much of his time helping the
sick. At that time the school was closed and used as a hospital.

Again, in 1920-'21-'22, the Bells operated a cafe on Sherman Street. Mr. Bell
also was a house mover in later years.

Albert and Mary were the parents of five children: Lester, born in 1900 in
Moville, IA, married Hilma Rinke of Leola in 1923. Their son Leo died while
serving in the U.S. Navy, in 1945. A daughter Marjorie and family, reside in
Idaho. Lester served as Justice of Peace in 1973. He died November 8, 1977.
Hilma died July 22, 1969. Both are buried in Green Mound Cemetery.

Minnie, born in 1902 in Moville, IA, married Hjalmer Turnwall of Leola in 1920.
They had one child.

Lola, born in 1904 in Edmunds County, on the farm called the Silver Spring
Ranch. Lola married Roland Christian, in 1928. Their son Warren lost his life
while serving in the Marines during the Korean War in 1952. A daughter, Lila,
married Ward Smalley. She is employed at the Leola State Bank. They have two
children: Mrs. Lee (Pamela) Rau and a son, Kevin. They all reside in Leola.

Alpha, born in Edmunds County in 1906, married Peter Sorensen in 1923. They had
four children.

Violet, born in Leola in 1919, married Milbert Potratz in 1940. No children
were born to this union.

BERLIN--CHRISTENSEN

May (Fosler) Berlin was born January 12, 1890, to Charles and Ella (Haberman)
Fosler, of Leola. She grew up and taught school in this area. In the summer of
1913 she met Ethel Houston at Teachers' Institute in Aberdeen. Ethel suggested
that May file a homestead near her claim at Faith, SD. May was always ready for
a challenge and decided to see what Faith looked like. She boarded the train,
and after a long trip (it took them almost a whole day from Mobridge to Faith
as they had to stop and replace ties on the railroad bed), she arrived and was
met by Miss Houston, who took her to her own shanty with her horse and buggy.
They looked at several claims, but one had a creek with a cottonwood on the
side of a hill, which suited May.

        May (Fosler-Berlin) Christensen.

They drove back to Faith to the land office where she filled out the form, and
the claim was hers. Within a week she bought a shack and a pony, signed a
contract to teach and hurried back to tell her parents and friends what she had
done. They were shocked and did all they could to talk her out of it, but she
was 23, insisted on going, and there was not much they could do except send her
sister Delphy along to help her get settled. She took her clothes, the rocker
she had been raised in, her iron bedstead, a few dishes and kitchen utensils
and some muslin, and went back to turn her 12'x14' shack into a home.

A big box was the table, and she kept her supplies under it. She used the
muslin to make curtains for the windows, and to make a curtain, attached to a
high shelf on one side. This made a closet for clothes. They went down the draw
to the creek and cut blocks of cottonwood for chairs.

She rode 4 1/2 miles every day to her school, a 12'x20' tar-papered shack where
she taught nine boys and girls. Once they killed a rattlesnake in the window.

Will Berlin arrived soon after, and he and May were married October 14, 1913 at
Dupree. He covered the shanty with sod and dug a well. Will sold the shack in
1914 and they returned to Leola, where they farmed north of town.

To the Berlins one son, Chester, was born, February 3, 1923. William died in
1935.

        Al & May Christensen.

After his death, May spent a year in Arizona and California. Returning to
Leola, she married Albert Christensen in 1938. When Al was asked why he left
Iowa in 1914 to come to McPherson County, he said it was to get away from rain.
He could not have made a better choice! Al worked on the Turner and Bell Ranch
until the outbreak of World War I, when he joined the army.

The Christensens continued farming on the home place until the late '70s, when
Chester operated the farm.

May was a founder of the Leola Country Club, a member of the Order of the
Eastern Star 124 and a member of the United Methodist Church. May died April
21, 1983, at the age of 93. Al continues to spend his summers on the farm.

The following is one of the many poems authored by May Christensen.

IN THE HOSPITAL

Well, now isn't it fun to lie in a hospital bed
With two pillows at your head?
Not a thing to do, just be cared for and fed.
With your hands gently folded across your chest
You just rest--and rest--and rest.
The smiling nurses will care for your every need.
They're so very kind indeed.
And if you're very ill, they'll give you another pill.
The doctor will come in and say,
"Well, how are you today?"
He gives a few orders and is on his way.
Yet with all these comforts you will find
The only thought running through your mind
Is, "I want to go home."

ALBERT and GLADYS BERRETH

Albert Berreth, son of David and Margaret (Sherer) Berreth, was born July 24,
1912 at Leith, ND. He was the fourth child having two sisters and an older
brother. Albert was baptized that same year on September 9, 1912, at Leith.

In 1915, the family moved to Menno, SD, where they lived a short time. Then
went on to Winner to work on a ranch, where Albert started school.

In the early 1920's the family moved by covered wagon to Highmore, SD. There
Albert continued his schooling. Then moving to another ranch near Holabird, SD,
where Albert finished the 8th grade and was confirmed at St. John's Evangelical
Lutheran Church on July 8, 1928.

In 1931, the family moved to Leola. Albert came to Leola the following spring
and was employed by Fred Tschappat, who farmed south of Leola. Staying here
until the death of his brother-in-law, who was killed in a train accident at
Ree Heights, SD. Albert went to help his sister, and later got a job in the
flour mill at Highmore, returning later to work for Fred Tschappat again.

On January 1, 1940, Albert was united in marriage to Gladys Tschappat, daughter
of Fred and Nellie Tschappat. Gladys grew up on the farm and received her
education in Leola and Washington Township schools. She attended three years of
high school. Prior to her marriage, Gladys was employed in several households,
including the E. W. Hilgemanns, Orrin Berridges and Alem Hagens.

On March 15, 1943, Albert moved his family to a farm south of Leola, from the
town of Leola, where Albert had been working for John Kulm as a mechanic. They
bought the farm that was known as the Heye Ferdinand farm. Here they farmed,
milked cows, raised hogs and chickens. Leland took over the family farm in
1974, at which time Albert and Gladys moved into Leola.

        The Albert Berreth Family. Back: Darlys, Larry, Leland and Marilyn.
        Front: Gladys and Albert.

Albert and Gladys are parents of five children. Darlys, born March 15, 1941;
Larry, born September 29, 1942; Leland, born September 4, 1946; Arlen, born
November 21, 1952; Marilyn, born December 6, 1954. Their son Arlen passed away
in September of 1961 after a
short illness.

Albert sold Standard feed and corn for a number of years. He was also employed
by the Leola Equity Elevator
in 1971 and worked until his retirement in 1977.

Albert and Gladys are members of St. Paul's Lutheran Church of Leola. Albert is
a member of the church council, and Gladys is a member of the Lutheran Women's
Missionary League. As a contribution to the Leola community, Albert served on
the Leola School
Board for 23 years.

LELAND and NANCY BERRETH

Leland Berreth, son of Albert and Gladys Berreth, was born September 4, 1946,
on the farm which he bought from his father in 1978. He attended Leola schools,
working part time for Bain Produce and Mobil. After graduation he worked in
Aberdeen for Mobil and Hub City Iron.

In 1967 he married his classmate Nancy, daughter of Clint and Virginia
Kindelspire, who was working for K. O. Lee. In 1970 they moved back to the
Tschappat farm, and in 1974 to the home farm where he began dairy farming and
does custom stacking and baling.

        Jodi Lyrm, Kelli Dawn and Jeffrey Lee Berreth.

They have three children: Jodi Lynn, born June 6, 1968; Jeffrey Lee, born July
5, 1970; and Kelli Dawn, who was born April 27, 1981. They are active in Trail
Riders,
the Catholic and St. Paul's Lutheran churches.

LeROY and JoANN BIEBER

LeRoy Bieber moved to the Leola area in 1961, having been raised on a farm near

        The LeRoy Bieber family.

He and his brother, Ron, were partners on the Bender place until 1964, when he

RON and LOIS BIEBER

Johann Jacob Bieber (great-grandfather of Ron Bieber) after 23 years of
marriage at the age of 49 years, came to America and homesteaded in McPherson
County with a family of five sons and four daughters. The Johann Biebers and
their children, ages three to 19, left Glucksthal, a village in the Ukraine of
Russia in 1884. They traveled by train to Bremer, Germany and boarded the
"Elbe," a Nort German-Loid ocean liner. They arrived in New York September 29,
1884 and traveled by train to Ipswich and drove by oxen to their final
destination 4 1/2 miles northeast of Eureka, a three-day journey.

The origin of Johann J. Bieber's ancestors were in the Wuertenberg, Germany,
area, prior to settling in the Ukraine about the beginning of the 19th century.
Many of these German immigrants came to the Ukraine at the invitation of
Czarian Catherine II who offered land tax incentives and military exemption.
The relatives and one daughter of Johann J. Bieber who remained in Russia not
only lost all tax and military exemptions but also lost their land, freedom and
lives in order that the communists could collectivise the farm.

Ron was born south of Java, SD, on the farm of his parents, Arthur and Emillie
Bieber. He attended country school and high school in Bowdle, SD. He furthered
his education at Augustana College for two years and two years at South Dakota
University at Vermillion where he received his BS in Business Administration.

He was employed in Kansas City at J. C. Penney as a time study engineer and in
Michigan in the Montgomery Ward management trainee program. He also spent 1 1/2
years in the U.S. Army.

In 1961 Ron and LeRoy Bieber purchased the Julius Binder farm and moved to
Leola, Arena Township.

On December 29, 1963 Ron married Lois J. Menzel at Lemmon, SD. They made their
home near Leola, nine miles west and one-half mile north of Leola.

They are engaged in a commercial cow, calf and steer operation.

        The Ron Bieber family.

Four children were born to this union: Craig John; Sandra Joy; Kristi Jean and
Stewart Arthur.

The Bieber Ranch has been involved in Soil and Water Conservation practices and
also irrigation. The ranch is the major producer of garrison creeping foxtail
in McPherson County.

In 1968 Ron purchased 14 Red Angus cows from which he has built a herd of 250
females.

In 1976 they held their first annual production sale, which is held annually in
the month of March.

In 1982, six cows were sold to George and Kyle McClaster of San Antonio, TX, to
be used in an embryo transfer program, these cows averaged $7,500 each.

In January 1983 Ron sold one-half semen interest in a young two-year-old bull
called RAB Abe Lincoln for $105,000. This was a record for the Red Angus Breed.

Ron has served as a director on the SD Beef Cattle Improvement Assn.; six years
as director on the National Board of the Red Angus Assn.; two years as Second
Vice President and two years as First Vice President of the Red Angus Assn. He
was the founder and first President of the Red Angus Breeders of South Dakota
and has served as director for four years. He is presently serving as director
for the South Dakota Stockgrowers Assn., and is a member of the American
National Cattlemen.

Ron served six years on the Leola School Board.

They are members of St. James Lutheran Church where Ron is a Sunday school
teacher.

Lois worked as a bookkeeper at the Spaulding Auto Ford Co. and K. O. Lee in
Aberdeen, since her marriage has been keeping the Bieber Red Angus Ranch
records. Lois is active in Leola Extension Homemakers, has been Extension Club
President, Treasurer and is now serving as Vice President; she organized the
Leola Circle L CowBelles and has held all offices; served as director for the
South Dakota CowBelles; has helped organize the Aberdeen, Ipswich and Pierre
CowBelles; has taught Sunday school for six years; is a member of the ALCW; 4-H
leader for the Willing Workers. She has served five years as Executive
Secretary for the Red Angus Breeders of South Dakota. Is advisor for the Jr.
Red Angus Breeders of South Dakota and is active in beef promotion.

Lois was born and raised at Morristown, SD.

The Bieber family also is active with Leola Trail Riders.

JIM and DIANNE BIDWELL

August 1980 saw the arrival of Jim Bidwell and Dianne Rood to Leola. They
purchased and now reside on the Bruce and Mildred Ecker farm on the north edge
of town, south of the Leola dam (formerly Doc and Idelette Lundquists' home).

        Dianne, Chris, Jody and Jim Bidwell.

Jim, son of S. P. "Tex" and Irene (Caldwell) Bidwell, originally of Coleman,
lived in many South Dakota communities while growing up in a bridge
contractor's family. He called Sioux Falls home until 1965 when he left South
Dakota to attend school in Denver, CO. His only sister, Joan Bakke of Sioux
Falls, died in 1980.

Dianne, daughter of T. M. and Nila (Metz) Rood of Aberdeen, originally of
Roslyn, left South Dakota in 1961 to attend college in Minnesota and Nebraska
before a tenyear teaching career in Arizona and Colorado. She has one older
brother, Jim, who lives with his family in Bloomington, MN.

Jim and Dianne met in Greeley, CO, where she was teaching and he was a crane
operator. During their first year of marriage they decided to migrate back to
South Dakota. Since moving to Leola, Jim has driven truck for Sid Schaible and
Harlan Krein in addition to his farrier (horseshoeing) business and raising and
boarding horses. Dianne has served two years as Program Assistant in 4-H for
the McPherson County Extension Service and also owned and operated The Thrift
Car in 1981-82.1n 1983 she was employed by Leola OK Hardware and currently owns
and operates The Wiser Miser downtown.

Jim's two children, Jody and Chris, who live in Denver during the school year,
spend summers here in Leola with him and Dianne. The family are members of the
Leola United Methodist Church and the Leola Trail Riders.

ALBERT and OLGA BINDER

Olga Lois Martha Haase was born to Frederick and Olga (Stebner) Haase, December
10, 1918, in Cleveland, OH. She was the first of two children.

Olga spent 40 years actively working as a registered nurse, while also raising
her family. She has three children: Beverly (Mrs. Lloyd Binder) of rural Leola,
Judi (Mrs. Danny Laws) of Plainview, TX, and Dr. Don Stevens, Jr., of Spring
Valley, OH.

When her friends in Oklahoma found that Olga and her husband, Clyde Ferguson,
planned to retire in South Dakota in December of 1980, they thought she had
"lost her marbles" and spared no opportunity to tell her so. However, she had
visited Leola often before, and was eager to belong to the community. They
bought the house next to the school bus garage, and as things go, she was asked
if she would consider becoming a substitute school bus driver. The Oklahoma
friends thought she had "flipped" for sure, this time. But Olga enjoyed this
new part of her life, as well.

        Albert & Olga Binder.

In 1982, Clyde died, and in 1983, Olga married Albert Binder, of rural Tolstoy,
a cousin of her son-in-law's father.

Albert was born to Christof and Rosina (Neis) Binder, November 2, 1913, in
rural Tolstoy. He has farmed in that area, and raised his family there. In the
fall, he enjoys traveling to Washington, bringing apples back for family and
friends. Christian and Lloyd Binder had ordered apples, and when they got them,
there was a small sack of apples set aside, for "Lloyd's mother-in-law" (Olga).
She says the apples started the romance--he says it was the thank you note.
Whatever. They plan to live in Leola, commute to the farm during seedtime and
harvest, and travel in warmer climate while the snow flies in South Dakota

ARTHUR H. and RACHEL BINDER

Arthur H. Binder was born on the farm of his parents, Daniel and Magdalena
(Zumbaum) Binder, the first of six children. He was born April 1, 1907, and has
remembered April Fool's day ever since.

In 1929, he married Rachel Bitzer, in Ipswich, SD. She was a daughter of Simon
and Deborah Bitzer. Art met her while she was doing housework for Ted
Kranzler's wife, who was ill.

At first they lived on a farm between Michael Binder and Daniel Binder, but in
1932 he purchased a farm 4 1/2 miles southeast of the home farm.

Art and Rachel had three children: Miriam (Mrs. Jim Shears), Lavern, and Ruby
(Mrs. Rodger Howell). Miriam lives in Englewood, CO, and she and Jim have three
children. Lavern and his wife, Barbara, have two daughters and live in
Maryland. Ruby and her husband, Rodger, live in Hannibal, MO, and have three
children.

Art moved to Leola in 1967 and lives there now. Rachel suffered a stroke in
1972, and died at the Ipswich Hospital. She is buried at the Seventh-day
Adventist Cemetery west of Leola.

Art retired from farming, but developed a reputation as a carpenter. The first
building he completed was the Baptist Church in Leola. Since that time he has
built or remodeled many homes and buildings in Leola and the surrounding area.

CHRISTIAN E. and ADELINE BINDER

Christian Edward Binder was born in 1913 to Daniel and Magdalena (Zumbaum)
Binder on the Daniel Binder farmstead. In 1936, he, with a number of others,
went to seek his fortune out west. The group traveled together in a truck owned
by John Dais. Gideon Dais and Ezra Hager were the drivers. The group arrived in
Washington on July 4. Christian spent a busy three months, making hay on a
dairy farm, picking blackberries, hops, and onions, and working in a quarry. He
returned to South Dakota with Bill, Freda and Hilda Banek. His gain included
$100.00 cash, new shoes, new work jacket, and new overalls--he felt rich. With
the money, he bought some calves and started farming. He still hired out at
times and in 1938 he worked near Hurley, running the combine during harvest.

Adeline Schumacher Binder was born to Jacob and Matilda (Pfeifle) Schumacher in
1917. She was the first of 12 children, one of whom died in infancy. She grew
up on the home farm, seven miles southwest of Long Lake. She got a lot of
practical experience working for various farmers during harvest or helping
along after someone's surgery. In November of 1937, she went to work at the
John Voegele, Sr. home, caring for Mrs. Voegele, who was an invalid. That
winter, Christian noticed that there was an extra attraction at the Voegele
farm besides sister Lillian who was married to John, Jr.

Christian and Adeline were married April 25, 1939, in the Seventh-day Adventist
Church, then located about 11 miles west of Leola. They set up housekeeping
with Christian's parents. When Daniel died in 1942, Christian and Adeline
bought the home farm.

        Darlene (Cook), Lloyd, Christian, Adeline and Roger Binder.

Christian and Adeline have three children: Roger, Lloyd, and Darlene (Cook).
Roger married Charlene Scholl, and lives in Lincoln, NE. They have four
children: Dale, Debra, Susan and Sherrie. Lloyd married Beverly Stevens, and
remains on the home farm. They have two sons, Steven and Garritt. Darlene lives
in National City, CA. She is employed at Paradise Valley Hospital and enjoys
music and photography as hobbies.

DANIEL and MAGDALENA BINDER

Daniel Binder was born in 1887, on the homestead farm of his parents, Michael
Binder and Magdalena (Rueb) Binder, located nine miles south of Long Lake. He
was one of nine children. In 1904 his father, a widower, remarried, and in
1907, Daniel married Magdalena Zumbaum, a daughter of his new stepmother.
Magdalena's father's name was Johan Zumbaum. Magdalena was born in 1883.

        Daniel & Magdalena Binder.

Daniel and Magdalena started their own farm one half mile north of the Michael
Binder farm. They had six children, two of whom died in infancy. The four
surviving children are: Arthur H., Lilian (Mrs. John Voegele), Beata (Mrs.
Herbert Jundt), and Christian E.

DAVE BROSZ CREAM STATION

        Cream stub from the Leola Creamery and Dave Brosz Cream Station--1933

Milking had always been part of life on the Lakeside Farm, as Daniel named it.
In 1928, an upright silo was built, and a DeLaval milking setup was installed.
It had a vacuum pump and two buckets. Up to 35 cows were milked in this
fashion.

In addition to his regular farming, Daniel enjoyed truck gardening, raising
watermelons being his special joy.

In the spring of 1942, while branding cattle, Daniel was kicked in the abdomen,
and gangrene set in. He underwent surgery the following day, but died the same
evening. Magdalena remained on the farm with the youngest son Christian, and
his family, until shortly before her death in 1974. They are both buried in the
Seventh-day Adventist Cemetery, three-fourths mile east of their farm.

LLOYD and BEVERLY BINDER

Lloyd LeRoy Binder was the second of three children born to Christian and
Adeline (Schumacher) Binder. On December 18, 1943, he arrived, assisted by
Idellet Lundquist, R.N., in the town of Leola.

After attending country schools through the 8th grade, Lloyd went to Plainview
Academy, a Seventh-day Adventist boarding high school in Redfield, SD. He
graduated in 1961, and spent a year working for his dad, and deciding that
farming was what he wanted to make his vocation. However, formal education was
not complete until he attended Union College in Lincoln, NE, for two years.

As luck would have it, the young lady who caught his eye was not from South
Dakota--not even from a farm background, but rather from a city way down in
Texas. But love will find a way, and Lloyd launched on a campaign to share one
of South Dakota' s best kept secrets--"South Dakota is really a good place to
live."

Beverly Helena was born to C. Donald and Olga (Haase) Stoehr-Stevens, March 24,
1944, in St. Helena, CA. She was the oldest of three children born to this
union. The family moved several times, eventually settling in Lubbock, TX.
After attending boarding school at Southwestern Jr. College, near Dallas, Bev
attended Union College, fulfilling her dream of becoming a nurse. That is where
Lloyd and Bev met. They were married December 26, 1965, and spent the first few
months of married life in Denver, CO, where Bev was completing nurse's
training.

In June of 1966 they moved back to the home farm, living next door to Lloyd's
parents, and have been "actively engaged" in farming ever since. They have
since purchased the farm, and have developed the dairy as their main business.
Any spare time available to Lloyd is filled with the construction of new or
restoration of old furniture, and restoration of old tractors, buggies and
cars. He is also involved in various church and musical activities. His
favorite hobby, however, is visiting with friends. Bev occupies her spare time
with music, art, sewing, and working with children in Pathfinder Club and
church.

        Garry, Lloyd, Beverly and Steve Binder

Lloyd and Bev have two sons, Steven Bruce, and Garritt Christian. Steve attends
Dakota Adventist Academy, in Bismarck, ND, and Garry plans to attend upon
completion of the 8th grade at Leola Public School.

MICHAEL and MAGDALENA BINDER

Michael Binder was born in 1852, in Gluckstahl, South Russia. In 1875 he
married Magdalena Rueb, daughter of Frederick Rueb. To this union nine children
were born: Fred, Michael, Jacob, John, Emma (Mrs. Christian Dollinger), Daniel,
Christof, Martha (Mrs. Jacob Renschler--then Mrs. Dave Renschler), and
Benjamin.

Concerned about political unrest and unfair conscription practices, they, with
friends, left the old world. In 1885, he and his family immigrated to Scotland,
SD, and in the same year they homesteaded nine miles south of Long Lake,
one-half mile south of old highway 10.

        Michael, Benjamin, Mary (Zumbaum), Martha and Rosina Maier
        Zumbaum Binder

In 1903, Magadalena burned to death in an unfortunate accident. She was buried
at the cemetery west of the farm. In 1904 Michael married Rosina Maier Zumbaum,
a widow with five children: Christ, Art, Katie (Mrs. Henry Renschler), Rosina,
Magadalena (Mrs. Daniel Binder), and Mary (Mrs. Edward Renschler).

Michael Binder died in 1907, and was buried in the cemetery on the homestead
also. Rosina died in 1925. She was buried in the Seventh-day Adventist Cemetery
near the farm.

WILLIAM and LENA BISHOP

Although William and Lena Bishop were not pioneer settlers in the Leola area,
Lena (Baertsch) was born in a sod shanty in North Dakota where her parents had
homesteaded in 1883, the year of her birth. William's grandfather homesteaded
in Iowa in 1883, and his mother was the first white child in the county.

        The William K. Bishop family Back: Irene and Lucille. Front: Lena
        Vincil and William K. Bishop.

The Bishops were married in North Dakota in 1909, and moved to Leola that year.
Mr. Bishop was the first principal of the new High School building. In 1916 he
became County Superintendent of Schools. In 1922 he became a State Senator; in
1926, the McPherson County Auditor, and in 1935, a State Representative. During
his 37 years in the Leola area he was also a farmer.

Their three children spent their early lives in Leola. Lucille, the oldest,
taught McPherson County schools, and from 1931-1935 was a grade school teacher
in town. The next year she married the Agriculture teacher, Ervin Boyd. He
became the County Extension Agent, later holding similar positions in Salem,
Sioux Falls, Custer, Brookings and Mitchell. They have retired to a farm near
Egan, SD, and have five children.

Irene, their second daughter, taught country schools, and for a time was Deputy
County Superintendent of Schools. She married Lester Heibel, son of John
Heibel, and they live in California.

Vincil, their son, after graduation from Colorado State U., joined the Army and
made it his career. After retirement from the service, he was a member of the
Arkansas Dept. of Health, retiring in 1981.

WILLIAM and ELSIE BLAKEMAN

William Blakeman was born August 21, 1886, on a farm near Ipswich, as with
Elsie Krueger (July 19, 1893), whom he married in 1914. Her parents had been
born in Germany and came to this area in the '80's.

        William & Elsie Blakeman.

SAMUEL (ROLLO) and HELEN BOSANKO

        ROLLO'S DOUGHNUT MACHINE: TRIBUTE TO THE MAN AND HIS MACHINES

Leola's first mail carrier was Samuel Bosanko. However, everybody knew him as
"Rollo," and as McPherson County's pioneer snowmobile inventor. During the
many years he carried mail, his machines or 'contraptions' as they were called,
brought lots of stares and stammers from young and old alike. Whenever his
machine was parked in front of the post office, it became the center of
conversation up and down main street. Then Rollo would appear, leather
mailpouch slung over his shoulder, ready to make another daily run out on his
route.

In 1912, at the tender age of 19, Rollo first started carrying mail by horse
and buggy, in a career that spanned over 34 years. The only break in that
career occurred during World War 1, while he served in the U.S. Army. When
Rollo returned, he found that times and transportation had changed, so he got
in step by driving one of Leola's first "horseless carriages."

Although times had changed, there was nothing different about the long winter
months he faced; it meant more and more snowstorms which blocked the roads and
stopped all mail runs, often for days and weeks on end.

But Rollo wasn't about to be discouraged. With the help of Gottfried Walth,
long-time mechanic at John Kulm's Ford garage, he built his first snowmobile.
Thin, metal snow runners were attached inside the front wheels to help the
snowmobile scale the big, hard-packed snowdrifts. Thick, heavy caterpillar
tractor treads riding over dual, three-wheel assemblies, supplied the power and
traction to propel this machine which looked like it belonged to another world.
During the worst blizzards, he not only packed the mail, but brought medicine
and groceries to many snow-bound farm families.

As Leola had no hospital or doctor, Rollo and his machine were put on 24-hour
call to transport Idlette Lundquist, the town's first nurse, on medical
emergencies. A hard knock on Rollo's door, or a frantic telephone call in the
middle of the night meant only one thing: someone needed help, and Rollo and
Idlette (black bag in hand) were on their way.

South Dakota is also well known for its quick spring thaws and chinook winds
which can melt snow-clogged roads overnight. Such freakish weather left long
stretches of road bare, thereby raising havoc with the caterpillar tracks on
the snowmobile. The result was numerous breakdowns, expensive repairs and hot
tempers. Rollo and Gottfried went back to the drawing board once more and came
up with as strange-a-looking machine as ever traveled the roads around Leola.

This snowmobile looked like it could easily belong on the moon, but a group of
retired farmers saw it in quite a different way. While gathered in the post
office lobby to pick up their mail, they decided to take matters into their own
hands and officially christened that strange-looking, mechanical beast parked
outside. They noticed that those four, big, fat balloon tires looked like giant
doughnuts ready to be dunked into a huge cup of coffee. Thus Rollo's machine
was dubbed 'the doughnut machine.' The nickname stuck through the years, and
even Rollo accepted it good-naturedly. Neither mud nor snow could stop him now,
as the doughnut machine helped him roll up a remarkable record of consistent
on-time mail deliveries year after year after year. The only problem he ever
had came when he attempted to make a sharp turn, as those big tires drastically
cut down the turning radius. "Seemed like it took at least two city blocks to
get
the darned thing completely turned around," he laughed.

        The Samuel (Rollo) Bosanko family. Back: Everett, Ivan and Kenneth.
        Front: Helen and Samuel.

After World War 11 ended, Rollo retired in 1946, while Earl Heibel continued
behind the wheel of the doughnut machine as his replacement. Years later, this
reliable machine was still bucking snowdrifts and fording muddy roads and
ditches. Meanwhile, Rollo and his wife (the former Helen L. Weisser) and their
three sons, Everett, Kenneth, and Ivan moved out west to Coeur D'Alene, ID, to
begin a new life.

W. E. and DAISY BRAKHAGE

Mr. and Mrs. W. E. Brakhage, known to their friends as Bill and Daisy, came to
Edmunds County from Webster, SD in 1916. In 1942 they moved to McPherson
County.

        Daisy & W. E. Brakhage.

Bill was born and raised at Webster. It was there he met Daisy Mentor, who was
born in Ida Grove, IA.

Lee, their first son, was born near Webster, before they moved to Ipswich. He
owned and managed a restaurant in Milwaukee, WI. He died at 47 years of age
from a heart attack. Goldie, their second child, was born at Ipswich. She
taught school in Edmunds and McPherson counties. She married Jacob Mardian of
Roscoe, and to them were born two sons, Ronald and Donald. Ronald lives near
Frederick, SD and Donald lives at Bardstown, KY. Leslie, Bill and Daisy's
youngest son, was born at Ipswich. He later met and married Margaret Tague of
Stillwater, OK. Leslie and Margaret farmed with his parents until they retired.
He continued to farm on the home place which was purchased from the Nelson
family in 1942, until his death in 1963 at the age of 37 years. Leslie and
Margaret had three children named Ginger, Rodney and Bradley. After Leslie' s
death, Margaret took her children and went back to Stillwater, OK. and
remarried. She passed away at the early age of 55 in 1983.

Jacob and Goldie Mardian took over the home place in 1964 and continued to live
there until Jacob became employed by the State Department of Agriculture.
Goldie taught in the Leola School System.

Bill Brakhage will be remembered as a great hunter and fisherman; Daisy, for
her beautiful gardens, flowers and home cooking. They kept hunters each fall
from all over the United States, in their spacious farm home.

Bill passed away in 1967 and Daisy died in 1976.

ALBERT C. F. and ESTHER BREITAG

Albert Carl Ferdinand Breitag, the first born of Otto H. and Mary (Potratz)
Breitag was born May 3, 1906 4 1/2 miles southwest of Leola. He attended public
school onehalf mile from there and received religious instruction in Leola at
St. James Evangelical Lutheran Church. He was baptized June 17, 1906 by Pastor
C. Knoll and confirmed July 18, 1920 by Pastor Wm. Reinecke.

Albert worked helping his father, relatives and neighbors as he was growing to
manhood.

        Albert & Esther Breitag.

Esther Guthmiller the eldest daughter of John P. and Maria (Krein) Guthmilier
was born July 7, 1905, 6 1/2 miles southwest of Leola. She attended public
school near-by, receiving religious instruction in the Reform Church. She was
baptized August 8, 1905, and confirmed August 1, 1920, both by Pastor Ulrich
Reue. She helped her mother care for the younger members of the family and
worked as a `hired girl' for various other people.

On March 14, 1928, Albert and Esther were united in marriage by Pastor Peter
Bauer in the home of the bride's parents. They began their married life on
Albert's grandfather's (Carl A. Breitag) farm four miles southwest of Leola.
This farm was one-half mile from the Otto H. Breitag farm. Albert and Esther
lived on this farm for 29 years. In 1933 Carl came to live with Albert and
Esther and stayed with them until his death in 1941. Times were rough those
first years through the "dirty thirties." They kept working, many times
realizing they hadn't made a thing. There were times when they didn't have the
money for a three cent stamp. They sold oats for six cents a bushel, wheat for
23 cents a bushel, raised and sold spring chickens for 25 cents each, and
ground horse radish to sell for 25 cents a quart. Times gradually improved and
they had better crops. Albert ran his father's threshing machine and the crew
threshed for several farmers in a season. The women spent many hours cooking
for the men. Besides cooking, many women did the farm chores, such as milking,
and feeding calves, pigs, chickens, etc.

This union was blessed with two children. Clemens Arnold was born June 1, 1929,
and now lives in Yuba City CA. Laura Marie (Schumacher) was born May 23, 1932,
and now resides in Leola.

Albert served on the Spring Township board for 20 years, was school clerk for
12 years, on church council nine years and remained active in Lutheran
Brotherhood, St. James Lutheran Church.

In 1957 they sold their farm because of Albert's back problems, and moved to
Lodi, CA, where Albert worked for a Tire and Rim factory. Esther worked in a
fruit packing plant for a short while. They stayed only a little more than a
year when they decided to move back to the 'home town' where their relatives
and friends were. They were then employed by the city to run the Leola Liquor
Store. Albert ran the store until his death on March 15, 1970. Esther then went
to live with her daughter where she now resides.

ARTHUR A. and VIRGINIA BREITAG

Arthur Breitag, the youngest of four sisters and six brothers, was born to Otto
and Mary Breitag November 16, 1926, on the farm that his father homesteaded. He
remained on the farm as he grew up, leaving it to serve in the Army during
World War II. Discharged from the service in 1946, he returned to the Breitag
farm to continue farming.

Virginia was born March 9, 1932, to Herbert and Mayme Koerner in Eureka. They
moved to Leola in 1934, where Virginia attended school.

        Virginia & Arthur Breitag.

Art and Virginia were married in a rural church in Aberdeen on June 16, 1950.
Together they took over the Breitag farm. Art and Virginia raised five sons:
Douglas, born November 11, 1951; Wayne, May 23, 1953; Brian, February 17, 1955;
Lloyd, July 19, 1956 and Donald, November 18, 1960.

Even though Art was busy farming, he became involved in the art of
salesmanship, and for a few years sold: Stainless-Steelware for the Rena-Ware
Company, World Book Encyclopedias for Field Enterprises, Inc. and seed corn for
Cargill Company. In 1972 he began selling Life Insurance for Modern Woodmen. He
is still employed by the company but has expanded into other areas of
insurance.

Art was not alone with outside interests, for Virginia began working for the
County in 1966 as a clerk in the Treasurer's office. In 1971, she became Deputy
Auditor and is still employed in the Auditor's office.

Art and Virginia decided to enlarge the Insurance business and retire from
farming in 1980. Wayne, with Lloyd's help, built their new home in the
southwestern part of Leola. Art farmed one more year and in 1981, they were
able to move into their home where they now reside. Donald, their youngest son,
still lives in the home that Art was born in on the Breitag farm.

Art and Virginia are members of St. James Lutheran Church in Leola and are very
active in all community activities.

CARL AUGUST and AUGUSTE BREITAG

Carl August Breitag, the eldest of Gottlieb and Justine Breitag's children, was
born April 14, 1855, at Turnow in the province of Brandenburg, Germany. When he
was 21, he was united in marriage to Auguste Loeffler on November 30, 1876. To
this union five children were born, two in Germany and three in America. Carl
and Auguste, along with his parents, three sisters (Augusta, Maria and
Wilhelmina), and one brother, Frederick, came to America in 1884. One brother,
Gottlieb, and his wife, Amalia, remained in Teltow, Germany.

        The Carl Breitag family. Back: Otto and Martha. Front: Auguste,
        Minna and Carl.

The Breitags, like many other dissatisfied people during that time, were
looking for a better land in which to live and America seemed most promising.
They landed in New York on April 18, 1884, and lived the first year in Meridan,
CT. From there, they came to what was the "Dakota Territory," and lived their
lives here except for a year and a half in Minnesota.

Having been of strong faith, Carl was one of the founders of the St. James
Evangelical Lutheran Church, founded in 1887. He served as Elder and Secretary
of the congregation from 1900 to 1909. Among the stories he related was how
they hauled lumber from Westport with a horse and oxen to build their church.
Carl was a religious man and was known for quoting the Bible often while
conversing with others. He remained an active member of that church until the
time of his death.

In the fire of 1888, when the fire came through the land, Auguste took their
small children and with them laid face down in the plowed field while Carl
carried water and poured it on their shanty. They lost their small barn and a
couple of animals but saved their shanty and their lives.

Carl and his family homesteaded four miles southwest of Leola (where the Elmer
Schocks now live) and Carl remained there until his death, when his grandson,
Albert C. Breitag and his wife, Esther, took over the farm. Carl had lived with
them for eight years. During his later years, he enjoyed walking and used this
mode of transportation to visit his son Otto, and the neighbors. He also
frequently walked to Leola.

Auguste passed away on April 12, 1924, and Carl died March I, 1941, of
influenza. They left behind three children: Otto Herman, Martha E., and Minna
Marie. Two children Carl Jr. and Anna preceded them in death.

GERHARDT and MARY BREITAG

Gerhardt Breitag worked at home on his parents farm when he met Mary Gutjhar,
the school teacher in Washington and Spring Township. Mary had taught school
for eight years and was still living with her folks at their home in Leola.
They were married in the Congregational Parsonage in Hosmer, SD, April 15,
1939.

Mary continued teaching school while they worked at converting the garage
building (which housed the car Mary drove) into a cream station. Gerhardt left
to serve in the Army during World War II and Mary was left to operate the cream
station.

They sold their home in 1948 and moved it off the foundation in order to
construct a new building. This new building had living quarters in the back and
the store in the front. This was known as Breitag's Market.

While living in Leola, Gerhardt and Mary had four boys; Gary, Bemidji, MN;
William, Clear Lake, IA; Melvin, Watertown, SD; and James, Sioux Falls, SD. As
they grew up the boys helped out in the store.

        Melvin, William, Gerhardt, Mary, James and Gary Breitag.
Gerhardt and Mary are members of the St. James Lutheran Church. Mary joined the
Ladies Aid and Gerhardt was co-chariman for the building of the new St. James
Parsonage. He was also a brotherhood member of the church.

Gerhardt was on the planning committee for Leola's 75th Anniversary and served
on the city council from May 5, 1952 until May 2, 1955.

They sold the business in 1958 and moved to Gerhardt's grandfather's farm which
they had purchased in 1957. They lived there until 1959 when they sold it to
Elmer Schock and bought the Stoecker farm where they now live.

For 17 years Gerhardt has been brand inspector for the Stockman's Association
of Bismarck, ND, and still inspects livestock at the Leola sale barn, and
substitutes at Britton, Sisseton, and Aberdeen.

In 1968, Gerhardt entered into a contract with the U.S. Postal Department to
become a rural mail carrier. Mary helped serve this route until 1978.

Gerhardt and Mary, still live west of Leola on the farm. Gerhardt still works
as brand inspector for the Stockman's Association even though he is
semi-retired.

        Rachel.

OTTO and MARY BREITAG

Otto Herman, the son of Carl Breitag, was born April 22, 1879, in Landsburg,
Germany. He migrated, along with his parents, to America in 1884. He grew to
manhood in Dakota Territory.

Mary Potratz, born May 11, 1885, grew up near Otto. Her familys' home was about
1 1/2 miles east of where Otto and his parents lived. Mary spent her early
years `working out' until she married Otto, June 20, 1905. This union was
blessed with 11 children: Albert, Reuben, Clara, Gregor, Gerhardt, Della, Anna,
Herbert, Alma, Ervin and Arthur.

        Back: Mr. & Mrs. Pete Mastel, Reinhold Potratz, Martha Schaeffer,
        Emil Kutschke and Minnie Fischer. Front: Otto and Mary Breitag.

Otto and Mary were homesteaders. They planted a tree-claim on section
27-126-68. This was one-half mile from Otto's parent's farm. During the early
years, Otto used to take wheat to Ipswich or Westport where there were flour
mills. He had the wheat ground into flour. This he brought home along with
other supplies for the winter Otto and Mary endured rough times working long
hours. Sometimes after a hard day's work, mealtime consisted of only bread and
milk.

In the depression years they struggled to keep a home for their family. The
whole family picked cow-chips and corn cobs to provide fuel for cooking and
warmth during the winter. In order to feed the livestock, they bought straw
from North Dakota, and mowed and stacked green thistles. Otto borrowed
$3,000.00 to keep from losing the farm. Like so many families, the older boys
went to Conservation camps to help support those back home. Amidst these trying
times, Otto and Mary had sickness to contend with. Otto had 50 percent of his
stomach removed due to ulcers, and Mary was near death from infection following
gall bladder surgery. Both regained their strength to continue on. With good
management and family cooperation, they survived the rough years.

War-time brought sadness to the family, for they lost Otto's father and one son
within one month's time. Carl Breitag passed away March 1, 1941 and his
grandson, Gregor, at Fort Snelling, MN, departed April 2, 1941. Three other
sons, Herbert, Gerhardt and Arthur left home to serve in the Armed Forces.

Otto and Mary remained on the farm until 1950, when Arthur and his wife,
Virginia, took over the farm. They moved to a new home in Leola which Otto
built. This home is now the Arthur J. M. Bender home. Mary passed away April
18, 1959, and Otto departed November 2, 1963.
