Philip, 23, is on the farm.

Joyce, 21, Tuscon, AZ, at present is a Selling Supervisor for a department
store.

Sidney will be a junior at Leola High this year, fall of '83.

Elvin had been county Commissioner for 15 years for District No. I and is at
present in his sixth year as McPherson County Highway Superintendent. Elvin was
Hoffman Township Supervisor for ten years and served on various other boards
and committees for McPherson County. At present he is serving on the Leola
School Board.

Christina enjoys sewing, reading and gardening. The family belongs to the
O.L.P.H. Catholic Church of Leola.

CARL and MARY FEICKERT

Carl Feickert was born in McPherson County, SD. He lived his first few years in
Wacker Township. Later his parents moved to Oregon and Carl was educated there.
He moved back to South Dakota in 1922 and farmed at the home farm.

        Mary and Carl Feickert.

July 10, 1934, Carl married North Dakota born Mary Merkel in Webster, SD. Their
marriage took place the same year Leola celebrated its Golden Jubilee. It was a
drouth year but Carl said they celebrated anyway.

While living on the farm, Carl and Mary had one child, Mae. Later they moved to
Petaluma, CA, and another child, Pearl was born.

Carl did odd jobs in California in 1936 and in 1937 he worked in a service
station. By 1940, he worked as a welder which provided a living until he
entered the radiator repair service where he stayed until his retirement.

FREDERICH JR. and BERTHA FEICKERT

Frederich came to America with his parents, Johann and Anna Maria
(Schlickenmayer) Feickert when he was about ten years old. (Refer to Johann
Philip Feickert history.) Fred was born October 30, 1883, in South Russia and
had six brothers and four sisters. They are all deceased. He married Bertha
Wacker in November of 1908. Bertha was born on November 21, 1884, at Menno, SD,
and came to Wacker Township in McPherson County when she was about five years
old. Bertha was the daughter of Carl and Barbara (Neuharth) Wacker and had four
brothers and seven sisters. Three sisters are still living, one in California
and two residing at the Eureka Lutheran Home.

Fred lived with his parents in the Frederick, SD area for several years, then
worked for some farm people by the name of Daltons for four years. After that
he hired out to the Howell ranch southwest of Forbes, ND, for some time. Then
he took a job working at the Turner ranch, which has recently been the Kohlhoff
ranch. Turners at that time owned a bank in Leola.

Fred and Bertha homesteaded about a mile south of his parents. Due to a water
problem they moved to a farm about five miles northeast of this homestead.
After a few years they bought the Bernard Kranzler homestead where Elvin was
born and raised. Elvin still operates this farm with his sons.

Fred and Bertha were the parents of six children, three sons deceased. In 1947
Fred and Bertha moved to Leola. Fred passed away in 1953 and Bertha in 1967.
They were buried in the rural Saron Reformed Cemetery northwest of Leola.

GEORGE and BARBARA FEICKERT

George Feickert was born in South Russia in 1877. He came to America with his
parents, the John George Feickerts, in 1892. On February 4, 1904, he married
Barbara at her parents', the Karl Wacker's home. A church wedding was
impossible due to a raging blizzard. There were no guests in their home other
than the minister. Seven miles away a young man, John Feickert, was looking
after things on the George Feickert farm on the morning of the wedding. John
had his heart set on attending the wedding. After doing the chores, he saddled
George's pony (the one George used while courting Barbara), put on his
sheepskin coat and let the pony be his guide. The horse took him there safely.
Due to the blizzard the horse had pipes of frost and ice about eight or ten
inches long on his nose when they arrived. John was the only guest at the
wedding that day and he took a good scolding for taking such a chance.

        Barbara, G. Carl, Joseph and George Feickert.

George and Barbara homesteaded in Wacker Township and farmed there for eight
years. During that time he was active in politics, became County Assessor in
1910 serving through 1912, and was appointed Justice of the Peace. He was
interested in insurance, and organized the Western Benevolent Society of South
Dakota serving as secretary-treasurer.

The family moved to Oregon in 1913. He trucked dried fruit from the Oregon area
to South Dakota. He sold fruit to Mound City, McLaughlin, Mobridge, Lemmon,
Timber Lake and Gettysburg and other areas. There may be some that remember him
as "the dried prune man from Salem, OR." He was often referred to as "der
gvetcha Feickert."

The Feickerts had eight children. Only Carl, the eldest survives. He lives in
Petaluma, CA. George died in 1932 and his wife, Barbara, died in 1955.

GOTTLIEB and MARY FEICKERT

Gottlieb Feickert was born November 15, 1898, at Leola, SD, to Johann and Anna
(Schlickenmayer) Feickert. Mary was born April 25, 1905 to Michael and Marie
(Beirsbawck) Mueller at Forbes, ND. They were married February 27, 1924.

Gottlieb and Mary were the parents of five children: Ida married Elmer Genter
in 1943. They have five children. Christian married Mary Lile and they have
three children. John married Margaret Speidel in 1953. They have three
children. Michael married Jill Glaab in 1968. They have two children.

Gottlieb operated a Dray Line in Leola from September, 1948, until August,
1951, when he was forced to sell the business due to ill health. He had surgery
in 1952 and in 1956 they moved to Lancaster, CA. There he worked for a paving
company until the fall of 1969.

Mary passed away March 8, 1976, and Gottlieb died November 17, 1981.

HENRY and SYLVIA FEICKERT

Sylvia M. Stickel and Henry Feickert were reared around Leola. Henry in Wacker
Township, Sylivia in Spring Township. Coming from farming backgrounds, the
couple met during threshing in 1935 and were married on December 29 of that
year at St. Paul's Lutheran Church in Leola. They ran the creamery in Leola
until 1941 at which time they moved to Ellendale, ND, with their three children
(all of whom were born in McPherson County). Nineteen forty-three saw a more
distant move for the Henry Feickerts, to St. Paul, MN, where Henry began in the
painting and decorating business which occupied his time for more than 36
years. Now retired and making his home in St. Paul, the business which Henry
began has been sold to his oldest son, Harold, who owns and operates Feickert
Decorating, Inc., in a suburb of St. Paul.

        Henry and Sylvia Feickert.

JACOB SR. and KATHERINA FEICKERT

Jacob Feickert Sr. was born on December 18, 1869, in Russia to John George
Feickert and Magdalena (Bauman) Feickert. His life was not easy and he had a
rough road to travel. When he was 18 years old he left Zebrikowa, South Russia
and came to America alone, prior to his parents in 1887. Lacking all necessary
things, he started working for a cattle farmer and many times was cold and
hungry. Through his careful effort he worked himself up and soon established a
home of his own. He found a companion and on January 24, 1893, he married
Katherina Gohl and lived on a farm 12 miles southwest of Forbes, ND. They had
eight children. George married Lydia Gienger and lived ten miles southwest of
Forbes, ND, and moved to California a few years later. Jacob Jr., Christ,
Rosina, David, Magdalena, Katherina, and a son Daniel, who died as a child.

They lived happily until April of 1909 when death took Katherina and left Jacob
with eight young children.

Jacob Sr. was united in marriage with a widow, Fredericka Flemmer (Schell) on
October 4, 1909. She had four children: Christ, John, Katherine, and Magdalena.
Oftentimes when they talked about their family they would say; my children,
your children, and our children. Although they already had 12 children, they
had seven more of their own. Mathilda, Ben, Karoline, Lydia, Eva, Adam. and
Daniel.

        Fredericka, Dan and Jacob Feickert, Sr.

On April 1, 1920 they sold their farm and moved to California, where they
settled near Elk Grove.

Jacob Sr. died on July 24, 1936 and Fredericka died on March 29, 1965.

JACOB JR. and CHARLOTTE FEICKERT

Jacob Feickert Jr. was born on November 9, 1895, to Jacob Sr. and Katherina
(Gohl) Feickert on a farm 12 miles southwest of Forbes, ND. He was raised on
the farm. He attended rural school; however, his education was limited. He was
a veteran of World War I. After returning home from service he married
Charlotte Wacker, daughter of Jacob and Margarette (Nuss) Wacker, on July 27,
1919, at Ashley, ND. They lived on a farm 11 miles west of Forbes, ND. Four
children were born. One girl died soon after birth. Albert J. of Wetonka, SD,
was born on September 20, 1922, and married Viola Gienger. Dena was born on
September 5, 1926, and married Edward Gehring of Long Lake, SD. Ann, born on
May 7, 1931 married Elwood Lechner. In 1932 the family circle was broken when
Charlotte died on July 8. On February 21, 1933, Jacob Jr. married Mary Heil.
Mary is the daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Jacob Heil of Ashley, ND. A daughter,
Delores was born on December 28, 1936, and she married Luther Hoffman of Leola,
SD.

        The Jacob Feickert, Jr. Family. Back: Anna, Albert and Dena. Front:
        Mary, Delores and Jacob.

In 1954, Jacob Jr. and Mary sold their farm and bought a house in Leola. Jacob
Jr. kept busy doing various jobs until his death on May 3, 1971. Mary still
lives in her home in Leola. SD.

JOHANN and ANNA FEICKERT

Johann Philip Feickert was another immigrant who settled in McPherson County.
He was born in Neudorf, Russia in 1854. He was the oldest of 11 sisters and
brothers. Johann married Anna Maria Schlickenmayer in 1878. They were always
thankful to Christoph Permann for sending the money to them in Russia so that
the family was financially able to come to this country.

They located first at Frederick, SD, arriving by train. Here Johann and Anna
Maria did harvest work for 50 cents a day. They lived for two years on a farm 8
1/2 miles northwest of Frederick, SD, then homesteaded in Hoffman Township,
McPherson County, about 13 miles northwest of Leola.

They were the parents of 11 children, four girls and seven boys. Johann passed
away in 1913 and Anna Maria in 1935 at the farm. They were members of the Hope
Lutheran Church.

Johann was a grandfather of Elvin Feickert of Leola.

JOHN and CHRISTINA FEICKERT

John A. Feickert was born in South Russia in 1886. At age eight, he came to
America with his parents, John and Anna Maria (Schlichenmayer) Feickert. The
family homesteaded northwest of Leola in Hoffman Township. John was one of ten
children.

On December 22, 1910, John married Christina Wacker in Leola, SD. They
homesteaded in Wacker Township 12 1/2 miles north and four miles west of Leola.
They farmed there until 1940 when they moved to Leola where John purchased the
Jeske Dray Line. He was the owner of that business until his death in 1944, at
which time his sons took over.

        The John Feickert Family. Back: Lydia, Luisa, Henry, Reinhold, Daniel,
        Otto and Hilda. Front: Leonard, Leo, Christina, Benjamin, John, Alma
        and Martha.

John was instrumental in bringing the telephone into his community. He helped
build much of the line and was lineman for Bell Telephone Co. for many years.
He was also insurance adjuster for Northwest German Farmers Mutual Insurance of
Eureka, SD, for a number of years.

The Feickerts raised 12 children, ten of whom are still living.

JOHN GEORGE and MAGDALENA FEICKERT

John George Feickert was born December 25, 1832, in South Russia. His parents
were born in Germany. John became an orphan and he was taken forcibly by the
Russians. He survived the ordeal of slave labor in the coal and salt mines.
Later he learned the blacksmithing trade, making steel plow lays used on wooden
plows. He continued blacksmithing after coming to America.

        John George and Christina Feickert.

John married Magdalena Bauman in Russia. She was born in 1830. The couple had
six children, Johann, Magdalena, Katherina, Gottlieb, Dorothea and Jacob
Feickert, Sr. Magdalena died sometime before 1873 and then John married
Christina Dockter Gohl on May 22, 1873 in Gluckstal, Russia. Christina was a
widow with four children: Jacob, Christina, Katherine and Christian. Her former
husband was George Gohl. With their families combined, there were 12 children.
Some of the children came to America before, some after their parents left and
some stayed in Russia.

John immigrated to America with his wife and two sons, George and Frederich Sr.
on May 20, 1892. They homesteaded land about 14 miles northwest of Leola, 1 1/2
miles northeast of the Feickert farm that is still owned by Elvin Feickert.
George and Frederich Sr. both homesteaded near their parents.

John George ran a blacksmith shop for some time on his farm. He was known for
his steel plow-lays and other steel items that helped solve farming problems.

John George suffered a stroke when he was about 60 years of age. In their later
years they lived with their daughter, Katherine Permann, 12 miles south of
Eureka. John passed away on June 12, 1915, and his wife Christina, died on
October 25, 1921. They are buried in a small roadside cemetery. They were one
of nine charter member families of the Hope Lutheran Church, 15 miles northwest
of Leola, organized on January 8, 1894 under the leadership of Pastor M.
Reischauer.

CHARLES and ELLA FOSLER

Charles Sidney Fosler was born in Ogle County, IL, January 8, 1863, to Ed and
Harriet Fosler. He came to McPherson County in 1884, when it was a part of
Dakota Territory.

Ella Nora Haberman was born September 5, 1870, at Portage, WI, to John and Rosa
Haberman and came with her parents to Weber Township in McPherson County in
1883.

Charles and Ella were married at Ellendale, ND, on November 28, 1888. For a
number of years they made their home one mile south of Leola, later moving to
Koto Township where they lived until 1913. They then moved to the south part of
Leola to the home presently owned by Christ Jakober. The Foslers, like most
pioneers, suffered many hardships in early times, such as blizzards, crop
failures, fires, even witnessing the hazardous prairie fire that swept most of
Leola away.

        Charles and Ella Fosler.

The Foslers were blessed with four daughters: May (Berlin/Christensen), Ada
(Pischke), Delphy (Fewings), and Cecile (Dexter).

In 1959, when Leola was observing its 75th anniversary, Mrs. Fosler was honored
by being chosen as Parade Queen. In 1961 she received the following:

                "PIONEER CITIZEN AWARD
                   DAKOTA TERRITORY
                1861-1961 CENTENNIAL"

"The Dakota Territory Centennial Commission extends greetings and hereby
declares that Mrs. Ella Fosler is a Pioneer Citizen of South Dakota and having
lived in Dakota Territory during the period commemorated in the centennial year
is hereby given official recognition and tribute."

The Foslers were members of the United Methodist Church. He belonged to the
Modern Woodmen and she, to the Royal Neighbors. Mrs. Fosler, who lived to be
97, died in 1967. Mr. Fosler preceded her in death in 1948. Both are buried in
Green Mound Cemetery in Leola.

WILLIAM and MABEL FREITAG

William Freitag was born July 15, 1927, to William Richard and Ethel (Henry)
Freitag in Mankato, MN.

Mabel Dockter was born February 13, 1928, in McPherson County on the farm her

Mabel recalls when, in 1936, her parents first owned a radio. It was a Philco
and cost $55. It was operated with a big battery since electricity was not
available. A radio was considered quite a luxury and she remembers the

S. D. and M. BLANCHE FROST

S. D. Frost was born on a farm near Amboy, IL in 1871. As a young man he began
trading and buying stock. He received his education by attending a commercial
college. In August of 1900 he married Minnie Blanche Smith of Amboy, IL. They
began farming near Amboy. In 1908, the Frosts bought a ranch five miles north
of Leola. Later they moved to Leola and S. D. operated his stock and ranch
business from his home. Blanche operated a hotel for a number of years in
Leola. This hotel is still on Leola's main street. It is now owned by Mary Lou
Lechner.

Mrs. Frost, a well-educated woman, was a cultural leader of Leola, promoting
the best of entertainment. She was a charter member of Disco Club (women's
study group) organized in 1912. As president of the Civic League, she worked
for the betterment of Leola. Because of her concern for children, she served as
a member of the school board for many years. She entertained often and
graciously in her lovely home. Children were her delight and she encouraged
their circuses and sideshows in her backyard. Her front porch with a swing was
a child's haven on summer afternoons. Mrs. Frost had the love, admiration and
respect of everyone who knew her.

Life was not dull for Mrs. Frost. Anyone who traveled by buggy pulled by a team
of horses had harrowing experiences. One such experience was printed in the
March 9, 1899, newspaper. It goes as follows: "Mrs. S. D. Frost and May Parks
had quite an unpleasant experience March 2. They were crossing the ravine just
north of the M. & St. L. tracks when the ice broke, and the team, sleigh and
occupants were plunged into the icy water. The women got out without
assistance, but it took a team of horses and several men to rescue the team."

On February 7, 1920, S. D. (age 49) died at his home in Leola after an illness
lasting over 15 months. He was buried in Amboy, IL. Blanche stayed in Leola
until 1948, when she moved to Rockford, IL, to be near relatives. She passed
away in September of 1951.

FRANK and ALICE GALSTER

Frank Galster came to Leola from Alma Center, WI in the spring of 1911. He
homesteaded 320 acres three miles east of Leola. He later shipped a steam
engine and a plow with eight bottoms. This came in on a train to Aberdeen. He
drove it to Leola. He used the engine to break up several acres of sod in the
eastern part of the county. In 1912 he returned to Alma Center, WI, and married
Alice Andrus Blair. They then returned to Leola to make their home

        Alice & Frank Galster.

For about five years, he rented a farm two miles east of Leola which had some
buildings on it. During this time he constructed a barn, granary, and a chicken
house. Later more buildings were moved on the homestead. A well was dug by the
Valentine Drilling Company.

In 1914 a new arrival came. Florence was born and, a step-son from Humbird, WI,
Miles Blair, came to live with the family.

Frank did lots of threshing for neighbors and friends. A cookcar followed the
rig wherever it went. His wife cooked for all the men. The crew consisted of
eight bundle haulers, four spike pitchers, two grain haulers, an engineer, a
separator man, and Frank, the boss. The steam engine furnished the power.

In 1925 or 1926 he built the road at the west city limits of Leola going north.
He had purchased an Avery Tractor to pull the blader. Mat Krambeal ran the
tractor and Frank ran the blader.

He not only farmed his own land but rented several quarters. In 1939 when he
passed away, he was farming 13 quarters.

Frank was a member of the school board and had served on the township board for
several years as supervisor.

ADRIAN and RUTH GEFFRE

Adrian and Ruth Geffre's blood and roots run deep in the Leola soil. Ruth's
grandmother Mary Lapka was part of the third family to settle in Leola. Her
first recollections were of the building of a sod house, and grass so tall that
little children could easily be lost forever. Beautiful sunsets, violent
storms, body-killing work, heat, cold, sickness, delivering babies, and freedom
from oppression were a few of her colorful memories in her last years. She
arrived in this country with her parents from Germany when she was six years
old. She left behind many relatives from the street where she lived in Germany.
She lived above the family's stable, as did everyone on both sides of the
street. The kids had a treat during the summer because they got to travel a few
miles from town to pitch a tent and camp all summer, as their parents planted
and harvested their crop.

Because of the political unrest in 1883, the family loaded as many of their
possessions as possible on a boat, and made the long journey across the ocean
only to find their money exhausted when they arrived in New York. It took two
years of work to get enough money to finish their journey. Even young Mary had
to stand on a box and wash dishes in a hotel. They finally saved enough to get
a "rail" ticket to Ipswich, where they bought a team of oxen and moved north to
find a home in now rural Leola.

Two years later, her cousin John Geffre and his family were sent for and
allowed to share their sod home until another home could be built.

Adrian's father, John (see John Geffre history) arrived in the Leola area in
1888 as a six-year-old child. His memories are of hiding in the tall grass as
the Indians traveled across the prairies on horseback from the Missouri River
to Sisseton. He told of being the oldest of seven boys and girls and having a
job eight miles from home. He had to walk home on Saturday night with a quarter
in his pocket, trying to be as quiet as possible so the howling coyotes
wouldn't attack him. After spending a few treasured hours on Sunday with his
family, he turned over his week's wages and started his long walk back to his
job.

Ruth's mother, Leona (Kallas) Lapka was the daughter of Joseph and Laura Kallas
and her father, George Lapka, was the youngest son of Ignus and Mary (Kraft)
Lapka. (See John and Elizabeth Lapka history.)

        The Adrian Geffre Family. Back: Dan and Scott. Front: Ruth, Michael
        and Adrian.

Adrian and Ruth were both born and raised in Leola and graduated from Leola
High School. Adrian served two years in the Army and traveled much of Europe
before settling into the farm and ranching profession. Ruth spent some time in
Florida following graduation, before returning and working in various
businesses and the Leola School system as a secretary. They were married in
1963 and established their home southeast of Leola where they still reside.
They have three sons: Dan, 19, who graduated from Leola High School in 1983 and
is currently attending Mary College in Bismarck, ND; Scott, 17, who will be a
senior in Leola High School; and Michael, four, who is still at home. Ruth is
currently attending Northern State College in Aberdeen.

JAMES and MARVA LOU GEFFRE

Lee and Rose (Kallas) Geffre were doubly blessed on January 19, 1933 when not
one but two babies arrived. The twins, James and Jerome, were born on a farm
east of Leola. Jerome died on October 26, 1938 of appendicitis. Jim grew up on
his parents' farm, attended grade school in Willow Township and graduated from
Barnard High School in 1951. After graduation Jim farmed and had various jobs
until he bought the Standard Station in 1959. He ran the station until 1968
when he started working for the State Highway Department.

        Fred, Jim, Jerome, Marva Lou and Alan Geffre.

Marva Lou, daughter of Fred and Emma (Ehresman) Rau, was born April 20, 1940 at
Long Lake. She attended grade school in Wacker Township and graduated from
Leola High School in 1958. Marva Lou was a Telephone Operator in Leola until
the dial system was installed. She worked part time in the County Treasurer's
Office and later for the Soil Conservation Service. She is presently the
secretary for the McPherson County Highway Department.

Jim and Marva Lou were married on September 6, 1960 at Leola. They have three
children. Jerome James was born June 17, 1961 and lives in Aberdeen. Fred Lee,
born September 12, 1964 is a student at Northern State College, and Alan Jay,
born November 21, 1967 is a student at Leola High School.

JOHN and AGNES GEFFRE

John Geffre was born December 8, 1882 at Strasburg, Germany, to Rochus and
Veronica (Mastel) Geffre. The family moved to Russia and in 1889 Rochus brought
Veronica and their three boys, John, Steve and Lee, to America. John (six)
remembered his trip over the ocean, especially his worried mother. It seems her
boys liked to climb up on the side of the ship and hang over the railing
watching the ocean. She constantly retrieved them. The family arrived safely
and settled seven miles northeast of Leola.

        John & Agnes Geffre.

John married Agnes Kessler in 1905 and in 1918, Agnes died from the flu. John
was left with five children: Mae, Steve, George, Helen and Inez.

        Catherine & John Geffre.

John met Catherine Reinbold whose family also originated from Germany. The
Reinbold couple (Adam and Cora [Kraft] Reinbold) came to this country in 1886
and settled in the Hosmer area. Catherine was born January 11, 1898 and was the
eldest of 15 boys and girls. She joined John in marriage on June 16, 1919 and
helped care for his five children. Catherine and John were the parents of 11
children: Joseph, Barbara, Benedict, Norbert, Herbert, Laurence, Raymond,
Harold, Mary Ann, Adrian and Gordon.

During his farming years, John found time to be a road supervisor and held
office on the school board. John retired and moved to Leola in 1958. He passed
away on June 3, 1974 and Catherine still lives in Leola. Both were members of
Our Lady of Perpetual Help Catholic Church, Leola.

JOSEPH and REGINA GEFFRE

Joseph Andrew Geffre Sr., was born September 25, 1889 on the family homestead
in Willow Township, about six miles northeast of Leola. His parents, Rochus and
Veronica (Mastel) Geffre immigrated from Russia in 1888. He married Regina
Hartman November 1916 at Aldrich, MN. To this union, Vincent and Grace were
born. Regina passed away in 1919. (Refer to Vincent Geffre history.) Grace
married Gordon Ganser at Leola, October 1943. They both died in 1958, Grace
from cancer, and Gordon in a car accident. They had five children: Joan, Carol,
Susan, Duane and Morris (Joey).

Joseph remarried, to Mary H. Hartman in 1920, at Leola. Mary was born at
Waconia, MN, August 13, 1896. Joseph and Mary were the parents of seven
daughters and two sons.

Regina married Joseph Dosch. They have four children. They live in Mina, SD.

Christina, (refer to Elvin Feickert history).

Dorothy, (refer to Floyd Hammerich history).

Alice married George Braun. They have two daughters. They live in Aberdeen, SD.

Andrew married Pauline Timmer. They have six sons and live in Minneapolis, MN.
Andrew passed away from cancer January, 1967.

Blanche married Ronald Ronkar. They moved from Aberdeen to Bremerton, WA. They
have six children. Ronald passed away in May, 1977. Blanche married Jack
Harkness in 1980.

Margaret married John R. Frank. They have four children and live in St. Paul,
MN.

Gerald is single, and lives in Olympia, WA.

Rose Marie married Wayne Hall. They have three sons and live in Holland, OH.

Joseph spent all his married life on a farm four miles southeast of Leola,
until they retired and moved into Leola in 1956.

Joseph served on various local boards throughout the years, and also served
several years on the Leola school board.

The Joseph Geffre family were members of the Our Lady of Perpetual Help
Catholic Church. Joseph passed away in 1969. Mary is presently residing in the
Aberdeen Nursing Home, since 1974.

LAURENCE and WANETA GEFFRE

Laurence Geffre was born on March 18, 1927 to John and Catherine (Reinbold)
Geffre, on a farm northeast of Leola. He attended country school graduating
from the eighth grade. When he was 18 he was drafted into the Army, taking his
basic training at Ft. Hood, TX. He served in Korea from 1946 to 1947. After his
discharge he returned to Leola and helped on his folk's farm.

In May of 1949 he married Waneta Meidinger and later they moved to Lead where
they made their home for 16 years. Waneta is the daughter of August and
Hildegard Meidinger.

        Waneta & Lawrence Geffre.

Laurence was a contract miner in the Homestake Gold mine in Lead. In August of
1966 they moved back to Leola where he took over the operation of the Meidinger
farm, and worked for the Mobil Service Station and Maier Garage. He then went
to work for Safeguard Industries in Aberdeen where he is still employed, and
does a little farming on the side.

The Geffres have five children. David was born July 17, 1950, and is living in
Rapid City. His son, Joshua, was born September 20, 1975 and a daughter,
Jessica, was born December 20, 1976. Sheri, born September 17, 1951, is married
to Lynn Ketelsen and lives in Mobridge, SD. They have two sons, Nathan, born
December 30, 1975, Derek, born April 17, 1979 and a daughter, Courtney, born
June 11, 1983. Debra, born July 1, 1957 is married to Don Fischer and lives in
Aberdeen. They have a daughter Laura. Timothy was born December 13, 1963, and
is a student at Northern State College. Neil was born March 2, 1970, and is a
student at Leola High.

Waneta enjoys telling tales of the sod house that she was born in. The walls
were 16 inches thick and her favorite pastime as a little girl was curling up
in the window sill and reading a good book.

LEE and ROSE GEFFRE

Lee Geffre was born on May 10, 1887 in Odessa, Russia to Rochus and Veronica
(Mastel) Geffre. He came to the United States in October of 1888 when he was 1
1/2 years old. They settled on a farm 1 1/2 miles east of Leola. Lee's family
consisted of Lee, Rochus, Joe, Steve, Martha (Grabowska) and Lizzie (Kessler).

Rose was born on June 9, 1893 to Julius and Sophia (Schmaglenski). Rose's
father Julius was born in Germany in 1855 and came to the United States. Sophia
was born in 1864 in Poland and came to the United States where they met and
married. There were 12 children born to this union. Of these only six are still
living: Rose, John, Vincent, Alex, Sister Leona and Sister Anicetus.

Lee and Rose met and were married at St. Hyacinths

Catholic Church northeast of Leola. They made their home on a farm 1 1/2 miles
east of Leola. Rose and Lee were blessed with 13 children: Norbert, born in
1913, died in infancy; Eleanor (Klein), 1915, living in Aberdeen; Mary, 1917,
died in infancy; Marcella, 1918, living in Minneapolis; Leo, 1919, and Frank,
1920, both of Leola; Rita (Braun), 1923, of Aberdeen; Clem, 1925, of Groton;
Clarence, 1928, Robert, 1930, twins James and Jerome, 1933 (Jerome died at the
age of five); and Joan (Weiszhaar) in 1936 of Leola.

        The Lee Geffre Family. Back: Lee, Jim, Frank, Clem and Clarence.
        Front: Rita, Eleanore, Rose, Marcella and Joan.

Lee died on October 2, 1954. Rose moved to Leola in 1956 where she made her
home until 1979. Rose is presently residing at Mother Joseph Manor in Aberdeen.

LEO and CHRISTIANA GEFFRE

Leo was born to Lee and Rose (Kallas) Geffre on February 23, 1919, Leola, SD.

        Christina & Leo Geffre.

Lorraine, who is unmarried at the present time.

LOUIS and EMMA GEFFRE

Louis C. Geffre, son of Peter and Elizabeth (Senger) Geffre was born June 7,
1892. He grew to manhood in the Leola area. On October 20, 1926, Louis married
Emma Lechner, daughter of John Sr. and Mary (Blumhardt) Lechner. Emma was born
March 30, 1908 in McPherson County.

Louis and Emma farmed in Koto Township until 1967 when they retired and moved
to Leola.

Children of the Geffres are: Harold, who lives in Eureka; Gerald, who married
Betty (Renz) on September 25, 1960, and lives on the home farm; Irene, who
married Wayne Jensen and lives in Zell, SD; Darlene, who married Garrold Friese
and lives in Tulare, SD.

        Louis & Emma Geffre.

Louis died July 25, 1981 and Emma died August 31, 1982. There are 15
grandchildren and 12 great-grandchildren.

NORBERT and JOANNE GEFFRE

Norbert was born to John and Katherine (Reinbold) Geffre in 1923. He grew up on
a farm northeast of Leola, attending a rural elementary school through the
eighth grade before he had to help support and raise John's growing family of
11 sons and five daughters. When he was 21 he struck out to seek his fortune by
working in a shipyard in Bremerton, WA, and the Homestake Gold Mine in Lead.
Later Norbert and his brother Harold owned and operated the Apex Bowling Alley
in Lead. Norbert always returned to help his father during the busy seasons.

In 1956 Norbert married Joanne Kornmann of Lead. She was employed by
Northwestern Bell Telephone there. Joanne is the daughter of Edward and Gladys
(Flanagan) Kornmann of Lead, SD. Joanne is of German, Dutch and Irish
descendants who settled in the Watertown, SD area and later moved to Lead.

        The Norbert Geffre Family. Back: Jerry, Patty, Mark, Larry, Tom, John,
        Kathy and Susie. Front: Joanne and Norbert.

Norbert and Joanne moved back to the farm one mile east of Leola in 1957, where
they still reside. They have eight children. Kathy married Dan Rodriguez, has
two children and lives in Denver, CO. Susie is married to Bob Faehn of
Watertown and they have two children. John is married to Kim Rognan of
Brookings and is currently farming with his father. Tom is attending Northern
State College in Aberdeen. Patty has one daughter and is attending Northern.
Larry is farming with his father. Mark is a 1984 graduate and is attending
college. Jerry is a student at Leola High.

Norbert and Joanne are members of the Catholic Church where Joanne is active in
the Altar Society, Church Choir and has taught religion class.

PETER and ELIZABETH GEFFRE

Peter and Elizabeth (Senger) Geffre came to America in the fall of 1888 from
Odessa, Russia. They brought with them four of their children: Maggie, Barbara
(Lacher), Jacob, and Elizabeth (Buechler).

        Elizabeth & Peter Geffre.

The Geffres settled down about nine miles northeast of Leola. Their first house
was only an old shack and later on in the year of 1891, they purchased their
homestead land where they built a sod house.

After a few years Katherine (Gisi), Theresa (Pheiffer) (living in Aberdeen,
SD), twins Tom (living in Aberdeen, SD) and Louie, Peter (living in Aberdeen),
John, Philipina (Kline), and Frances (Lechner) (both living in Leola) were born
to Mr. and Mrs. Peter Geffre.

In the year of 1908 Peter and Elizabeth decided to build a new house with the
help of Gregory Gisi, their son-in-law. They built a two-story house. This
house is still on the Joseph and Ruth Lapka farm, but has been remodeled and
enlarged.

Peter and Elizabeth retired in 1919 and moved into Leola. Mr. Peter Geffre
never was a patient and never went to a hospital and only when he was dying did
he see a doctor. Peter passed away in 1943 and Elizabeth was very active up to
her death in March of 1950.

ROCHUS and VERONICA GEFFRE

Rochus Geffre was born in South Russia August 15, 1858. He grew up in Russia
and married Veronica Mastel, who was born December 23, 1862 in Strassburg,
Russia. They were married September 26, 1880. In 1889 they came to America and
settled in Willow Township which was a vast prairie at that time. They built a
sod house. The first winter they burned slew hay tied in bundles or rolls. In
the spring, they broke up land with oxen and hauled their produce and grain to
Frederick. At times they carried the produce to Frederick so they could buy
flour and sugar.

        Rochus & Veronica Geffre.

Rochus and Veronica had five sons, John, Steve and Lee (born in Russia), Joe
and Rochus, and two daughters, Elizabeth and Martha (born on the homestead).

John married Agnes Kessler who died October 24, 1918. He remarried Catherine
Reinbold June 16, 1919.

Steve married Elizabeth Brendel.

Lee married Rose Kallas.

Joe married Regina Hartman who died in 1918. He remarried Mary Hartman.

Elizabeth married Felix Kessler.

Martha married Frank Grabowska.

Rochus married Mayme Grabowska.

Rochus and Veronica moved to Leola in 1920 and spent their remaining years
there. Rochus died at the age of 75, February 25, 1933 and Veronica died July
31, 1956 at the age of 93.

VINCENT and VIOLA GEFFRE

Vincent was born November 10, 1917 to Joe and Regina Geffre on a farm four
miles southeast of Leola. He attended rural school and Leola High School.
Vincent farmed with his father until 1941 when he was drafted into the Army. He
was stationed at Panama Canal for two years, at Fort Hood, TX, and received his
discharge in October of 1945. He accepted a job with Barzen Grain Co. as
manager in 1946, and worked until the spring of 1951 when he accepted a job as
bulk agent for the Standard Oil Co. He retired January 4, 1972 as bulk agent,
but continued operating the Standard Oil Service Station for several years. On
July 1, 1974 he purchased the produce station where he buys cream and eggs and
sells other produce. The Geffre Produce Station is managed by Jake Kirschman.
As a hobby, Vincent has built up a salvage yard (in the northwest corner of
Leola) which he operates on his own time.

Viola Dalke was born January 4, 1921 to Mr. and Mrs. Andrew Dalke on a farm
eight miles south of Lehr, ND. She attended rural school and graduated from
Lehr High School in 1938. She married Julius Kranzler of Lehr, ND in October of
1938. They were the parents of four children. Faye married Tom Montez. They
have three children. Judy married Joe Ricard. They have two children. Bonnie
married Phil Hartz and they have two children. Ralph married Jane Beaver and
they are the parents of twin boys. Julius passed away in February, 1956.

        Faye, Ralph, Bonnie, Judy, Viola and Vincent Geffre.

Viola married Vincent on September 11, 1957 in Leola. They made their home in
Leola where they still reside. Vincent is a member of the Catholic Church, the
American Legion, Leola Sportsman Club and the Leola Golf Club. Viola is a
member of the Methodist Church, The American Legion Auxiliary, The Past
Presidents Parley, Star Extension Club, Methodist Eve Circle, United Methodist
Women's Society and the Leola Ladies Golf Club. Both enjoy traveling and have
traveled many miles through the U.S. and Canada.

JACOB and LEA GEHRING

Jacob Gehring was born November 22, 1917, near Long Lake, SD, to John and
Johanna (Jesser) Gehring. Jacob served in World War II, from 1941 to 1946.

Lea (Hoffman) Gehring was born August 4, 1918, near Long Lake, SD to Christoph

        Lea & Jacob Gehring.

On June 9, 1946, Jacob and Lea were united in marriage. They made their home on
the family farm for 30 years. In 1977, they sold the farm and moved into Leola.
Jacob is semi-retired and Lea works at the Leola Bakery.

Jacob and Lea have two children, Carol and Arlen, and one granddaughter,

Carol, born April 11, 1947, lives in Phoenix, AZ.

Jacob and Lea are members of St. James Lutheran Church of Leola. They are also
members of the American Legion and Auxiliary of Long Lake.

WILLIAM J. P. and JULIA GIEDT

William J. P. Giedt was born in Danzig, Russia in 1877. His parents came to the
United States in 1886 and settled on a farm in McIntosh County, ND. After
maturity, Mr. Giedt engaged in farming, the merchandising business, served as
Mayor of Eureka and was Treasurer of McPherson County. In 1928, he purchased
the Golden Rule Store in Leola. He operated the Golden Rule until his death
November 1, 1941. He is well remembered by older McPherson countians for his
generosity in extending credit during the difficult depression years. He was a
member of the school board (also president), the Masons and the Methodist
Church.

Julia Emelia (Klauss) Giedt was born in Hutchinson County, SD in 1881 in a sod
hut. She continued operating the store (after Wm. J. P.'s death) until late
1942, when she sold the building (located on the west side of Main Street) to
Perry Conahan. He built a new restaurant on the site. Mrs. Giedt was very
active in the Methodist Church and the Eastern Star. She passed away in 1968.

        William J. P. Geidt.          Julia Geidt.

The Giedts had six children (listed below) and 18 grandchildren. There are now
25 great-grandchildren.

Arthur W. was born in Ashley, ND in 1898. Art was an accountant in Lodi, CA,
where he passed away in 1970. He had two children. His wife, Amy, lives in
Fresno, CA.

Josephine L. was born in 1899 in Wishek, ND. She married Patrick O'Connell and
they were parents of four children. She died in 1972 in Fremont, CA.

Ida E. was born in Hillsview, SD in 1904. She married W. P. Greenawalt
(deceased). They were parents of four children. She lives in Seattle, WA.

Warren H. (one of twins), born November 1, 1920 in Leola. Warren was a pilot in
the Army Air Corps during World War 11. He has been a professor and dean in the
Mechanical Engineering Department of the University of California until his
retirement in 1983. Warren and his wife, Leta, reside in El Macero, CA.

Wallace R. was also born November 1, 1920 in Leola. He served as a Naval
Officer during World War II. Wallace has been with the General Electric Company
since then as Sales Engineer. He and his wife, Nora live in Arcadia, CA. They
have six children.

John G. was born in Leola in 1923. John was a Naval Aviator for 22 years and
retired as Commander in 1967. He became Manager, Quality Control with the B. F.
Goodrich Company in Troy, OH. John married Delores LaFontaine in 1945. They
reside in Troy, OH and have two children .

EDWARD and ANNA MARIE GIENGER

Edward Gienger was born in McPherson County near Long Lake, SD on November 19,
1898 to Ludwig Sr. and Eva (Ehresman) Gienger. Edward was orphaned at the age
of 12 years. His mother died of severe burns received while heating oil for
cleaning, on a cook stove, in 1911. Edward's father died of injuries received
while trying to load a cream can into a buggy. The horses shyed, pulling the
buggy away so that the cream can landed on his chest. He died in 1914. Theodore
Geidt of Eureka was appointed Edward's guardian, but he made his home with his
sister, Magdalena Heyd. In his later teens he worked for Christ Opp of Eureka.

On August 17, 1919 he was married to Anna Marie Feickert. Mary, as she was
known, was born on October 30, 1900, northwest of Leola, to Johann and Anna
Marie (Schlickenmayer) Feickert. Mary stayed at home helping her mother, for at
the age of 13 she lost her father.

        The Edward Gienger Family.

After Edward and Mary's marriage, they made their home, farming, in the
Leola-Long Lake area. In the dirty '30 s Edward worked on WPA, along with many
others, to keep food on the table for six hungry mouths. He also repaired
watches and clocks, sewing machines. cream separators, etc. In 1957, having
decided to quit farming they moved to Pierre. He worked as a custodian in
Pierre until the time of his death. They were lifelong Lutherans, belonging to
Hoffnung Lutheran Church northwest of Leola and St. James Lutheran in Leola,
until moving to Pierre. Edward was custodian at the Hoffnung Church and also
helped teach Sunday School. Edward died of cancer on November 23, 1960. Mary
had also worked, along with her husband, as a custodian. After his death, she
worked at St. Mary's Hospital in Pierre, until ill health forced her to retire.
Mary died on December 26, 1978 of cancer.

Edward and Mary were the parents of six children. Ludwig, married to Ann Auger,
lives in St. Paul, MN. Clara, married to Clifton Tschappat, lives in Leola.
Richard, married to Eileen Johnson, lived in Herreid until he died of cancer on
September 4, 1982. Ruben, married to Esther Sperle, lives in Aberdeen. Emma,
married to August Rieger, lives in Pierre, and Benjamin, married to Sharon
Mclntire, also lives in Pierre. They had 22 grandchildren and 28
great-grandchildren.

RICHARD and EILEEN GIENGER

Richard Gienger was born on December 13, 1923 to Edward and Mary (Feickert)
Gienger. He had five brothers and sisters.

On October 15, 1950 Richard married Eileen Johnson, daughter of Nels and Hilda
(Tveit) Johnson of Frederick, SD.

They made their first home on a farm near Frederick until 1955 when they moved
to the Ben Rott farm south of Leola. In 1962 they moved to Leola where Richard
was employed by Rueb's Chevrolet as a body man. The family moved to Herreid, SD
in 1963, where Richard worked for Senftner Chevrolet as an auto body technician
until his health forced him to retire in April of 1982. Richard died of cancer
on September 4, 1982.

Richard and Eileen had two children. Douglas, born on September 5, 1951,
married Margaret Boostma of Pollock. They have one daughter and live in
Minneapolis. Myrtis Gienger, born July 1, 1955, married Mark Vojta of Mound
City. They have one son and live in Herreid.

        Doug, Eileen, Richard and Myrtis Gienger.

Richard was an avid outdoor sportsman. He was a charter member of Herreid Lions
Club, past member of The Commercial Club and Alderman on the city council for
ten years, being chairman of the board at the time of his death. Richard and
Eileen have been lifelong Lutherans. Richard was sexton for many years and a
member of the church council, and Eileen, a member of ALCW and treasurer of the
church.

LOREN (BUD) and BONITA GILL

Loren (Bud) Gill was born November 1, 1920 in Leola and Bonita (Bonnie) Swanson
was born March 18, 1926 in Moorhead, MN. They were married May 31, 1947 and
made their home in Leola where Bud worked for the State Highway Department and
Bonnie worked in the County Agent's office. In September of 1948 they moved to
Brookings where Bud attended S.D.S.U. They returned to Leola in January of
1952. Bud taught a government sponsored agricultural program for World War II
veterans. He returned to NSC in 1958. He then taught in Leola High School until
his retirement in 1980 due to illness. He was a veteran of World War II. He
entered the service January of 1942 and was discharged December, 1945. He
served 44 months in the South Pacific.

        The Loren Gill Family.

Bud, like his father, was a hunting enthusiast and he instilled this enthusiasm
in his sons. He delighted in telling of hunting with his father in the north
and northwestern part of the county. In later years, he and his four sons
traveled many miles in this same area looking for a prime site for calling in
fox.

Bud passed away March 29, 1982 following a long illness.

Before her marriage, Bonnie taught Carl No. 2 school and worked in Fargo, ND,
as well as working in her parents' bakery during her school years.

Bonnie and Bud have seven children. Gregory John was born July 9, 1948 in
Ipswich, SD. He married Kathi Degnan, Ayrshire, IA on August 1, 1980. Both are
employed in St. Luke's Hospital in Fargo, ND. They had one daughter, Erin
Nicolle, born September 16, 1982 and died in 1982. Merilee Sue was born
December 30, 1949 in Brookings, SD. She has three children, Leisha, ten;
Justin, eight; and Nathan, six. She attends NSC. Lance Dixon was born September
2, 1951 in Brookings, SD. He married Colleen Rath, Long Lake, SD on September
30, 1972. They have two children, Megan, five; and Matthew, three. Lance taught
school and is now employed by Minnkota Power Cooperative in Center, ND.
Kimberlee Ann was born April 20, 1953 in Leola. She married Richard Geary,
September 6, 1979. They have one son, Judd Wyatt, two. Both are employed in
Aberdeen. Kerry Scott was born February 27, 1955 in Leola. He married Wanda
Bobbe of Forbes, ND in December 29, 1979. They have one daughter, Nicki, four.
Kerry is a student at Presentation College and Wanda is employed by Dakota
Midland Hospital. Lorrilee Gay was born November 3, 1957 in Leola. She
graduated from DSC in Madison, SD. She is a vocalist with a band. Jason Lee was
born July 23, 1959 in Leola. Jason married Dianne Tobalsky of Aberdeen, SD on
August 18, 1979. He is currently employed at the Leola Co-op station and Dianne
attended Stewarts School of Cosmetology.

Bud and Bonnie and their seven children are all graduates of Leola High School
and were all members of the United Methodist Church.

ALBERT and ILENE GISI

Albert was born March 19, 1918. He started school when he was only four years
old. After his father's death he operated the family farm. He married Ilene H.
Adler, daughter of Leo and Helen (Sahli) Adler of Ipswich, SD on July 9, 1940
and they made their home near Leola. In 1944, they purchased a farm 1 1/2 miles
north of Leola where they still reside.

Besides farming, Albert did carpenter and electrical work. Albert's electrical
license was the first in the Leola area. He served as treasurer of McPherson
County Livestock Improvement Association for 30 years and was a 4-H leader for
several years. In 1978, Albert suffered a heart attack forcing him into
semi-retirement.

        The Albert Gisi Family. Back: Bonnie, Kenneth, Diana, Harvey, Margie,
        Gary and Mary Lou. Front: Cheryl, Dene, Mardell, Albert and Charlene.

Ilene graduated from Ipswich High School in 1938, and worked as secretary in a
government office in Ipswich until her marriage. Albert and llene were blessed
with ten children. Kenneth was born September 15, 1941. He served in the United
States Army from 1959 to 1962. In 1966 he married Willa Lee Steen of Ipswich.
They have two daughters and one son and live in Ipswich, SD. Gary, born August
30, 1942, married Linda Weber of Ipswich in 1963. They have two daughters and
one son and live six miles southeast of Ipswich where Gary farms. Diana, born
August 1, 1943, married Roy J. Hauck of Leola. They have two sons and one
daughter. They reside in Ipswich where both are employed. Harvey, born January
6, 1945, married Faye Kindelspire and they had one son and one daughter. Harvey
died from Hodgkin's disease on May 6, 1968. Bonita, born September 11, 1946,

GREGORY and KATIE GISI

        Katie & Gregory Gisi.

buildings. This farm later became the Kohlhoff Ranch and the house was moved

Gregory was a carpenter, and built many homes and barns and several churches in
the Leola area. Gregory passed away in 1939, and Katie continued to live in

AUGUST and FRANCIS GRABOWSKA

August was born in Bouse, Germany. He was the son of a teacher who acquired a
life certificate in his field. August was only a small boy when his father died
while teaching in the schoolroom. Forced to care for his mother and sister,
August had to give up his dream of becoming a carpenter. The occupation's low
pay and ten year apprenticeship were the reasons behind his decision.

August married Francis Smaglinski, daughter of Matt and Katherine (Spranga)
Smaglinski, while still in Germany. The couple lived in Germany for eight years
and had four children.

August and Francis decided to leave Germany after
August was selected to be a military leader. At that time
the government was training seven-year-old boys for
military duty. August disagreed with this policy. Consequently,
he and his family left for America.

August and Francis reached the New York harbor on May 11, 1881, after a six
week crossing on the ship Frisia. It was then that August's family changed
their last name to Grabowska to avoid being found by German military leaders.

The Grabowskas lived in Michigan for a short time and then moved on to
Scotland, SD. They finally homesteaded four miles north and five miles east of
Leola. Ten additional children were born there, although four died in infancy
and two died during early adulthood. Their remaining children consisted of six
girls and two boys.

        The August Grabowski Family. Back: Nettie, Alex, Frank, Annie and
        Clara. Front: August, Mayme, Francis and Josephine.

Angela "Nellie" Grabowska remained single and was the housekeeper for Father
Walloch, who was at one time the pastor of the Leola Catholic Church.

Martha became the wife of Frank Marker, and together they ran a general store
in Leola.

Alex married Rosalie Mack and they resided on a farm northeast of Leola.

Clara married veterinarian John Lebold, who practiced in the Leola area.

Frank took Martha Geffre as his wife and they farmed near Leola.

Nettie wed Mike Schwartz, who farmed on the homestead for ten years. Nettie and
Mike later owned a dairy farm in Wisconsin.

Josephine became the wife of Carl Lapka. They farmed northeast of Leola.

Mamie married Rochus Geffre, who farmed and was a veterinarian around Leola.

Mick's grandfather, Vern Guffey, who died in 1982 in Vermillion, SD, enjoyed

also worked at the livery. When his brother Bee contracted small pox they were
quarantined in a line shack somewhere between Leola and Wetonka. He recalled
walking a quarter of a mile to get food that was left for them. When he finally
returned to Leola for a visit in 1972, he was very interested in all of its
changes.

JOHANN and CHRISTIANA GUTHMILLER

Johann's father, Michael Guthmiller Jr. brought his family to America in 1874.
They settled on land seven miles south of Tripp, SD. Michael's son, Philipp
married Christiana Liedle in 1878 and four sons were born: John, Emanuel,
Philipp and Christian. Philipp died suddenly in August, 1884 and a short time
after Christiana married Michael's other son, Johann.

Johann and Christiana homesteaded land eight miles east of Eureka in the year
of 1887. After a few years the boys all left home and in 1913, Johann and
Christiana moved to Billings, MT. They returned, after a short stay, and
purchased a grain elevator in Leola. After a few years, he sold his business
and bought another elevator in Tripp, SD.

Johann and Christiana had four daughters: Martha, Bertha Rose, Emma and
Caroline, and one son, Robert. Robert died at the age of 22, from rheumatoid
arthritis and influenza. About one week later Christiana died from influenza.
Johann then married Carolina (Dietrich) Waltz.

In 1920, the Tripp elevator burned and the Guthmillers moved to Wishek, ND
where he built a home and retired.

JOHN J. and JOHANNA GUTHMILLER

John J. Guthmiller was born in rural McPherson County on December 3, 1899 to
John P. and Maria Guthmiller nee Krein. Being the oldest of a large,
industrious farm family, he learned early how to make a living on the Dakota
prairie. There he grew to manhood on his parents' farm seven miles southwest of
Leola in Howard Township.

Johanna Reinecke, daughter of the Rev. William and Margaret Reinecke nee
Blumenschein, was born in Castle Grove, Jones County, lowa on March 28, 1903.
She had moved with her family to the various congregations her father had
served in the Lutheran churches of Illinois and Iowa prior to coming to Leola
in 1919. She had taught schools in McPherson County prior to her marriage.

On June 1, 1930, Johnny and Johanna were married in the St. James Lutheran
Parsonage by her father. This young couple built the necessary buildings to
start their farmstead 5 1/2 miles southwest of Leola in Section 36 of Spring
Township. Throughout the early years of their marriage they struggled against
drought and poor economic times with vigor and determination.

Three children were born to Johnny and Johanna in their farm home with the
assistance of Dr. C. G. Lundquist and his wife, Idelette. Margaret arrived on
January 2, 1933, Harold on January 2, 1935 and Arlen on October 28, 1939. All
attended schools in Howard and Spring townships. In 1937 Dr. Ted Keller
diagnosed Harold as being a victim of diabetes. Through careful medical
attention, accompanied with insulin and strict diet, Harold was able to enjoy
his childhood and growing up to manhood along with the restrictions of
diabetes.

        The John J. Guthmiller Family. Back: Harold, Arlen and Margaret.
        Front: Johanna and John J.

In 1943 the farm buildings were relocated to a higher level "across the creek"
and a new barn was built. Several years later the original three-room house was
remodeled and enlarged, accompanied with plumbing and electricity, the latter
being eventually provided by the REA.

Johnny was a longtime director and insurance agent for the NWGF Mutual of
Eureka, as well as an agent for American Family. Johanna was active in church
activities including the Ladies Aid of St. James Lutheran, which the family
attended.

Death came early to this farm couple as cancer dealt its stealthy blow. Johanna
died on March 24, 1952 after surgery and a lengthy illness. Johnny died in
surgery on January 25, 1957. Harold and Arlen continued on the farm while
Margaret attended school at NSC and would assist on weekends and through the
summer. Many kind relatives and friends helped in a variety of ways through
these difficult years.

Since 1954, Margaret has been teaching in Sioux Falls. Here she met and married
Ray E. Novak on February 10, 1962. Harold and Arlen continued to live in the
Leola area with their families.

The family picture was taken in November, 1950.

JOHN P. and MARIA GUTHMILLER

John P. Guthmiller was the son of Philip and Christina (Liedle) Guthmiller. He
was born November 25, 1879, at Bon Homme County, Scotland, SD. His parents and
grandparents, the Michael Guthmillers, immigrated to the U.S. from Neudorf,
South Russia in 1874. They settled on a homestead seven miles south of Tripp,
SD. John had three brothers: Philip, Emanuel and Christian. The father passed
away suddenly in August, 1884 at the age of 29. He was buried in the Emanuel
Creek Reformed Cemetery. The mother soon remarried her husband's brother,
Johann, in order to keep the property and small savings in the family. Five
children were born to this union: Martha (Schnuerle), deceased; Bertha
(Potratz); Emma (Gross); Carolina (Eggelston); and Robert, deceased. In 1886,
the parents had the opportunity to homestead land eight miles east of Eureka.

At the age of 19, John was married to Maria Krein on December 6, 1898, at
Eureka. Maria was the eldest of 14 children of Frederick and Margaretha
(Mehlhaff) Krein. Six of their children died in infancy. Maria was born October
15, 1880, Neudorf, South Russia. She came to the U.S. with her parents in 1885.
They made the journey by train to Ipswich and by oxen and wagon to Eureka. The
Krein homestead was located seven miles east and three miles south of Eureka.
Their life began with hardship and great courage. They lived in a sod house for
some time. During the big blizzard of '88, Mr. Krein made a trip to Ipswich and
Mrs. Krein was home with her family. She tried to get out of the house but
everything was buried in snow. Her only alternative was to place kettles on the
stove and go out through the chimney.

        John P. & Maria Guthmiller.

Before her marriage, Maria, at the age of 13, began her first bread baking. The
oven was made of earthen clay and heated with straw and weeds until it was a
golden yellow. The ashes were then cleaned out and the bread was placed in the
oven to be baked. This large oven provided heat for the entire house. Maria's
entire life was baking bread and kuchen for a large family. This was one of her
most gifted talents.

In 1900 John and Maria moved to a homestead in Howard Township, McPherson
County, located two miles west and 3 1/2 miles south of Leola. They lived in a
small house for several years and in 1914 they built a new house. The smaller
house was used for a summer kuche to do laundry, cooking and feeding of the
threshing crews. Their family of 14 children were born and raised on this farm.
The children are: John J. (deceased), Arthur, Emma (died in infancy), Theodore
(deceased), Esther (Breitag), Martha (Rath), Julius, Ruth (Dahl), Calvin, Ella
(Eichelberg), Bertha (deceased), Alma (Dodd), Albert (died in infancy), and
Olive (Lapka). They all attended school at Howard School District No. 1,
McPherson County.

John Guthmiller was school treasurer for many years, a director of the Leola
State Bank and Equity Elevator, and also active in the Reformed Church and
other community affairs.

Julius took over the farm in 1942. The parents purchased a home in Leola where
they lived until their deaths. John passed away May 30, 1950 and Maria on
August 29, 1963. Burial was in the Green Mound Cemetery, Leola.

Only memories remain of this homestead and farm.

TED and CLARA GUTHMILLER

Ted Guthmiller entered the world on October 27, 1903. His parents were John and
Maria (Krein) Guthmiller. He attended the Guthmiller school in Howard Township.
He married Clara Breitag June 28, 1928. They began life together on a farm
southwest of Leola, remaining on that farm until 1957 when they moved to Leola.
They lived there for four years and in 1961, Ted passed away.

Clara was born August 9, 1909 to Otto and Mary Breitag. She attended the
Breitag school in Spring Township and during those years she remembers having
many men teachers. Clara has fond memories of spending winter evenings with her
oldest brother, Albert and their school friends, Wilma and Rex Stickel. They
spend many happy hours sledding down their steep hills by the creek. Part of
the fun was the delicious lunch Mrs. Stickel prepared for them. Clara and
Albert were musicians and played for house parties. Albert played the violin
and accordian and Clara, the organ. She remembers being paid $3.50 for the
evening and tells of the people square dancing and enjoying themselves for
hours.

Clara recalls "threshing time" as a very special time in her life. She helped
her mother cook and when she was 13 years of age, she helped all of her aunts
prepare meals for the threshing crews. She considered herself to be honored to
be so needed. Clara's sunshine cake was one of the favorites of all the crews.
She spent many of her married years cooking for threshers and most of them
looked forward to her tasty meals.

Ted and Clara had four children: Irvin, born June 8, 1929 (residing in
Mobridge); Gerald, born September 1, 1932 (residing in Wright, WY); Arvilla,
born January 30, 1936 (residing in Mankato, MN); and Lila, born May 29, 1942
(residing in Burnsville, MN). They have 11 grandchildren and four
great-grandchildren.

CHRISTIAN and CHRISTINA GUTJAHR

Christian was born in Russia on January 27, 1898 to Fred and Caroline Gutjahr.
When he was seven years old his family came by boat to the U.S. His parents
farmed in the Hosmer and Leola area until 1919. His father started a blacksmith
shop in Leola. Christ first attended school in a farmer's upstairs room. Later
school was held in a one-room schoolhouse. He had to walk 2 1/2 miles to get
there. He attended school until around the sixth grade. As a young boy, Christ
liked to hunt geese, ducks and prairie chickens. He greatly disliked digging
rocks and milking cows. One thing he remembers well was the big celebrations
held on the 4th of July. There were foot races which paid money to the winners.
Christ's father would offer him $2.00 to stay home or $1.00 if he went to the
celebration. He would take the $1.00, go to the celebration with a horse and
buggy, enter the races and often came home with more than he took.

        The Christ Guthmiller Family. Back: Violet, Ella and Alvena. Front:
        Christina and Christ.

On August 21, 1919 Christian married Christina Lechner. Christina was born
December 20, 1903 to Fred and Christina Lechner. The family lived in Arena
Valley on a farm where Christina grew up. Christina tells of how they lived in
a two room sod house. The kitchen had a dirt floor and the front room had a
board floor where they put their cornhusk mattresses to sleep.

Christ and Christina farmed until 1921 when they moved to Leola to help
Christ's father in the Blacksmith shop. In 1948 Christ's father retired and
Christ ran the shop until 1973. Then his health would no longer let him put in
all of the many long hard hours needed. Christ says one of the best times of
the many years of being a Leola businessman was on January 26, 1964, his 66th
birthday. Over 450 people held a surprise birthday party for him. They honored
him with a gift of a drill press to ease his jobs. He will always remember the
fun and appreciation shown him.

Christ and Christina still live in the same house since they moved to Leola.
Christ took an active part in the Leola Fire Department serving as a volunteer.
He was made an honorary member in appreciation of his many years of service.

Christ and Christina have three daughters: Alvena, born in 1920; Ella born in
1922 and Violet born in 1929. There are eight grandchildren, 14
great-grandchildren and one great-great-grandchild.

FREDERICK (FRED) and CAROLINE GUTJAHR

Frederick (Fred) Gutjahr was born in Gluckstal, South Russia on March 30, 1876.
His parents had migrated from Germany to South Russia to homestead. Fred was
baptized April 14, 1876 into the Lutheran Faith and in 1891 became confirmed.
He spent his early years getting a little education before he (at age 15) was
apprenticed to a blacksmith. He learned this trade until he was drafted into
the Russian-Japanese rebellion and for 20 months served nursing wounded
soldiers in the medical department and on the battlefield in northern Siberia.

In 1897 the rebellion ended and Fred married Caroline Lessle. A son, Christian,
was born January 27, 1898. Being fed up with Russia, after the war, Fred and
his family packed and set out for America. They arrived at his brother's farm
at Hosmer, SD in 1905 where they stayed until he could open a blacksmith shop
in Hosmer. The two years the Gutjahrs lived in Hosmer they did blacksmithing,
joined the Congregational Church, gave birth to a daughter (Caroline [Mrs. Earl
Lacey], deceased) on April 10, 1905.

Wanting to get into the country, Fred bought a claim from Phrene Junge in Arena
Township in 1907 and moved his family into the sod house and small building he
had erected. Later he built a house for them to live in. Fred tilled the land
and did blacksmithing for his neighbors. In 1908 another daughter, Lydia (Mrs.
L. W. Lancaster, San Diego, CA) was born and on August 20, 1910, Mary (Mrs.
Gerhardt Breitag, Leola) was born. Needing to expand, Fred bought some of the
claims his neighbors had proved. One was from Frederick J. Jung which he broke
and used as pasture. February 20, 1915, Katherine (Mrs. G. Warren, Canoga Park,
CA) was born.

Fred and Caroline left the farm on October 29, 1919, since Caroline was in ill
health, and moved into the Fred Young home that Fred bought. Again Fred did
blacksmithing, purchasing the Lortsher Lumber Yard, September 19, 1919 and
later in 1946 purchasing the McPherson County shed.

In 1928, the forge exploded and burned Fred's face and arms to the elbows so
that he couldn't work. Conrad Ehresman then helped in the shop. Fred served on
the city council from August 11, 1930 to November 4, 1932. Fred semi-retired in
1946, leaving Christ to continue the blacksmithing. He spent his time operating
a small farm north of the depot (now owned by Reinhold Schaible). Fred wanted a
Congregational Church in Leola since he was a member of one in Hosmer so he
bought the Hoffman church in the Long Lake territory and had it moved to Leola.
This building is now Straub's funeral parlor. After working so hard for many
years, Fred passed away on March 30, 1952 at the age of 76.

ERNEST and ANNA HABERMAN

Ernest Haberman was born September 26, 1879, on a farm near Waterloo, WI to
John and Rosa (Yanish) Haberman. When he was only three years old, he came with
his pioneering parents, who settled in Weber Township, McPherson County, in
1883.

He married Anna England July 12, 1905. She was born April 9, 1883, to Franklin
and Rebecca England of Benton, IA. While still a young girl, Anna came to
Dakota Territory with her parents.

        Ernest & Anna Haberman.

Ernest and Anna lived on the farm his parents had homesteaded until 1913, when
the house burned. Fortunately, they had already nearly completed a new house on
the land Ernest owned directly north of the home place, which provided them
with immediate shelter.

The Habermans farmed in Weber Township until 1930, when they moved to
Ellendale, ND. Ernest had always been active in community affairs, serving on
the township board and the school board for many years.

They were the parents of ten children, all born in McPherson County. Myrtle
married John Wetzler of Frederick (five children). Esther married Howard
Anderson of Ellendale (two children). Gladys married Roy Hanson of Ellendale
(one child). Edwin married Maie Schaffer and lived in Leola for a number of
years. They are both deceased (two children). Frances married Irwin Gesme
(deceased). Frances continues to live in Eugene, OR (four children). Lawrence
married Gladys Gentz and lives in Aurora, MN (six children). Harold married
Nancy Andradl, and lives at Sacramento, CA. Howard married Doris Gentz. They
have six children. Mildred married Alden Jenson (deceased), and lives at
Currie, MN (six children). Ernest married Betty Mallon, and lives at Salt Lake
City, UT (one child).

Anna Haberman died July 7, 1952, and Ernest Haberman died February 2, 1961, at
Ellendale. ND.

JOHN and ROSA HABERMAN

John Haberman was born near Vienna, Austria, April 28, 1840, to Mr. and Mrs.
Engelbert Haberman. He came with his parents to the U.S. in 1852 and settled in
rural Waterloo, Jefferson County, WI. As he grew to manhood, he came to know
Rosa Yanish, whom he later married October 10, 1865. Rosa was born May 23,
1848. She, like John, had also come from Austria with her parents, and they,
too, had settled in the Waterloo area.

        The John Haberman Family. Back: Zeno, Nellie, Emil, Edward, Ella and
        Ernest. Front: Rosa, George, Fred and John. Not pictured: Anna, Max and
        John, Jr.

In 1864 John served in the Illinois Regiment, 1st Brigade, 3rd Division of the
17th Army Corps of the Civil War. According to official records he volunteered
and served in "Sherman's March to the Sea" and the "On to Richmond" campaigns.
He was honorably discharged at Louisville, KY, July 17, 1865.

After his discharge from the army, he returned to Waterloo where he and Rosa
were married. They moved to Dodge County, WI, where he resumed farming. As time
went on, the lure of the spacious prairie land being opened for homestead entry
in Dakota Territory tempted them to join the westward movement. After much
deliberation, the Habermans consulted a land agent in 1883, and with his aid
they chose Weber Township in McPherson County as a suitable location for their
new home on the prairie. At this time their family had increased to ten
children.

Mr. Haberman with his two older sons, William and Edward, went on ahead to
build a home for the family, hauling the lumber for their frame house from
Frederick, the nearest railroad.

With the help of her father, Rosa and the remaining eight children boarded the
train at Portland, Dodge County, WI and headed west to Dakota, arriving June
10, 1883, at Frederick. With a wagon and team her husband and the boys were
waiting for them at the station.

As they poked along to their new home, mile after mile over the trackless
prairie, seeing no one, they longingly recalled all they had left behind in
beautiful Wisconsin--relatives, friends and civilization. However, there was
one redeeming feature--they would not have to clear the land. "No trees" meant
that the land was ready and waiting to be broken by the plow. And John and the
boys were eager to get started.

The following spring the Habermans set out many trees, which eventually became
a fine grove, sheltering the farm. Their fruit trees supplied them amply with
apples, cherries and plums. In the nearby gulches berries were there for the
picking. And the prairie, abloom with wildflowers, helped make the surroundings
more pleasant.

Life was not all hardships. The Habermans soon became acquainted with their
neighbors who, like them, had recently come from Wisconsin and other states.
Joseph Haberman, brother of John, settled nearby with his family. According to
the C. F. Hargitt account, for amusement the settlers piled into wagons or
sleighs and went to each other's homes for dancing parties held twice a month
during the winter. The main dancing place was Weber's, but the first dance, as
he recalled, was at Haberman's. He particularly remembered Ella Haberman. Mr.
Whitehouse was the one-piece orchestra furnishing the music with his fiddle. In
time, Max and Fred Haberman took their turns fiddling for dances.

After coming to Dakota two more children were born to the Habermans. William,
1867; Edward, 1868-1916; Ella, 1870-1967 (Mrs. Charles Fosler); Nellie,
1872-1961 (Mrs. George Hagerty); Anna, 1874-1955 (Mrs. John Hepperle); John,
Jr., 1877-1899 (Spanish American War); Emil, 1878-1964 (Doctor--WWI Medical
Corps, married Eva Lamont, and then Thilda Stensland); Ernest, 1879-1961
(married Anna England); Max, 1881-1973 (married Ebba Fagerstrom); George,
1883-1975 (married Anna Ulrich); Zeno, 1888-1959 (married Gladys Jenkins);
Fred, 1892-1967 (WWI Army Band, married Mae L. Sly).

Mrs. Haberman died April 18, 1910, and Mr. Haberman, February 13, 1921. Both
are buried in Green Mound Cemetery at Leola.

JOSEPH and ROSA MARIE HABERMAN

Joseph Haberman, born in 1841 in Remich, Germany migrated to the U.S. in 1851,
with his family. They settled in Wisconsin and Joseph served with the 29th
Wisconsin Infantry during the Civil War. In 1885 he married Rosa Marie Kaschper
who had been born in 1851 in Knoppendorf, Germany, and who had come to the U.S.
in 1881. Looking for a new life, they moved to McPherson County and
homesteaded. Their first house was a one-room shack, 10x12; so small that it
was often covered with snow in the blizzards that raged through. They planted
10 acres of trees by hand, and dug their own well. Only the men wore leather
shoes; the rest of the family wrapped their feet in cloths during cold weather.

        Joseph & Rosa Maria Haberman.

Joseph and Rosa had four children: William, Mollie (Mrs. Abner Hart), Henry and
Ida (Mrs. Fred Robinson).

Joseph and Rosa lived on the homestead until their deaths in 1917 and 1934.

YVONNE HAEFNER

transferred from Timber Lake to Leola by the Soil Conservation Service for

In April, 1982 she joined the J.W. (Just Women) club for promoting activities

for the Prairie Rustlers 4-H club, and is a member of the Better Leola Club.

She has participated in the adult showmanship class at 4-H Achievement days for

She was born November 11, 1953 to Art and Ruth Haefner in Mobridge, SD and was
raised on a ranch southwest of there. She completed her four-year degree from
Dickinson State College in 1978 and began working with the Soil Conservation
Service in 1979 at Timber Lake.

JOHN P. and ANNA HAMMRICH

immigrated from Lukenburg, Germany to Chicago. They moved to Edmunds County

WILLIAM and ANNA HANKS

Will Hanks, his wife Annie, and daughter Kittie moved to McPherson County in
the spring of 1910. They purchased the Sutherland farm ten miles northeast of
Leola where the Sutherland Post Office had been located.

William McClelland Hanks was born April 14, 1861, at Quincy, IL the fifth child
of nine children born to Joseph Hanks III and Martha (Bartholomew) Hanks. He
graduated from Gen City Business College in Quincy and in 1886 went to Canon
City, CO where he established a large transfer line that freighted with wagons
and mule teams . In 1888 he returned to Illinois to marry Anna Howes, daughter
of Francis Marion Howes and Mary Jane (Knox) Howes, born July 13, 1861 near
Warsaw, IL. They were married March 15, 1888 at the Howes home and made their
first home in Canon City, where their daughter, Kittie Ethel was born on May
15, 1889. When Kittie was three they moved to Grand Junction, Co and shortly
thereafter purchased a farm at Delta, CO where their son, Joseph Phillip was
born June 20, 1895. Four months later the family returned to Illinois where
Will went into partnership in a meat market at Basco, IL. He bought cattle and
hogs and his partner butchered and managed the meat market. Will delivered and
sold meat with a horse and meat wagon. He had a daily route due to lack of
refrigeration. Housewives came to the wagon and picked out their meat when they
heard his bell.

In 1908 Joseph died following an appendix surgery and Will decided to leave the
area where everything reminded him of his son. In August of 1909 he visited his
brother Charles, who lived northeast of Leola, and being favorably impressed
with the fields of waving grain, he bought in that area. He raised and bought
purebred Hereford cattle throughout the midwest.

Will loved to sing and was proud of his wife's musical talent. Their organ was
one of the first in the neighborhood and was used for special occasions at the
church services held at the Koto school. Annie and Kittie found other ways for
entertainment such as embroidery work, crocheting and tatting. Annie did
macrame, knitting and pieced beautiful quilts. They also made all their own
clothing.

In the fall of 1929, Will was critically injured when his horse fell on him. He
died on May 11, 1930 and Annie lived with her daughter until her death on March
11, 1946.

EVERETT and LORETTA HART
