JAMES R. and ANNA HART

James R. Hart (born 1845), a Civil War veteran married Anna Kribs, a widow with
two daughters, Anna and Josephine, in 1867. In 1881 they moved from Minnesota
to Dakota Territory, living in Brown County before moving to Weber Township in
McPherson County. During his lifetime he was actively engaged in the activities
of the John A. Spellman Post, G.A.R., and when he died only three of his fellow
veterans were alive to attend his funeral--G. H. Keyes, C. P. Crary and J.
Scott. Anna was for many years the postmaster for Alpha, SD.

        Anna & James Hart.

James and Anna's children were: Etta, Katherine, Winifred, Maud and Harold born
in Minnesota; Abner, Charles and Dorothy born in Weber Township.

In common with other pioneers they endured drouth, wind, and cold winters; but
they enjoyed housewarmings for new settlers, dances and music. One of their
early sources of income was from gathering and selling tons of buffalo bones to
sugar refineries. They worried through Indian scares whenever the Indians
traveled the Standing Rock Trail.

The first school in the area was held in Ruth Krib's claim shanty, with Ruth as
a teacher. Another early school was taught by Katie Scott in a shanty near the
Howell homestead. The first real school building was built in 1884, and when
Minnie Syle was the teacher it was the largest school in the country with
children from the Weber, Scott, Howell, Pepper, Barden, Mitchell, Aylesworth
and Hart families in attendance.

James Rufus died April 28, 1928 at the age of 82 years. He had a full and
adventurous life. At age 17, he enlisted in the Infantry, serving throughout
the Civil War. He was among the early settlers of Dakota Territory.

Anna Kribbs Hart died on August 25, 1929. She spent some of her last years
living with her children, including the two children from her first marriage;
Anna Ruth Kribbs (Hanson) and Josephine Anna Kribbs (George).

ABNER JAMES and MOLLIE MARIE HART

Abner James Hart, son of James Rufus and Anna (Remington) Kribbs Hart was born
September 14, 1883 in Kassen, MN. Looking for a place to settle, he moved to
Dakota Territory and filed on a homestead about five miles west of Forbes in
the spring of 1905. Abner married Mollie Haberman August 9, 1905 at Lamoure,
ND.

Mollie Marie Haberman was born September 16, 1888, the daughter of Joseph and
Rosa Marie (Kaschper) Haberman, at Alpha, SD.

        The Abner Hart Family. Back: Jesse, Maude, Edith and Genevieve. Middle:
        Harding, Leslie, Neale, Joseph and Charles. Front: James, Florence,
        Abner, Mollie, Evelyn and Everett

The family did not stay long in the hills. They moved to the Pete Kabrud farm
four miles south of Forbes, and from there they went to the "Old Hart Farm" at
Alpha, SD, in 1906. In the fall of 1917 the family purchased a farm in
McPherson County, Carl Township. The land was completely bare and the Harts
moved in a house from the Flakoll place with horses and wagons. A well was dug,
other buildings moved in and fences put up. Abner plowed the ground with a
walking plow to raise some grain, and the children followed behind to make sure
every furrow laid nice and flat. The whole family liked it here and they made
lots of friends. They had house parties on weekends at someone's house, nice
midnight lunches, and Abner always played the violin for entertainment. His
favorite was "Red Wing" and he played it often.

In the fall of 1923, the family moved to the Howell place where they farmed
until 1931. They then moved south of Forbes until 1938 when they moved to the
Haberman Homestead in Weber Township. They lived there until they retired and
moved to Forbes in 1960. Abner passed away December 25, 1967 and Mollie on
January 31, 1971. Both are buried at Sunset Memorial at Aberdeen, SD. They had
64 grandchildren, 126 great-grandchildren, and 25 great-great-grandchildren.

Abner's brothers and sisters were: Anna Kribbs, Josephine Kribbs, Etta Hart,
Katherine Hart, Winnifred Hart, Maude Hart, Harold Hart, Charles Hart and
Dorothy Hart. Mollie's brothers and sisters were: Ida, William and Henry
Haberman.

Children of Abner and Mollie Hart are listed here. Maude Evangeline, born
January 24, 1906, married Marion J . Holsworth, May 28, 1923. They had 11
children, and are both deceased. Florence Geraldine, born April 19, 1907,
married Lawrence Austin October 20, 1926. They had nine children and live in

in Aberdeen, SD. Genevieve Ida, born March 5, 1910, married Arthur N. Moore,
February 12, 1930. They had three children. They are both deceased and buried

1911, married Mildred Austin, October 5, 1931. They had three children, and
live at St. Helens, OR. Evelyn Esther, born April 30, 1914, married Carl L.
Rogers, November 13, 1929. They had four children. Carl is deceased and Evelyn

June 30, 1934. They had four children. Charles is deceased and Edith lives in

ALBERT C. and ALMA HAUFFE

Albert C. Hauffe was born in Chicago, July, 1898. He traveled to South Dakota
in 1914 to visit relatives, Otto and Wanda Hauffe, who lived 3 1/2 miles north
of Leola in Koto Township. For four years he attended school, between harvests,
in Chicago and Omaha to become a court reporter, but decided in 1918 to become
a farmer instead. In October of 1920 he married Alma Hauffe, daughter of Otto
and Wanda Hauffe, and the young Hauffes rented the Pinkerton farm north of
Leola. In addition to medical bills from Alma's recurrent illnesses, the
Hauffes endured farm problems such as rent payments, poor crops and low prices
which kept their income marginal for the first 10-15 years.

Witnessing young and well-established farmers alike sink with the depressed
farm economy in the late 1920s and 1930s was enough inspiration for Albert to
speak out on agricultural issues. Several publications carried his letters
citing areas needing improvement, and Albert twice ran for the State
Legislature--once as an independent in 1926 and then as a Republican in the
1930 primary. Another person who agreed with Albert's view for greater farmer
unity through cooperatives was David Crouch, neighbor, legislator and
co-founder of the Leola Equity Exchange. He encouraged Albert to take a seat on
the South Dakota Wheat Growers Association board of directors in 1928 and on
the local Equity Exchange board in 1933. In 1934 Albert also served as an
incorporating director of the Aberdeen Production Credit Association and was
that organization's vice president before retiring from the PCA.

The New Deal's agricultural relief programs were the kinds of progressive
solutions that Albert wanted to be a part of as he began his longtime
association in 1933 with the Agricultural Adjustment Administration. He started
with the AAA by measuring McPherson County crop land, and then served as
chairman of the county AAA committee. This was followed by six years of working
as an AAA fieldman in northeastern South Dakota.

As time went on, Albert's efforts to increase the quality of farmlife led him
to recognize the key role electricity could play. Joining Ted Martel of Long
Lake and Paul Hausauer of Eureka to represent McPherson County on the FEM Rural
Electric Cooperative, they helped launch the cooperative in 1948. Over the next
28 years, Albert was president of that successful community enterprise.

In 1947 the FEM board selected him to represent the cooperative on the SD Rural
Electric Association board of directors. While serving as president of the
statewide association for the next 22 years, Albert worked with 35 electric
cooperatives as they secured an adequate supply of low cost power from the dams
constructed on the Missouri River and developed independent G & T cooperatives.
He campaigned strongly for nearly 1,000 electric cooperatives before Congress,
from 1949 until his death in August, 1976. He was South Dakota's representative
on the National Rural Electric Cooperative Association headquartered in
Washington, DC and served as that group's president.

        The Albert Hauffe Family. Back: Ruth, Harry and Paul. Front: Alma and
        Albert.

Albert maintained an interest in his home and the Leola community over the
years. Both Albert and Alma were active in the Masonic Lodge and Eastern Star;
he as Master of the Leola Lodge in 1933 and 1934 and Alma as Worthy Matron in
1933. Albert served as clerk of Koto Township and Alma served as school clerk
of the township. Alma participated in the St. James Lutheran women's
organizations and in the Country Club. She also actively supported Leola's
community hospital from 1952 until its closing. Albert retired from active
farming in 1966 and rented the land while he and Alma continued to reside on
the farm. He was an avid golfer at the Leola Country Club and a supporter of
Leola's Senior Citizens Club.

The Hauffes were parents of three children, Paul, Ruth and Harry, who each
attended 12 years in the Leola public school system.

OTTO A. and WANDA HAUFFE

Only four miles separated the birthplaces of Otto Andrew Hauffe and Wanda
Wilhelmina Zauft in the east German province of Posen. While growing up, they
never met. However, years later and thousands of miles away, the two formed one
of the well-known farm families during the formation of the Leola community.

Born in 1864, Otto grew up near Walheide, Germany, on a farm that could not
support his parents' family of six children. Lured by reports of economic
opportunities in America, Otto joined the flow of German immigrants in
September 1886 who arrived at New York City. Otto joined his sister, Ernstine,
and her husband, Gustav D. Tonn, who were homesteading on Section 4 of Leola
Township.

It was here that Otto established his roots and, along with the Tonns, became
one of the founding members of the German Lutheran Church on July 24, 1887, the
present St. James Lutheran Church.

It was also here Otto met Wanda Zauft who worked as a waitress in Tarquin
Franklin's hotel on the corner of Sherman and Moulton streets. Compelled by a
sense of adventure, 18-year-old Wanda had left her parents' home at Eichquast
in 1888. She was happy to have the chance to come to the Dakota Territory in
America with her Aunt Augusta and Uncle Henry Schultz. For a while the Schultz
family lived one mile southeast of Otto Hauffe and the Tonns.

The Schultz family was present, as was Henry Green, at the wedding of Wanda and
Otto on November 8, 1890, before the Rev. Martin Reischauer. Otto purchased his
brother-in-law's farm equipment and livestock, and then rented the improved
southeast quarter after the Tonn's decided to move to Oregon in 1890. The
newlyweds resided for eight years on Otto's rented acreage where the first
three of their children were born--Elsie, Theodore, and Olga.

Having acquired some capital Otto established a homestead on the NW 1/4 of
Section 3 after an early settler, George Schimpf, relinquished his timber
claim. Construction of the two-story home, plus a granary, barn and a well were
completed for the family to occupy the farm by the fall of 1898.

By November of that fall, the family had a double reason to celebrate. Alma,
the 4th child was born. Over the next ten years, three other children were
added, Otto Jr., Hilda and Ilsa. The three oldest began their education at the
rural schoolhouse on the SW 1/4 of Section 3 also attended by Robert Mastel's
five children.

        The Otto Hauffe Family. Back: Olga, Theodore and Alma. Front: Hilda,
        Otto Sr., Ilsa, Wanda and Otto Jr.

By the time Alma reached school age, the children had switched to the Koto No.
1 school. All eight grades were taught to the dozen students who included the
children of John Dexter, Peter Geffre, John Lapka, Mark Warnick and Heile Yost.
The Leola Independent School began accommodating town and rural students by
1910. Both Hilda and Ilsa attended all 12 years of their education there and
became school teachers.

Expansion on the Hauffe farm took place with the beginning of the next century.
The early 1900's brought both good prices and crops allowing Otto to diversify
his farming operation. By 1920, the Hauffes owned 800 acres of the 1,120 acres
they farmed.

Mechanical innovations enhanced rural life for the Posen natives and their
children, as did homespun entertainment and visits with neighbors. Families
would pack aboard buggy, wagon, and sled to spend an evening visiting while
children played games, ate popcorn, and sang around the piano. Otto often
performed for dances in homes with his concertina. Probably the most popular,
large social event was the barn dance, many of which were held in the hayloft
of Hauffe's large barn. Frequent visitors were neighboring families of Heile
Yost, Henry Young, Peter Geffre, August Grabowska, John Lapka, John Kallas, and
Emil Kutschke.

Hospitalized during the last three of his 75 years of life, Otto died in 1940.
Wanda continued to live in Leola until 1954. She lived another two years in her
daughter's homes and nearly reached 87 years of age.

FRED J. and EMMA HEPPERLE

Fred was born to John J. and Anna (Haberman) Hepperle at Leola, December 28,
1899, on his parents' first wedding anniversary. He was the oldest of seven
children.

Growing up and attending school in Leola, Fred became one of the members of the
first graduating class of Leola (four-year) High School in 1917. He then
attended South Dakota State University for one year before entering the army in
WWI.

Fred then spent six years in Loyalton, SD, as manager of the Central Lumber
Yards and Hardware. Here he met and married Emma A. Rittierodt, daughter of
Henry and Alvina Rittierodt, in 1928. They then moved back to the Leola area
and farmed north of town for three years.

In 1933 Fred was elected McPherson County Register of Deeds. He was filling
that capacity in a second term, when he was accepted as the Leola Postmaster on
August 17, 1936, and held that position for 31 years, retiring in December of
1967.

Emma joined Fred in the post office as a substitute clerk, and for many years
she was active in all community affairs. She served as church organist for St.
Paul's Lutheran Church, as secretary of the American Legion Auxiliary, county
chairman and state director of the Cripple Children's Society. And, too, she
was a member of Disco Club, Dial Bridge Club, and Country Club. Emma died June
22, 1961.

The one day that Fred remembered the most in his postal career was when the
community gathered and honored him for his friendly, courteous and dedicated
service on FRED HEPPERLE DAY, May 5, 1968.

        Emma & Fred Hepperle.

Fred remarried in August of 1964 to Elma Heibel and was spending the winter in
Tucson, AZ, when he passed away on December 14, 1970. He was a member of the
St. James Lutheran Church, Masonic Lodge, the American Legion and Volunteer
Firemen. His wife Elma is still residing in her home in Leola.

JOHN and ANNA HEPPERLE

John Joseph Hepperle, who was instrumental in the development of the town of
Leola and of McPherson County, was born May 22, 1873 to Johann and Elizabeth
Hepperle, nee Keller, at Guldendorf, a village near Odessa, Russia. In 1820 his
great-grandparents, Johann and Agnes (Roser) Hepperle were part of the
thousands of German inhabitants who had immigrated to South Russia. And, yet,
before the turn of the century their descendants were emigrating from Russia by
the thousands, primarily because Czar Alexander II had issued decrees which
abolished the privileges granted to the German settlers by Catherine the Great.

In 1885 Fred, at the age of 22, brother of John, was the first of the Hepperles
to join the great exodus from Russia to the United States. Already established
in Eureka, he was making his second trip back to Russia to see his family, and
especially to bring John back with him to Eureka, where he could help him get
started in America. And so, in 1891 John, who had just graduated from the
Gymnasium (German secondary school) in the village, came to America. Although
John had studied English as a foreign language, he lacked practice in usage. In
later years as he related some of his experiences while he had attended SDSU
and USD during the school terms of 1893 and 1894, he said he had found it
necessary to translate much textbook matter into German to obtain clear-cut
understanding. This possibly accounts for the command he eventually had of both
languages.

        John & Anna Hepperle.

On December 28, 1898 he married Anna Haberman, daughter of John and Rosa
Haberman, who lived on a farm in Weber Township. Anna was born June 15, 1874
near Portland, WI, where her parents had emigrated from Austria. The family
moved to Dakota Territory in 1883. Anna attended Brown County Normal Institute,
Aberdeen Business College and took courses from American Correspondence Normal.
Before her marriage she taught in rural schools and in 1897-1898, in the Leola
Public School. For many years Mrs. Hepperle served as treasurer of the Green
Mound Cemetery Association of Leola. Until her death she was a member of St.
James Ladies Aid and of Disco Club.

John Hepperle was active in church, school, business and politics of the town,
county and state. He was elected president of the village board of trustees in
1910, and reelected in 1915. In 1898 he was elected county treasurer and
subsequently held the offices of auditor, register of deeds and commissioner.
In 1918 he was elected to the South Dakota State Senate. He served on the Leola
school board intermittently throughout his lifetime. He was president of the
First State Bank of Leola for many years. Other business ventures included
considerable real estate in Leola and the surrounding area. He also worked
diligently for the relief of people of German descent still living in Russia
and contributed significantly to that cause.

Of the nine children born to John and Anna Hepperle, two died in infancy. The
remaining seven attended Leola schools. All attended college.

Fred John (see Fred Hepperle Family).

Ruth Elizabeth was born July 22, 1904. She received a B.A. degree from USD and
taught in Leola and Aberdeen schools before her marriage to Homer B. Slater. He
died in Kansas City, MO, where Ruth now resides.

Helen Esther was born May 18, 1907. She received a B.S. degree from Iowa State
and managed a Myron Green Tea Room in Kansas City before her marriage to Carl
F. Rudi. They live in Chicago.

Lillian Natalie (see Eugene and Lillian Kindelspire).

Walter Louis was born October 9, 1911. He attended USD and Iowa State. He was
the proprietor of the Leola Cafe for two years before moving to California
where he worked for Safeway Stores for many years. After the death of his wife
M. Delphy (Turner), he retired to Tucson, AZ. He is now married to the former
Mary L. Lende.

Mary Ellen was born September 30, 1916. She attended NSC and Minnesota
University and taught in the Leola area before her marriage to Lester E.
Lindley. He died in 1980 in Tucson, AZ, where Mary still resides.

Curtis Monroe was born December 26, 1918. He graduated from Illinois Institute
of Technology with a B.S. degree an did graduate work at MIT and Iowa
University before his marriage to V. Doris Howard. He was employed at Hughes
Aircraft Company for many years as Manager of the Laser Division until his
retirement in 1982. The Hepperles live in Tarzana, CA.

John and Anna Hepperle were lifelong residents of Leola, living their entire
married life in the home they had built for them in 1907. Gene and Lillian are
still living in the Hepperle home, which they now own.

The Hepperle family belonged to the Lutheran Church. Mr. Hepperle died June 29,
1930 and Mrs. Hepperle, June 2, 1955. Both are buried at Green Mound Cemetery
at Leola.

AUGUST G. and MARIA HEUPEL

August Heupel, born August 10, 1891 at Kassel, Russia came to America on the
North German Lloyd Ship when he was seven years old. August and his parents
arrived on May 2, 1899. They came to Hosmer along with approximately 700 people
and remained there until 1905 when they moved to Arena Township, west of Leola.

Maria Klooz was born March 14, 1892 in Kassel Russia. Her parents migrated to
America when she was two years old. Maria married August December 9, 1913 and
they lived with his parents until they built their own home nine miles west of
Leola where they raised their ten children. In 1956, they moved to Aberdeen,
SD, returning to the farm in the summer to help their son Harold farm. They
sold the farm in 1969 and spent their remaining years in Aberdeen, SD. Maria
died in 1975 and August died in 1982.

        The August Heupel Family. Back: Harold, Viola, Rene and Lily. Middle:
        Vivian, Annie, Alma, Irma, Edgar and Olivia. Front: Mary and August.

Children in the Heupel family are: Alma (Vilhauer), Edgar, Olivia (Young),

JACOB SR. and ROSINA HEUPEL

Jacob, the son of Jacob and Rosina (Gohl) Heupel, was born on September 30,
1892 at the homestead near Eureka, SD. Jacob had three brothers: August,

Stabler, Mrs. Edwin (Christina) Kallenberger, who are all deceased. Mrs.

Berreth, Moses Lake; Mrs. Walter (Anna) Frankfurth, Spokane; Calvin, Kent;

Zantow, Leola; Mrs. Larry (Shirley) Wilson, Westport; Eugene, Lead; Jacob,

Jacob and Rosina farmed for many years in Petersburg Township, 11 miles
northwest of Long Lake, SD. In 1935, they moved southeast of Leola and years
later, east of Leola to the "eight mile corner."

They retired from farming in 1947, had an auction sale and moved to Westport,
SD.

        Rosina & Jacob Heupel.

The picture of Jacob and Rosina was taken at their 50th wedding anniversary
celebration, six months before Jacob passed away. Jacob died January 25, 1967.

JACOB and CHRISTINA HEUPEL

ARTHUR and BLANCHE HICKMAN

Arthur Irving Hickman and Blanche Beach were married March 12, 1913 at the
Methodist Church in Leola. They lived on the original homestead until 1930 when
they moved to Leola. In 1934 they moved to the Long Lake area and later to
Cherry Grove, OR.

In his early years, Arthur herded cattle in the hills a few miles west of their
farm and for pastime he chiseled a cowboy hat and the year 1901 on a large rock
in a gully. This rock is located in Section 36 in Wacker Township and can be
seen to this day. His brother, Charley, lived a mile or so west of his farm on
what is now known as the Morrison place. They also moved to Leola. Charley's
wife Adelaid ran the hotel and for a while Charley was a county highway
supervisor. They later moved to Ipswich where he did the same type of work for
the state and his wife was cook at the C & C Cafe. Their children were:
Charlotte (Mrs. Ralph Edel), Lancaster, PA; Evelyn (Mrs. Bob Goodbarn) deceased
in 1981 and Douglas in California. These two brothers stayed in the Leola area
longest and the families were very close. They enjoyed hunting, fishing,
picnics and holidays together.

        George Leslie, Blanche and Arthur Hickman.

The George Hickman Family.

Arthur and Blanche had four children: George Leslie, Grants Pass, OR, born
February 24, 1914. He was a retired lumber man at the time of his death,
February 15, 1982. Irving Beach, Hillsboro, OR, was a retired WWII veteran and
farmer. He died April 7, 1969. Maude Lucille (Mrs. Rudolph Heyd) was born
November 16, 1917 and lives at Long Lake, SD. (The above three are graduates of
Leola High School.) Beverly Mae, (Mrs. Howard Koerner) Fullerton, CA was born
May 15, 1921.

GEORGE W. and ROXANNA HICKMAN

George W. Hickman was born in Rothenberg, Hessen Dormstadt, Germany April 24,
1849 to John George and Elizabeth (Lehn) Hickman. He came to America with his
parents in 1854. They settled in Buffalo, NY where they resided until 1858 when
they moved to Galena, IL in La Salle County.

On December 24, 1871 he was united in marriage to Roxanna Howe and the
following year they moved to Sac County, IA. Ten years later they moved to
Dakota Territory settling in Marshall County. During their residence there, Mr.
Hickman was elected Probate Judge. Their next and final move was to McPherson
County where they homesteaded nine miles north of Leola.

In 1890 he was elected Representative to the second general assembly of the
South Dakota Legislature and later served six terms as Superintendent of
McPherson County Schools. He died in 1916 and his wife in 1912.

To this union were born six sons and one daughter: William, Bertha, George,
Arthur, Charles, Elmer and John, all deceased.

RUDOLPH and LUCILLE (HICKMAN) HEYD

Rudolph Heyd and Lucille Hickman were united in marriage October 23, 1938 at
Salem Emmanuel Lutheran Church in Long Lake, SD. Rudolph was born March 12,
1914 in Bergdorf Township to John D. and Eva (Gienger) Heyd. They farmed the
original homestead plus purchased acreage, starting with horse drawn machines
and gradually acquiring a full line of powered machinery. Quite a transition!
After the devastating tornado of 1966 the farm was rebuilt.

Lucille taught school 16 years in McPherson County. They are members of Salem
Emmanuel Lutheran Church where Rudolph has served as council member many times.

In 1975, having decided to retire, an auction sale was held. They continued
living on the farm until 1980 when they purchased a home in Long Lake. Here
they enjoy the community activities and do a lot of fishing and biking.

Their children are: one daughter, Judith Ann and one son, Jerome Irving. Judith
Ann, born July 18, 1943 at Eureka Hospital, is a Eureka High School graduate.
She operates a family business, Kelley Enterprises, Inc. at Aberdeen, SD. She
married Allen G. Kelle June 25, 1961 at Zion Lutheran in Eureka, SD. They have
two sons: Brian George, born May 8, 1962, stationed at Panama City, FL in the
Air Force and Daniel Arthur, born March 18, 1970, a Jr. High student.

Jerome Irving, born August 6, 1945 is a Eureka High School graduate and has a
B.S. degree in Chemical Engineering from the School of Mines and Technology at
Rapid City, SD. He married Linda Schmid Taylor February 8, 1969 at Ponca City,
OK. They have one son, Andrew Rudolph, born September 7, 1969. At the present
time Jerome is Process Superintendent at the Ponca City Continental Oil
Refinery and they live at 1501 Pioneer Rd., Ponca City, OK.

CALVIN C. and CHRISTINE HILGEMANN

Calvin C. Hilgemann was born to Fred and Karolina Hilgemann on February 2, 1901
in a sod house on the family homestead north of Eureka, SD. He started his
boyhood years by attending rural country schools. His father was often his
teacher. Later he attended school in Leola when his father was McPherson County
Treasurer.

        Calvin C. Hilgemann.

Calvin has had experience in many interesting areas of work. He began clerking
in the Leola Leader after school and in the summertime. Later he clerked in
Eureka, SD and Zeeland, ND stores. He taught rural schools for three years
until he accepted employment in the Greenway State Bank. When Calvin's brother
died, he moved back to the family homestead and farmed for several years. While
on the farm he was married to Christine Kammerer. Calvin and Christine have two
sons: Fred D., born January 30, 1933 and Harry D., born January 5, 1937. Fred
resides in Arapaho, CO and Harry makes his home in Wall, SD. Both sons are
married.

As the years progressed, Calvin was called to serve in many capacities. He was
school board member for several years and in 1934 he was elected County
Auditor. In the later part of 1934, Calvin moved his family to Leola. After
serving his term as Auditor, he was elected County Treasurer. He alternately
held these offices for 18 years. While he was in office, Calvin acquired a
small business from the Gellings. He later enlarged it by purchasing the former
Brosz Red Owl Grocery building where he has continued his business (The
Apparel) majoring in shoes and clothing. This business is still in operation.

During his tenure as Mayor, Calvin brought about many improvements in the city.
Nearly all of the city streets were oiled except one previously oiled block in
the main business section. He was instrumental in procuring the present ball
park, which later was enlarged to include a football field. He also obtained,
for the state, the site where the present State Highway shop is located.

When Calvin no longer held county offices he was elected and served four years
in the State Legislature. Following this service, he was employed by the
Commissioner of School and Public Lands as a fieldman selling and leasing state
land. He served in that capacity for 7 1/2 years. Always forging ahead, Calvin
turned his attention to an Insurance Agency and he has spent the past several
years successfully managing the store plus the Insurance Agency.

The multiple ventures pursued in the numerous years of service with honesty and
integrity gave Calvin a vast amount of experience and knowledge which he has
used endlessly helping the common people. He has earned the respect of his
'fellow men' and that he enjoys to this date.

ED and WILMA HILGEMANN

I, Ed Hilgemann, was born at Leola, SD to Gustave Hilgemann and Elizabeth (Opp)
Hilgemann. My grandparents migrated to this country from Germany and Russia and
settled in the Eureka area. My father taught school northeast of Eureka where
he met and married my mother. They moved to Leola in about 1920 where my father
was Clerk of Courts at the time of his death in 1927. I grew up in Leola with
three brothers, Gottfried, Harold, and Allen. I graduated from Leola High
School in 1944 and soon thereafter I entered the Army Air Force. I was
discharged in August 1946 after foreign service in Guam, Taiwan, and the
Philippines.

I was married in 1945 to Wilma Wunner who came to Leola to work as deputy
County Superintendent of Schools after graduating from Eureka High School.
Wilma was born to Adam Wunner and Ida (Netzer) Wunner. Adam was courthouse
custodian as well as Deputy Sheriff until his retirement. He came to this
country direct from Bavaria, Germany as a young man.

After discharge from the service, I spent one year at Northern State College
after which we moved back to Leola where I was employed by Peavey Company.
Carol Hilgemann was born August 27, 1947 and is at this time teaching art in
Eilsen Air Force Base, Fairbanks, AK. In 1948 we went to Langdon, ND where I
managed a Peavey Lumberyard. We returned to Leola in 1949 where I managed the
Peavey Lumberyard. Julie Hilgemann was born June 30, 1953 and is presently
married to Roger Harmon and residing in North Platte, NE. Julie is an
elementary music teacher and Roger is an electrician.

        Roger and Julie Harmon, Ed, Wilma and Carol Hilgemann.

In 1955 I terminated employment at the Peavey Lumberyard and began working for
Hauck & Neuharth Insurance Agency. I purchased the Hauck & Neuharth Agency in
1961 and changed the name to Ed's Insurance Agency. I operated the agency until
January 1, 1972 when a merger took place with Knudson Insurance Agency. It
operated as Leola Insurance & Real Estate until March 8, 1983 when the
insurance part of the agency was sold. I continue to be active in the real
estate business.

I have been Veterans Service Officer for 35 years and also a member of the
Leola Fire Department for the same length of years. Through the years I have
held offices on the City Council, School Board, American Legion, Better Leola
Club, Country Club, St. James Lutheran Church, Development Corporation, and
Republican Party. Wilma also has been active in many of the community
activities such as Eastern Star, Legion Auxiliary, Disco Club, etc.

Becoming a rockhound through the years, Wilma established "Wilma's Museum &
Rock Shop." I enjoy making jewelry. (See history under Wilma's Museum.)

We like living in Leola where people are friendly, helpful, religious and hard
working. There is very little crime and lots of fresh air and sunshine. What
more could people ask for in life.

ERNEST W. and ELLA HILGEMANN

Ernest W. Hilgemann, the son of Friedrick and Wilhelmiena Hilgemann, was born
October 6, 1874, at Westphalen, Germany. He spent his early childhood there and
came to the U.S. in 1887 when only 13 years of age. He lived for a number of
years on a farm near Eureka with his uncle and aunt, Rev. and Mrs. Ulrich Reue.
He received his education in Eureka and during this time was employed in the
general merchandise business. He attended Business College in Minneapolis, MN
and in 1905 went to work as manager of a general merchandise store, the Artas
Union, in Artas, SD.

He met a young lady, Ella Ludwigs, who came from Milwaukee, WI to work for her
brother in the Artas Bank. He spent a year at Greenway, SD opening a store for
his employers and then in 1910 purchased the Johnstone Bros. Store in Leola. On
June 22nd of the same year he and Ella were married at Milwaukee. They made
their home in Leola and started the Leola Leader which he operated until
October 1959. His 49 years of operation was one of the longer business runs in
Leola's history.

E. W. was very active in civic and school affairs and was known to help those
in need. He is probably best remembered by the youngsters of the area for that
bag of candy treats when they accompanied their family to the "Leader" on a
Saturday shopping trip. The youngsters that span that 49 years of business are
still in evidence when the talk turns to "the old days" in Leola. Ernest passed
away in November of 1959 and Ella in June of 1965.

        The Ernest W. Hilgemann Family.

Ernest and Ella raised a family of four children. They were all at some time
involved with work in the store. They all attended school in Leola and were
graduates from high school there.

Gretchen became a Social Worker with degrees from Jamestown College and the
University of Minnesota. She retired in 1975 to Leola and passed away there on
May 8, 1983.

Ernest W. Jr., "Bud" was a graduate of the Law School at the University of
South Dakota and later of the Lutheran Seminary in Dubuque, IA. He served in
the Army in the European Theater during WWII. He married Priscilla Nelson in
1946. They made their home in Elgin, IA and raised five children. Bud passed
away from a heart attack in 1977.

Vera became a stenographer and secretary after graduation from Mankato Business
College. she worked in government offices in Pierre and Washington, DC. She
married Charles Estes in 1942 and they raised two children. Vera passed away in
October 1973.

William L. "Bill" attended Jamestown College and Northern State College. He
served in the Navy in the Pacific Theater during WWII. He married Eva Valentine
in 1946 at Minneapolis. After several years in the store business in Leola they
moved to Kalispell, MT where Bill worked for the U.S. Forest Service and for
Pacific Power and Light Co. for 17 years. They have three children and
presently live in Leola.

ERNEST and PRISCILLA HILGEMANN

Ernest William Hilgemann, Jr. was born at Leola, SD, on February 27, 1915, the
son of Ernest and Ella Hilgemann. Almost as soon as he was tall enough to see
over the counter, he was sharing responsibilities at the Leola Leader Store.
Many a lost art was learned there: adding without a calculator, conversing in
German, delivering groceries, candling eggs. The latter was least enjoyed,
occasionally eggs packed in oats were cracked, broken and messy.

Bud attended NSTC for two years, worked a year in the store, and graduated from
Jamestown College. After teaching, he studied law at the University of South
Dakota.

Returning to Leola, he managed an exchange branch of the Ipswich State Bank.
Setting up that office had some tense moments. Bill Feickert, Gilbert Miller,
and another man were moving the safe. Suddenly everyone disappeared through the
floor. When the dust settled, it was a great day of thanks, no one was hurt.

Nineteen forty-two to '45 were World War 11 years. For Bud it was the U.S. Army
in Africa, Sicily and Italy. He worked with the claims service.

Again Leola was home, and Bud set up a practice of law, serving as City
Attorney and McPherson County Attorney. Bud and Priscilla Nelson were married
in 1946. They met in 1940, when he cashed her teaching check. She also taught
the 1946 school year.

After purchasing an interest in a Clermont, IA bank in 1950, Iowa became home.
Later he studied at Wartburg Seminary and served a Nebraska church. In 1961 the
family returned to northeast Iowa. Five children and a busy law office kept
life interesting, eventful and rewarding. Finally retirement plans were taking
place. In 1978 Bud had a sudden fatal heart attack. Priscilla completed the
closing of the office, and continues to live in Elgin.

        The Ernest Hilgemann, Jr. Family.

The five children include: Karen of Dubuque, who works for Polk City
Directories; Robert of St. Louis, who is a computer analyst for Monsanto, his
wife Amy works for Social Services. Donald of Los Angeles works at UCLA's
Health Research Center, heart research; Marie of Brooklyn, NY works in theatre
arts, costume design, painting and dyeing; David of Cedar Falls, IA is Asst.
Coordinator for Operation Threshold, and his wife Sandy works at Station KUNI.

Leola holds fond memories. Trips to South Dakota were the highlights of the
year. All too soon, we had to say, "Auf Weidersehn."

FRED and KAROLINA HILGEMANN

Fred Hilgemann was born on September 22, 1867 in Lengerich, Westfalen, Germany
to Rudolph and Wilhelmina Hilgemann. He received his education from his parents
and school training in his home country before migrating to the United States.

In the year 1888, he came to this country and established residence by
homesteading in McPherson County north and a little east of Eureka. The first
`must' for existence was the building for shelter. Fred owned a pair of oxen, a
plow and a spade. With this type of equipment he, with the help of his
neighbors, erected a sod house and a barn built with stones and mud. In 1889 he
married Karolina Kasekamp who came to this country one year later than Fred.

        Fred & Karolina Hilgemann.

Fred became acquainted rapidly in the neighborhood. In a short time neighbors
and friends recognized the fact that he possessed many unusual abilities. They
consulted him often for advice. He was a man of sterling character and soon
became well known throughout the county. He was a most respected person in his
community.

Times were hard at the beginning. Cattle were scarce and horses were very rare
so the start was made with a team of oxen. Food products were raised in the
family garden for there was not much of anything else. Many times rabbits and
prairie chickens were delicacies as far as meat was concerned. After several
years cattle became more common and horses were acquired as land holdings
increased. A frame home was also built during the better years.

Along with economic hardships were the hard winters they all endured. Sometimes
their farm buildings were buried under the snow. One such occasion, after a
three-day blizzard, Fred had to shovel a tunnel through the snow in order to
get out of the house. While working, he heard a noise above him. Suddenly the
snowdrift broke and a man came plunging down. The visitor turned out to be his
uncle, the Rev. Mr. Reue, who had come to see how the Hilgemann family had
fared in the blizzard.

Fred was elected to county offices several times. He served four years as
School Superintendent, two years as County Commissioner and later, McPherson
County Treasurer. He also taught rural school for several years. In those days
the school districts had only three to four months of school. His first
teaching salary was $20 per month.

Fred and Karolina were the parents of ten children. Two of them, Gustav and
Calvin also held public offices. Gustav was elected Clerk of Courts in 1926 but
died in February, 1927, a few months after taking office. Calvin served many
years in county offices and became a State Legislator. (See C. C. history.)

Fred was not only an honest and aggressive office holder but also a devout
Christian in every respect and a loving family father. He passed away while
serving as McPherson County Treasurer on October 13. 1915.

WILLIAM L. and EVA HILGEMANN

William Ludwigs Hilgemann was born August 19, 1922 to Ernest W. and Ella
Hilgemann at the family home in Leola. As he grew up he developed a great love
for the outdoors and learned to hunt and fish at an early age. He felt starting
school each fall was a great imposition on these interests. Coming from a store
family he learned to know and love the people of the surrounding area.

He graduated from high school in 1940 and attended Jamestown College until he
enlisted in the U.S. Navy. He served in the Medical Service in the Pacific
Theater for 3 1/2 years.

In 1946 he was married to Eva Maxine Valentine. Eva was a graduate of Leola
High School in 1942 and later of Minneapolis Business College. They lived for a
time in Aberdeen and Leola and moved to Kalispell, MT where Bill worked for the
U.S. Forest Service and later as a Plant Superintendent for Pacific Power and
Light Co.

In 1971 they moved back to the midwest where they operated a hardware store at
Madison, MN. They are presently living at the family home in Leola.

        The William L. Hilgemann Family.

Bill and Eva have three children and one grandchild.

James William is a graduate of the University of Montana and lives at
Kalispell, MT.

Jane Eva is a graduate of Kinman Business University. She is married to Randy
Ehrismann and they have one son, Joshua Joel. They live in Sioux Falls, SD.

William "Joel" is a graduate of Brown Institute and S.D. State University. He

JULIUS and EMILIE HOEFT

Julius Hoeft was born February 13, 1869 in Germany. He spent his early life
there. In 1889 he came to the U.S.A. at the age of 20 and settled in the
Columbia, SD vicinity. On December I, 1896 he was united in marriage with
Emilie Jasmer at St. James Lutheran Church at Leola.

Emilie Jasmer was born October 4, 1874 at Winona, MN. Her parents were
Friedrich and Auguste (Gerth) Jasmer. Emilie Jasmer came to McPherson County,
Dakota Territory (Leola) with her parents, brothers and sisters in 1884, at the
age of ten. On April 2, 1889, she, along with the other members of the first
Confirmation class of St. James Lutheran Church of Leola, fled the fire that
destroyed most of Leola.

After their marriage they established their home near Columbia, SD. In 1901
they came to Leola and settled on a homestead southwest of Leola. In 1944 they
retired from the farm and moved to Leola. Mr. Hoeft died March 12, 1956 and
Mrs. Hoeft died April 14, 1945. They both are buried at Green Mound Cemetery at
Leola.

        The Julius Hoeft Family. Back: Walter, Frederick, August and Ernestina.
        Front: Clara, Julius, Viola, Emilie and Ella.

They were blessed with 11 children: Walter H. F. Hoeft, August C. Hoeft, Mrs.
Daniel (Ernestina A.) Schumack, Frederick H. Hoeft, Mrs. Ernest (Clara E.)
Bobier, Lena Hoeft, Arena Hoeft, Mrs. Arthur (Ella R.) Krein, Mrs. Clarence
(Viola A.) Jamser, and two who died in infancy.

WALTER and HANNAH HOEFT

'Walt' was born June 9, 1898 at Columbia, SD to Mr. and Mrs. Julius Hoeft. He
moved with his parents to a Leola farm in 1904.

Walter married Hannah Ferdinand October 15, 1925 and the couple farmed near
Leola for a few years. In 1928, the couple moved to Leola where Walt worked
where he was needed. In 1935 he took a job in the Farmer's Co-op elevator and
worked there until 1948 when he moved to Isabel where he managed an elevator.
Walt and Hannah moved back to Leola in 1949 when he accepted employment with
Leola City. Walt was Police Chief from 1949 until he retired in 1970. He was
Water Commissioner and Caretaker of the Cemetery for many years. In 1967 he
received citation from the Leola Legion honoring his outstanding service to his
community as a police officer. Walt has kept up his membership in the National
Peace Officer's Association.

Walter, Raymond, Hannah and Gerald Hoeft.

Hannah, who was born March 14, 1905 has served her community in many ways. She
began her career as cook in the Gene Kindelspire Cafe and continued cooking
when the cafe business changed hands. She had 14 bosses during her years of
cooking at various cafes and then worked five years in the Leola Hospital.
Hannah has many hobbies. Her excellent crocheting, quilt-making, cooking and
baking has made her one of Leola's most beloved citizens. Hannah is also known
for her beautiful flowers. In 1969 she won five blue ribbons in different
classes of flowers at the Town and Country flower show held in Leola, the grand
prize winner.

Hannah and Walt had three children: Raymond, born April 28, 1927; Gerald, born
October 20, 1932 and Arlen Wayne born and died at birth November 28, 1940. They
have six grandchildren, and seven great-grandchildren. Due to illness, Walt now
resides in the Colonial Manor of Ipswich, SD and Hannah still lives in Leola.
Both are members of St. Paul's Lutheran Church.

F. ALLEN and JANE HOFFMAN

Frank Allen Hoffman was born July 11, 1908, to Amos and Minnie Hoffman, nee
Fulker, at Leola, SD, where he grew up and graduated from high school.

Later he was associated with his father in the McPherson County Abstract
Company until his father's death in 1944, at which time Allen became the sole
manager of the business.

Allen served in the Navy during WWII. While in the service he married Jane
Ellen Mulligan at Great Lakes Naval Training Center, March 21, 1945. Jane, a
WAVE in the U.S. Navy, also served in the armed forces. Jane was born November
1, 1919, in St. Louis, MO.

After leaving the service, Jane and Allen built their first home in Leola,
living there until 1949, during which time they took an active part in all
community affairs. From Leola they moved to Minneapolis where they lived for
five years. During that time they had one son, James Allen, born January 30,
1951.

        Jimmy, Al and Jane Hoffman.

In 1954 they moved to Sarasota, FL, making their home there until the early
1960's when they moved to Palm Beach for a short time. While living in Florida,
Allen was engaged in the business of title insurance. At present Allen and Jane
are living in retirement at Ft. Lauderdale.

AMOS and MINNIE HOFFMAN

Amos Hoffman, one of the early native-born Americans to pioneer in this area,
was born September 9, 1869, on a farm in Clinton County, IN. In 1886 he came to
McPherson County, Dakota Territory, where he worked as a ranch hand for $75 a
year. A few years later he homesteaded about eight miles southeast of Leola. By
1892 he had established the first herd of shorthorn cattle in this area. In
1908 he sold his farm and equipment and moved into Leola, where he organized a
land and title company and later became the manager of the McPherson County
Abstract Company.

A few years prior to this time he had met Minnie Fulker, born in 1880 in
southern Ohio and who, as a young girl, had come to the Leola vicinity with her
parents to live. Amos and Minnie were married in June, 1907. To them was born
one child, a son, Frank Allen.

        Amos & Minnie Hoffman.

The Hoffmans belonged to The Methodist Church and to the Order of the Eastern
Star, Minnie having served as past matron. At one time Amos served as
worshipful master of Lodge No. 154, A.F.&A.M. His civic duties included serving
on the local school board and as justice of the peace. In 1926 he was elected
to the South Dakota State House of Representatives, and re-elected in 1928,
serving two terms. He was a member of the Board of Directors of each of the
following: Northwest Grain Growers Association, the Farmers' Elevator
Association, and the Equity Creamery (of Aberdeen).

Mr. Hoffman continued to operate the abstract business until his death,
November 25, 1944. Mrs. Hoffman resided in her home in Leola, active in church
and community affairs until her death, August 23, 1952.

in Leola. Albert was born November 5, 1932. He married Janice Pitkin of
Britton. They live on the homestead farm northwest of Leola.

DANIEL K. and HERTHA HOFFMAN

Daniel K. Hoffman was born April 16, 1912, in Hoffman Township. He was the
twelfth child of 13 born to Karl and Elizabeth (Lechner) Hoffman. His father
was born December 17, 1870, in Marienburg, South Russia, to John Hoffman. His
mother was born March 20, 1873, in Kassel, Odessa, Russia, to Nicklous and
Barbra (Heupel) Lechner. Since their father's name started with a "K" all 13
children have "K" as their middle initial. It identifies which branch of the
Hoffmans they are from.

His wife, Hertha, was born on October 9, 1914, in Bergdorf Township, to John B.
and Kathrina (Schnieder) Hoffman. Her father was born November 14, 1879, in
Bergdorf, South Russia, to Jacob and Christina (Lammle) Hoffman. Her mother was
born August 17, 1883, in Russia, to Peter and Katharina (Fuhrman) Schnieder.
Hertha grew up with a brother, Albert, who married Anna Hoff, and lives in
Lodi, CA; and a sister, Elsie (deceased), who married Fred K. Hoffman
(deceased), and lived in Sacramento, CA. Two brothers and two sisters died in
infancy.

        Hertha & Daniel K. Hoffman.

Daniel K. married Hertha Hoffman on October 16, 1934, at Eureka. Prior to his
marriage he farmed with his brother Fred. In 1939, Dan and Hertha purchased the
homestead farm and from that time on they continued to buy land from Dan's
brothers and sisters. Upon the death of Dan's father, Karl, the land had been
divided between his wife and the 12 surviving children.

While on the farm, they raised three children. The first, a daughter, Leone,
was born on April 7, 1938. She married Curtis Hoffman of Long Lake on October
16, 1957, at Leola. They are farming in Hoffman Township, about 16 miles
northwest of Leola. They have three children; Karley, Colette, and Carmen.

Wilton was born on July 18, 1946. He married Betty Lapka of Leola on November
7, 1969, at Leola. They own the homestead farm. It's about 15 miles northwest
of Leola. They have two children; Brett and Jolyn.

Gene C., an adopted son, was born on February 7, 1927. He married Della Voegle
of Long Lake on September 22, 1953, at Long Lake. They have four children;
LaDean, Wanda, Charlotte, and Angie. Gene died in a fishing accident at Leola
on August 23, 1977. Della married Marvin Ulmer on February 18, 1982, and lives
in Ellendale, ND.

In 1969 Dan and Hertha purchased and moved onto the Walter Ottenbacher farm,
which formerly was the Christ K. Hoffman farm. Due to some health problems, Dan
and Hertha sold the farm in 1972 to their son, Wilton. In 1973 they moved into
Leola, where Hertha still resides. Both are members of St. James Lutheran
Church. Dan continued to help on the farm until he died on October 23, 1981, of
a heart attack at the age of 69.

EMIL K. and ELIZABETH HOFFMAN

Karl and Elizabeth (Lechner) Hoffman gave birth to a son, Emil K., on February
19, 1908 in their homestead northwest of Leola in Hoffman Township. The Hoffman
family was large and when Emil was five years old his sister Elizabeth married
and he went to live with her.

For eight years he lived with Elizabeth and attended school north of Long Lake.

Emil returned to his grandfather's homestead and worked two years for his
oldest brother, Karl. Karl bought the homestead that was seven miles west, and
2 1/2 miles north of Leola.

Emil left Karl's and returned home to help his brothers, Fred and Dan, and
sister Ida.

In 1928 Emil bought eight head of registered Herefords from the Bill Hanks
ranch and this proved to be the beginning of the Hoffman Herefords.

Emil and Elizabeth Fauth were wed September 27, 1931.

Elizabeth Fauth was born February 13, 1914 to Jacob and Christina (Goehring)
Fauth.

They lived at the home place with Fred and Dan until March, 1933 when they
bought the permit to, and later purchased the Frost Ranch for $10 an acre. This
ranch was located five miles west and 1 1/2 miles north of Leola. This was
school land and was not deeded.

They began to build a house but since times were tough and dry and money short
they lived in the unfinished basement for five years before finishing the
house.

There was no hay to cut in 1934. Elizabeth raised 400 turkeys to sell to pay
for the new barn. Turkeys sold for as much as a cow. The first cow sold for
$7.50 or three-fourths of a cent/pound. The hip roof barn was finished in 1936;
more land was broken and in 1938 things were somewhat easier.

Two registered Hereford bull calves were sold for $12 to $18 to Fred Fischer
and Henry Schmidt of Long Lake.

Other livestock was shipped to Ames, IA and brought back in the spring.

The government bought many cattle paying $12-$20 for cows and $6-$8 for calves.
Trenches were dug and the cattle killed.

Three children were born: Gerald, born March 8, 1936; Marcella, born March 13,
1940; and Mary Ann, born September 6, 1942.

Marcella married Elmer Kaul on June 4, 1961 and moved to Bismarck, ND. There
were two children born: Jeffery and Karman.

        The Emil Hoffman Family.

Mary Ann married Richard Pitkin on September 3, 1962 and were the parents of
four children: Charles, Dana, Paul, and Ryan Lee (stillborn). After Richard's
death, Mary Ann remarried February 5, 1983 to Dennis Roehr.

Emil and Elizabeth belong to the St. James Lutheran Church. Emil was active as
a Sunday school teacher, township assessor for two years, and supervisor for 23
years. He is also a member of the Hereford Association and served eight years
on the hospital board. Elizabeth is a member of the Hereford Auxiliary and
Ladies aid.

In September 1981, they celebrated their 50th wedding anniversary and still
enjoy the good life they have together.

FREDERICK and MAGDALINA HOFFMAN

Frederick Hoffman was born January 6, 1865 to John Hoffman in Marienberg, South
Russia. He married Magdalina Schock in South Russia. She was the daughter of
George and Karolina (nee Kurle) Schock. Magdalina was born on November 22, 1864
in Bergdorf, South Russia. They left Russia to avoid the Russian Czar's empty
promises as well as serving in the Russian Army. They came to America November
1889 and purchased their first 160 acres (southeast of 6, 127, 68) in Hoffman
Township, 15 miles northwest of Leola on July 28, 1890 for $475. They later
acquired more land through the Homestead Act and for a time owned a total of
800 acres.

        The Frederick Hoffman Family. Back: Karl F., Fred F. and John F. Front:
        Frederick, Magdalina and Magdalina

Frederick was one of nine Charter members when Hope Lutheran Church was
organized on January 8, 1894 under the leadership of Pastor Martin Reichauer.
These members brought their Bibles, hymnals and sermon books from Germany and
Russia and conducted services in their homes until 1897 when a building was
bought in Aberdeen and moved to the site just south of the present Gary Hoffman
farm. In 1914, a new church was built one mile west in Hoffman Township, one
mile east of Frederick's farm. Frederick donated this land for the church site.
Not far from the church, he donated a portion of his land for a school, known
as Hoffman School District No. 1, which all the children in the area attended.
Their children were: Fred F., John F., and Mrs. John Fischer (Magdalina). His
wife Magdalina passed away May 26, 1930, at the age of 65, of cancer. Frederick
then married Katharina Ladner on November 9, 1931, who was born November 22,
1882 in Russia, and died October 24, 1965 at Eureka. Frederick passed away at
Leola August 31, 1950 at the age of 85.

FRED F. and ELISABETH HOFFMAN

Friedrich F. Hoffman (Fred), was born in Marienburg, South Russia, on January
10, 1889. He was the oldest son of Friedrich and Magdalina (Schock) Hoffman. At
the age of ten months he arrived at New York Harbor with his parents. They
traveled to the Long Lake area where his uncles, Johann, Christoph and
Christina Hoffman had already settled on farms. He grew to adulthood on his
parents' farm in Hoffman Township (the present Curtis Hoffman farm). He had two
brothers, John F. and Carl F., and one sister, Magdalina (Mrs. John Fischer).

        The Fred F. Hoffman Family.

Elisabeth Spitzer, was born in Harrison Township near Long Lake, on December
20, 1894. Her parents were Johann and Elisabetha (Streyle) Spitzer. Elisabeth
had three sisters: Christina (Mrs. Friedrich Feickert); Katherina (Mrs.
Gotthilf Pfeifle); and Eva (Mrs. Fred Wolff); and one brother, Jacob J.
Spitzer.

Fred F. and Elisabeth were married January 7, 1913. They resided on a 640-acre
farm in Harrison Township. There they raised eight children:

Herbert, born November 25, 1913, farms northeast of Long Lake.

Hilda (Mrs. Art C. Nitschke), born November 16, 1915.

Walter, born February 16, 1918, owner-operator of Standard Service & Bulk in
Leola.

Erwin, born February 24, 1920, farms northeast of Long Lake.

Werner, born January 21, 1922, farms near Wetonka.

Gerhard. born May 4, 1923, farms the homestead.

Lillian (Mrs. Richard Nitschke), born September 2 1924.

Violet (Mrs. Harry E. Hoffman), born September 26, 1928.

Fred F. helped improve the community. He served on the church council of Hope
Lutheran and as a County Commissioner for four years.

In 1948, Fred F. and Elisabeth decided to build a retirement home in Leola.
After three months in Leola, Fred passed away in August, 1948. Elisabeth
continued to make her home in Leola, where she did babysitting, took in
boarders and served as custodian for St. James Lutheran Church, where they were
members. Elisabeth passed away in September of 1968, following a short illness.

FRED K. and ELSIE HOFFMAN

Fred K. Hoffman was born February 1, 1910. He was the son of Karl and Elizabeth
(Lechner) Hoffman.

On June 15, 1933 he married Elsie Hoffman. She was born April 13, 1912. She was
the daughter of John B. and Kathryn (Schneider) Hoffman. She grew up on her
parents' farm about six miles west of Long Lake, SD.

        Fred K. & Elsie Hoffman.

After their marriage at Eureka, they lived on the farm his parents homesteaded,
15 miles northwest of Leola. They attended Hope Lutheran Church, rural, and
later they attended St. James Lutheran Church at Leola. In the fall of 1935,
they bought a farm five miles west of Leola from Valentine Lehr. They lived
there until it was diagnosed that Fred had multiple sclerosis. They rented the
farm for one year to a nephew and his wife, the Ernest Schocks, while they
moved to Aberdeen, as it became difficult for Fred to do the farm work. Elsie
was employed at the S & L Clothing Store as an alteration lady. Fred did not
enjoy being home alone while Elsie worked. So they sold their farm to his
brother, John K., for his son, Harry. Later, Harry Hoffman sold the farm to
Curtis and Arlene Job, who still live there.

Fred and Elsie sold their farm property at an auction and headed for Lodi, CA
where they purchased the Perman' U Motel which later became the Hoffman's U
Motel. In 1952 they sold this motel and purchased the St. Francis Motel at
Sacramento, CA. Here they lived until Elsie's death September 16, 1972. Fred
passed away nine days later, September 25, 1972. They had no children.

They are buried at Sacramento Memorial Mortuary Lawn, Broadway St., Sacramento,
CA.

GERALD and DOROTHY HOFFMAN

Gerald Hoffman was born at Leola March 14, 1936, and has spent his entire life

GERHARD and ELLA HOFFMAN

Gerhard Hoffman was born May 4, 1923 at the farm near Long Lake where he still
resides. He attended rural school.

On November 9, 1947 he married Ella Rau, daughter of John and Rosina Rau, who
was born and raised only three miles from the Hoffman farm. She was born on
August 9, 1928.

After their marriage they continued living on the family farm. They started
farming their 600 acre farm with a few cows and horses. The horses were the
source of power used for planting and haying. In 1950 or 1951 crops were poor
so part of the cow herd was sold to pay the farming expense for the year. In
1949 a tractor was added to supplement the horse power. A new tractor sized to
a 3-bottom plow at that time cost about $1,500. The milking and separating was
all done by hand for several years. In 1952 R.E.A. came in which made many
chores much easier. The minimum utility bill was about $6 a month.

A refrigerator was the first electric appliance they bought. That eliminated
the chore of running to the well to pull up a can which was hanging from a rope
lowered to near water level. That can contained meat, butter and any other
items that needed to be kept cool.

In 1954 they purchased the Rau farm, which was Ella's home place, and added it
to their farm.

        The Gerhard Hoffman Family.

Three children were born to this union: Kenny, born September 17, 1948, who
stayed on the farm until 1970. He married Lana Libis and is now living at
Bismarck, ND where he is employed with Wylie Piano Co. They have two children:
Ryan, age 11, and Darren, age eight.

Rodney, born November 20, 1954, is now a carpenter and lives in Long Lake. In
1982 he married Susan Abel and they now have an infant son Kyle.

Glen, born October 22, 1958, has chosen the farming profession and is still on
the family farm which he purchased in January, 1983.

HARLEY and SHARLENE HOFFMAN

HARRY E. and VIOLET HOFFMAN

Harry E. Hoffman, son of John K. and Christina (Rath) Hoffman was born in Arena
Township, near Leola, on February 13, 1925. He was engaged in farming with his
parents as he grew to adulthood.

Violet Hoffman, daughter of Fred F. and Elisabeth (Spitzer) Hoffman, was born
in Harrison Township, near Long Lake on September 26, 1928.

        Violet & Harry Hoffman.

Harry and Violet were married October 16, 1949. They purchased the Fred K. and
Elsie Hoffman farm located five miles west of Leola. Harry pursued his interest
in diversified farming, taking special pride in his Hereford cattle operation.
He served as a member of the Spring Township school board and of the Spring

In March 1971, for health reasons, they sold their farm to Curtis and Arlene
Job and moved to Leola. In March 1972 they moved to Jefferson, IA where they
currently own and operate a Coast to Coast Store.

JACOB C. and EVA HOFFMAN

Jacob C. Hoffman was born on February 20, 1902 to Christoph and Christina
(Schumacher) Hoffman. He was one of 13 children and grew up on a farm eight
miles southeast of Long Lake, SD in Hoffman Township.

Jacob's parents were both born in Russia. His father, along with several
cousins, came to America when he was 17 years of age. His mother came with her
parents at the age of 15. They homesteaded the land on which Gary Hoffman lives
today.

Being especially fond of horses, Jake was known to always ride a good saddle
horse. He remembers well, as a young lad, a certain cattle drive made by
himself and a cousin, Fred F. Hoffman. They had to deliver about 50 head of
two-year-old cattle to Forbes, ND, where they were to be shipped further by
train. They accomplished the cross-country drive in one day. They were more
than willing to ride back home in the buggy when their fathers came to pick
them up. Their ponies trailed behind the buggy.

On December 31, 1925, he was united in marriage to Eva Rath. She was the
daughter of John and Christina (Jesser) Rath. She was born on October 13, 1905
and was one of ten children. She grew up three miles southeast of Long Lake,
SD.

A house and barn were built 1 1/2 miles north of Jacob's homeplace and in July,
1926, they moved onto their new farm in Wacker Township. A well was dug a year
later. A 1925 green Ford was their first car.

        Marvin, Larry, Darlene, Eva and Jacob Hoffman.

On June 17, 1933 their daughter Darlene was born. She is married to Arvin Hauck
and they live on a farm near Forbes, ND.

Their first son, Marvin, was born November 5, 1934, is married to Marion Job
and they live on a farm near Leola.

A second son, Larry, was born May 28, 1946, and lives in Wichita, KS. He is
production control manager for Steffans Dairy Food Company.

In 1957 Jacob and Eva built a new home in Leola and are still living there.

JOHN K. and CHRISTINA HOFFMAN

John K. Hoffman, son of Karl Hoffman and Elizabeth (Lechner) Hoffman was born
April 16, 1899 in Hoffman Township (the present Wilton Hoffman farm). Christina
Rath was born in Highland Township, near Long Lake on March 27, 1901. She was
the daughter of John Rath and Christina (Jesser) Rath. John and Christina were
married March 15, 1923. They established a farm in Arena Township.

John's main interest was in purebred Hereford cattle and in diversified grain
farming. He was a pillar in building his community in that he served on many
committees. He was an early director of a local telephone company, served on
the governing board of the Leola Equity Exchange, the Green Mound Cemetery
Association, McPherson County Extension Board and was active in establishment
of the Leola Community Hospital. He was also active in Hope and St. James
Lutheran churches and was keenly interested in local, state and national
government.

        The John K. Hoffman Family. Back: Arthur, Clarence, Leo, Luther and
        Harry. Front: John K., Christina and Vera.

They had six children: Leo J., born December 30, 1923, is a farmer in Hoffman
Township northwest of Leola; Harry E., born February 13, 1925, is
owner-operator of the Coast to Coast Store in Jefferson, IA; Arthur, born May
5, 1926, is owner-operator of a photograph studio in Northfield, MN; Luther J.,
born December 1, 1930, is a farmer in Arena Township northwest of Leola (on the
John K. Hoffman homestead); Clarence, born August 7, 1933, has a real estate
and insurance agency in Charter Oak, IA; Vera (Job) born August 11, 1935, is a
retail sales clerk in Sisseton, SD. John and Christina built a new home and
moved to Leola in 1954. In spite of failing health, John took a keen interest
in his community until his death January 24, 1970. Christina is currently a
resident of Americana Health Care Center in Aberdeen, SD.

KARL and ELIZABETH HOFFMAN

Karl Hoffman was born on December 17, 1870, in Marienburg, South Russia, to
John (Johann) Hoffman. He came to America in April, 1890.

His wife Elizabeth was born on March 20, 1873, in Kassel, Odessa, Russia, to
Nicklous and Barbra (Heupel) Lechner. She came to America in 1884, at the age
of 11, with her parents. They settled in McPherson County.

        Elizabeth Hoffman.

Karl married Elizabeth Lechner on December 5, 1893, at Leola. The Rev. M.
Reischauer officiated at the ceremony. In 1900 Karl homesteaded in Hoffman
Township, McPherson County, on the SW 1/4 of 8, 127, 68.

During their lifetime, Karl and Elizabeth had 13 children. Since there were
several Hoffman families living in the area and they were related to each
other, the children were given the middle initial of their father's first name.
This was to help distinguish which family they came from. Karl and Elizabeth's
children were:

Elizabeth K. (Mrs. Christ B. Schock), Ellendale, ND, December 12, 1894.

Magdaline K. (Mrs. Karl K. Schock), May 30, 1896-September 2, 1971.

Karl K. (Margerita Rath), Leola, December 6, 1897.

John K. (Christina Rath), April 16, 1899-January 24, 1970.

Frieda K. (Mrs. Christ Voegle, Christ died and she remarried Henry Ohlhauser)
October 30, 1900-July 17, 1977.

Jacob K., February 16, 1902-1918.

Christ, died as an infant December 10, 1903.

Christ K. (Ida Bender), April 13, 1905-January 23, 1972.

Christina K. (Mrs. Christoph Schock), November 20, 1906-February 19, 1973.

Emil K. (Elizabeth Fauth), Leola, February 19, 1908.

Fred K. (Elsie Hoffman), February 1, 1910-September 25, 1972.

Daniel K. (Hertha Hoffman), April 16, 1912-October 23, 1981.

Ida K. (Mrs. Rudolph Haux), January 14, 1914-December 26, 1968.

All the children were born on the farm with the help of a midwife, Mrs. Jacob
Feickert.

At the time of his death on December 20, 1919, Karl had acquired 1,560 acres of
land. Because there was no will the land was divided between his wife and the
12 surviving children. Elizabeth continued to operate the farm until about
1929, when she moved to Leola. She remarried four times. Her last marriage was
to John Brunmaier in April, 1956. All her husbands preceded her in death. She
died February 16, 1961. Karl and Elizabeth were both members of the Lutheran
Church. The children who were still at home continued to run the farm until
1939. At that time Daniel K. and Hertha Hoffman bought the farm.

KARL F. and CAROLINA HOFFMAN

Karl F. Hoffman, youngest son of Frederick and Magdalina (Schock) Hoffman, was
born July 7, 1892 in Hoffman Township. He attended rural school and college at
Eureka for three years. On January 16, 1917, he married Christina Walth at
Leola. They took over the family farm when Karl's parents retired and moved to
Leola. They had one daughter, Wilma, born November 22, 1917. Christina died May
3, 1919 at the birth of their second child; the child died also.

Karl F. married Carolina Meier of Long Lake on November 11, 1919. Carolina was
born July 11, 1894.

        Karl F. & Carolina Hoffman.

Karl took pride in his 100 head of Shorthorn cattle. Having studied legumes in
college, he planted some of the first alfalfa in the area. He was active in
community affairs as well as conducting reading services at Hope Lutheran
Church until the time of his death. Karl and his pony were struck by lightning
on the hills east of the farm on June 16, 1932.

Carolina was left with eight children to raise. She continued to live on the
farm and raised her family there. Carolina passed away October 31, 1962.

The Hoffman children are as follows: Wilma, married to David C. Wolf on
September 30, 1935. She died August 24, 1940. Elmer was born September 13, 1920
and married Ruth Kapp. Elmer passed away June 9, 1982. Florence was born
December 12, 1921, married Albert Krege, and lives in Columbia, SD. Harold
(Harry), born August 14, 1923, married Doris Torguson and lives in Rapid City,
SD. Leslie was born April 22, 1925, married Virginia Jundt, and lives in
Brookings, SD. Milton was born October 11, 1927, married Evelyn DeForrest, and
lives in Frederick, SD. Alice, born October 21, 1929, married C. W. Huthison
and lives in Napa, CA. Curtis, born April 27, 1931, married Leone Hoffman.
Curtis lives on the family farm, 15 miles northwest of Leola, which was
homesteaded by his grandfather, Frederick Hoffman.

LEO J. and DELORES HOFFMAN

Leo J. Hoffman was born December 30, 1923, northwest of Leola, SD in Arena
Township to John K. and Christina (Rath) Hoffman. Leo grew up with four
brothers and one sister (see John K. Hoffman history). He attended rural school
and farmed with his family until he married Delores Schell on May 9, 1948. She
is the daughter of Christ and Frieda (Rueb) Schell.

Delores was born December 9, 1930, west of Leola in Moscow Township, where she
spent her growing years with three sisters and one brother. She attended rural
school. After marriage, she and Leo purchased and moved to the former Zenker
farm in Hoffman Township. This is still their home.

Leo and Delores have one son, Terry, born June 1, 1953. Terry married Mary
Fischer July 7, 1973 and they have one child, Michelle, born August 30, 1975.

Leo and Delores are members of St. James Lutheran Church in Leola where Leo
takes an active part in church affairs. He has been serving on the church
council and Delores has been teaching Sunday School for several years. She is a
member of A.L.C.W. also.

Leo has found time in his busy schedule to serve on the Highland school board,
cemetery board and has been on the township (Hoffman) board for several years.

LUTHER J. and DELORES HOFFMAN

The present Luther J. Hoffman farm was homesteaded by his father, John K.
Hoffman. Luther was born December 1, 1930 to John K. and Christina (Rath)
Hoffman. Luther has four brothers and one sister: Leo J. of Leola; Harry E. of

Delores Feickert was born December 28, 1936 near Long Lake to Jacob Jr. and

(Mrs. Elwood Lechner) who lives in Leola.

On November 21, 1954, Luther and Dorothy Delores were united in marriage.
Luther and Delores were blessed with five children: Marcia, born November 13,
1955, is a social worker at Veterans Hospital in Sioux Falls, SD; Sandra (Mrs.
Gary Rueb) was born January 21, 1957, she is director of nursing in a nursing
home in Circle, MT; Dale, born June 19, 1958, works for Production Credit
Association in Ivanhoe, MN; Jenny, born November 15, 1959, is a R.N. in Sioux
Falls, SD; Brian, born April 4, 1962, farms with his parents near Leola.

        The Luther Hoffman Family. Back: Marcia and Jenny. Front: Delores,
        Dale, Sandra, Brian and Luther.

Luther and Delores are members of St. James Lutheran Church. Luther and Delores
are also members of the American Legion and Town and Country Twirlers, a local
square dance club.

MARVIN L. and MARION HOFFMAN

Marvin Leo Hoffman was born November 5, 1934 to Jacob and Eva (Rath) Hoffman.
On September 25, 1956, he was united in marriage to Marion Job (daughter of
William and Bertha Opp Job). They farmed on Marvin's homeplace for nine years.
In 1965 they sold the farm to Deuwayne Hoffman and bought another farm from
Marcus Job in Leola Township. This is where they are presently living.

In 1970 Marvin received the McPherson County Conservation Farmer of the Year
Award. They are both members of the Trailriders Saddle Club and St. James
Lutheran Church.

        The Marvin Hoffman Family. Back: Marvin and Tony. Front: Wanita, Marion
        and Sharry.

They have two children. A daughter, Wanita, was born July 17, 1957. She

is employed as a secretary at the Wichita Osteopathic Hospital. She married
Richard Long of Newton, KS on September 13, 1980.

A son, Tony, was born September 13, 1961. He graduated from Leola High School
and Vocational School in Watertown, SD. He is employed as a mechanic at
Cantwell Equipment, Miller, SD. He married Sharry Ann Palmer of Miller, SD on
June 24, 1983.

MYLO and JENNETTE HOFFMAN

Mylo Hoffman, son of Christoph and Fredia (Gienger) Hoffman, was born in 1943
at his parents' farm north of Leola. After graduation from Leola High School
and earning a B.S. degree from Ellendale State College, he taught school in
North Dakota.

In 1969 he married Jennette Bendewald, daughter of the John Bendewalds of
Leola.

They lived in Aberdeen for five years while Mylo taught school and earned his
M.S. and Jennette earned her B.S. at Northern State College. In 1974 they moved
back to Leola with their two children and Mylo taught in the Leola school and
Jennette was a substitute teacher and gave piano lessons. Since 1980 they have
lived in Sisseton, SD where Mylo is grade school principal and Jennette teaches
at Peever. SD.

TERRY and MARY HOFFMAN

Terry L. Hoffman was born June 1, 1953 at Leola, SD to Leo J. Hoffman and
Delores (Schell) Hoffman. He attended Leola grade school and graduated from
Leola High School. After graduation, he worked with his father on the farm 11
miles northwest of Leola, SD.

On July 7, 1973 he was united in marriage to Mary A. Fischer, daughter of

Leola. She attended grade school in Long Lake and graduated from Leola High
School.

They are now making their home in Leola, where Terry is employed at the State
Highway Department. To this union one daughter was born August 30, 1975,

They are members of St. James Lutheran Church in Leola. Terry is a member of
the Leola Fire Department. Mary is a member of the Long Lake American Legion
Auxiliary.

WALTER and ELENORA HOFFMAN

Walter F. Hoffman was born on February 16, 1918 to Fred F. and Elisabeth
(Spitzer) Hoffman of Long Lake. Walter grew up on a farm northeast of Long Lake
with four brothers and three sisters. He attended country school in Harrison
Township. He farmed with his father until he entered the service in 1942.
Walter served during WWII and spent three years overseas. After his discharge
in 1945 he purchased some land near Wetonka and started farming.

Elenora Rau was born on July 21, 1922 to Fred and Emma (Ehresman) Rau at Long
Lake. She was the oldest in the family with three brothers and three sisters.
Elenora attended grade school in Wacker Township after which she helped out at
home until her marriage.

        Walter & Eleanor Hoffman.

Walter and Elenora were married on April 28, 1946 at Long Lake. Their parents'
farms were only about three miles apart so Walter didn't have far to drive for
his courting. After their marriage in the Hope Lutheran Church, they moved to
his farm nine miles east and one south of Leola, near Wetonka. They made their
home on this farm until 1979 when they sold the farm and moved to Leola. In
1980 Walter purchased the Standard Station and one year later also bought the
Standard Bulk Plant which he is presently managing.

They have two children, Bill of Leola and Marsha Ringler of California. They
have three grandchildren: Jared Hoffman and Heather and Amy Ringler.

Walter and Elenora are members of the St. James Lutheran Church.

WERNER and ELSIE HOFFMAN

Werner Hoffman was born to Fred F. and Elisabeth (Spitzer) Hoffman on January
21, 1922. He grew up near Long Lake where he attended rural school.

On May 18, 1947, Werner married Elsie Nitschke, daughter of Gottlieb C. and
Katherine (Heyd) Nitschke of Ashley, ND. They lived with Werner's parents until
fall, when they purchased a farm 12 miles east of Leola. They still live on
this farm.

Werner and Elsie are the parents of four children. Wayne married Sharon
Tollefson and they have two children. Wayne is farming with his parents.

Keith married Carol Redfield and they have two girls. Keith is shop foreman at

        Werner & Elsie Hoffman.
