live in Bristol where he is manager and vice president of First National Bank.

Evie, unmarried, lives in Aberdeen where she is office manager of Magic Carpet.

WILLIAM F. and SHEILA HOFFMAN

William Fred Hoffman was born February 10, 1953, at Rapid City to Walter and
Elenora (Rau) Hoffman. He graduated from Leola High School in 1971. Sheila Ann
Knapp was born October 5, 1953, at Eureka to Orville and Wilma (Opp) Knapp. She
graduated from Eureka High School in 1971. Bill and Sheila met August 13, 1971,
and were married May 18, 1974 at the Eureka Reformed Church in Eureka. They
lived at Brookings where both were students at SDSU, spending one summer in
Minneapolis, until their graduation in 1976. Bill received a B.S. in biology
and chemistry and Sheila received a B.S. in pharmacy.

        The William F. Hoffman Family.

After graduation they spent two years in Leola where Bill farmed with his dad
and later worked as a mechanic in Houghton. Sheila was employed at pharmacies
in Ipswich and Eureka. In 1978 they moved to Britton for a short time where
both were employed and later moved to Eureka. Bill continued work as a mechanic
and Sheila was employed in the pharmacies in Eureka. In 1979 they moved to
Glenside, PA, where Bill was a student for two years at Westminster Theological
Seminary in suburban Philadelphia. He also worked m the Seminary maintenance
department while a student. Sheila was employed in a pharmacy in Roslyn, PA,
and as an administrative assistant for FOCUS.

In September, 1980, they adopted their son, Jared Christopher, born March 17,
1980 at Ellsworth Air Force Base, SD.

In September 1981, they moved to Leola and began operation of Hoffman Parts &
Service, an implement and repair shop formerly owned by Leo and Vi Smolnisky.
Bill and Sheila both work in the business. Sheila also continues pharmacy work
mainly at Heilman Drug and Eureka Rexall Drug, both in Eureka.

They attend the Leola and Eureka Reformed churches. Bill is vice president of
the 4-H Expansion Council.

WILTON and BETTY HOFFMAN

Wilton Hoffman was born on July 18, 1946, at Aberdeen. He is the son of Daniel
K. and Hertha (Hoffman) Hoffman of Leola. Wilton grew up on and farms the
original homestead of his grandparents, Karl and Elizabeth (Lechner) Hoffman,
in Hoffman Township.

Wilton's wife, Betty Ann, is the daughter of Francis J. and Althea (Glaser)
Lapka of Leola. She was born on January 16, 1951, at Aberdeen. She comes from a
family of eight children. She graduated from Leola High School in 1969.

After attending grade school one-half mile from his home in Hoffman Township,
Wilton graduated from Leola High School in 1964. From December 1965 to
September 1967 he served in the United States Army and was stationed in
Kirch-gons, Germany. After his discharge he returned home to farm with his
father.

Wilton and Betty Lapka were married on November 7, 1969 at Leola. They
continued to live on his parents' farm. Dan and Hertha moved onto an adjoining
farm, purchased in 1969 from Walter Ottenbacher and which formerly was the
Christ K. Hoffman farm. In 1972 Wilton and Betty purchased the farm and in 1973
Dan and Hertha moved to Leola. They have two children. Wilton is a member of
St. James Lutheran Church and Betty is a member of Our Lady of Perpetual Help
Catholic Church in Leola.

On April 12, 1970, a son, Brett Travis, was born at Aberdeen. The arrival of
Brett wasn't the only big thing that year. In May a fire destroyed a granary
with a basement and some feed and seed. A new shop-granary and a basement pole
barn were built to replace the granary.

        The Wilton Hoffman Family.

A daughter, Jolyn Sue, was born on January 1, 1974, at Aberdeen. She was the
first baby born for the New Year. Ten minutes and one second favored her
arrival over the second baby born. Not to be outdone by her brother, Jolyn's
year was also one to be remembered. In July the big hip roof barn burned. The
barn was being used for hogs. It was farrowing time and over 100 head of hogs,
sows and their litters, died in the fire. With the help of a lot of relatives
and neighbors, a new large pole barn was built.

In December 1979, while Wilton and Betty were gone, the shop caught on fire.
Luckily, due partly to the fact no children were born that year, it did not
destroy the entire building. Only the roof and some equipment and a
three-wheeler Honda ATC had to be replaced. To date there isn't an original
building left on the farm. Due to storms or fire, each generation has replaced
some buildings; and some have been replaced twice since the farm was originally
homesteaded.

Wilton and Betty still maintain a herd of registered Polled Hereford cattle
that Daniel K. and Hertha started in 1948. Cross breeding is also used. They
also raise feeder pigs in a continuous farrowing operation. The farm is now
known as Hoffman Farms, Inc.

JOHN V. and KATHERINE HOHMAN

John V. Hohman came to South Dakota at age 21 from Harrietsville, OH. He taught
school in Ohio and came west to homestead and continue teaching. Later he went
to work in the Mitchell Lumber Co. of Leola. He was part owner and manager of
the hardware and lumber company. He became the first to use the title of Mayor
of Leola.

        Katherine & John V. Hohman.

Around 1907 he married Katherine Lapka who was born about 1884 in Cleveland,
OH. She was brought to South Dakota when she was one year old. She spent her
entire life, after coming to Dakota, near and in Leola.

In 1922 John and Katherine went farming north of Leola.

Children of the Hohman family are: Francis (deceased), and Althea (Chittick) of
Nalcrest, FL.

John and Katherine were members of the Catholic Church in Leola.

JOHN E. and FRANCES HORD

John E. Hord was born October 3, 1876 in Auville, MO to John and Alice William
(Hanley) Hord. Alice received her middle name from her mother who wanted a boy
to name after her husband who was killed in the Civil War.

Frances Clara Kelly was born August 3, 1873 in Jacksonville, IL to William and
Catherine (McGuire) Kelly.

John and Frances were married February 6, 1901 in Denton, NE. In 1910 John
arrived on an immigrant train to Wetonka, SD. Frances came on a passenger train
with Mary Alice, born in 1903, John William, born in 1905, and Paul Gilbert,
born in 1908. They arrived in Wetonka at the same time because John's train was
waylaid in a small town along the way. They loaded their furniture on two
wagons with two teams of horses. The family had to travel through roads that
were only tracks and creeks to a farm which they purchased, 11 miles northeast
of Wetonka.

        John E. & Francis C. Hord.

On May 1, 1911, a baby girl, Kathryn was born. On February 27, 1914, another
daughter, Margaret, was born. They lived in the Wetonka area for ten years. In
the summer of 1920 they bought a farm 9 1/2 miles north of Leola, where they
moved to in October of that year.

On July 9, 1933, Paul drowned in the Sacramento River in California. He left
South Dakota because of lack of jobs during the depression. He was 25 when he
died. On October 8, 1934, Frances died from cancer. In May 1938, Mary and John
moved to Leola. On November 13, 1939, John died from Hodgekins disease. J. W.
(Bill) married Maude Witte and lives in Keokuk, IA. Katherine married Don
Kindelspire February 9, 1932. She is now living in Phoenix with Mary. Margaret
married Byron Kindelspire on January 17, 1940. She lives in Leola.

JACOB and LORETTA HUBER

Jacob Hubers moved to Leola from the Hosmer area in the spring of 1937. He was
employed by the John Kulm garage. Throughout the years, Jake worked for W.P.A.,
McPherson County, Ed's Produce Station, Rueb's Chevrolet Garage and Independent
Elevator Co. Jake managed the Elevator for 15 years (1953-1968) retiring
because of ill health. During this time Jacob and his wife owned and operated
the Knudson Hotel. In 1970, they sold the hotel and moved to Aberdeen.

Loretta has been an energetic part of the Huber team, for she began working
soon after they moved to Leola. She worked in her brother's produce station
part-time. Later, when her brother opened a grocery store, Loretta worked
full-time. When they were in the hotel business, Loretta was the manager. In
1970 she began employment at Presentation College in Aberdeen, where she has
worked for 14 years.

Jake and Loretta have three children: Jerald, who is Superintendent of Schools
at Marshall, MN. His wife Ruth is a mail carrier. They have three children,
Mark, Kristin and Ann.

Bob teaches and coaches in Milbank, SD. His wife Carole also teaches. They have
one son, Robby.

Sheila works for Lutheran Social Services in Aberdeen. Her husband, Milo, is
running a milk farm. They have no children.

Jake and Loretta are members of the Congregational Church in Aberdeen, where
Loretta is a deaconess and a member of the church circle.

JOHN and CATHERINA JACOBER

John Jacob Jacober was born May 7, 1857. In 1883 he was united in marriage with
Catherina Krenzler, who was born August 25, 1860. John, his wife, and three
daughters immigrated to America from Gluckstal, S. Russia in 1889. John had a
shoe shop in Russia. His sister, Mrs. Christian (Freda) Freftzg, who came to
South Dakota several years before settled at Tolstoy, SD. She wrote to John and
his wife, in Russia that there was land that could be claimed in South Dakota
by homesteading.

After their arrival due to water problems in Tolstoy, they decided to move.
John walked to McPherson County and back again to look things over. At this
time he had to stay out on the prairie in the rain while traveling on foot.
They moved to McPherson County about 1890 and homesteaded ten miles west and
two miles south of Leola. They later moved about two miles north of this farm
and eventually bought more land. Their first homes were built of sod. A well
was dug by hand and water was drawn from the well with a bucket on a rope.

John and Catherina raised 11 children. One girl died in infancy. The three
oldest girls were born in Russia and eight children were born in South Dakota.
Mary married Christ Maier. Catherina married Jacob Dufloth and Elizabeth
married Carl Walter.

        Catherina & John Jacober.

John married Louise Bitzer and are living in Monroe, WA.

Rosina never married. She lives in Broadview, IL.

Louise married Dan Capen and lives in Harrah, OK.

        Emma & Dave Jacober.

David never married. He farmed southwest of Leola until 1951, when he moved to
town. He continued to farm until his retirement and for the past 3 1/2 years
worked at Walt's Standard Station. He was a member of the Leola Senior Citizens
and their choir. He was the church janitor until his death November 21, 1983.

Ida married George Cook and lives in Seattle, WA.

Emma never married. She lives in Leola and is member of the Seventh-Day
Adventist Church.

Anna married John Bitzer and lives in Berrien Springs, MI.

Mary; Catherine; Elizabeth; John and Christina are deceased.

Their parents, John Jacob died May 1, 1931. Catherina died August 7, 1925.

CHRIST and ANNA JAKOBER

Christ Jakober is one of 12 children (one died in infancy) born to Jacob and
Katherina (Vilhauer) Jakober. Christ was born April 10, 1910, on a farm where
the family first homesteaded, in McPherson County. In 1918, he moved with his
parents to a farm in Moscow Township, 18 miles west of Leola. Christ's mother
passed away in 1925. In 1926, his father was united in marriage with Johanna
Mutschall, a widow with eight children. Together the couple had 19 children.
All of the children attended country grade school and worked at home or for
neighboring farmers, helping to support the large family. At age 20 each child
was given a calf for their work. Christ left home at age 20. He began working
for Gross Brothers, earning $20 a month, which was top summer wages. In the
winter time wages were $5 to $10 per month.

On March 31, 1935 Christ was united in marriage with Anna Neuharth. Anna was
born April 11, 1911 to Henry and Mary (Kessler) Neuharth. The Neuharths lived
on a homestead in Arena Township, 15 miles northwest of Leola. That is where
Anna, three brothers and five sisters attended school.

Because of the drought in 1935, Christ and Anna went threshing with Anna doing
the cooking, and Christ worked for various farmers for $35 a month. They worked
for Lars Herseth at Houghton, SD, for a short time. They then returned to this
area and worked throughout the harvest season, for $50 a month. For seven years
they managed the Doc Hoven ranch, now the Ordway Conservancy, receiving shares
and interest in the livestock instead of a salary. Christ also worked during
W.P.A. days, building roads. He also dug a trench to bury water line for ten
cents a running foot (all manual labor).

In 1942, Christ and Anna purchased a farm in Dewey Township, southwest of
Leola. Christ bought the tenant's share of oats for 13 cents a bushel in the
bin.

Farming, dairying, raising livestock and poultry was their livelihood.

        The Christ Jakober Family. Back: Agnes, Glenn and Charles. Front: Anna
        and Christ.

Three children were born to this union: Agnes married Rudy Wageman. They have
four children and live in Portland, OR.

Glen is married and they have a son and live in Aberdeen, SD.

Charles lives in Aberdeen.

Since 1958 Christ and Anna have lived in Leola and still have cattle. They
delivered milk and cream in town until 1964; Christ did carpentry work and Anna
worked at the school cafeteria.

They are members of St. James Lutheran Church.

JACOB and ELIZABETH JAKOBER

Jacob Jakober Jr. was born June 10, 1907 rural Hosmer, SD to Jacob Sr. and his
wife, Katherina Vilhauer.

Parents of Jacob Sr. were Friederick and Christina (Albrecht) Jakober. Parents
of Katherina were Fred and Sophia (Hieb) Vilhauer.

Jacob Jr. and Elizabeth Mutschall were married December 4, 1927. Elizabeth was
born July 10, 1908 in Tschalid, Russia to Heinrick and Johanna (Aberle)
Mutschall. She came to America with her parents by ship in 1910. They lived on
a farm at Linton, ND. Later they moved to a farm near Trail City, SD.

Jacob and Elizabeth are the parents of four children.

        The Jacob Jakober Family.

Mrs. Allen (Virginia) Liedle was born in 1929 and lives in Rapid City.

Verlin--(refer to Verlin Jakober history).

Mrs. Lee (Evelyn) Layton was born in 1941 and is a LHS graduate. (See Lee
Layton family history.)

Mrs. Michael (Eunice) Howard was born in 1947 and lives in Rapid City.

There are 11 grandchildren and seven great-grandchildren.

Jacob and Elizabeth farmed about ten miles west of Leola until 1957 and in 1958
moved to Leola. In 1964 Jacob took over the operation of hauling freight; until
train service was discontinued in Leola.

Jacob and Elizabeth are active members of the Senior Citizens organization.
They deliver meals twice a week to shut-ins. The meals are prepared at the
Senior Citizens Center in Leola. They like to travel and a trip to Israel in
1976 was most enjoyable. They are members of St. James Lutheran Church.

FRIEDRICH and AUGUSTE JASMER

Friedrich Jasmer was born January 12, 1830 in Brofke, Germany. He was married
to Auguste Gerth in Germany, in 1855. Auguste was born March 3, 1837 at
Nichorsch in West Prussia, Germany. They lived in Germany until 1872 when they
immigrated to America, settling near Winona, MN where he farmed and was a
blacksmith. They moved to McPherson County in 1884 to do pioneer work. He filed
a receipt on October 15, 1884, covering the SE 1/4 of Section 35, Twp. 126,
Range 68, located in Spring Township.

Mr. Jasmer was the first elder of St. James Lutheran Church of Leola and also a
charter member when it was organized on July 10, 1887. He died November 11,
1910 and Mrs. Jasmer died March 19, 1923. They are buried at Green Mound
cemetery, near Leola.

ANTON and KITTIE JESSEN

Anton (Tony) Jessen was born January 15, 1883 to Bahne and Hanna Dorothea Meier
Jessen at their farm home in Marshall County, IA. Bahne came to this country
from Denmark in 1873. In 1875 his betrothed and her family arrived at Lyons, IA
and they were married there. Anton was one of six children.

In 1908 Anton worked in the Leola area and in 1909 he bought land southeast of
Leola. In the spring of 1911 he worked with the Koepenick crew breaking sod
northeast of Leola and helped Kittie Hanks around the outfit. On December 24,
1913, Tony and Kittie were married at the Hanks home. Theo made their first
home in a cook car on his farm southeast of Leola while Tony built their house.

One experience of Kittie's has always fascinated her grandchildren. Her father,
Will Hanks, asked Kittie to take a team of driving horses hitched to a
one-seated buggy and travel to Leola for groceries for her mother. After
purchasing her supplies they were packed in the buggy. The 100-pound sack of
sugar placed at her feet and the other groceries piled around her, Kittie
started for her parents' home. She had just passed the Woodall place when the
buggy wheel went into a hole in the trail. Unable to brace herself with the
sugar at her feet, she was thrown out causing the horses to bolt and the rear
wheel of the buggy went over her. The frightened team ran for home. Kittie knew
her mother would be terrified when the team came in without her so she hurried
back to the William Woodall farm where Mrs. Woodall called Mrs. Hanks and
William had their son, Lawrence, hitch up a team and take Kittie home. The
doctor from Forbes was called and he discovered that she had broken several
ribs.

Kittie and Anton's first son, William Anton, was born November 19, 1916. He
died March 25, 1917. His was one of the first graves in Green Mound Cemetery.

        Anton, Kittie, Joe and Dee Jessen.

Anton traded their farm for one closer to the Hanks place and their son Joseph
Elmore was born there on August 1, 1918. The Jessens moved to St. Paul, MN in
1920 where they bought a farm at the edge of west St. Paul. Anna Dorothea
Jessen was born March 17, 1929 at St. Paul. Anna shortened her name to "Dee" as
soon as she could talk.

When Will Hanks, Kittie's father, was critically injured the Jessen family
returned to Leola to help the family out. They left Leola in March of 1932 and
lived 2 1/2 years at Aberdeen and later in Milbank, SD.

Joe Jessen married Anna Schneck July 4, 1942. He served in the Army's 12th
Armored Division in Europe during WWII. Joe and Anna had one son, Donald Duane,
born December 10, 1947. They are presently living in Kingman, AZ. They have two
granddaughters.

Dee Jessen married Wilbur Warnick November 20, 1948. Following the death of
Wilbur's father they returned from Rapid City to help his mother with the
ranch. They bought the Stugelmeyer place two miles north of the Warnick Ranch
and lived there until the summer of 1955. Kittie and Anton Jessen were frequent
visitors and enjoyed their grandchildren and renewing old friendships in the
area.

Anton Jessen died March 26, 1968 at his home in Milbank. Kittie lived alone
until May of 1980 when she entered the Whetstone Valley Nursing Home at Milbank
at the age of 91. She died August 3, 1982. They are buried in their family lot
in Green Mound Cemetery with Kittie's parents and their baby son. They were
devout Christians and seldom missed church services for over 60 years. Kittie
belonged to Extension Club for over 50 years and was active in the W.C.T.U.

LUDWIG and ROSINA JOB

Ludwig Job left Russia at the age of 21 as a stowaway on a ship and arrived in
Canada in 1880 where he worked on a farm in Alberta for a year. His parents and
brothers came to South Dakota a year later where they homesteaded near Hosmer.
Ludwig then joined the family. He married Rosina Kranzler in 1882. The Kranzler
family had homesteaded in the Hosmer area. Dry years and poor crops
necessitated outside work; and to supplement the family's income Rosina worked
as a waitress in an Ipswich Cafe for 50 cents per week. After their marriage
Ludwig and Rosina lived on their own farm near Hosmer where their children were
born. In 1907 they purchased a farm from Karl Maier (15 miles southwest of
Leola) where they lived until their retirement in 1924. Upon retirement they
purchased a house in Leola where they lived until their time of death.

        Ludwig & Rosina Job Homestead.

WILLIAM and BERTHA JOB

William Job was born to Ludwig and Rosina (Kranzler) Job on a farm near Hosmer,
SD. William married Bertha Opp of Eureka, SD on December 23, 1923. Bertha is
the daughter of John and Elizabeth (Neuharth) Opp. Upon his marriage William
took over the operation of the farm, having received six horses and some farm
machinery from his parents. Bertha received nine cows, a few ducks and geese
and some furniture as her endowment from her parents. From this meager
beginning they bought land, farmed it, milked their cows by hand and raised
their five children. Horses were William's special pride and joy and most all
farm work was done with horses until the tractor took over much of the labor.

Their early years of marriage included some prosperous years, followed by the
bank failure and depression of the '30s, worsened by drought and well problems.
Despite the difficulties, the family survived and thrived partly due to hard
work and frugal living. Church services were not missed unless roads were
impassable or illness in the family. Playing baseball and horseshoes provided
recreation from the hard work. Music played an important part in the family--a
piano, guitar and harmonica were always present. The whole family gathering
around the piano and singing is a pleasant memory and continues even now at
family gatherings.

Farming conditions improved in the 1940's and in 1952 William realized a
long-held dream when they bought a farm on the west edge of Leola, presently
the Marvin Hoffman farm. In 1956 they retired from farming and moved to Leola.
They are active in church activities and in the Senior Citizen organization.
Their love of music still prevails as they are faithful members of the Senior
Citizens chorus.

        The William & Bertha Job Family.

Eight children were born to the couple, three died at birth. They have 14
grandchildren and six great-grandchildren at this writing. The children are:
Selma, married to Arnold Lapp, resides in Eureka; Marcus, married to Marcella
Will, lives near Underwood, MN; Ruth, married Leroy Ganser, lives in Sunnyside,
WA; Marion, married to Marvin Hoffman, resides in Leola; Rosina, married Harry
Hilgemann and lives in Rapid City, SD.

LEOLA HAYNES JONES

It all started back in 1978. A casual remark made by my mother, that in the
state of South Dakota, 20 miles north, 20 miles west of Aberdeen, lay nestled a
small farming community and in this community is a small town called Leola.
This town was named after my paternal grandmother, Leola Haynes Jones. You can
imagine the excitement that I felt when I heard of this.

        Leola (Haynes) Jones.

Leola was born April 8, 1879, in Menominee, MI to Capt. Edwin D. and Caroline
Haynes. Capt. Haynes was a surveyor and surveyed the town May, 1883. In
appreciation of his work, the town was named Leola, after Capt. Haynes' young
daughter and also the town's first girl.

When Leola was a small child and came into town, the townspeople would pick her
up and swing her around and call her "Little Mother."

Leola lived here until around the age of 12, with her parents, and two
brothers, Albert and William.

She married Thomas C. Jones, an electrical engineer with the U.S. Army. He
passed away in 1913, at the age of 42. He had three military funerals. (1) Ft.
Howard, MD; (2) deck of boat going from Ft. Howard to Hampton, VA; (3) Hampton,
VA. At place of burial he received three volleys and three taps.

They had three children. Cornelius, (my father) deceased; Mildred, of Winter
Haven, FL; and Winton, of Baltimore, MD.

Cornelius married Lillian McEwan, 1922. They had two children: Betty Champagne
Porter, of Leola, and Cornelius, Jr., "Hank", of Minooka, IL. Mildred married
B. A. Tyree in 1919. They had one daughter, Alice, deceased. Winton married
Virginia Beck in 1928. They had three children: Wayne, of Berwick, PA; Nancy
(Mrs. Wm.) Borgerding; and Peggy (Mrs. Maurice) Howard, both of Baltimore.

All three of Leola's children had the privilege of celebrating their 50th-plus
wedding anniversaries.

Leola passed away in 1942, at the age of 62, in Maryland.

There is a stained glass window above the front door of the Camp Chapel
Methodist Church, in Perry Hall, MD in Leola's memory.

        Frank & Betty (Jones) Porter.

I am Leola's first granddaughter. My husband, Frank, my mother and I had the
opportunity of coming to Leola, in August 1982 and purchased a home here. In
October, 1982, Frank, my son, Kevin and I left Michigan and made Leola our
permanent home. Frank passed away November 13, 1983.

History has a strange way of repeating itself. Leola left Michigan to come to
South Dakota and almost 100 years later I left Michigan to come to South
Dakota. In June of 1934, at the age of 55, Leola and her mother returned here
for the 50th Anniversary, and now 50 years later and at the age of 55, I will
be here for the celebration of the Centennial.

Two things are still in evidence here. They are: (1) the land that our home is
on belonged to my great grandfather, Capt. Edwin D. Haynes, and (2) Capt.
Haynes surveyed a plat of land and donated it to the town, which is now Green
Mound Cemetery, 1 1/2 miles south on Highway 45, in 1889.

FRED and ROSE JUNDT

Fred was one of ten children born to Jacob and Catherina (Krangler) Jundt. He
was born in McPherson County on their farm on August 22, 1899. Jacob and
Catherina both came to America from Russia. Fred's mother died when he was only
seven. He lost his father when he was 12. Fred remained on the family farm with
his older brother Henry. Fred hired out to other farmers to help out
financially.

On November 27, 1923 he was married to Rose Mayer. Rose was born to Jacob and
Carolina (Hieb) Mayer on February 1, 1901 on their farm 17 miles southwest of
Leola. Rose had six brothers and six sisters. Her parents came to America from
Russia in the early 1880's. They settled on a farm. Rose did much of the
household chores and milking. She attended school in Blaine Township until the
fifth grade when it became necessary for her to stay home and take care of her
younger brother.

Fred and Rose received eight cows, two horses and a pig from her father as a
wedding gift. Fred's oldest sister, Christina, gave them 100 chickens. With
these gifts, they started their married life on Fred's home farm and lived
there for five years, then bought state land one mile south and started a new
farm and lived there for the next 21 years.

They shared their home with Fred's brother Jake, who lived with them for 15
years. His brother, John, and his family lived there for five years.

"Barn dances" helped pay for the new barn Fred had built on his farm. Rose told
about the night someone threw a match into the hay. Fred quickly jumped into
the burning area and extinguished the fire.

In 1949 the Jundts bought a farm south of town (now occupied by the Darrell
Yost family). They bought another farm west of Leola so they could graze
cattle. They retired and moved to Leola in 1978.

Fred and Rose were both injured in a car accident in 1981. They spent some time
in the hospital and nursing home in Aberdeen. They returned to their home in
August 1981, where they reside at present.

        The Fred Jundt Family.

Fred and Rose were the parents of five children: Agnes Jundt Swanson--(see Sid
J. Swanson, Jr. history).

Eelila was born February 11, 1931. She married Frederick R. Landy March 25,
1958. To this union were born Matthew Brite and Kathleen Eelila. The Landys
reside in Woodridge, NJ and are part of a family catering business.

Larry James was born June 1, 1939. He was united in marriage with Myrna Olsen
on July 23, 1966. Their daughter Syndee Kay was born in Sidney, Australia.
Myrna and Larry reside at Custer, SD. Myrna is a teacher and Larry farms near
Oral, SD.

ADAM and ESTHER JUNG

Adam Jung was born February 20, 1903 near Hosmer. He attended rural school
there. His parents Jacob and Dorothy (Hottman) Jung were married in Russia in
1882. They came to America with three children and arrived in Eureka in the
fall of 1889.

Jacob made his way by foot to Jamestown, ND, where he found work. He came back
to South Dakota about a year later and established a homestead for his family
14 miles east of Hosmer. Here they built the customary sod home and barn. They
later sold this farm and started another about five miles east of Hosmer in
1908. Here they built a home and barn of lumber.

Jacob died in 1941, Dorothy in 1923. They were the parents of 11 children; only
David and Walter are still living.

On March 19, 1929 at Hosmer, Adam Jung was united in marriage with Esther
Gutjahr. Esther was born September 4, 1909 to Christian and Katherina (Kessler)
Gutjahr at Hosmer, SD. She grew up with two sisters, Katherina and Lydia; four
brothers, John, Christian, Edwin and George. Lydia and George are deceased.
Esther's parents were married in Russia in 1896. They and one child immigrated
to America from Gluckstal, South Russia in 1898. Christian Gutjahr was born
April 9, 1870. Katherina was born July 8, 1874. She died January 23, 1927 at
Hosmer. The family homesteaded 5 1/2 miles southeast of Hosmer. All the
children were raised on this farm. Christian retired and moved into Hosmer in
1929, where he died November 18, 1936.

        The Adam Jung Family.

Esther and Adam Jung were the parents of two sons, Raymond was born November
25, 1929 and Delbert November 29, 1932, both born at Hosmer. Raymond, 20, lost
his life in the Korean War. He had served his country about a year. Delbert
served in the Air Force for about four years in California and Texas. He
married Sandra Barbara Norheim of California, at St. James Lutheran Church in
Leola on May 29, 1957 and returned to California. They reside in Lancaster.

Delbert and Sandra are the parents of two children: Timothy and Kathleen.

Esther and Adam moved to Leola in September 1944. Adam died. Esther is a member
of the St. James Lutheran Church of Leola and is a Gold Star mother.

SAMUEL and MARTHA JUNG

Samuel (Sam) Jung was born near Hosmer, SD, July 8, 1907 to Christian and
Kathrina (Guthmiller) Jung. He came from a family of 13 children.

His parents came from Russia and settled in the Hosmer area.

Sam married Martha Grischkowsky August 1934. She was born in Hosmer September
28, 1914 to John and Kathrina (Schuler) Grischkowsky. Her parents also came
from Russia with a family of three children. She came from a family of 12
children.

        Martha & Sam Jung.

Sam and Martha farmed for nine years on a farm southeast of Hosmer. In October,
1943, they moved to a farm five miles southwest of Leola.

A son, James, was born to them. He now lives in Seattle, WA. He married June
Strout and they have three children. Their daughter, Marleen, married James
Layton and resides in Coon Rapids, MN. They have two children.

Sam died in January 1980.

FRIEDRICH and BARBARA JUNGE

Friedrich Junge was born in Germany and came to America in 1848. Barbara
Barnardy Junge was born in Luxemburg, Germany and came to America in 1846. They
were married in 1855 and lived in Michigan until 1885 and then moved to
McPherson County to get land through the Homestead Act.

They first lived on land west of the courthouse, then they moved to land in
Arena Township. The younger children grew up there. Later they moved to Leola
and lived with their daughter, Phrene.

        The Friedrich Junge Family.

The Junge family had nine children, five sons, who were: Fred, Albert, Jake,
Frank and Xavier. They had four daughters, who were: Carolina Haynes, Phrene
Junge, Barbara Morrison and Adeline Schlenker.

When Leola was getting started, Albert, Fred and Xavier worked at businesses of
their own. Frank was the postmaster of Leola for a number of years. Jake lived
on a farm west of Leola with his family. Barbara Morrison and Adeline Schlenker
lived with their families on farms in Arena Township. Caroline Haynes spent her
later life in Virginia. Phrene worked for many years at the county courthouse.

Friedrich Junge was one of the first Representatives in the South Dakota
government in Pierre.

PHRENE JUNGE

Phrene Junge was born to Friedrich and Barbara Junge in Michigan, and came with
her family to McPherson County in 1885. She grew up in Leola and lived with her
parents.

        Phrene Junge.

As an adult she held many positions both on the city and county level. She
worked at the First State Bank when John Hepperle was president. She worked in
the Leola Post Office from 1914 to 1920. She also worked as secretary to the
County Treasurer, the Auditor, and the Register of Deeds. Later in life she was
elected County Treasurer of McPherson County and served there for many years.

She also spent some of her life out of Leola. She lived a number of years in
Norfolk, VA with her sister Caroline Haynes, and she later spent several years
in California with her brother Fred and his family. She then moved back to
Leola. She passed away in Leola after a short illness.

She was a devoted member of the First Methodist Church. She was a willing
worker in a number of community organizations. Her friendly charm and
helpfulness made her an outstanding citizen, and she is remembered by many.

ALVIN and NANCY KALLAS

Alvin Eugene Kallas, son of Paul and Agnes (Geffre) Kallas, was born in Leola
in 1941. He and his two brothers, Gerald and Donald, and his sister, Arlene,
all attended the Leola Public Schools. After Alvin's graduation he spent six
months in the National Guard. In 1961 he started farming.

        The Alvin Kallas Family.

In 1967 he married Nancy Lee Rawstern, daughter of Elias and Bernice (Dickey)
Rawstern. Nancy is a graduate of Central High School and Aberdeen School of
Commerce. Alvin and Nancy have five children, Michael, Melissa, Mary, Carrie
and Amy.

Alvin and Nancy are beef, dairy and grain farmers and members of the Catholic
Church.

DOMINIC and DOROTHY KALLAS

Dominic Kallas, youngest son of John and Cecilia Kallas, grew up on his
parents' homestead in Carl Township. He entered the Armed Services in 1942,
serving with the 102nd Infantry Division in Europe. After his discharge in 1946
he farmed with his brother Leo.

Dorothy, daughter of Philipina and Nick Kline, was born in Wacker Township and
grew up in Carl Township, where she attended country school. She was employed
at the Leola Hospital for several years, and then worked at St. Joseph Mercy
Hospital, Mason City, IA.

        The Dominic Kallas Family.

Dominic and Dorothy were married in 1956 at Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church
in Leola, with Father Marvin Macmahon officiating. They have three daughters,
LaDonna (Mrs. Bob Leibrich) now in Hartington, NE; Bernadette, an LPN in
Witchita, KS; and Sheila, at home. Their six sons, Michael, Kevin, Anthony,
Mark, and Jason live at home except for Gabriel, who lives in Thermopolis, WY.

Dominic is Clerk of Carl Township, a member of the Parish Board and the
American Legion and a past 4-H Club leader. Dorothy is a member of St. Teresa
Altar Society, the American Legion Auxiliary, teaches CCD and is certified
Emergency Medical Technician.

JOHN and CECILIA KALLAS

John Kallas was born in Tushel, Germany in 1867. He was about 20 years old when
he came to Cleveland, OH to stay with his sister. He worked there one year
before he came to McPherson County to join his brother Julius. Here he
fulfilled his dream of owning land by filing on a quarter in Township 127.

        The John Kallas Family.

In 1901 he married Cecilia Hartman, who had come to America with her brother
from Odessa, Russia, at St. Hyacinth in Koto Township. They had seven children:
Mary (Sister Crispiniana), St. Rose Convent, LaCrosse, WI; Elizabeth (Mrs. Al
Ruther), Groton, SD; Margaret (Mrs. Joe Mumm), Staples, MN; Regina (Sister
Beatrice), Presentation Convent, Aberdeen, SD; Bertha (Mrs. Clifford
Klapperick), Conde, SD; Leo, Aberdeen, SD and Dominic, Leola.

John added 400 acres of land to the original homestead which he and Cecilia
farmed until 1944, when they purchased a home in Leola. John died in 1950,
Cecilia in 1965.

JULIUS and SOPHIA KALLAS

Julius Kallas was born in Germany in 1855 and after completing his army service
there, he came to the U.S. to file on a tree claim in Carl Township. In 1884 he
married Sophia Schmaglenski, who was born in Poland, had come to the U.S. with
her three sisters. They lived in a sod shanty, until Julius built the first
wooden home in the township. He had walked from the claim to Aberdeen to get
the deed to his land.

Julius and Sophia had 12 children, two of whom died in infancy. Joe (1887),
John (1889), Martha (1891), Rose (1893), Anna (1897), Francis (1899), Paul
(1901), Clara (1903), Alex (1905) and Vincent (1907) all grew up in the area.
Joe, John, Martha, Paul and Anna have died.

        Sophia & Julius Kallas.

Francis and Clara joined religious orders early in life. Francis, Sister
Anicetus, belongs to the Dominican Order and taught school for 55 years and now
lives in Dubuque, IA. Clara, Sister Leona, who became a registered nurse, lives
in Aberdeen, SD. Rose is a resident of Mother Joseph Manor in Aberdeen.

Alex and Vincent operated a cattle ranch, where they raised a little bit of
everything until 1975, when they moved into Leola. They remember well when the
family bought their first Model T in 1919. Their older brother drove it out
from Leola, and all his brothers and sisters rushed out to meet him. They
remember too, the fun that barn dances were when they were all growing up. They
spend their time now in visiting their brothers and sisters, and hunting and
fishing.

Julius died in 1926; Sophia in 1955.

PAUL and AGNES KALLAS

Paul Joseph Kallas, son of Julius and Sophia Schmaglenski Kallas, was born in
Leola in 1901. He lived on the home place until 1940, when he married Agnes
Geffre (daughter of Jacob and Barbara Pfeiffer Geffre of Leola) and purchased a
farm northeast of Leola.

Paul and Agnes had four children: Alvin, Gerald, Donald and Arlene; all of whom
are married and all except Alvin have moved away from Leola. Paul and Agnes
have 17 grandchildren.

In 1978 Paul's health began to fail, so they sold their farm to Alvin and moved
to Leola. Paul died in 1979. Agnes is active in the community; a member of St.
Anne's Altar Society, the Bible Study Club, and Senior Citizens.

VICTOR and JUNE KAMM

June later met and married Victor Kamm. He was the son of Fred Kamm and the

June and Victor were married June 21, 1941 and lived in the Wetonka area until

JACOB and LYDIA KAPP

Jacob Kapp was born in Odessa, Russia January 18, 1892. He came to America at
the age of nine years. He and his parents had settled in the Eureka area and
later moved to a homestead seven miles north of Ashley, ND. Jacob died October
17, 1963.

Lydia (Gohl) Kapp was born in Odessa, Russia November 17, 1897. At the age of

the Eureka area and lived there until her marriage.

        Lydia & Jacob Kapp.

resided until 1959 when they moved to Leola.

Jacob and Lydia were blessed with nine children:

ERWIN and OLIVIA KAUL

The Erwin Kaul family grew up in the Ashley, ND area. Erwin and Olivia were
married in 1945. They moved to a farm northeast of Ashley. The land they were
farming had hills and rocks, so in 1951 they decided to look for better farm
ground.

Erwin's parents, the John Kauls, moved to Leola in 1945 and liked the area.
Erwin's father decided to sell his land to Erwin and moved to Leola. Erwin and
Olivia lived on the farm until 1972 when they decided to sell the farm and move
to Leola.

        The Erwin Kaul Farm.

Handicapped in Aberdeen.

and Talie Kaul.

JACOB and ERNA KAUL

Jacob Kaul was born October 14, 1897 at Gluckstal, South Russia. He and his

was employed as a farm laborer in the Ashley and Eureka areas.

        Erna & Jacob Kaul.

In February 1942, the Kaul family moved to the Leola area, having purchased a

JOHN and ROSE KAUL

John Kaul was born in Prussia in 1893. He came to the United States when he was

John married Rose Strobel in 1934. Rose was born in North Dakota in 1903. They

Athens, OH; and Rose Sabers, Rock Valley, IA. They continued to live on the

moved into Leola with the four younger children.

They were members of St. James Lutheran Church. They enjoyed attending school
activities that their children participated in.

Rose died in 1979. John sold his home and moved to the Ashley Nursing Home.
John is 90 years old and still enjoys fairly good health.

ARTHUR and LUCIE KIESZ

Arthur Kiesz, (b. 8-10-14) and Lucie Strand (b. 2-19-16) were married in 1937.
They made their home in Leola until 1962, when they moved to Lodi, CA. Their
children are: Phyllis, married to F. Carl Bruhn in 1959. They have two
children, Gregory and Steven.

Robert, married Nancy Bayne in 1976. They have a daughter, Christina. All live
near Lodi, CA.

Arthur's parents were Jacob and Christina Kiesz. Jacob was born in Glueckstal,
South Russia, in 1890. At age eight, his father died. He, his mother, six
brothers and sisters, immigrated to America, McPherson County, settling on a
homestead near Long Lake.

Jacob and Christina were married in 1913. They lived on a farm until they moved
to Leola in 1919. During their first years in Leola, Jacob worked as a mechanic
in a garage, and as electrician and electric light plant operator for the city,
until he purchased a service station which he operated with his two sons, for
25 years.

        The Arthur Kiesz Service Station.

Christina's parents, Christian and Carolina (Schnabel-Maule) Hoffman, both born
in Russia, arrived in 1888. Christian died December 28, 1934; Carolina January
28, 1954, nearly 96 years of age. Jacob and Christina's children were: Arthur
and Reuben. Reuben married Esther Seaton. Their children are Janet, Nancy and
Dale. They live in Moorhead, MN.

Christina, age 89, December 19, 1982, had resided at the Bowdle Nursing Home.
She passed away August 8, 1983. Her sister Frieda and brother Theodore, also
reside at the Bowdle Nursing Home.

Lucie's parents were Henry J. Strand and Chlora Payne. Henry's parents came to
the United States from Norway and to Brown County in 1878 where they farmed on
the state line. The farm still belongs to the Strand family. Henry's parents
were Syvert E. and Helen Strand. Henry and Chlora's children are: Harold,
Lucie, Leona Jones, and Dorothy Jean Hansen.

Chlora was a teacher before her marriage and they farmed for many years.
Chlora's parents were Benjamin M. and Lucy Ann (Graham) Payne. Mr. Payne was
born in Virginia in 1856. He married Lucy Ann Graham in 1879. She was born in
Indiana in 1861. They came to Frederick by train. They then traveled west with
horses and wagon, settling in Carl Township in 1886. They retired from the farm
in 1918, having sold the farm to son-in-law Lou Henry, married to Leila. They
and their son, then their grandson, lived on the farm for many years.

ART and MYRTLE KINDELSPIRE

Art Kindelspire, born May 1, 1908 at Spencer, IA, moved with his parents,
Stephan and Jenny Kindelspire, to Montevideo, MN. The family moved many times
before settling on the Frank Barnard ranch, about ten miles north and two miles
east of Leola, SD. Art grew up on the farm with his brothers, George and Don;
two sisters, Bessie and Grace. He attended school and helped with the farming.

Myrtle Neff was born March 27, 1907, about eight miles west of Frederick, SD.
Her parents lived in the Elm River flat and put up a new set of buildings south
of the "old" place. Myrtle had three brothers, Emery, Lloyd and Clyde and two
sisters, Olive and Eva.

Myrtle is a graduate of Frederick High School and Aberdeen Business College.
She was a secretary in the Aberdeen Business College office for a while.

Myrtle's grandparents, William and Mattie Mann, came to South Dakota in 1882
and settled on a claim about ten miles west of Frederick, SD. This site was
about one-half mile west of the Brown County line in McPherson County. William
Mann came to Pennsylvania from Holland. He was a drummer boy and fought in the
Civil War on the Union side. He was in the famous Andersonville prison and
nearly died there. He worked his way back north after release from prison. He
worked at the Satterwhite home near Lexington, KY, and married Mattie
Satterwhite. They lived at Sheldon, IL, then moved to Missouri before coming to
South Dakota. They had four children: John, Robert, Luella and Alverda.

Art and Myrtle were married December 9, 1929 at Redfield, SD. Their first home
was on the old "Mulligan" ranch up in the hill country and they were called the
"Hillbillies." They lived on different farms and finally bought the Albert
Morrison farm, where they lived until moving to Leola in 1975.

        Janette, Bob, Faye, Art and Myrtle Kindelspire.

They are the parents of three children: Janette, born May 5, 1932, married
Melvin Zenker. They had two children, Sheryl and Gary.

Robert (Bob) was born August 26, 1938. He married Arlene Kraft. The couple had
four children: Mark, Brian, Pamela and Keri.

Faye, born September 10, 1945, married Harvey Gisi They had two children, Julie
and Rodney. Harvey died May 6, 1968. Faye later married Donald Kallas. They
have two sons, Dean and Bradley. Janette, Bob and Faye are Leola High School
graduates.

In the spring of 1981 the Art Kindelspires moved to Aberdeen, where Art is

CLINTON and VIRGINIA KINDELSPIRE

Clinton Kindelspire, the son of George and Laura Kindelspire was born November
13, 1915 in Montevideo, MN. He moved many times with his parents before they
settled on the farm called "Midway Stock Farm," northeast of Leola, SD. He
married Virginia Ganser in Leola June 5, 1942. They have spent all their
married life on the farm. Clinton has enjoyed the modern farming in comparison
to the "horsepower" of the '30s. Clinton has been on the Weber Township board
for many years.

Virginia was born March 1, 1916 on the Ganser farm six miles northeast of
Leola. She graduated from Leola High School in 1934 and attended Northern State
College in Aberdeen, where she obtained a certificate to teach country school.
She taught eight years; five of those years in Koto School No. 1, 16 to 18
pupils filled the one-room schoolhouse, having pupils in all grades one through
eight. She walked to school many times; kindled the coal stove and then waited
an hour for the room to warm up.

The salary at the highest was $150 a month. A county superintendent supervised
the rural schools at that time.

        Virginia & Clinton Kindelspire.

born in 1942, attended Weber School eight years. He spent four years in the

Kindelspire farms of Forbes, ND.

Anliker of Forbes, ND in 1968. She has two children, Deron and Kari.

Mavis, born in 1955, married Wayne Breitag in 1974. She attended Stewart School
of Hairstyling, is employed at the Classic in Aberdeen. She has two sons, Aaron
and Joshua.

GEORGE and LAURA KINDELSPIRE

George was born at Dickens, IA to J. S. and Mary Jane (Evans) Kindelspire on
June 6, 1891. He attended school at Lake Center, IA, where he graduated from
Lake Township Consolidated High School. In 1910, he moved with his parents to
Montevideo, MN where he attended Windom College for two years.

Laura M. Mills was born August 25, 1894 near Montevideo, to Benjamin W. and
Elizabeth (Herm) Mills. She attended country grade school and also Windom
College at Montevideo.

On January 1, 1914 George and Laura were united in marriage at the home of her
parents, near Montevideo. A train trip to Ipswich, SD, began their two week
honeymoon where they visited at the ranch home of the Matt Kindelspires. They
met them at the train with a team of horses and sled and went cross country in
the snow, as there were no fences at that time.

The family moved many times. In 1915 they moved to Montevideo, where George was
engaged in the furniture business. Two years later they moved to Raleigh, ND,
where he tried farming the rocky land, which wasn't very profitable, and also
did the town deliveries with horses and wagon. He had a paige touring car to
transport salesmen and their trunks of wares from McIntosh to Bismarck, ND to
catch the ferry. The family moved back to South Dakota where they tried farming
for several years. In 1926 the family moved to Hudson, WI where George was
engaged in the Chevrolet car and garage business. The company could not supply
enough cars for the demand. In the fall of 1927, George moved his family back
to South Dakota. They located on a farm 12 miles northeast of Leola where they
settled to raise their family. The children attended country school at Weber
No. I through the eighth grade. In the winter time Lloyd, Clinton and Byron
attended Normal Industrial School in Ellendale, where they took up woodworking.

Wayne and Deloris graduated from Leola High School. During these years a
neighbor boy, Eddie Malmstrom, made his home with the Kindelspire family. He
attended Weber School No. 1 and graduated from Leola High School. He and his
wife live in Sun City, AZ, where he is retired.

While living in Hudson, WI, Laura found time to take an infant into her home;
the child's mother had died at childbirth. The child was later adopted by a
Lutheran minister and his wife.

        George & Laura Kindelspire.

George and Laura were the parents of five children: Lloyd, born October 1,
1914, married Vera Bain on October 6, 1937. They farmed before purchasing the
LaMoure Hotel from Tom Heibel. Lloyd died August 9, 1968. Their children are:
Mrs. Don (Judy) Sanford, Anchorage, AK; Mrs. Les (Jane) Fischer, Portland, OR;
Del, of LaMoure, married Debbie Koehlerand; Mrs. Louis (Ava) Holub, Verona, ND.

Wayne, born June 20, 1919 married Kathryn Schneidler of St. Charles, MO on
March 11, 1944. He retired from McDonald Aircraft Corp . in 1981. Their
children are: Mrs. Ken (Audrey) Clancy, Greenbay, WI; David, in the service at
Virginia Beach, VA; Mrs. Gordon (Julie) Brokaw, Potosi, MO; Mrs. Bob (Betsy)
Schreiter; and Tony Kindelspire of St. Charles, MO.

Clinton, Byron and Mrs. Lloyd (Deloris) Bain, are included in the histories of
their families.

Laura belonged to the country club for several years.

Special moments for the Kindelspires are spent visiting with their children, 22
grandchildren, and 46 great-grandchildren.

George and Laura celebrated their 69th wedding anniversary on January 1, 1983.

EUGENE and LILLIAN KINDELSPIRE

Eugene (Gene) was born November 30, 1906, to Matt and Elizabeth Kindelspire,
nee Sunderland, at Spencer, IA. He moved with his parents to South Dakota where
he was engaged in ranching for several years. In 1933 he married Lillian
Hepperle, born May 13, 1909, to John and Anna Hepperle of Leola.

        Lillian & Eugene Kindelspire.

Gene managed the Leola Cafe for a number of years until 1943, when he joined
the Army in WWII. Later on he was employed by the South Dakota State Highway
Department until his retirement in 1970. In 1973 he became a school bus driver,
which continued through the school year of 1982-83.

Lillian received a B.S. degree from the University of South Dakota and an M.S.
degree from Northern State College. Other than the one year she taught in St.
Lawrence High School (when Gene was in the Army) her teaching career of 35
years was centered in the Leola area in rural, elementary and high school. In
1957 she developed the library in the Leola schools and served as librarian
until her retirement in 1971.

The Kindelspires belong to the St. James Lutheran Church. Lillian is a member
of the A.L.C.W. and is also a volunteer church librarian. She is a member of
the American Legion Auxiliary and an honorary member of Disco Club. Gene is a
member of the American Legion and of the Sportsman's Club.

Their son Larry (Duke) enlisted in the Navy shortly after graduating from LHS
in 1951. He is a veteran of the Korean War. After serving his hitch, he settled
in Los Angeles where he married Mary Jane Snicks in 1963. They have two
children, Donald and Heather Gene. Duke is a crane operator.

MATT and ELIZABETH KINDELSPIRE

Matt Kindelspire, an enterprising rancher, contributed much to the growth of
McPherson County. He was born October 3, 1879 to Simon and Roxanne Kindelspire.
He married Elizabeth (Libby) Sunderland December 28, 1898. She was the daughter
of George and Ida Sunderland, born July 17, 1879. All lived at Spencer, IA.

In 1902 the Kindelspires moved to South Dakota and eventually settled in Dewey
Township on the Morris and Davis ranch, which became better known as the Matt
Kindelspire ranch, 16 miles southwest of Leola. Later they also bought a farm 4
1/2 miles south of Leola. It was here in 1924 they built a barn 64 by 100
feet--the home of the well-known weekly Kindelspire barn dances of the
mid-1920's. Exceptional orchestras, including such entertainers as Lawrence
Welk, attracted many from nearby towns. The barn is still in use at the Dave
Rath farm.

The first school of Dewey Township was organized in 1912 at the request of Matt
Kindelspire, who was one of the first officers. One of the houses on the ranch
was converted to a schoolhouse. Nina Lile was one of the first teachers at this
school. The pupils were the Strudle, the Jundt, and the Kindelspire children.

At their ranch in 1917 the Kindelspires had a cement reservoir built on a hill
to provide running water for the household and the livestock. Windmills pumped
the water uphill, and gravity flow brought it down again through pipes to the
desired points of the house and the barns.

        The Matt Kindelspire Family. Back: Viola, Gene and Estella. Front:
        Matt and Elizabeth.

Three children were born to the Kindelspires: Estella (Mrs. Freeman Nelson),
Viola (Mrs. Arnold Nelson) and Eugene (Gene).

Mrs. Kindelspire was a member of the United Methodist Church and of the
W.S.C.S. She was also a charter member of the Agricola Club.

Mr. Kindelspire died in 1953, and Mrs. Kindelspire in 1962.

JACOB and EMMA KIRSCHMAN

Jacob Jr., (Jake) was born August 23, 1912, to Jacob Sr., born May 22, 1889 and
Kathren (Kaul) Kirschman, born March 18, 1891. He grew up on a farm six miles
southeast of Ashley, ND, where his parents, sisters Lydia, Rose, Kathern, Anna;
and brothers Johnnie, Edward, George, Herbert and Ervin had homesteaded. Their
mother passed away March 25, 1925. The father passed away September 11, 1954.

Jake completed school through the eighth grade. He stayed on the farm until his
father sold out and moved to Ashley.

Jake came to McPherson County in 1930, working as a hired hand, often for board
and room.

On October 12, 1941, he was united in marriage to Emma, the daughter of Fred
and Louise (Dohn) Loebs. Emma was born March 31, 1915. She grew up on a farm 11
miles northeast of Eureka, where her parents, sisters, Mrs. Oscar (Ladena)
Ketterling, of LaMoure, ND and Violet (now deceased) had homesteaded.

Jacob and Emma bought the farm from her parents and farmed for themselves until
1959. They sold the farm and moved to Leola in 1960. Jake went to work for
Wesley Rueb, hauling cream to market. In 1964, Jake went to work for Lloyd
Bain, at Bain Produce. Vincent Geffre bought the station in 1974. Jake is still
employed. Since 1975, Emma has been employed at the Leola Bakery.

        The Lake Kirschman Family. Back: Jake, Raymond and Shelby. Front:
        Emma, Tyson and Myla.

A daughter, Shelby Jean, was born at Eureka on September 24, 1944. Shelby was
married on August 5, 1965 to Raymond, the son of Robert and Emma (Roehl)
Johnson. He was born May 21, 1941. They are the parents of Myla Rae, born June
1, 1969 and Tyson Eric, born July 21, 1972. Raymond bought the farm from his
parents. His father is deceased, his mother lives in her house on their farm.
Jacob and Emma are members of the Leola Baptist Church, where Jake has served
as treasurer for a number of years.

CLARENCE and ESTHER KNUDSON

Clarence and Esther Knudson were married in 1938. They bought the Elk Hotel in
Leola and renamed it the "Knudson Hotel."

On April 1, 1940, Clarence became manager of the Branch Bank in Leola. He
became cashier of the newly organized Leola State Bank in 1944, later becoming
the bank's president. He also managed an insurance agency and did some farming.

The Leola sale barn was built in 1949. Partners in the venture were George
Geffre, Roy Stover and Clarence Knudson, each had a third interest therein.

Mrs. Knudson taught rural area school and also in Leola. She also taught
private piano for about 30 years.

        Esther & Clarence Knudson.

Their son Craig was born in 1940. Craig is President of the Heritage Leasing
Co., at San Diego, CA.

AUGUST and FREIDA KOERNER

Leola always was home for Freida and August Koerner. Their parents were Russian
immigrants, who homesteaded in McPherson County in the year 1885.

August was born October 27, 1892 at Eureka and Freida on February 3, 1895 near
Long Lake. They grew up on the family farm. In those days farming was hard work
and long hours. They were married on December 16, 1913. His father started them
in the Agri-business with two quarters of farmland, three miles west of Leola.
To begin with, they built a barn and a granary (grain storage building). They
lived in the granary for several years. Crops were good for them so in 1921
they built a new home.

        Freida & August Koerner.

Raising grain, livestock and milking was their livelihood. Freida raised many
chickens, which she would often dress and sell to people at the low price of
five for one dollar. That, along with eggs at 16 cents a dozen and a five
gallon can of cream, would buy the groceries for one week.

After several years they saved enough money to buy a Dodge Coupe. It was a
luxury in those days. Never having driven a car before, one day Freida got into
the car, started it and put it in gear. She shouted to the children and a
neighbor, "Stand back, it's going to go, but I don't know in which direction."
That was long before Drivers Education. During their 60 years on the farm they
employed very little hired help. Freida was the "hired man," everything they
did, they did together.

August died suddenly on July 5, 1973. Freida decided to give up the farm. She
sold in the fall of the year, and moved into Leola. She died in September 1981.

They were the parents of three daughters: Della, born September 3, 1916,
resides in San Francisco, CA. Eileen Nickerson, born January 1922, lives in
Aberdeen, SD . Sonja Bailey, born January 17, 1938, lives in Long Beach, CA.

HERBERT and MAYME KOERNER

Herbert and Mayme Koerner moved to Leola from Eureka in 1934 when Herbert
became a steady employee of McPherson County Highway Department. Herbert was
born February 25, 1906 to Karl and Bertha Koerner, Eureka, SD.

        Herbert & Mayme Koerner.

Mayme was born March 17, 1908 to Sievert and Anna Lee, Aberdeen, SD. Mayme
attended Northern State College and taught country schools around the Eureka
and Leola area. She met Herbert during this time and they were married January
11, 1929. They made their home in Eureka for four years. Herbert worked for
McPherson County until 1940 when he became foreman of the State Highway crew.
He was known to be an extremely hard worker, often working throughout the night
opening the snow-packed highways. In the summer and fall of each year Herbert
and his crew spent many hours putting up snow fences in the farmer's fields
along the highway, preparing for the hard winters that were expected. According
to the family, "There was hardly a day he returned home from work before dark.
" He was accidentally asphyxiated in March of 1948. Mayme remained in Leola
where she was employed by the Hauck-Neuharth Abstract Company, later as a clerk
in the Register of Deeds office and in March, 1953 she became Deputy Auditor
(McPherson County) serving until December 1954. In 1954 she remarried and moved
to Aberdeen. She now resides in Minneapolis, MN.

Their children are: Doris (Jones) born March 8, 1930, died May 20, 1983;
Virginia (Breitag), born March 9, 1932; Keith, born September 3, 1937 and Avis
(Moore), born April 12, 1947. There are 14 grandchildren and six
great-grandchildren.
