EMIL and ADELINE KOLB

The first record of the Kolb family in the Leola area was the immigration of
Fredrick and Margaret (Oster) Kolb and five sons from Gluckstal, South Russia
to the US in 1906. The five sons were Karl, Jacob (father of Emil), Gottlieb
(father of Adeline), Christ and John Kolb.

Jacob Kolb was born November 1884 in Gluckstal South Russia. He married Lydia
Rau, daughter of Christian and Christiana (Weller) Rau, on December 30, 1909 at
Hosmer, SD. Jacob and Lydia farmed in the Timber Lake area before returning to
the Long Lake and Leola area to farm.

They lived on a farm south of Long Lake, SD. The remains of the farm can still
be seen while driving on the Long Lake road south of Long Lake. They later
moved to the Hanks farm north of Leola which is now the Gordon Mack farm.

They were the parents of five sons and six daughters: Martha (Mrs. Richard
Singer), deceased; Arthur, Eureka, SD; Emil, Leola, SD; Leo, deceased; Gust,
deceased; Freda (Mrs. Joe Brtna), deceased; Marilda (Mrs. Art Heiser),
California; Viola (Mrs. Anton Petrak, Jr.), Pukwana, SD; Otto, Leola, married
Dorothy Mack; Lydia (Mrs. Walter Bertsch), California; and Amelia (Mrs. Bennie
Osborne), Chamberlain, SD.

Lydia died October 1, 1930 and her husband Jacob died October 20, 1964 in
Baker, MT.

Gottlieb Kolb was born November 24, 1886. He married Carolina Herrmann,
daughter of Solomon and Caroline (Dewalt) Herrmann, on December 26, 1910.

Gottlieb and Carolina lived in the Long Lake area, then moved to Elmer, MT.
They returned to the Long Lake area where they lived in a house made of straw
and clay. The remains of the house is south of the Gilbert Zumbaum farm.

Gottlieb then settled seven miles north of Leola which is now the Louie Kolb
farm.

Gottlieb and Carolina were the parents of seven sons and six daughters: Louie,
Leola; Reinhold, Aberdeen; Gottlieb, Jr., Leola; Helen (Mrs. Anton Kvasnicka),
Aberdeen; Adeline (Mrs. Emil Kolb), Leola; Hilda (Mrs. Hans Melland), Idaho;
Alvina (Mrs. Otto Sperle), Aberdeen; Ella (Mrs. Clarence Tschappat) Coon
Rapids, MN; Herbert, Westport; Violet (Mrs. Raymond Fauth), Aberdeen; Harold,
Barnard; Carl Gilbert, Leola; and Albert, Wetonka.

Carolina died February 1, 1936 and Gottlieb died June 23. 1971.

Emil Kolb, son of Jacob and Lydia Kolb, was born November 9, 1914 at Timber
Lake, SD. He married Adeline Kolb, daughter of Gottlieb and Carolina Kolb on
June 24, 1937. Adeline was born March 18, 1921 in the Long Lake area.

Emil did many odd jobs as a teenager. He was hired by farmers to shuck corn and
haul bundles. Fridays and Saturdays he worked for the railroad tightening rail
bolts. During the depression he worked for the WPA for a year or more,
gathering rocks and also helped build a dam near Wetonka. He also dug basements
and ditches by hand in Leola. He later moved to Tulare, SD where he worked on a
farm for Henry Blume.

In October 1943, Emil and Adeline and children moved to a farm located 3 1/2
miles east of Leola, where they presently reside.

Emil and Adeline are members of St. James Lutheran Church. They are the parents
of two sons and one daughter.

Duane and Darlene are twins, born October 10 and October 11, 1937 at Leola.

Duane married Aileen Golz, daughter of Adolph and Martha Golz of rural
Aberdeen, on June 9, 1973. Duane was a member of the South Dakota National
Guard. Duane and Aileen are members of St. James Lutheran Church. They
presently live 2 1/4 miles northeast of Leola at the former Carl Turnwall farm.

Darlene married Merle Heupel, son of Edwin and Emma Heupel, formerly of Long
Lake. Darlene and Merle presently reside in Aberdeen. They have one daughter,
Laurie Beth, born August 13, 1959.

Richard was born September 20, 1941 at Tulare, SD. He married Susan Janes,
daughter of Ivyl and Leitha Janes, of Aberdeen, SD, on December 29, 1967.
Richard and Susan have one son and two daughters: Kevin, born September 5, 1968
at Cedar Rapids, IA; Ann, born May 6, 1972; and Erin, born August 13, 1982,
both born at Aberdeen.

Richard attended Northern State College and SD School of Mines and Technology,
where he earned a B.S. and M.S. in Electrical Engineering in 1965. He was
employed by Collins Radio Co., Cedar Rapids, IA as an electrical engineer for 5
1/2 years and in 1971 moved back to the home farm near Leola where he presently
farms with his brother, Duane. Richard also has a privately owned agri-tax
business, which he operates with his wife and children.

OTTO and DOROTHY KOLB

Otto Kolb was born March 8, 1927 to Jacob and Lydia (Rau) Kolb of Leola.

In 1955 he was united in marriage to Dorothy Mack, the daughter of Arthur and
Irene (Mathemeier) Mack. Dorothy was born September 24, 1931, at Leola.

They have three sons: Kurtis married Brenda Laughlin, of Whitewood, SD, in
1980. He works for Anthony Kessler of Wetonka.

Scott is employed at Taylor Implement at Ipswich, SD.

Kent is a junior at Leola High School.

ANTHONY and ELIZABETH KOPPY

Elizabeth (Schneider) Koppy was born in Wallern, Burgenland, Austria in 1886.
Left motherless at age 11, she lived with her father, two brothers and an aunt,
from whom she acquired the basic skills of homemaking. She received an
elementary education. She learned to speak, read and write the English language
when William, the oldest child, started school. At age 21, she left Austria,
came to South Dakota to live with an uncle and her brother Mike, at Sisseton,
SD.

Anthony Koppy came to Leola in 1917. Tony' s parents, Martin and Elizabeth
(Koelandorfer) Koppy, came from Pamhagen, Austria with relatives to St. Paul,
MN, where they met and were married. Tony was born in 1882, his sister Julia
one year later. Three more children joined the family; George and Joe, both
served in WWI and Katherine, who later entered the Sister School of Notre Dame
in Mankato, MN. She is the only living member of this family, at age 88.

        Anthony & Elizabeth Koppy.

Tony and Elizabeth were married in 1908. They farmed near Eden, owned a
steam-powered threshing rig which accommodated the area farmers. In 1915, the
family moved into Eden, bought a well-drilling rig, as a need for water was
urgent. Many of the wells dug then are still supplying water.

This new venture soon took the family in a Model-T Ford, followed by a hayrack
full of furniture, driven by Tony's brothers, Joe and George, across the
swollen Jim River in the rainy April of 1917, to Leola to stay.

In 1919 Tony bought four lots of the Grimes Addition, where he built a home. In
September of the same year, Tony's parents bought the entire block of the
Hardenbrook Addition. They lived into their 80s.

Tony was hired by the city of Leola to take care of the power house and water
system in combination with the marshal duties (a part-time job on call 24 hours
a day).

Later, he helped in the management of the Blakeman Pool Hall, which he bought
in 1929. (See business history.)

In 1941, Tony was again hired by the city to serve in the former capacity of
power plant, water and marshal duties. Tony retired in 1953, a born fisherman,
hunter and volunteer fireman until he retired. He died in 1967 at age 85.

Tony and Elizabeth were both members of the Catholic Church, where Elizabeth
was a member of the Altar Society and Catholic Study Club. She was a member of
the Star Extension Club for many years. She sold her home in Leola and spent
her remaining years with daughter, Martha Delire, in Platte, SD, where she died
at age 92.

Tony and Elizabeth had five children: four born in Eden.

William enlisted in the Army in 1940. He served in the European Theater and
also in the supervisory capacity in building airfields in Okinawa and Iran. He
was honorably discharged as a Major. He retired with his wife, Nikki, in her
home area of Athens and Crete, Greece.

Marie was chosen Miss Leola in 1935. She taught school in McPherson County five
years. She married Harley Christopherson, band instructor, in 1935. She taught
26 years in elementary and special education and served 12 years in Scouts and
Campfire Girls. She is a member of Our Lady Queen of Heaven Church and church
organizations. Five children were born to this union: Joanne, Gloria, Jim,
Karen and John.

Leo, a Leola High School graduate, went to C.C.C. Camp in 1933. He enlisted in
the Army in 1940, served in the African and Italian campaigns. He was honorably
discharged. He was married and had two daughters, Toni and Janis. He moved to
Puyallup, WA in 1960, where he passed away in 1972 at age 59.

Martha married Wm. A. Raymer in 1939, who died in 1956. She taught music and
special education for 20 years. She married Edward L. Delire in 1961, moved to
Platte, SD and operates the Delire Insurance Agency there. She has been active
in church choirs and is an organist, member of Hospital, V.F.W. and Legion
Auxiliaries also Senior Citizens, and many professional organizations.

Loretta, born in Leola, now lives in Fort Worth, TX. She has excelled in both
violin and piano. She is currently a violinist in the Dallas-Fort Worth Civic
Orchestra and in the Mid-City String Ensemble. Loretta married Frank H. Kring
Jr. in 1944. They had three daughters: Pamela, Barbara and Gail, two grandsons
and four granddaughters. Frank died in 1962.

Loretta belongs to many professional organizations, St. George Catholic Choir
and Altar Society. She taught 30 years as Choral Director and music teacher.
She retired in 1982.

ORIN KRANZLER

Orin's grandparents, the Bernhard Kranzler family, immigrated to the United
States in 1900, coming from Odessa, Russia.

The family homesteaded on one-fourth section of land, 13 miles northwest of
Leola, SD.

Christian D. Kranzler, the son of Bernhard Kranzler, married Louise Bitterman,
in 1911, at Zeeland, ND. They homesteaded on one-fourth section of land three
miles east of the homestead of his parents. They continued farming until 1941,
when they sold out and moved to Leola, SD.

Louise died August 8, 1945. Christian died August 9, 1959.

They were the parents of four sons and one daughter. Three sons served in WWII.
Conrad and Fred served in Germany; Orin in Okinowa, during the Japanese
conflict in the South Pacific.

MICHAEL and KAROLINA KRAUSE

Michael Krause was born in Tarodino, South Russia, August 10, 1871, where he
lived until he was 14, when he came to America with his parents. They settled
near Scotland, SD, staying about six months and then moved to Campbell County,
where his father filed a claim. It was there that Michael became acquainted
with Miss Karolina Wahl, born July 19, 1876. She, too, had come from South
Russia with her parents when she was about eight years old. Michael and
Karolina were married in Mound City October 22, 1894.

        The Michael Krause Family.

To this union eight children were born: Anna 1895-1953 (Mrs. John Wattier);
Bertha, 1896-1963; Emilie, 1899-19-- (Mrs. A. H. McMillin, Leola); Edwin, 1902-
1961; Arthur, 1904-1970; William, 1906-19--, Sunnyvale, CA; Irvin, 1908-1967;
Nadine, 1916-19-- (Mrs. Nicholas Gear, Satellite Beach, FL).

The Krauses lived on a farm near Eureka for 3 1/2 years. In 1890 Michael was
elected to the office of Register of Deeds for McPherson County after which
date they made their home in Leola. Mr. Krause was prominent in political
affairs of the county and an active businessman being the senior member of the
firm of Krause and Lortscher, machine dealers. He was a member of the first
Leola Band.

Mr. Krause died at his home in Leola, October 8, 1917. Mrs. Krause died January
3, 1965, at the Lutheran Home in Eureka, SD.

ARTHUR and ELLA KREIN

Arthur Krein was born in 1910 on a farm near Eureka, SD to Paulina (Martel) and
Edward Krein. As a young child he moved with his family to Howard Township,
where they lived on a farm. Art grew up with two brothers, Reinhold (deceased)
and Milbert of Leola. He had three sisters, Edna and Hilda, Clara (deceased).
Art attended grade school and helped his parents with the farming. His father
died in 1931, his mother, in 1981.

Art was united in marriage with Ella Hoeft in 1934. Ella, born in 1915, in
Howard Township, attended grade school and helped her parents with chores on
the farm. Ella grew up with three brothers, Walter, Ipswich; (August and Fred
are deceased) and three sisters, Clara and Viola of Aberdeen, and Lena
(deceased).

Ella's father, Julius Hoeft, was born in Germany in 1869. He came to South
Dakota in 1889 and settled in the Columbia, SD area, until 1901, when they
homesteaded on a farm seven miles southwest of Leola. Julius and Emilie
(Jasmer) Hoeft were married in 1896. Emilie was born in Winona, MN in 1874. She
died in 1945, Julius, in 1956.

        Ella & Art Krein.

Art and Ella lived with her parents the first year of their marriage and then
rented a farm from Rollo Bosanko. In 1937 the family moved to the home farm of
Art's parents, where they farmed and raised their family. Shirley Ann was born
in 1936, at the home of Ella's parents. She was employed as a telephone
operator for Northwestern Bell until the office was terminated in 1981. Shirley
married John Fishback in 1960; they have two sons and one daughter.

Joanne Marie, born in 1938, took a short course at the University of Minnesota
and was employed as a dental assistant for Dr. Bauer of Aberdeen. She married
Robert Baer in 1960 and moved to Fort Sill, OK where Bob served in the Army.
Their son, Scott was born in 1961. They returned to South Dakota and moved to a
farm south of Roscoe, where Joanne died of cancer in 1968.

Karen Jean, born in 1940, married Ray Mehlhoff in 1959. They live in Crofton,
NE, where Ray manages the Bogner Steak House. They had two sons: David, and
Bruce (deceased). They have two grandsons.

Dean Arthur, born in 1942, joined the National Guard. He was engaged in farming
with his parents. In 1966, he was united in marriage with Gail Fischer. They
lived on the farm until 1973, when Dean lost his life in a silage wagon
accident. They were the parents of three children; two daughters and one son.
Gail and her family reside in Aurora, CO.

Shirley, Joanne, Karen and Dean graduated from Leola High School.

Art and Ella lived on the farm until 1966, when they moved to Leola. Due to ill
health, Art sold the farm in 1975. He retired from farming and cattle raising.

The Kreins are members of St. James Lutheran Church where Ella has served as
treasurer and president of the Ladies Aid. She also is active with Circle L.
CowBelles, Star Extension Club and Legion Auxiliary.

Art was most active and served in the following capacities while living in
Howard Township: St. James Lutheran Brotherhood, Board of Education, Farmers
Union, Leola Equity Exchange, school board and township supervisor, Lone Star
telephone, township assessor and director of the Saddle Club. He is a member of
the Leola Sportsman Club and the local Masons.

HARLAN and LORRAINE KREIN

Harlan Krein was born four miles east of Leola, SD on October 22, 1935 to
Florence (Galster) and Reinhold Krein. At the age of six he moved four miles
south of Leola. He graduated from Leola High School in 1954 and entered
Northern State College of Aberdeen in the fall of 1954. He received his B.S.
degree in 1958 and his M.S. degree in 1964. He received a Professional Degree
from the Denver University, Denver, CO in 1969 and a Ph.D. degree from Laurence
University at Sarasota, FL in 1972.

He entered the Army in 1958 and was discharged in 1960, serving 19 months in
Germany. Harlan has taught and coached in Groton, Webster, Ellendale, Peru, NE
and was superintendent at Conde, SD.

He married the former Lorraine Pfeiffer of Aberdeen on December 29, 1962. They
have three children, Susie, a sophomore at Northern State College, Aberdeen;
Brad, a senior at Leola High School; and Laurie, a third grader at Leola
Elementary School.

Harlan is a member of the Leola American Legion, Better Leola Club, Leola Trail
Riders Saddle Club, McPherson County Commissioners, Phi Delta Kappa, Northern
Alumni Wolves Club, NSC Foundation Board of Directors, Masons, Scottish Rite
and the Yelduz Shrine.

Harlan is presently engaged in farming, ranching and trucking and is still
residing at the farm he grew up on.

REINHOLD and FLORENCE KREIN

Reinhold Krein and Florence Galster were married in late fall of 1932. They
lived with Frank Galsters until Frank passed away in 1939. They rented the
Galster farm for three years, when they purchased a quarter of land four miles
south of Leola. The next year another quarter of land was bought, as things
seemed to be getting better after the dull '30s. They farmed this land and more
was bought later. They raised livestock and a lot of chickens at one time.

Three children were born to the family. Larry lives in Minneapolis, MN. Lilas
married Duane Skoglund of Leola. She lives in Hecla, SD. Harlan lives on the
home place.

Reinhold served on township board for several years, was County Commissioner
for 16 years. He later served on the school board. He served on the church
board, where Florence was very active in church work and was a Sunday School
teacher for 20 years. She also was a 4-H leader for 20 years.

Reinhold passed away June 13, 1973, due to a heart attack. Florence then sold
the farm, cattle and machinery to Harlan. She built a home in Leola, later sold
it and moved to Aberdeen, SD.

JOHN and BARBRA KULM

John Kulm was born in Germany in 1885. He later moved to Russia with his family
at the age of three. John came to America with his mother and two brothers.
John's mother remarried John Kapp in Eureka. One son, Ted, and two daughters,
Martha and Anne, were born to that marriage.

        Barbra & John Kulm.

John Kulm married Barbra Spitzer of Long Lake in 1915 and moved to Eureka, SD
in 1917. One daughter, Ella, was born in Eureka.

In 1919, John Kulm moved to Leola where six sons were born: Eugene, Irven,
Elmer, Jack, Allen and Martin.

John started a garage and filling station and took the Chrysler-Plymouth
Dealership and Case Implement line, until 1935 when he discontinued
Plymouth-Chrysler and Case Implements. John took the Ford Car and Truck Agency
and Allis Chalmers Implement line. His son, Eugene, started the McPherson
County Implement Company, in 1945. Eugene sold the Implement Company to Fred
Bain of Leola, in 1958. Eugene moved to California.

John Kulm owned and operated the Kulm Garage from 1919 to 1952.

Jack and Irven took over the business and named it Kulm Motors. Jack was a
partner with Irven for ten years, when he turned it over to Irven and moved to
Lodi, CA.

Irven continued in the Ford Dealership and Versatile line, until 1969, when it
retired a half-century business in Leola. (1919-1969)

Irven was active in civic affairs. He was chairman of two major celebrations in
Leola--the 70th anniversary in 1954 and the 75th anniversary in 1959.

Irven's wife, Leona (nee Wahl) was a grade school teacher in the Leola School
System. She died in 1980.

A son, David Kulm, is teaching school in Eureka, SD. A daughter Mary, and her
family are living in Sioux Falls. Irven has four grandsons.

In 1981, Irven, with his two daughters Patricia and Susan, moved to Lodi, CA.
Patricia will teach in Marysville, CA. Susan will go back to college for two
more years.

Allen Kulm and his family live in Aberdeen, SD. Eugene, Jack, Elmer and Irven,
live in California. Martin in Loveland, CO. John Kulm passed away in 1962. His
wife Barbra, at the age of 88, lives in a rest home in Lodi, CA.

HIRAM and LORRAINE KUSLER

Hiram Kusler was born July 20, 1929 at Leola, SD, to John and Amelia (Maier)
Kusler. He grew up in Leola graduated from Leola High School in 1947 and taught
country school for three years near Long Lake.

On October 4, 1949, he was united in marriage with Lorraine Schmitt at Roscoe,
SD. She taught rural school near Roscoe for two years and one year in the Long
Lake area.

        Hiram & Lorraine Kusler.

In 1950 the couple moved to Aberdeen where Hiram was employed with Forseth
Insurance Agency. He was transferred to Rapid City in 1955, where he spent two
years before returning to Aberdeen. He joined Reed-Johnston Insurance Agency
and Real Estate. He sold his share of the agency and in 1978 became owner of
Dak Claims Adjusting Service for five years. Presently he is engaged in Life,
Health and Accident Insurance and Real Estate.

Three children were born to this union: Nolan lives in Omaha, NE. He is
Assistant Manager for the Bell Telephone Company.

Joel is employed at Riddle's Jewelry. He is married to Barbara Johnsen from
Winner, SD. She is a teacher at Henry Neill Elementary School in Aberdeen. They
have two children. Kristi is eight years old and in the third grade. Jason is
three.

Paul is a student at Simmons Jr. High. He is active in sports and school
activities.

JOHN and AMELIA KUSLER

John Kusler was born in Leola, SD to Fred and Sophie (Brunnmeier) Kusler. John
grew to manhood in the Leola area and on April 22, 1924 was united in marriage
to Amelia Maier at Long Lake, SD. The two of them farmed nine miles southwest
of Leola. They raised five boys: Howard, Pierre, SD; Ervin, Aberdeen, SD;
Hiram, Aberdeen, SD; Myron, Pierre, SD; and Ernie, Aberdeen, SD.

John and Amelia moved to Aberdeen in April 1950. John was custodian at the
Aberdeen National Bank for 16 years. During this time he managed the 3rd Ave.
Laundromat for six years. John retired in September of 1966 and did various
part-time jobs.

        Amelia & John Kusler.

Amelia passed away in April of 1980 and now that John is 82 years old, he has
become a resident of Bethesda Nursing Home in Aberdeen, SD. John is a member of
the Zion Lutheran Church in Aberdeen. He has a favorite verse he wants to share
with all:
        "The dust storms and troubles have passed
        but the memories we cherish will always last."

EMIL O. KUTSCHKE SR.

Mr. and Mrs. Emil O. Kutschke came to Leola in 1900. They had immigrated to
America, originally from Pomerania, Germany, in the fall of 1880, settling
first in Chicago. Mr. Kutschke worked as a carpenter there, until he was
crippled by a fall when working on buildings for the World's Columbian
Exposition.

Their next move was to Hammond, IN in 1886, where they lived 14 years.

Emil was no longer able to work as a carpenter due to his accident in Chicago.
Since his sister, Lena, Mrs. Chris Christianson lived in the Leola area, he and
his wife, Mathilde, and six of their seven children decided to move there also.
Their eldest daughter, Mathilda, had remained in Chicago.

        Mathilde & Emil Kutschke.

The Kutschke family took up 160 acres of land northeast of Leola in Carl
Township. All six of their children attended school there. Two of them became
teachers themselves. Margaret Kutschke taught school nine years in McPherson
County until her marriage to Frank Young in 1914, and then moved with him to
Choteau, MT, where he managed a lumberyard. William "Bill" Kutschke taught in
the Leola area. Another daughter, Elizabeth, married Supt. E. C. Peterson of
Frederick. Years later their son Glenn Peterson, became Supt. of Schools in
Leola.

Emil Kutschke, Sr., and his family farmed their original homestead until 1917,
then moved into the town of Leola.

All members of the Kutschke family were devoted to their Lutheran Church, their
schools, and to the community life in their area, in which they took an active
part. Mr. Kutschke served on the School Board of Carl Township as well as
various other committees. He was a prosperous farmer and taught his children to
be grateful that their parents had come to America, and were citizens of this
great land.

Mrs. Kutschke died in July 1922 at Leola. Emil Sr. died in January 1926, in
Leola.

At this writing the only living member of this family is the youngest son,
Bill, who lives in Choteau, MT. The eldest daughter, Mathilda Graham, lived and
died in Chicago. Ernest Kutschke was employed by the railroad in Chicago, and
died there in 1965.

George Kutschke was employed by Northwestern Railway in Faulkton and Aberdeen.
George and his wife Winifred were well known in South Dakota, being active in
Masonic and Eastern Star Lodges. They died in Aberdeen in 1974 and 1977,
respectively.

Mrs. E. C. Peterson died at her home in Aberdeen in 1959.

Margaret Kutschke Young died in 1977 at the home of her daughter, Erma, in
Bartesville, OK.

EMIL JR. and OLGA KUTSCHKE

The only member of the second generation of the Kutschke family to make his
home in McPherson County was Emil, Jr.

He and his wife Olga farmed the original Kutschke farm. They were also active
in school affairs in Carl Township, as well as faithful members of St. Paul's
Lutheran Church of Leola.

        Olga & Emil Kutschke.

In the early 1940's they moved to Aberdeen and later to Salem, OR. They are now
deceased.

Emil and Olga Kutschke had no children of their own, but they had 11 nieces and
nephews, the children of Margaret Young and Elizabeth Peterson.

KATHERINA LACHER

Katherina (Katie) Lacher, daughter of Anton and Barbara (Geffre) Lacher was
born February 16, 1913 on a farm near Venturia, ND.

At an early age she came to Leola and lived with her grandparents, Peter and
Elizabeth (Senger) Geffre, seeking work. Being an ambitious youth she worked on
farms helping with housework.

        Katherina Lacher.

Katie spent nearly 30 years working for Mark Holmes and Lila Kramlich,
respectively, in the Leola Rexall Drug. She was forced to retired due to ill
health. She passed away on November 23, 1982.

HARRY and PEARL LaFONTAINE

Harry LaFontaine's parents, Peter and Elisabeth (Sattler) were among the first
settlers in the Leola area, arriving in the 1880's. They came from Pennslvania
where Elisabeth was born. Peter (Pierre) was born in Canada. They settled east
of Leola. Harry was one of seven children in the family.

Harry married Pearl M. Magee in Leola. They spent all of their lives in the
Leola area, except for a few years after their marriage when they lived in
Canada, where the two oldest children were born.

After returning to the Leola area, Harry managed the Dodge Garage (located next
to the Catholic Church at that time) until the depression. He then became a
farmer and established a milk delivery route. He was a Mason and a member of
the Methodist Church. He died at age 72 in 1962.

Pearl attended high school in Aberdeen and taught school until her marriage.
She belonged to Eastern Star and was a member of the Methodist Church. She died
a month after Harry at age 71 in 1962.

The LaFontaine children are: Bernard A. (Frenchy), married to Betty Harter and
is living in Sacramento, CA. They have children, Sharon (married to Dr. James
Lewis) and Michele Rae (married to Joseph Martinez). Sharon has four children.
Dorothy Blanche is married to Harris D. Holmgren. They live in LaFayette, MN
and have one daughter, Patricia J. (married to Thomas Sislo) and two
granddaughters. Delores Jeanne is married to Ens. John G. Giedt. They live in
Troy, OH and have two children: Elisabeth (Dr. Lissa) married Dr. Richard A.
Solwitz, and John Peter II, who lives in Troy, OH also. Elisabeth and Richard
have one son, Benjamin.

JOHN JR. and MAGDALENA LAMMLE

John Jr. was born April 3, 1890 at his parents', (John Sr. and Magdalena
[Hoffman] Lammle) homestead. On December 18, 1913 he married Magdalena Knapp.
She was born January 10, 1894 on her parents' farm northeast of Eureka.
Following John Sr.'s death, they moved onto the original Lammle homestead and
enlarged the farm approximately 1,000 acres. Considering that most of the work
was done with horses, this was at that time, a large farm. One daughter and
five sons were born to John and Magdalena. All of them attended rural school
(Bergdorf No. 3 School). Four sons served in the military service during WWII
and Korea. John Jr. died May 21, 1945 and Magdalena died September 7, 1960.
Both are buried in the Long Lake Cemetery.

The Lammle children are: Reuben, born November 14, 1914, married Lydia Sperle
in 1935. They have three children and seven grandchildren.

Oscar was born April 14, 1916. Oscar served in WWII and Korea. He returned from
service and lived in Lodi, CA where he was employed. He passed away August 9,
1981.

Irene, born April 10, 1918, married Otto Burkhardt September 11, 1948. They
made their home in Stockton, CA. They have two children and four grandchildren.

Lenard, born November 18, 1925, served in the Army after WWII. He lives in
Reno, NV where he is in the building business.

Chandler was born August 12, 1937. He served in the Army in Korea. Chandler
married Maxine Finstad at Bradley, SD. They live in Aberdeen and have two
children.

Melvin was born December 27, 1919. He served in the southwest Pacific with the
24th Infantry Division 3 1/2 years during WWII. He married Catherine Mathern at
Sacramento in June, 1954. They have seven children and reside in Aberdeen.

CARL and JOSEPHINE LAPKA

Carl Lapka was born in 1898, on a farm located four miles north and seven miles
east of Leola. He is the son of Ignatius and Mary Kraft Lapka.

        Carl & Josephine Lapka.

Carl married Josephine Grabowska, daughter of August and Francis Smaglenski
Grabowska, in 1920. Carl and Josephine spent eight years farming in the
Epiphany area. They returned to the Leola area in 1931.

Carl and Josie had four children. Margie, the eldest, resides in Dodge City, KS
with her husband Lane Hefner. Their first son John died in infancy. Rita and
her husband Tony Thares live in Ipswich, SD. Joseph and his wife, Ruth Weisser
Lapka, farm near Leola. Carl and Josie also have 14 grandchildren, as well as
15 great-grandchildren.

Carl and Josie left the farm and moved to Leola in 1952. Carl worked for the
Water and Soil Conservation Service.

Josie passed away in 1981. Carl spends his time taking care of the Catholic
Church and Parish Hall. He is also caretaker of the Catholic Cemetery.

FRANCIS and ALTHEA LAPKA

Francis Jerome Lapka was born May 27, 1921 to George and Irene (Ganser) Lapka.
He was one of six children. He grew up with three brothers, Laverne, Gerald and
Bernard; and two sisters, Lucille and Anita.

Francis served in the armed forces during WWII and saw action in Germany. Upon
his discharge from the service he married Althea Glaser February 7, 1946 at
Minneapolis, MN.

Althea is the daughter of Christian C. and Minna M. (Breitag) Glaser. She was
born August 22, 1926. She has three older sisters, Malita Stoebner, Hilda
Guthmiller, Erna Hiebel, and a brother Karl.

Eight children were born to this union: James Francis was born July 5, 1947. He
died at the age of ten days.

Kay Lynn was born December 10, 1948. She married Tony Kamm, son of Marvin and
Mary Kamm, December 19, 1972. They have one daughter Sharyce Rae. Kay is an RN
and is employed at St. Luke's Hospital in Aberdeen. The family resides nine
miles west of Aberdeen, SD.

Betty Ann was born January 16, 1951. She married Wilton Hoffman, son of Dan K.
and Hertha Hoffman, on November 7, 1969. They have two children, Brett Traves

FRANK and OLIVE LAPKA

Frank Joseph Lapka, son of John and Edith (Dexter) Lapka was born March 6, 1919
in Koto Township and also attended school there. On July 29, 1945 he was united
in marriage to Olive Guthmiller, daughter of John P. and Mary (Krein)
Guthmiller. Olive was born March 13, 1924 in Howard Township, attended grade
school there and graduated from Leola High School. After attending summer
sessions at Northern, Olive taught school several years in Koto Township.

        Frank & Olive Lapka.

Frank, who had been running the family farm five miles north and one-half mile
east of Leola continued to do so after their marriage. Frank did have a few
jobs away from home during the '30's. He recalls hauling hay to Leola for Ed
Hickman. It took two days and he got $ 1 for each load. He also picked corn by
hand at Britton, SD for $20 a week. Frank's brother Mark's adage always was,
"It isn't what you make--it's what you save."

On October 8, 1952, Frank and Olive became the parents of their son, Kevin
John.

Frank and Olive are members of St. James Lutheran Church. Frank served various
offices in the St. James Brotherhood, Koto Township and served many years on
the Leola Equity Exchange. Likewise, Olive has held various offices in the St.
James ALCW and the Country Extension Club.

Kevin married Kay Melland on June 5, 1976 and has joined in managing the family
farm. Frank and Olive built a new home in 1976 and live nearby. Frank still
keeps busy on the farm but takes time to enjoy fishing for walleyes at the
Missouri River. More recently he has added beekeeping to his list of hobbies.
Olive keeps busy with gardening, crafts, calligraphy and enjoying their
grandchildren.

GEORGE and IRENE LAPKA

George Lapka was born in Carl Township on May 9, 1886. Irene Ganser was born
February 18, 1894 in Worthington, IA. They were married June 11, 1913 at St.
Hyacinth Catholic Church. They lived on the farm until 1921, where George was
born. Laverne and Lucille were born in Carl Township. They moved to Willow
Township where Gerald, Francis, Bernard and Anita were born. They had a
three-room house so had beds all over the place. Summer wasn't too bad because
they could take a big hard coal heater out and had a little more room in the
living room. In 1926 George and Mr. Gisi built a big square house and they all
had a room, which was enjoyed by all.

        George & Irene Lapka.

George died at the age of 56, July 9, 1942. Irene died September 3, 1976 at the
age of 82. Irene lived in Leola for 28 years. The family didn't move too far
away. Lucille married George Geffre on July 14, 1932 and lived 1 1/2 miles east
of the home place. They have two sons, Marvin and Ronald.

Laverne married Elta Bain on June 11, 1940. They have three sons: Leon, Ray,
and Loel, and daughter Eileen.

Gerald married Elenor Hoeft on February 8, 1943. Their children are Leland,
Patricia, Charles, Paul, Mark and Judy. They live in Aberdeen.

Francis married Althea Glaser on February 7, 1946 and they have seven children:
Kay, Betty, Jerome, Peggy,

Bobbie, Georgiann and Karl. A son James died in infancy. Bernard married Annie
Geffre on September 3, 1946. They live in Aberdeen. They have four adopted
children: Dan, Tom, Lori and Pam.

Anita married Eugene Geffre on October 6, 1948. They had six children: Connie,
Steven, Donald, Joyce, John and Eugene. Anita lives in a nursing home in
Ipswich. Eugene died in 1976.

GEORGE and LEONA LAPKA

George Lapka and Leona Kallas, both natives of McPherson County, were married
October 29, 1935 in Leola Catholic Church. George, born May 31, 1915 is the
youngest child of Ignatius and Mary Kraft Lapka. George grew up on a farm ten
miles northeast of Leola, with his older brothers and sisters: Carl, Lawrence,
Josephine (deceased), Anne, Helen, Rosella and Fern. One older brother died
shortly after birth.

Leona, the oldest sister of Evelyn, Gertrude and Bernard, was born April 17,
1916 to Joseph and Laura Mensendick Kallas. Joseph, who died at the age of 46,
was the oldest of the five boys and five girls in the Julius Kallas family.
Laura Mensendick, the only child of Henry and Sarah Bride Mensendick, came to
Leola in 1906 from Illinois. Laura's parents built a home 2 1/2 miles northeast
of Leola with lumber hauled by horses from Ipswich, SD. The house was 24 by 24
feet and cost around $600.

        George & Leona Lapka.

After their marriage, George farmed with his father for a time and then on a
farm north of Leola until 1939. The farming years were lean ones due to the
depression and drought of the '30s. George and Leona remember a budget that
allowed $2.50 for a whole week's groceries although they did have their own
eggs, milk, cream and meat from the farm. In those days ten pounds of sugar
sold for around 49 cents. Besides the drought, there were the grasshoppers to
contend with. In the summer of 1938, when George and Leona went to check a
promising wheat field, they heard a rustling noise which turned out to be the
sound made by the falling wheat heads as they were being cut off by
grasshoppers.

In the early summer of '39 George and Leona moved to Sloan, IA, where George
worked for a hardware store. Later they moved to Veblen, SD where he sold
Maytag washers and DeLaval cream separators. Later they moved to Fridley, MN
where George worked for Northern Pump, a company that made huge pumps for the
Navy which was gearing up for WWII.

In 1942, the family moved back to Leola. Leona and George have five children:
Gary, Ruth, Henry, John and Jay. George worked as a cattle dealer and truck
driver until October 1969 when George and Leona, John and Jay moved to Swan
Valley in northwestern Montana.

IGNATIUS (IGNESS) and MARY LAPKA

Ignatius was born in Germany to John and Elizabeth (Fritz) Lapka. He came to
America as a lad of ten. The family stayed in Cleveland three years then made
their way to South Dakota where they homesteaded northeast of Leola. He had
four brothers and four sisters.

Mary Kraft was born on March 2, 1877 in Germany to John and Martha Kraft. She
was the oldest of eight children.

In 1883, when Mary was six years old, the family came to America. Upon arriving
in New York, after a 22-day ocean trip, Mary and her three brothers and sister
came down with measles, which caused the death of two of the children, one of
whom died in Mary's arms. From New York they traveled by covered wagon to a
homestead nine miles from Leola where they built a sod house, their first
permanent home in the new land. While her father broke the sod, Mary (seven or
eight years old) led the oxen while her father handled the plow. After seven
years of crop failures the family moved to LaMoure, ND where Mr. Kraft went to
work for the railroad. Mary, at the age of 15, worked at the Leland Hotel doing
dishes and waiting on tables for $3 a week. Later at the age of 17 she did the
cooking and earned $10 a week.

Mary Kraft and Ignatius "Igness" Lapka were married October 28, 1896 and took
up a homestead where they lived until they retired in 1941 and moved to Leola.
They were blessed with nine children; Carl, George, Lawrence, Ann, Helen,
Rosella and Fern. One son, Joseph, died at birth and daughter Josephine died in
1954.

        The Ignatius Lapka Family.

Igness died on June 13, 1948 ending a happy marriage of 52 years. Someone once
asked Mary how she came about marrying her husband. She said, "I knew he had
his eye on me and he thought I'd be a good worker, and I looked at him and knew
he would be good to me, so I agreed to marry him."

Mary continued to live in Leola. She was known to be a helpful neighbor and
friend always doing for others. As a mid-wife she delivered over 60 children.
In 1965 she moved to Mother Joseph Manor in Aberdeen. She was 100 years old
when she passed away in March of 1977.

JOHN and ELIZABETH LAPKA

John Lapka came from Tucel, Germany in approximately 1870. He landed in New
York and continued on to Pittsburgh, PA. After a brief stay, he went to
Cleveland, OH where some of his relatives lived.

Elizabeth Fritz was born in Swansburgh, Germany on September 23, 1847. She was
married to John Lapka in Germany. She arrived in the U.S. two years after John.
She brought her children: Ignatius (ten), John (eight), Mary (six), and a
step-daughter, Rose. They lived in Cleveland for three years where John was
employed. Two children, Frank and Kate, were born in Cleveland. The family
decided to homestead in South Dakota and traveled by train, leaving Rose, who
remained in Cleveland.

Julius Kallas, an acquaintance from Germany, met the Lapka family and helped
them acquire some land near the Kallas farm. They built a sod house and started
farming. The rest of the ten children: George, Annie, Joe and Nellie were
born on this farm. Besides raising her family, Elizabeth was a midwife and
delivered over 100 babies for friends, neighbors and relatives. Most of her
children married and made their homes around the Leola area.

        John, Joe, George, Mark and Maime Lapka.

Ignatius married Mary Kraft and they had nine children.

John married Edith Dexter and they had 12 children.

Mary married John Dexter and three children were born.

Frank did not marry and died at the age of 20.

Kate married John Hohman and had two children.

George married Irene Ganser and six children were born.

Annie married Tom Ganser and they had four children.

Joe married Lilly George and they had three children.

Nellie married Ed Ganser and four children were born.

John died March 7, 1901 and Elizabeth moved to Leola in 1911. She died June 3,
1923. Both are buried in Our Lady of Perpetual Help cemetery in Leola.

JOE and LILY LAPKA

attended school in the area and farmed with his parents until he entered the
U.S. Army September 21, 1917. He served until June 2, 1919, when he returned

ALBERT and PAULINE LAUER

Pauline's parents, John and Katherina (Boschee) Dockter, and their four
children arrived in Scotland, SD in May of 1893. They came from Neudorf, South
Russia and when John arrived he had 25 cents to call his own. After living with
relatives, they moved to Hosmer, SD for the winter. Pauline was born September
27, 1893 and the family moved to a homestead 24 miles west of Leola in the

        Pauline Lauer.

AUGUST and MARY LEBOLD

August Lebold was born September 9, 1825 in Sarsburg, Prussia. He came to
America in 1852 and lived in Kentucky. He later moved to Henry, IL where he met
and married Mary Tomas in 1858. Mary Tomas was born April 16, 1834 in Saar
Brucken, Germany.

August and Mary came to South Dakota in 1883 with seven children: Louise,
Frederick, Margaret, William, Joseph, Charles, and John. The family homesteaded
160 acres on the SE 1/4 of Section 23, Township 126, Range 66 near Dehli,
McPherson County. Dehli was a post office located ten miles east of Leola.

August Lebold was a carpenter and put many improvements on his homestead
besides farming and raising cattle. August and Mary were devout members of the
Catholic faith.

Mary passed away October 12, 1895, 12 years before her husband died. He died at
the age of 82 years on April 14, 1907.

JOHN BERNARD and CLARA LEBOLD

John Bernard Lebold, was born in 1876 in Henry, IL, moving to Dehli, SD (post
office) with his parents in 1883. He continued living on the homestead after
his parents were deceased, still farming and raising horses.

        John Lebold.

In 1905 his veterinarian practice was started and in 1907 he married Clara
Grabowska. They lived on the homeplace until about 1913, then moved into Leola
where he owned a general store, took care of the post office, and still did
veterinary work.

In 1915 he moved his family to Salem, OR. There he farmed and raised fruit
until he died in 1962, at the age of 86.

WILLIAM and CORA LILE

William Henry Lile, son of John Martin Lile, Jr., and Mary Jane Murray Lile was
born March 5, 1865 in Goldsberry, Macon County, MO. He married Cora Alice
Franklin February 4, 1892, in Macon County, MO. Cora Alice was born April 29,
1872, in Sullivan County, MO, to W. Franklin and Sara Louisa Dover. William and
Cora left Missouri about 1900 and bought a farm in Section 2, Howard Township,
McPherson, County, SD. Both of their children were born in Missouri; Nina on
June 13, 1893, and Hubert, October 11, 1895.

Mr. Lile was known as a great horsebreaker and taught his son as well. After
Mr. Lile's death August 16, 1933, Mrs. Lile sold the farm and moved to Auburn,
WA, to live with her daughter. She then had time to resume her skill as a
professional dressmaker, making gowns for brides and bridesmaids, and for
Eastern Star ladies, too. She lived with Nina for 33 years. She died August 28,
1967.

William H. Lile (Bill) was born to Hubert and Thelma Bishop Lile September 29,
1918, and as a small child, came to live with his grandparents, Mr. and Mrs.
William Lile at Leola. He attended the rural school (Howard No. 1) which was
directly across the road from his grandparents' farm; consequently it was known
as the Lile School.

After attending Leola High School, Bill served in the Army Corps of Engineers
in WWII. In civilian life he was president of the Tri-Valley Construction
Corporation of Lancaster, CA.

Bill married Gertrude E. Miller July 13, 1946. The Liles have one daughter,
Marta Lile Barker and three grandsons, living in Great Falls, MT.

Bill was back in South Dakota the summer of 1979, he had a great time visiting
with the few old friends still around Leola. He drove out to his former home,
the Lile farm. It was difficult to locate--all the buildings were gone,
including the old schoolhouse across the road. He died December 15, 1982.

GEORGE BURTON and ELIZABETH LINDLEY

George Burton Lindley was born November 22, 1849 at Fox Lake, WI. He died
August 19, 1925 in Eli, NE. His wife, Elizabeth (Snowden) Lindley was born
September 23, 1849, in England. She came to America via sailboat. They
encountered many events on the way over. If the wind did not blow strong
enough, they barely made progress. On other occasions there were gale winds, in
which everything had to be tied down. They arrived on the coast of Florida and
then went to Wisconsin, where she met and was married to George Burton Lindley.
George and his new bride immigrated to Leola, SD about the time the town of
Leola was in its early beginning. They settled in the south part of town. For
many years it was called Mrs. Frost's farm. The Darrel Yost family are the
present owners

        Elizabeth & George Lindley.

The G. B. Lindleys moved to Merriman, NE. While living in Merriman, they
encountered Indian scares, gypsies and rattlesnakes. They are both deceased and
buried at Merriman, NE.

George and Elizabeth were the parents of five children; all born while they
were living in Wisconsin. Two boys died early in infancy, one daughter died as
a young child of scarlet fever. Cora Estelle, the wife of Andrew Williams, was
born in June 1879 and died July 3, 1905. Both Cora and Andrew Williams are
buried in Green Mound Cemetery, at Leola. They were the parents of one son,
Lindley Williams.

William Lindley was born November 23, 1885 and grew to manhood in Leola. He was
married to Leslie Moulton on February 27, 1910. William and Leslie shared the
same date of birth, November 23. William died suddenly on October 14, 1936 of a
heart attack.

WILLIAM and LESLIE LINDLEY

Will Lindley's family came from Wisconsin during the early formation of the
settlement of Leola. The family consisted of his mother, Elizabeth, his father,
G. B. and one sister, Cora. Three children had died in infancy. Will was born
in Fox Lake, WI on November 23, 1885.

Leslie was born in Eureka on November 23, 1888. Her parents, Fred and Minnie
(Slye) Moulton, originated from Wisconsin. She married Will Lindley on February
27, 1910. The couple had a lot in common including their birth dates, November
23. Soon after their marriage they moved in with Will's parents. Later his
parents went to Nebraska to take up a homestead. Will and Leslie followed. It
was here, on their claim, they built a little shanty. They had wonderful times
while they lived there. They made their own amusement. Both of them played
piano and Will played the violin and a mandolin. They didn't live very far from
his parents so they were able to commute, sometimes by horseback. The land was
sandy and the area had rattlesnakes. It is difficult to say which they
considered the worst drawback, sandy soil, rattlesnakes, Indians or Gypsies. At
any rate after a while both families moved to Merriman, NE, where Will worked
for the Walwrath Sherwood Lumber Co. All of their children were born in
Merriman. Moulton was born in 1911, Lester in 1913, Burton in 1915, and
Virginia in 1917. A few years later the family moved to Eli where Will ran his
own lumberyard. It was in Eli where the Lindley family got a yen for hunting
and fishing. The town of Eli had water on three sides which encouraged the
sportsmen. Will and Leslie started a small community church in Eli. They
furnished music and sang for most of the funerals. They were instrumental in
beginning a Ladies Aid. Things went very well for the Lindleys in Eli but
Leslie's mother suffered a severe stroke, so they moved back to Leola. While in
Leola both Will and Leslie accepted jobs with the Western Mutual Telephone Co.
Will died unexpectedly from a heart attack on October 14, 1936. Leslie
continued working for the Telephone Co. for 32 years until the new dial system
went into effect. She then retired and lived in Leola the rest of her life. She
died August 25, 1983.

        The William Lindley Family.

The three Lindley boys all died at an early age. Moulton died in 1950, Lester
in 1979 and Burton in 1960. Will and Leslie's daughter, Virginia married Christ
Schanzenbach and resides in Leola at the present time.

ALBERT and ELLA LOEBS

Albert Loebs was born September 16, 1920 to Gottlieb G. Loebs and Katharina
(Heupel) Loebs on a farm 15 miles northwest of Leola. On November 2, 1941
Albert married Ella Opp. They now farm the homeplace.

Albert and Ella have two children, Jerald and Joann.

Jerald Albert, born August 21, 1942, lives in Aberdeen with his wife Marlene
(Geffre) Loebs, and their three children: Jeffrey Jerald, born March 10, 1971;
Chad Albert, born February 25, 1975; and Christa Marie, born April 23, 1979.

Joann Ella (Loebs) Nixon, born November 19, 1945, lives in Olivehurst, CA with
her two children: Jay Dee, born August 6, 1966 and Jan Ella, born January 24,
1970. Joann's husband, Robert Dee Nixon, born April 6, 1940, died suddenly
November 8, 1979.

        Ella & Albert Loebs.

Ella was born on a farm four miles northwest of Long Lake to Christian Opp and
Lydia (Lautt) Opp. Ella's sisters and brothers are: Anna Fink, died May 18,
1964; Arthur, died January 6, 1970; Caroline, of Medicine Hat, Alberta, Canada;
Robert, died September 23, 1981; Harold, of Rapid City; Wilbert, of Ashley, ND;
and Leona Trautman, died in a car accident along with her husband on December
25, 1964. Albert and Ella are members of the Leola Baptist Church.

EDWIN and EMGARD LOEBS

Edwin Loebs was born northeast of Eureka, SD on April 30, 1909 to Gottlieb and
Kathrina Heupel Loebs. When Edwin was three years old, his parents moved to a
farm six miles south of Long Lake, SD and one mile east. Edwin was raised and
went to school there. Later he farmed with his parents.

Emgard Mund was born to Jacob Mund and Katherian Reich Mund on March 2, 1914.
Emgard lived three miles west of Fredonia, ND where she grew up and went to
school.

        The Edwin Loebs Family.

On September 25, 1936 Edwin married Emgard Mund. They lived with his parents
for four years and six months, then moved to a farm one mile northeast from his
parents. Edwin and his family lived there for 17 years. To improve his farming,
he purchased a farm one mile south. He moved some of the buildings and
remodeled the house, which they moved into on March 25, 1959. Edwin and Emgard
farmed for another four years. Then they sold their farm and moved to Leola, SD
in 1963. Emgard worked part-time cleaning houses and the dentist's office for
ten years; she also worked in the bakery for a short time. Edwin still kept
busy working on surrounding farms. He worked for Don Zetterlund for seven
years, and Earl Rott five years. Edwin had to quit the farm work because of his
health. Edwin started to work part-time for the City of Leola in August 1977.
The Loebs family are Baptists. Edwin served in church as Deacon, Trustee,
Sunday School Teacher, and Sunday School Treasurer. Emgard was a Sunday School
teacher for the little children. Edwin and Emgard have three children.

Melvin Loebs married Helen Howell of Aberdeen, SD on September 24, 1966. They
have two children, Sheila and John. Sharlene Loebs married Darrel Chapman of
Park River, ND on October 19, 1963. They live in Greeley, CO. They have two
children, Roxann and Rodney. Leslie Loebs married Darlene Hopper of Aberdeen,
SD on November 26, 1977.

FRED and LOUISA LOEBS

Fred Loebs was born October 7, 1894 to Gottlieb, Sr. and Margaret (Nies) Loebs
on a farm 11 miles northeast of Eureka, SD. Fred married Louisa Dohn January
27, 1914 in Eureka, SD and they lived on this home farm for six years.

Louisa Dohn was born October 28, 1891 14 miles northeast of Eureka, SD. She
grew up in a family of six brothers and two sisters.

In the spring of 1920 Fred and Louisa moved to a farm 13 miles northwest of
Leola. In the fall of 1944 they sold the farm to their son-in-law, Jake
Kirschman. They bought some land close to the farm and farmed until 1957 when
they sold the land to Jake Kirschman. They moved to Leola where Louisa worked
for Elsie Baker and Fred did some odd jobs for a few years. In 1972 they moved
to the Lutheran Home in Eureka.

        The Fred Loebs Family.

Fred and Louisa were the parents of three daughters: Emma (Kirschman), Lodeva
(Ketterling) and Violet (Clayton), deceased.

Louisa died in the Lutheran Home January 1, 1974 and Fred died in the Eureka
Hospital February 19, 1978. Both were members of the Leola Baptist Church.

GOTTLIEB JR. and KATHARINA LOEBS

Gottlieb G. Loebs Jr., was born January 29, 1890 in Gluckstal, South Russia. He
was two years old when he came to the U.S. with his parents Gottlieb Loebs Sr.
and Margaretha (Nies) Loebs. Gottlieb Jr. grew up on a farm about 12 miles
northeast of Eureka. He married Katharina Heupel January 2, 1909. They lived
with his parents for three years. In 1912 they moved on a farm 15 miles
northwest of Leola. In 1947, they moved to Leola, Gottlieb died March 8, 1957.

Katharina (Katie) was born June 20, 1891, to John Heupel Sr. and Katharina
(Weisser) Heupel 15 miles northeast of Eureka. In 1968, she made her home in
the Lutheran Home in Eureka. She died November 9, 1974.

        Mr. & Mrs. Gottlieb Loebs.

Gottlieb and Katharina had six children: Edwin, of Leola, married Emgard Mund;
Martha, LaMoure, ND, married Eugene Heyd; Arthur, of Lodi, CA, married Wilma
Ketterling; Ella, of LaMoure, ND, married Harry Merkel (he died October 13,
1970); Albert, of Leola, married Ella Opp; Leona, of Marion, ND, married Elmer
Pinke.

Mr. and Mrs. Loebs were members of the Leola Baptist Church.

THOMAS and OLIVE LOHNER

Thomas Lohner, "The Candy Man," was born February 28, 1894, to Thomas and Marie
Lohner in Audubon County, IA. He attended school there before moving to
Kingsbury County SD, with his parents. He later moved to Wetonka, where he was
engaged in general merchandising.

In 1922 he married Olive Broadbent, the youngest child of William and Harriette
Broadbent. She was born on a farm south of Leola April 12, 1900. In 1906 she
moved with her parents to Leola where she attended grade and high school,
graduating in 1918. As a school girl, she worked in the local ice cream parlor
through three owners; the Dentons, the Hickmans, and the Ray Langs. Later she
worked at the drugstore for Henry Knutson and when he sold the store to Mark
Holmes, she stayed on working for Mark.

The Lohners operated their Wetonka store until it burned in 1930. He then
established Tom's Candy Company, which had five trucks serving the surrounding
territory. The warehouse was located at Eureka. Far and wide, everyone knew the
Candy Man, whose trucks supplied fresh candy and cigarettes to all the small
towns within a radius of a hundred miles of Eureka. Mr. Lohner served as
president of the company until his retirement in the 1960's. The Lohners moved
to Aberdeen in 1951.

        Olive & Thomas Lohner.

He was a past elder of the First Presbyterian Church, and a member of the Blue
Lodge No. 211, Scottish Rite, Yelduz Shrine, Elks Lodge No. 1046, Kiwanis
International, Sons of Norway, The Oden Club and the Senior Center.

Mr. Lohner died May 5, 1981. Mrs. Lohner resides in Aberdeen. Their daughter
Geraldine Hastings lives in Des Moines, IA. Their niece, Ann Sherman Silman,
whom they raised, lives at Ft. Washington. PA.

FRANK DeFOREST and IDA LOWRY

Frank DeForest Lowry was born at Pine Island, MN on November 29, 1865. He came
to South Dakota with his parents, Mr. and Mrs. Wm. H. Lowry in 1879. He
pioneered as a cattle rancher with his father in Brown and McPherson counties.
He began to learn the printing trade at Pine Island and later coming to South
Dakota he established the McPherson County Herald.

Frank married Ida M. Stone of Leola in 1894. They had three children: Harriet
Jane (McMillin), William Leonard and Thearon Dean.

He continued the publication until 1919, over a period of 25 years, until poor
health required him to retire. During his active years he served the community
in various local offices and for a long period he was also Postmaster of Leola.

He was a member of the Masonic, Modern Woodmen and Maccabee Fraternities.

Mr. Lowry died at Leola, SD on September 11, 1922.

ARNOLD and MARY ANN MACK

Arnold was born June 25, 1923 in Carl Township to Carl and Anna Mack. He
attended rural school in Carl Township.

Mary Ann (Lechner) Mack was born July 26, 1933 to John and Frances (Geffre)
Lechner.

Mary Ann also attended school in Carl Township and graduated from Leola High

Arnold and Mary Ann were married November 19, 1958 in Leola and established
their home on the family farm northeast of Leola.

Arnold and Mary Ann were blessed with four children; Gary, married Shirley

        The Arnold Mack Family. Back: Karen, Shirley, Gary, Wanda and Glen.

CARL and ANNA MACK

Carl was born November 10, 1891 in Koto Township, northeast of Leola. His
parents were John and Anna (Breunig) Mack. Anna (Kallas) Mack was born on
October 17, 1896 to Julius and Sophia (Schmaglenski) Kallas. Carl attended
rural school in Koto Township when not needed at home. Anna attended school in

        Carl & Anna Mack.

Carl and Anna were married August 19, 1922 in a country church northeast of

Carl and Anna established their home 12 miles northeast of Leola in Carl

DONALD and VIVIAN MACK

Donald was born in 1923 to William and Alice Mack. They lived on a farm north
of Leola, where he attended rural school.

Don farmed with his father and later with his two brothers. In 1954, Don, Dean
Pade and Herbert Weisz bought the Leola Livestock Sales Co. Later Don and Dean
bought Herbert Weisz's share and they owned and operated the barn until Don's
death in 1978.

Vivian, born in 1936, to John and Rose Kaul, attended rural school and
graduated from Leola High School. She attended business college for one year
and then started working for the McPherson County Highway Department in 1955 as
a bookkeeper. She held this position until 1982. Vivian is currently serving
her first term as McPherson County Register of Deeds. She is active in church
and community organizations.

Don and Vivian were married in 1958. They made their home in Leola. They had
one daughter, Jacklynn Kay, born in 1960. Don served on the City Council and
was also elected mayor of Leola (1968-1976).

Jacklynn graduated from Leola High School in 1979 and from Northern State
College in 1983, with a degree in music. She has been active in school and
church activities. She is currently teaching music in Roslyn, SD. Vivian and
Jacklynn are members of St. James Lutheran Church.

GORDON and BETTY MACK

Gordon Alfred Mack was born to Arthur and Irene (Mathemeier) Mack at Leola on
January 20, 1933.

        Betty & Gordon Mack.

Gordon was married to Betty Serdahl on January 25, 1956 in Aberdeen, SD, where
Betty was employed by Bell Telephone Co. Betty was born December 28, 1935 to
Russell and Christine (Glaser) Serdahl at Leola.

After Gordon and Betty were married, they moved to a farm one-half mile east of
his home farm. They have a dairy herd and do diversified farming and have a
stock and cattle operation with Gordon's brother, Derald Mack. They continue to
live on the same farm.

The living room of the house on this farm served as the Sutherland post office.
When some remodeling was done in 1956, newspapers dated 1887 were found as
shims in the walls. It could be seen where the post office counter was. The
floor was worn down to the tongue and groove. It could also be seen where the
double doors went out to the west. Running kitty-corner through the yard was
the stagecoach track that ran from Forbes, ND, to Sutherland and on to Leola.
Part of the track is still visible west of the house.

Gordon and Betty have seven children, born between 1956 and 1965. Debra is
married to rancher Ed Dodson, at Edgemont, SD. Debra works as a medical
secretary at the Veteran's Hospital in Hot Springs, SD. They have one son,
David. Wayne is married to Carla Henrick. He manages the Sandvig's store in
Pierre, SD. Carla is employed by the Federal Housing Authority. They have one
son, Eric. Marcia is married to Scott Beukelman, Cenex manager in Hector, MN.
Marcia is employed by a Cable TV company as a computer programmer. They have
one son, Matthew. Linda is married to Dave Netjes, a student at the University
of SD. Linda works for the First Bank System in Vermillion, SD. Jerome attended
SDSU and is at home on the farm. Merle is a student at SDSU as a
Business-Economics major. Bruce is a student at Leola High School.

Gordon and Betty Mack have always been active in community affairs. Gordon
served on the school board for 11 years. He is a member of Better Leola Club,
was a 4-H leader and served on ASC committees and township offices. Betty is
active in Country Club Extension, PTA, Catholic Ladies Society, was a 4-H
leader and taught CCD classes.

ARTHUR and IRENE MACK

Arthur (Art) Mack was born November 9, 1888 on the family farm. His parents
were John and Anna (Breunig) Mack, who settled in Koto Township in 1886. Art
spent his entire life in Koto Township.

In 1925 Art met Irene Mathemeier who was teaching in Weber Township. They were
married June 14, 1927. It was a short, happy marriage ending in a tragic
accident. Art was injured while putting up hay. He died September 14, 1944.
Irene was left with five children, the oldest, 13 years old and the youngest,
eight months. She employed a hired man for one year and then she and the
children operated the farm alone. As time moved on, more land and buildings
were added and eventually they remodeled the old house.

Irene had eight children. Three babies died in infancy, twin daughters and a
baby boy. Two of the eldest, Derald and Gordon, manage the farming and cattle.
One son, LeRoy, is the assistant Chief of Police in Aberdeen, SD; Dorothy
(Kolb) teaches in the Long Lake Hutterite Colony, and the youngest daughter,
Virginia, lives in Moorhead, MN.

Irene still lives on the farm with her son, Derald. Although she had many days
of sadness, the years have also brought her some rewards. Irene went on a
three-week European trip which had been her dream for many years. She also
toured 15 eastern states with the Senior Citizens of Aberdeen.

Irene is a member of the Catholic Church and an honorary member of the Leola
Country Extension Club, of which she holds the longest membership.

WILLIAM and ALICE MACK

William Mack was born February 21, 1894 to John and Anna Mack in Koto Township,
McPherson County. Alice M. McConville was born March 5, 1897 in Dickey County,
ND to Henry and Hannah McConville. She attended Ellendale, ND Normal and taught
school in rural Dickey County and Forbes Public School. She married

        Alice & William Mack.

William A. Mack on June 16, 1920 at Ellendale. They settled on a farm in Koto
Township until 1951 when they moved to Leola. William then operated a cattle
spraying service until his retirement. He was a member of Our Lady of Perpetual
Help Catholic Church, Leola. He was a veteran of WWI and a past commander of
the Leola post of the American Legion No. 78. He served many years as a member
of the Koto Township school board and also on the McPherson County weed control
board. He died July 27, 1971 in Aberdeen, SD.

Alice was a member of Our Lady of Perpetual Help Catholic Church in Leola, the
Altar Society and the American Legion Auxiliary Post 78. She was a resident of
the Americana Healthcare Center in Aberdeen, SD for seven years. She died
August 4, 1982, in Aberdeen, SD. They had seven children: Donald, deceased;
Gordon, deceased; Bernard, Mildred, Armella, Velma and Norma.

FRANK E. and MARY ELLEN MAGEE

Frank Magee and his wife "Ella" were both born in Wisconsin. After their
marriage they moved to Kidder, SD where Pearl and Iva were born. Later they
moved to Plana, east of Aberdeen, where Amos and Bernice were born. Amos died
in infancy. The family came to Leola in 1909.

The Magees ran the Leola House, later called the Brosz Hotel. In the obituary
published by the Leola paper, upon the death of Mary Ellen in 1925, it said,
"It was Mrs. Magee who made the old Leola House seem like home to all of the
people who stayed there. The community has lost A real friend and model woman."

        Pearle, Frank, Bernice, Mary Ellen and Iva Magee.

The Magee children are: Pearl Mae, married to Harry R. LaFontaine, deceased;
Iva Elizabeth, married to Henry G. Young, Iva was 90 years of age in 1983; and
Bernice, married to Frank Smith, deceased.

THOMAS and DEB MAHLKE

Thomas Wayne Mahlke was born on June 20, 1956 in Kensal, ND to Emil and Marilyn

Deborah Eva Mahlke was born at Ipswich, SD on April 28, 1957. Her parents are

EDWIN and ANNIE MAIER

Edwin R. Maier--born in Eureka, SD, August 8, 1905, son of Jacob and Katherine
Maier, brother of Jacob, Pauline (Kiem), Roland, and John Maier. He graduated
from Eureka High School and began his barber apprenticeship at an early age.
After barbering in Eureka during the '20s, he moved to Leola in the 1930's,
where he barbered with Bert McMillan. He married Annie R. Lapka in 1942. Ed
opened his own shop in the 1940's, serving the public and staying open very
late in the evenings (1-2 A.M.!), especially when convenient for the community.
Farmers who worked in their fields until daylight was spent wanted a fresh
haircut for church on Sunday mornings. Ed barbered for 50 years, cutting old
friends' hair, even when he was very ill. He died in 1974 after several
operations for cancer.

        Edwin R. Maier cutting grandson's hair in his barbershop (1960).

        Annie R. Maier, R.N., with patient Lizzie Young, in the Maier home
        (1953).

Annie R. Maier, R.N.--daughter of John and Edith Dexter Lapka. Her identical
twin, Mary (Mrs. Raymond Caspers), lives in Hecla, SD. Annie and Mary were born
in Koto Township on October 21, 1910; they attended school at Koto country
school. Annie attended Leola High School from grades eight through 11; she was
accepted into nurses' training at Britton Clinic and Hospital in 1929. After
receiving her R.N. degree, she worked for two years before taking a post
graduate course in pediatrics in the Minneapolis, MN, Hospital of Ripley
Memorial. She then returned to work at the Britton Hospital before moving to
Rapid City, SD and employment in private duty nursing. (Private duty nurses
were expected to do 20 hours care per day or $3.00 wages a day.) She married in
1934, and then returned to Leola in 1940, where she was a nurse at the
Lundquist Hospital in 1941. She married Edwin R. Maier in 1942. In 1943, she
was employed at the State Hospital at Sanator, SD, where Edwin, her husband,
was a patient.

Ed and Annie returned to Leola in 1944. Annie did house to house nursing and
was busy administering the new wonder drug, penicillin, to patients every three
hours. She sometimes cared for five patients at home and 50 to 70 house calls
daily, working 24 hour days, sustained only by taking short naps. She consulted
closely with Dr. Bloomendahl of Ipswich and many other doctors throughout the
nation, depending where patients were from. Dozens of babies were born in their
home, since Leola did not have a resident doctor or hospital then. Many types
of emergencies were taken care of. Annie was at her parents' side, working
tirelessly; when her father was ill, when her mother broke her hip at the age
of 76, and her sisters, Clara and Mamie, when they were very ill. Before
retiring in 1968, after 40 years of nursing, she worked for the Ipswich and
Herreid hospitals.

Annie presently lives in Leola, enjoying the first leisure years of her life.

Edwin and Annie Maier are the parents of LaRue E. Maier and LaDell I. Maier
Smieia.

JACOB JR. and OTILLIA (TILLIE) MAIER

Jacob Maier Jr. was born in Eureka, SD on December 13, 1900. His parents were
Jacob Maier Sr. and Katherina (Klinger) Maier. Jacob Sr. and Katherina
immigrated from Odessa, Russia.

On January 6, 1927, Jacob Jr. married Otillia (Tillie) Hager. Tillie was born
December 2, 1902 in Ashley, ND. She was one of eight children born to Karl and
Christina (Schultz) Hager . Her parents were married in 1888 in Boradens, South
Russia. They immigrated to America in 1892 and farmed east of Ashley, ND.

Jacob Jr. and Tillie began married life in Eureka where Jacob was a carpenter.
He built many homes in Eureka and also a Lutheran church west of Eureka. A few
years later, the church was struck by lightning and burned.

While living in Eureka, their first child, Luella, was born August 4, 1929.
When Luella was four years old, Jacob moved his family to Leola. Shortly after
arriving the family became very ill, confining them to bed. Their neighbors,
the Stephen family, came to their home and nursed them back to health. Another
daughter, Mary Jane, was born February 28, 1934. Mary Jane's birth, along with
the moving and sickness, makes 1934 a memorable year for the Maier family.

Jacob served as Sheriff of McPherson County in 1934 for two terms, then as
Register of Deeds for another two terms. Following this public service, he was
employed by the State Division of Taxation and Licensing in Pierre, SD. In 1957
Jacob and his family moved to Rapid City, SD where he was employed by the SD
Cement Plant as a salesman until his death on June 21, 1960.

Jacob Jr. and Tillie are charter members of South Canyon Lutheran church in
Rapid City, SD.

LUELLA (MAIER) GRAVES

Luella moved to Leola with her parents and attended Leola Public Schools. She
graduated in 1947 and attended NSC, Aberdeen, SD. She married Richard Graves in
1959 and moved to Duluth, MN. They later moved to Kansas, Colorado and then
Springfield, MO where they remained. Richard died in June 1976. The Graves
children are Renee and Roger, both born in Duluth, MN.

MARY JANE (MAIER) THOMAS

Mary Jane was born in 1934 in Eureka, SD. She attended school in Leola. Upon
graduating from high school, she pursued the profession of nursing. She is
currently employed by the Veterans Administration Hospital at Ft. Meade, SD.
Mary Jane married Harold Paul Thomas in 1962 at Rapid City, SD. They are the
parents of one daughter, Michelle Rae, born November 2, 1972. The Thomas family
lives in Rapid City, SD.

        Harold, Michelle and Mary Jane Thomas.

OSCAR and OTILLIA MAIER

Oscar Maier was born March 15, 1914 to Jacob J. and Carolina (Rath) Maier, Long
Lake, SD. Jacob and Carolina were born near Long Lake and lived there all their
lives. Oscar became a rural mail carrier in 1938 from Long Lake, SD. He was
inducted into the service in 1941 and served four years. Oscar married Otillia
Heupel October 13, 1946.

        Oscar & Otillia Maier.

Otillia was born January 29, 1924 to Fred G. and Rosie (Kirschman) Heupel on a
Leola farm. Her parents were born in South Russia to parents that immigrated to
America when they were small children. Otillia grew up in the rural area and
taught school in McPherson County for a number of years. After marriage she and
Oscar lived in Long Lake for a short while and on September 21, 1951 they
purchased what was then the Ferkin Garage. This consisted of a franchise for
Chrysler and Plymouth cars and John Deere farm Implement. They were in business
until August of 1969. They sold the business and moved to Hillsboro, OR where
they lived for 14 months. They moved to Flagstaff, AZ where they purchased a
laundry and diaper service business. They later terminated the business and
became involved in the antique business. They have operated an antique store
since the spring of 1972.

LUDWIG and MATHILDA MARTZ

Ludwig Martz was born in Friedinstal, Bessarabia, Rumania on January 25, 1876.
He married Mathilda Hager, who was born January 30, 1883 in Jacobstal,
Bessarabia, Rumania. Mathilda and Ludwig were married in 1902. They farmed in
McIntosh County later moving to Houston, TX where they raised cotton and
farmed. This venture proved unsuccessful due to insects and poor water. They
returned to Ashley, ND, later moving to Leola where Ludwig was acting city
marshall and sheriff for a short time. He then went to work as custodian in the
Leola Courthouse where he was employed for 20 years. They moved to Lodi, CA
where he was employed by the government during WWII. He had to retire because
of illness. He died April 24, 1944 at the age of 68. Mathilda died June 15,
1961 at the age of 75.

        Ludwig & Mathilda Martz.

born March 20, 1924; Gordon, born October 1, 1926. All of the children were

OTTO and EMMA MAYER

Otto Mayer from Hosmer and Emma (Gugel) of Leola, were married in Hosmer on

ALONZO and HARRIET McMILLIN

Alonzo (Lon) McMillin was born in 1891 to Harry and Helen McMillin. In 1914 he
married Harriet Lowry, born in 1896 to Frank and Ida Lowry.

        Harriet & Alonzo McMillin.

Lon was a barber and bought half interest in the local barbershop from his
brother Albert (Bert) in 1921. Lon was an avid sportsman, running the gamut
from baseball to hunting. He and his wolfhounds are well-remembered throughout
the area as they took care of marauding wolves and coyotes. The following item
taken from the 4-28-21 issue of the McPherson County Herald is just one of the
several which testify to the effectiveness of Lon and his dogs.

"When Lon McMillin received a message from George Bain that a big wolf that had
been molesting his farm all winter and now had just killed one of his larger
calves, Lon and Stanley Junge piled into a car, taking Lon's four hounds with
them. When they got to Bain's place, seven miles east of town, they found
George herding the wolf. Lon turned his dogs loose; it was a run of about a
mile down the road until Grace, Lon's newest hound, caught up with the wolf and
wrestled her. Jack-the-Killer, Lon's most famous hound, put the finishing
touches to the wolf. According to Bain, many attempts had been made during the
past six months but all had been failures until Lon took over with his hounds."

The McMillins had three children: Ivan, Evelyn and Loren. Ivan, born at Leola
in 1915, attended school there graduating from LHS in 1934. He received a B.A.
degree from Fresno State U of California and a M.S. degree from U of Southern
California. He served in the Navy in WWII. He married Evalena Fuller in 1940.
They have two children, Lee Lon and Jay Ivan. Evelyn was born at Merced, CA in
1921. She married Cecil Heptner in 1939. Loren, born at Watertown, SD,
graduated from Merced High School in 1948. He is engaged in insurance sales. He
married Joan Werner in 1950 at Merced. They have two children, Robert and
Michael.

Lon died in 1946, and Harriet in 1978 at Merced, CA.

JOHN and LYDIA MEHLHOFF

John J. Mehlhoff was born May 12, 1892, in McPherson County. At 18, he started
a carpentry career building farms, some of which are still standing. On
November 26, 1914 he married Lydia, nee Bender, in a triple wedding. Lydia was
the daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Jacob Bender, lifelong McPherson County residents.
The Mehlhoffs had four children: Lenora (Mrs. Otto Schick), Ruben (married to
Jacquelyn Haar), Arlene (Mrs. Arnold Herrboldt), and Adeline (Mrs. Adeline
Dorsey).

        John & Lydia Mehlhoff.

In 1917, they bought a school section of 320 acres which included the farm site
northeast of Hillsview. To start farming they had four horses, a plow, and
wagon and a home made of clay. Water was a big problem in the early years. At
one time, well diggers stayed on the property for 18 months digging for water
while John hauled it 1 1/2 miles. In 1940 John bought the Hillsview Elevator
and in September 1942 they bought a home in Hosmer, SD. In his retirement, John
did carpentry work as a hobby.

Mrs. Mehlhoff died in September 1964 and Mr. Mehlhoff in November 1980.

AUGUST and HILDEGARDE MEIDINGER

FLOYD E. MEIDINGER

Upon graduation from the University of SD School of Law in January, 1959, and
after admission to the SD State Bar in February of 1959, Floyd Meidinger began
practicing law in Mobridge, SD associating with Ivan F. Borman. Meidinger left
the Borman Law Office in March of 1960 to join State Farm Mutual Insurance
Company as a claims adjuster. After completing 2 1/2 years of service with
State Farm Insurance Company as a claims adjuster, Floyd Meidinger began his
duties as McPherson County States Attorney in January of 1963. His first office
was opened in Eureka in November of 1962 and continued until July 1, 1963 when
he began officiating in the McPherson County Courthouse in the States
Attorney's Office and continued until the end of 1976. He also engaged in
private practice during said time.

In 1965 Meidinger purchased the building located across to the east of the
Courthouse where he presently has his office.

In 1978 after the resignation of the incumbent mayor, Meidinger was elected
mayor at a special election and has been re-elected in 1980, 1982, and 1984.

After nearly 20 years of serving the county of McPherson and the city of Leola,
he contemplates continuing to engage in private law practice in the Leola and
McPherson County area and to work for the continuing good of the community.

FREDERICH and KATHERINA MEIDINGER

Frederich (Fred) Meidinger was born November 23, 1880, in Bon Homme County to
Jacob and Barbara (Fink) Meidinger. When Fred was a child he and his family
moved to McPherson County and settled on a farm in Petersburg Township
northeast of Eureka. A few years later the Meidinger family moved to a farm a
few miles southwest of Leola.

As a young man Fred worked for the railroad near Freeman and Menno, SD. In 1906
he homesteaded 3 1/2 miles south of Long Lake. He married Katherina (Katie)
Buchholz on March 28, 1908. There were five sons and six daughters born to this
union.

In 1933 Fred and Katie joined the Baptist Church. Fred participated in many of
the church activities. He was a laypreacher, Sunday School teacher, and deacon
for many years.

Fred led a useful and interesting life. He had many hobbies that filled the
hours of his days. He loved to take pictures of family and friends. All the
pictures he took he developed himself. Another of Fred's hobbies was to tend to
his swarms of bees and to sell their pure honey. Because he was a lover of
nature, Fred always had a flower garden and many fruit trees. While doing all
of these hobbies, he still had time to hunt, fish, and sell Rawleigh Products.

Fred served on the AAA Farm Program for many years. He was also on the school
board for 20 or more years. Fred, being mechanically inclined, was the
neighborhood mechanic. He also made his first radio.

Fred died August 22, 1957, at the age of 76. His wife Katie died August 17,
1974, at the age of 88. Fred's eldest son Herbert bought the farm in the '40's
and still farms the land today. Herbert has made the farm into a sizable grain
and cattle ranch.

Children of Fred and Katie Meidinger are: Herbert, born January 13, 1909, lives
on the homestead and is a farmer. He is not married.

Ruth, born February 18, 1910, was married to Theo. E. Heupeh They lived in
Aberdeen. He died November 13, 1979. They have six children.

Elsie, born September 25, 1911, died April 27, 1933.
