Huntsville, AL. They have three children.

Josephine, born January 25, 1915, is married to Melvin Buchholz, they live in
Avon, SD and have no children.

Hildagarde died in infancy.

Theodore Emmanuel, born April 11, 1918, was married to Margret Wood. He died
December 31, 1957. They had five children.

Leona, born May 21, 1920, is married to Alvin Hauck, they live in Spokane, WA.
They have six children.

Harold, born May 25, 1922, was married to Lois Johnson of Dalton, GA. He died

JACOB and BARBARA MEIDINGER

Jacob Meidinger came to America, arriving at Yankton on June 5, 1879. He filed
a homestead about 40 miles northwest of Yankton. To earn money, Jacob and his
wife, Barbara (Fink) worked for neighbors, each earning $1 a day. They lived
there five years, then in 1884 sold their homestead of 160 acres for $800. In
August of 1884, the family boarded the train from Scotland to Frederick,
shipping their possessions by freight. Since there were no roads west of
Frederick, the journey had to be continued over the rough prairie by ox team.
Recent fires had raged over the land, and the outlook for miles was one of
bleak desolation. After two days of travel, they arrived at John Becker's farm,
where they remained while inspecting the surrounding country.

        Jacob & Barbara Meidinger.

Up to this time, it was impossible to file on land due to the fact that it had
not been surveyed. This task was accomplished by October, however, and
accordingly, Jacob took up a pre-emption and timber claim, located in
Petersburg Township 15 1/2 miles northeast of Eureka. A temporary dwelling was
erected, consisting of only a roof made of boards, which was set with the eaves
on the ground. This form of dwelling was satisfactory during sunny weather,
but during a heavy rainfall the unshingled roof leaked badly and the occupants
sometimes had to sleep in the mud, soaked to the skin.

After digging a well, and making hay, these roofs were completed into sod
houses, which needless to say, were much more comfortable.

These early years were fraught with much hardship. Due to the many prairie
fires, farm property was often in danger of destruction. The snowfall during
the winter was usually very heavy, sometimes almost completely covering the
buildings. The oxen, walking over the roofs of the houses, occasionally broke
through, and the sudden appearance of an ox hoof descending from the kitchen
ceiling was not an uncommon occurrence.

Working with oxen was also, at times, a severe strain on the patience. While
plowing they would suddenly take it into their heads to run into a nearby pond,
dragging the plow along. They insisted on demonstrating their traditional
stubbornness by refusing to come out until cooled off.

School and church buildings were none during the early years. Jacob was a
charter member of the Gluckstal Reformed Church in 1887.

In 1901 the Meidingers sold their land and bought land owned by John Luce
southwest of Leola which is still being farmed by a granddaughter and her
husband, Laurence and Waneta Geffre.

Jacob and Barbara had seven children, Carrie, Fred, Adolph, Emilia, August,
Christine and Martha. Martha is the only one still living and she resides in
Minneapolis, MN.

years of high school in Leola, where he graduated with the class of 1972.

School.

FRANCIS and REBECCA MINCKS

Francis Mincks was born on April 5, 1850 in Crooked Tree, OH. He married
Rebecca Mentzer in March of 1873. In the spring of the year 1883, Francis,
along with his wife and their four children, arrived in what is now McPherson
County of South Dakota. They came on an immigrant train to homestead in Dakota
Territory, where they built a stone house southeast of Leola, SD.

        Frank & Rebecca Mincks.

Francis and Rebecca Mincks had ten children, only five of which lived to reach
adulthood. Their names were: Ella, Myron, Mary, Emmett, Edna, Iva, Obeda,
Lilly, Cecil, and Silvy. Emmett later became a state legislator in Arizona.
Ella, Myron, Cecil (Joy), and Silvy all lived in the northeastern part of South
Dakota most of their lives. Silvy is still alive and lives now in Hudson, SD.

Myron Mincks was born August 20, 1875. As a young man he had a tree claim next
to his father's homestead in McPherson County. Most of his life he spent
farming near Wetonka, and later Westport, SD. On June 28, 1916, he married Mary
Steele. To this union were born four children: Jennie, Francis, Owen, and Iona.

Jennie Mincks Ellison now resides in Miranda, CA.

Francis Mincks lives in Santa Ana, CA, where he works as a maintenance man in a
hospital.

Iona Mincks Noot lives near Stockton, MO. She and her husband have seven
children.

Owen Mincks has spent much of his life near Wetonka and Westport, SD. On March
31, 1946, he married Arlene Brown of Sioux City, IA. The early part of their
married life they farmed near Westport. In 1960 Owen was ordained a minister
with the Assemblies of God church. For nine years he was a Bible instructor at
Trinity Bible Institute. In 1970 he and his family moved to Neosho, MO, where
he taught at Ozark Bible Institute. For the past five years Owen has lived in
Mobridge, SD where he is the president of Good Shepherd Indian Bible Institute.
Arlene died September 21, 1982. Owen and Arlene had five children, Terry,
Eldon, Melba, Reeta, and Rebecca.

Terry Mincks now lives in Neosho, MO, where he is the principal of Ozark
Christian Academy. He and his wife, Linda, have one son, Seth.

Eldon Mincks is an ordained minister. He and his wife, Nanci, live in Miami,
FL. They have six children, Tony, Jason, Michala, Benge, Chanteil, and Andrew.

Melba Mincks Schauer lives in Findlay, OH where her husband, Paul, works as an

Reeta Mincks Baker and her husband, Jon, pastor a church in Wann, OK. They have
four children, Israel, Johnna, Nathan, and Amber.

Rebecca Mincks has been attending Good Shepherd Bible Institute in Mobridge,
SD.

Eugene Willforth Morrison was born on August 7, 1888 in Monticello, MN. He came

Eugene and Gladys farmed in Koto and Weber townships. Eugene and Gladys were

MELVIN and ELDORA MORRISON

Melvin Morrison was born in Arena Township September 8, 1917, to William and

Melvin is a member of the Leola Methodist Church serving many years on the

Eldora (Hoffman) Weisser was born November 16, 1930 to Carl K. and Margaret

        The Melvin Morrison Family. Back: Peter, Suzanne and Charles. Front:
        Dan, Ollie, Zachary, Eldora and Melvin.

WILLIAM and BARBARA MORRISON

William Morrison was born in Monticello, MN in 1882. He came to South Dakota as
a young boy to live with Frank Mitchell, his uncle, who lived in Weber

bought land in Koto Township. He had one brother, Eugene, and one sister, Anna.

of them.

Barbara Junge Morrison was born in Michigan in 1880 and came with her pioneer
family, Mr. and Mrs. Fredrich Junge to the Leola area. She had five brothers:

        William & Barbara Morrison.

Feickert (Alice), Sterling, CO.

The Morrison family raised Hereford cattle and grain. William was a member of
the school board, the Leola Livestock Association and the Leola Co-op. They
retired and moved into Leola. Both are deceased.

ARNOLD and VIOLA NELSON

Arnold Nelson was born August 31, 1893, in rural McPherson County to Fred and

FREEMAN and ESTELLA NELSON

Freeman Nelson was born in rural McPherson County to Fred and Mary Peterson

CARL G. and JESSIE PADE

Carl G. Pade, son of Edward L. and Bertha (Krueger) Pade was born southeast of
Leola in Washington Township on January 10, 1910. Carl spent all of his early
years on the farm and attended school in Washington Township. He had three
brothers; Henry, Fred and Albert. They enjoyed fishing, hunting and trapping
gophers and teasing their two younger sisters, Adeline and Ermina. Carl stayed
on the farm, helped his father put in the crops and was a helper on the
threshing crew. When his folks moved into Leola in 1934, he worked for his
cousin, Edgar Valentine, of Houghton, at the Standard Oil Station.

On May 6, 1939 Carl and Jessie Cole Humphrey were married and established their
home in Leola. Carl owned and operated the "Pade Recreation Parlor" for several
years. On April 1, 1943 he entered into the service of his country in WWII. He
served one year in the states and 19 months as an M.P. in the European theater
in England, France and Belgium, where he was awarded two battle stars. On
November 18, 1945 he received his honorable discharge and came back to Leola.
There he worked in his place of business until 1959, when he went into a
farming partnership with Clarence Knudson, retiring in the fall of 1974.

Carl's wife Jessie is a graduate of Roscoe High School and attended Northern
Normal and Industrial School in Aberdeen and Black Hill's Normal in Spearfish.
She taught rural schools in Edmunds, McPherson and Brown counties for 15 years.
In December, 1955 she became a bookkeeper in the Leola State Bank where she
worked 18 years, retiring in December of 1973.

        Carl & Jesie Pade.

Carl and Jessie are both members of the United Methodist Church. Carl is a
38-year member of the Roy S. Hickman Post No. 78 of the American Legion, and an
honorary member of the Leola Fire Dept., having been a member 44 years. He is
also a member of the Better Leola Club and the Comet Lodge No. 216 A.F. & A.M.
of Mound City, SD. Jessie is secretary of the Julia Circle of her church, an
honorary member of Disco Club, a 38-year member of the American Legion
Auxiliary and a Past Matron of Leola Chapter No. 124 of the Order of Eastern
Star.

G. F. and DEAN PADE

In 1881 Gottlieb Pade brought his family to America from Germany. Cold spring
was emerging from a winter mantle when they arrived at home of friends near
Ordway. However, Gottlieb ventured westward over rolling prairies as yet
unsurveyed, and found himself in another spot of trouble.

"Listen Gottlieb," the land office men were saying to him, "this land you've
settled on--it's school property. You're not supposed to be here. You've got to
go somewhere else to live."

But Gottlieb could understand little English and was intensely mystified at all
this argument, for hadn't he been told that the U.S. was the country of
opportunity, where land was had for little or nothing?

"Well, okay, Gottlieb," the land boys finally said, "you have your sod house
practically built, so maybe you can stay here after all."

So he proved up his quarter of land. It was cold out there on the prairie that
early spring of 1882. The Pades threw blankets over the wagon to protect them
from the wind. They slept on the ground until the sod house was finished.

But they, like other McPherson County folks, never gave up the contest.

G . F. Pade was born September 4, 1889. In 1906 G. F. and his brother Edward
rented the farm, and Gottlieb eventually moved to Salem, OR. In 1911, G. F.
bought out his brother's half-interest in the home place, married Emma Huntley,
a schoolteacher, and settled down to a career of his own.

        Gottlieb & Emma Pade.

The first few years that G. F. and Emma put in on the farm were years of
drouth. Every year they planted their 500 acres of crop and got nothing back.
They kept all the cows that two people could milk. Eventually tactics were
changed and the farm became a feeding unit for stock. G. F. started with
Shorthorns, then changed to Herefords. Buying and selling horses kept the farm
going during the dry years.

Two sons were born to G. F. and Emma Pade, Virgil in 1915 and Dean in 1917.
Virgil moved to Salem, OR in 1936 and Dean stayed with his dad. Both boys
graduated from Leola High School.

In 1930 G. F. and Emma moved to town, but still continued to operate the farm.

In 1942 Dean married Berniece Neuhauser, a schoolteacher in Leola, and they
moved to the "homestead" where two daughters were born: Sherry in 1947, and
Gwyn in 1949.

        The Dean Pade Family. Back: Lowell, Becky, Tracy, Gwyn, Sherry and
        Carl. Front: Scot, Berniece, Polly, Penny, Dean and Chad.

In 1954 Dean went into partnership with Herb Weisz and Donald Mack, and they
bought the sale barn. Don and Dean eventually bought out Herb and they operated
the barn for 22 years.

In 1958 Dean bought his own farm where he still farms today.

                Sherry Pade Ellwanger

Sherry graduated from Leola High School and Northern State College. She married
Carl Ellwanger of Hermosa, SD. Twin sons, Chad and Scot were born to them.
Sherry teaches Business Education in Edgemont, SD, and Carl works for the Hines
Lumber Company in Hill City, SD. They live in Custer, SD.

        Gwyn Pade Walter

Gwyn graduated from Leola High School. She married Lowell Walter of Ipswich, SD
where they live today. Gwyn attended Northern State College and is now
secretary for the United Church of Christ and does rough draft typing for a
court reporter in Aberdeen. Lowell works at the Brown County Implement Company
in Aberdeen. They have four daughters: Tracy, 16; Becky, 12; Polly, five; and
Penny, three years old.

EDWARD L. and BERTHA PADE

Edward L. Pade, son of Gottlieb and Magdalena (Conrad) Pade was born on the
home farm in Washington Township south of Leola, August 5, 1883. His father
filed a claim on the SWI/4 of Section 16 in Washington Township on September 2,

Ed and Bertha raised six children; four boys and two girls: Henry (his wife

        Bertha & Edward Pade.

served as its first president. In 1936 they moved to Salem, OR where Ed worked
for Paulus Cannery until his retirement. Bertha passed away November 25, 1969

VIRGIL and LOIS PADE

Virgil L. Pade was born in Leola, SD on March 7, 1915. He attended school
there, and after graduating from high school, left for Oregon in 1936. There he
worked for his uncle, Ben Pade, who was in the grocery business, until 1941.

July, and a girl, Magdelaine, four years old. They live in Aloha, OR.

Virgil and Lois still are Oregon State basketball and football fans. and travel
with them for fun.

JOHN LYSANDER and MARYETTE PIERCE

John Lysander Pierce and Maryette (Hakes) Pierce, with their four children;
Nathan, Colonel, Frank and Alta, came to Ordway, SD in the spring of 1884. They
traveled in an emigrant railroad car. They hauled their things across the
prairie and settled in Washington Township on Section 8. John hauled supplies
from Ipswich by team and wagon. His family became a part of the community and
soon his daughter, Alta, worked in the County Courthouse and his sons began
farming. Frank farmed near Leola until 1913 when he moved into Leola. Colonel
farmed until 1920 when he moved to the state of Washington. Nathan filed a tree
claim one mile north of Section 8 and farmed there for many years. John died in
1893 and Maryette and her daughter went back to Tampico, IL to live.

NATHAN and REBECCA PIERCE

Nathan Pierce came to Leola with his parents, John and Maryette (Hakes) Pierce
in 1884. Rebecca Chappel came to Eureka in 1889. She was employed in Eureka
until she married Nathan Pierce October, 1894. They lived on a farm near Leola.
Nathan filed a tree claim in Washington Township and they lived with their
family on that farm for many years. The couple were blessed with five children:
Maryette, born December 16, 1896; Elizabeth, born April 15, 1898; Helen, born
March 11, 1900; Alice, born July 19, 1901; and one son who was born in 1903 and
died in 1905.

Nathan saw many changes through the years. He farmed with horses for several
years and was one of the first farmers with a tractor. His first was a Mogul,
followed by an Avery. His right hand was his daughter, Maryette (Sears), who
helped with all the field work and was the one to drive his first tractors.
They also did their own threshing.

        The Nathan Pierce Family.

Rebecca passed away in 1921 and Nathan quit farming in 1922. Nathan married
Isabel Robinson in 1922. They spent the winter in Ipswich, SD. In the fall of
1923, Nathan, Isabel and Maryette went to Washington and spent the winter with
Nathan's brother, Colonel. In the spring of 1924, they went to California.
Nathan and Maryette came back to South Dakota in the summer of 1927 and
Maryette decided to stay in Leola. Nathan went back to California. He remained
there until his death in 1955.

AUGUST and WILHELMINA PISCHKE

Following the lead of his sister, Caroline, in becoming an early settler in
northeastern Leola Township, August Pischke acquired ownership of the SE 1/4 of
Section 10 by pre-emption in October 1884. Two years later sister Hattie became
owner of the NE 1/4 of the same section of land. While both sisters left Leola
later, August remained in the community and subsequently developed his land
ownership and farm operation centered around Section 19 of western Willow
Township.

August was one of nine children who grew up near Princeton, WI, after his
parents, Daniel and Wilhelmina Pischke, had immigrated from Oschek in the
province of Posen, Germany in July 1860. After getting a sufficient start in
farming, August married Wilhelmina Dreblow, a young, sociable woman whom he had
grown to know while he lived in Wisconsin. Wilhelmina's parents lived at
Marquette, WI, where they too, had immigrated from Oschek in Posen, Germany.
The Pischkes had been one of the charter members of the German Lutheran Church
when it was formed in July 1887.

Eight children were born in the Pischke family: Henry, Lena, William, Daniel,
Reinhold, Edward, Walter and Rueben. Edward and Walter married two women from
Leola--Ada Fosler and Christine Opp. They were the daughters of the Charlie
Fosler and Daniel D. Opp families.

        Ed, Will and Dan Pischke.

Besides the five quarters that the Pischkes owned, they rented an additional
300 acres to raise crops and to support livestock. After the elder Pischkes
retired from active farming in 1917, sons Edward and William operated the farm
in 1918. Then for the next ten years, Walter and Christine farmed the land.
Eventually adverse weather conditions that produced poor crops, and low farm
prices forced Walter and Christine to abandon the farm and to move to
Minneapolis, where they operated an auto body repair shop with brothers
Reinhold and Rueben.

The Pischke children attended several rural schools in western Willow Township
and were taught by such teachers as Bert Hurst and Pearl McGee. One of the most
exciting forms of entertainment in the early 1900's recalled by Walter and
Christine Pischke, was the dances which were held at the barns of such farms as
the Kesslers and Hauffes during the summer months, and the "kitchen sweats"
during the winter months. Taking his father's advice that one should acquire
something that increases in value with the passage of time, Walter purchased a
violin and learned to play it well. He and his brother Dan served as alternate
musicians to Johnny and Annie Kessler, who played the violin and piano at
dances. Other bands in the area were the Rapp brothers, and Rod and Ree
Roynane. Walter and Dan delighted in playing "Redwing" and "Turkey in the
Straw" as the floors throbbed to the rhythm of the dancers' feet. Older
brothers Ed and William also worked as a team of musicians at dances in the
community. The four boys apparently inherited their musical talent from their
father who himself was proficient in playing violin and accordion.

August and Wilhelmina Pischke died in 1937 and 1933, respectively and are laid
at rest at Lakeland, FL. Three of their children, Henry, Lena and David are
buried at Leola's Green Mound Cemetery.

JOHN PORTER

Mr. and Mrs. John Porter, Jessie, John and Dorothy moved from Lake Beulah, WI
to Westport, SD in the spring of 1909. They lived on a farm east of Westport
until the fall of 1909, when they moved to Leola. They ran a large herd of
cattle on what was then cheap state land. In 1910 they built a home on the
ranch and lived there until 1913. They then moved to a farm just west of Leola
and farmed there until March, 1916, when they purchased the "Home Hotel" in
Leola. They remodeled the hotel and changed the name to "The Virginia," after
their first grandchild. It was the social spot in Leola for several years,
serving banquets, clubs, and parties for the people in the area. The Porters
made their home there for 33 years.

John Jr. enlisted in the Navy in WWI, and served the duration. He taught school
around Leola for 12 years and bought Galloway cattle with the money he saved.
Later he and his father changed to Aberdeen Angus cattle, and developed a large
herd.

Jessie died in 1927. The older children, Ray, Mae and Beula married and lived
in Wisconsin. Mae died in Milwaukee in 1925 and left two young sons, Robert and
Edward Morris. They came to Leola to live with their grandparents until they
graduated from high school. They then returned to Wisconsin and attended the
University of Wisconsin for four years each.

Mr. Porter Sr. was elected mayor of Leola and served until 1925. The family was
of the Catholic faith. Mrs. Porter died in May, 1939. Mr. Porter died in April,
1940. John Jr. and Dorothy lived at the hotel until September 1948, when it was
badly damaged by fire. They rebuilt the hotel and made several apartments. They
sold the hotel to A. J. Shafer of Leola. It has changed hands several times,
but as of now the Elmer Zulks live there. Later the Porters had a small house
built in the east part of town and managed a very successful herd of Angus
cattle. They sold to and started many young men in South Dakota in the Angus
business. They also had out-of-state buyers from Wisconsin, California and
several in Canada.

John Jr. died in July 1974, and Dorothy Porter, the only remaining member of
the family, still lives in Leola.

ALVIN and MARGARET POTRATZ

Margaret Hammrich and Alvin Potratz were married on August 6, 1949. Margaret
was the first of 12 children born to John P. and Anna Hammrich, and Alvin was
the first born to Reinhold and Bertha (Guthmiller) Potratz.

        Margaret & Alvin Potratz.

Alvin and Margaret made their home on a farm west of Leola for several years
until they moved to Leola, where both were employed. Margaret worked as a
waitress and Alvin worked 22 years for the SD Division of Highways in Dist. No.
1.

Margaret has a hobby of collecting little shoes. The first pair was given her
by her mother and is about 75 years old. She has a large collection of them.
Alvin likes to collect old tools.

Margaret and Alvin are members of St. James Lutheran Church.

FERDINAND and AUGUSTA POTRATZ

Ferdinand Frederick Potratz was born in Dobberkuhl, Pommerania, Germany,
January 17, 1849. He apparently lived in this area until after his marriage to
Augusta Reunzel who was born in Volzin, Pommerania, Germany on July 25, 1851.
Ferdinand and Augusta were married October 4, 1874 and moved to Stettin,
Pommerania where Ferdinand worked in a saw mill. Fourteen children were born to
this union. Seven died in infancy. The surviving children were: Martha
(Joireman), Paul, Mary (Breitag) Richard, Reinhold, Minna Louisa (Fischer) and
Otto.

        Ferdinand & Augusta Potratz.

In the year 1883, the Potratz family migrated from Stettin, Germany to the
state of Minnesota. They were most unhappy with the hilly, rocky land and after
a year's stay, they decided to try their luck in the state of South Dakota.
Arriving in Leola in 1884, they filed a tree claim in Washington Township on
Section 33.

Ferdinand became a legal citizen of the U.S. on June 15, 1899. In 1902 on May
1, Ferdinand filed a claim on Section 24-126-68 which lies 1 1/2 miles west and
one-half mile south of Leola. They lived there until their retirement in 1918
when they moved to Leola. Augusta lived in Leola only three years before she
passed away on May 12, 1921.

Ferdinand spent some of his last years with his son, Otto, who farmed in Koto
Township and his daughter, Martha Joireman, who lived in Spring Township.

Ferdinand was known as a religious, kind man who never spoke a harsh word of
anyone. He was one of the charter members of the St. James Lutheran Church in
Leola. His many friends and family mourned when he left them on March 25, 1937.

REINHOLD and BERTHA POTRATZ

Reinhold Johann Potratz and Bertha Rose Guthmiller were married March 27, 1912
at Leola. Their first home was southeast of Leola. Then they moved to a farm 2
1/2 miles southwest of Leola. Later they moved to a farm 6 1/2 miles northwest
of Leola, where they lived until they retired and moved to Leola in 1949.

        Reinhold & Bertha Potratz.

Reinhold passed away December 31, 1951 at Leola. Bertha lives in the Aberdeen
Nursing Center in Aberdeen. They were members of St. James Lutheran Church.

Their children are: Alvin, born November 23, 1912 at Leola, married Margaret
Hammrich and lives in Leola; Edgar, born at Billings, MT September 18, 1914 and
lives in Texas; Adeline, born January 29, 1919 at Leola, married Jake Hammrich,
(Adeline passed away December 24, 1963); Viola, born September 11, 1923 at
Leola, and lives in California; Reinhardt, born September 23, 1925 at Leola,
married to Josie Ettles, and lives in Leola; Elwood, born December 10, 1927 at
Leola, passed away October 10, 1959; Ervin, born September 23, 1931 at Leola,
married Bonnie Sagre, and lives in Lead, SD.

EDWIN and ELSIE RALL

Edwin Rall, the son of John and Christina Rall, was born July 21, 1918, on a
farm nine miles north of Long Lake, SD, where he grew up and helped with the
farming.

In 1942, Edwin entered the Army, serving in the 95th Infantry Division. He
spent one year overseas. He was discharged from the service in September 1945.

        Edwin & Elsie Rall.

Edwin was united in marriage to Elsie Schock. Elsie was born on June 21, 1925.

In the late '40's, they purchased the Standard Oil Station, operating it in
conjunction with the International Harvester Dealership in Long Lake,
established as Rall's Implement, which he purchased in 1951. The business was
sold in 1971.

In 1972, Ed was elected Treasurer of McPherson County. He served in this
capacity until June 1983, when he retired.

Ed has been active in the community and in the town of Long Lake. He has served
on the town board for many years, serving as mayor for at least 15 of those
years. He has served as a fire chief and legion commander. Ed and Elsie are the
parents of two daughters. Joann married Dale Moench, they live in Devils Lake,
ND. They have one daughter and one son. Dale is employed with the National
Guard.

Karen married Tom Herron and lives in Denver, CO. Tom is employed in a bakery,
Karen by an insurance company.

GORDON and DELORES RATH

Gordon, with his parents Chris C. and Anna, moved from the Long Lake area to

Serving his country for two years, he spent 18 months in Korea. After

JOHN and MARTHA RATH

John was born to John and Christina (Jesser) Rath on June 22, 1902 near Long

He started working for Leola Oil Company in 1928 when it was owned by

        The John Rath Family. Back: Laurie, Viva, Orley, John, Martha, Mickey.

ERVIN E. and LILA R. RAU

        Lila, Ervin, Jenny, Pam and insert Randy Rau.

FRED and MAGDALENA RAU

Fred Rau was born on July 16, 1897 at Long Lake to Jacob and Magdalena

REV. K. J. and LOUISE REIMER

Pastor Karl J. Reimer was born and grew up at Elkader, IA, where he attended
and graduated from high school and junior college. He received his B.A. degree
at the University of Southern California; then studied at Wartburg Theological
Seminary at Dubuque, IA for three years. He served a three point parish in
Alberta, Canada for a year, and then Christ Lutheran Church at Luther College
in Regina, Sask. for six years.

There in Regina he met and married Louise Kroeger, a native of Saskatchewan,
the daughter of a pioneer Lutheran pastor. She graduated from the Moose Jaw
Collegiate and from business college, and was employed in Regina by the Dept.
of Public Health, Government of Sask. Four sons were born to this marriage.

From 1945 to 1949 they lived at Moose Jaw, Sask. from where Pastor Reimer
served four congregations and also supplied other congregations of the area.

From 1949 to 1957 they lived at Neche, ND, serving also a congregation at
Gretna, Manitoba, Canada. Then from January 1957 until November 1958 they
served at Verona, ND, from whence they moved to Leola.

At Leola Pastor Reimer served St. James Lutheran Church, and also Hope Lutheran
Church in Hoffman Township until it disbanded at the end of 1960. During those
years he and the St. James Men's Choir participated regularly in the German
radio services sponsored by Lutheran congregations of the area. The present
parsonage and the educational unit of St. James Church were built and paid for
during his ministry. Mrs. Reimer was active teaching in the church school,
serving as organist, and giving private piano lessons.

At the end of October 1970 the Reimers left Leola for a rural parish near
Monticello, IA, where they served through August 1978, retiring to Muscatine,
IA. In 1979 he was asked to supply the Lutheran Church of the Good Shepherd in
Wellman, IA, and still serves them. Mrs. Reimer serves as organist and teacher.

Children in the Reimer family are: William, Robert, Richard and James.

William, born at Regina, Sask., Canada. He married Annette Roepke of Aurora,
IA. They have two children, Janet and David, and live in Muscatine, IA. William
is a pharmacist and runs the Nietzel Pharmacy in Muscatine.

Robert, born at Regina, Sask., Canada. Robert is an ordained Lutheran minister
and has organized mission congregations in St. Edward and Albion, NE. He
married Connie Bokelmann of Belgrade, NE in 1973. They have four children:
Amanda, Erik, Nikolas and Timothy.

Richard, born at Moose Jaw, Sask., Canada. Richard married his high school
classmate, Patricia J. Fewings of Leola. They are the parents of two children,
Christie and Bradley. They live in Huron, SD, where Richard teaches in Huron's
high school.

James, born at Altona, Man., Canada. He married Diane Mecchi, R.N. of
Pawtucket, RI in 1977. Since 1982 he has been in private practice of Internal
Medicine at Hyannis, MA, specializing in renal medicine and kidney dialysis. He
and his wife have a son, Christopher, born in 1982.

REV. WILLIAM and MARGARET REINECKE

The name "Reinecke" became common in Leola only after the Christmas of 1919,
because it was on December 14 of that year that Rev. William Reinecke came to
Leola in answer to a call from the St. James Lutheran Church to serve as its
pastor. Coming from north central Iowa and traveling by way of the Minneapolis
and St. Louis Railroad, he brought with him his wife and six children.

Pastor Reinecke was born in Koeckte, a little village of Germany in the area of
Gardelegen, which is now 16 miles behind the Iron Curtain. After graduation
from the Missions Haus in Hermansburg in 1899, he came to the United States and
was ordained into the Lutheran Ministry in Ohio. It was there that he married
Margaret Blumenschein, a daughter of an established farmer near Marysville.

        The William Reinecke Family. Back: Clara, Johanna, Erna and Hattie.
        Front: Margaret, William, Erwin and Martin.

Johanna, the oldest of the children, taught school for many years and married
John J. Guthmiller, Leola. They had three children: Margaret, Harold and Arlen.
(See John J. Guthmiller history.)

Clara married William Bash of Portland, IN. They had two sons, Ewald and
William. Both sons are ordained Lutheran pastors. Clara died in 1978 and death
had taken her husband earlier, in 1972.

Martin married Alma Gramita of Kulm, ND. They have three children: Mary,
married to Dennis Potter, lives in Pierre; Hannelore, married to Thomas Tweed,
lives in Chicago; and Max, who opened the Reinecke Chiropractic Clinic in Sioux
Falls in 1982.

Hattie, after teaching school in the state for many years, married Joseph
(Chip) E. Bell. They live in Dubuque, IA. The Bell children are: Nancy, married
to Donald Dalzell; and Timothy, married to Vaughn Rinner of Des Moines.

Erwin married Erna Koosman, a Wisconsin native and they live in Santa Rosa, CA.
They have two sons, Tom and John, and one daughter, Kathy.

Erna married James Gray of Detroit and she has lived in that city ever since.
They had two children, Bill, who lives at home and Barbara, who is married to
Richard Schmitt. Erna's husband, James died in 1962.

Pastor Reinecke served St. James, and for many years Hope and Salem Lutheran
congregations during his 22 years in Leola. In 1941 he accepted a call to
Bridgewater, SD to serve the Wolf Creek congregation there. Mrs. Reinecke, who
had been confined to a wheel chair for many years because of arthritis, died in
Bridgewater in 1942. Pastor Reinecke died there in 1946. They lie buried in
Springfield. MN.

HENRY J. and KATIE RENSCHLER

Henry J. Renschler was born to Henry J. Renschler, Sr. and Katherine Renschler.
In 1908 he married Katie Zumbaum, daughter of John Zumbaum and Rosina (Maier)
Zumbaum. They began farming about 13 miles west of Leola. Three children were
born to this union: Esther (Mrs. Roy Mounce) in 1909, Hank in 1913, and Herbert
in 1924.

        Katie, Herbert, Henry Jr., Esther and Hank Renschler.

The family moved to Leola in 1918, where Henry J. had a garage west of the
Catholic church. He sold Chevrolet cars and Maxwell trucks. They lived across
the street from the business, in a two-story house, which is still there. It is
now the Albert Breunig home.

In the spring of 1921, they moved 13 miles southwest of Leola to farm. Henry
built a house and barn there, and farmed until 1926, when the family returned
to Leola, and bought cream for the Sunlight Produce Company. Esther was her
father's partner in the business. They moved their farm house into town and set
it on a full basement, which housed their cream business. This is presently the
Fred Jundt home, located across the street from the courthouse.

Henry J. and family moved to Lodi, CA, in 1932. In 1941, he died, and Katie
remained in Lodi until her death in 1968.

Esther Renschler and Roy Mounce came back to Leola and were married in the
spring of 1933. They operated the cream business until October, when they
returned to Lodi. They owned and operated a machine and welding shop until
Roy's death in 1967. Roy and Esther had three sons: Roland, Marvin and Leland,
and five grandchildren. Esther lived in Lodi until her death December 13, 1983.

Hank Renschler had a garage in Lodi, and later worked for the school as a
superintendent of transportation. He has two sons, two grandchildren, two
step-children and five step-grandchildren. Hank and his wife are retired in
Lodi.

Herbert Renschler lived in Angwin, CA. He married Mary Jane Gaede in 1942, and
died of a kidney ailment in 1948.

        Gerald J. and Carl.

Carl and Evelyn had four children: Leo, born May 5, 1930, married Lorentina
Weisz on October 10, 1955; Carl Jr., born December 30, 1932, married Evelyn B.
Stengel January 2, 1954; Larry, born September 9, 1938, married Lorella Dosch
November 29, 1958; and Gerald J., born March 3, 1948.

Evelyn is a member of the United Methodist Church, Julia Circle, UMCW, and the
Leola Country Club.

ELDON and GRACE ROGERS

Eldon Rogers, son of Noah Rogers, was born February 28, 1884 in Adair, IA. He
moved to Illinois after the turn of the century. A few years later he met Grace
Sells, a former schoolteacher of Basco, IL. They were married in March of 1907.
Two sons were born: Carl, on February 16, 1908 and Clifton, on July 3, 1909.
Carl passed away April 14, 1974.

        The Eldon Rogers Family.

Eldon and Grace made their home on a farm south of Basco until the year of 1910
when they moved on a farm nine miles north of Leola. May 14, 1915, a baby girl,
Zella, was born, bringing joy and happiness to the family. Another child,
Irvin, was born June 28, 1924, completing the Rogers family. The Rogers
continued to farm until Eldon's health failed and he passed away April, 14,
1950. Grace moved to Leola in the fall of 1950 and Irvin took over the family
farm. Grace maintained her home in Leola until her health began to fail. She
spent her last few years with her daughter, Zella, of Stockton, CA. She passed
away April 17, 1975. Her last wish was to be laid to rest by her husband's side
in the Green Mound Cemetery, south of Leola.

Eldon and Grace were members of the United Methodist Church in Leola. Eldon was
a member of the Masonic Lodge and Grace was a charter member of the Eastern
Star and the Country Club.

MICHAEL OLIVER and MARY RONAYNE

In the early 1880's, Michael Oliver Ronayne, who was born in Ireland, came to
South Dakota, which was then a territory. He worked as a printer on newspapers
in Huron and Yankton. In 1887 he returned to Iowa and married Mary Grimes. They
had been friends since childhood. They returned to White Lake, SD, where their
first daughter, Ree, was born in 1888.

        Michael Ronayne.

Michael was in Yankton when statehood was attained in 1889. He moved his family
to Sioux City, IA in 1891 and a son, Roderick was born. Their next move was to
Aberdeen, SD, where Michael's relatives lived. From there they moved to Leola,
where he was involved in the founding of the McPherson County Herald. They then
moved to Eureka where Ronayne and Theodore Giedt started the Northwest Blade.
Ronayne then returned to Aberdeen where he was employed by the Dakota Farmer.
Two sons, Thomas and Felix, were born while they lived in Aberdeen. The family
moved to Leola in 1902. Michael was no longer able to work at printing, due to
an accident which nearly blinded one eye. He started the Leola Creamery and
spent the rest of his life in that business. He sent his son, Roderick, to
Brookings College to learn the buttermaking trade. Another daughter, Constance,
was born in Leola.

Rod and Ree were musicians, playing in the Leola Concert Band and an orchestra
which played for dances. Ree played the piano in the orchestra and was also
Catholic church organist for 40 years. She taught country school and later was
deputy in three different county offices for 20 years.

Thomas and Felix grew up in the creamery business. Later they both worked as
field representatives for large creamery companies.

Constance taught rural school and was Deputy County Superintendent of Schools.
She married John Chesire of Aberdeen, SD and they moved to Bismarck in 1939,
where he was Superintendent of an electric generating plant at Mandan, ND until
his retirement. John passed away in December of 1978.

All of the Ronayne family has passed away except Constance (Mrs. John Chesire)
who lives in Bismarck, ND.

BENJAMIN and LILLIAN ROTT

Benjamin Rott was born on September 18, 1915 at Fredonia, ND to Jacob and
Christina (Schaffer) Rott. His parents were both born in south Russia.

Ben married Lillian Joachim on October 14, 1935 at the Joachim Church 14 miles
north of Eureka. Lillian was born to William and Elizabeth (Iszler) Joachim on
April 21, 1915 at Greenway, SD. Ben and Lillian lived at Ashley until the fall
of 1942 when they moved to a run down farm three miles south of Leola. With
lots of hard work the farm flourished, as did their family. Earl was born
November 29, 1936; Sylvia, April 29, 1942; Cynthia, August 15, 1946; and
Monica, on February 9, 1958.

In 1955 Rempfer and Rott started an implement dealership with International
Harvester Co. Located on the west edge of Leola. Nineteen sixty-one brought
many changes; the implement partnership was dissolved and the name was changed
to Rott Implement. Ben and Lillian moved to town but continued the farming
operation for ten more years.

        Sylvia, Lillian, Earl, Ben, Cynthia and Monica Rott.

Ben has been active in many community organizations, such as Better Leola Club
and 4-H leadership. Lillian and Ben are very active members of the Leola United
Methodist Church. Ben has put his hobby and talents of woodworking to use by
designing and crafting the altar crosses and spearheading much of the
remodeling project on the Leola Methodist Church in 1982. Many other churches
have benefited from the labors of his love in working with wood.

EARL and SYLVIA ROTT

Earl James Rott was born in Ashley, ND on November 27, 1936 to Bennie and
Lillian (Joachim) Rott. In the fall of 1942 he moved with his parents to Leola,
SD to the present farm site which is 3 1/2 miles south of Leola.

Earl attended Washington Township school for eight years. In the fall of 1951
he started his freshman year at Leola High School and graduated in 1955. He
attended college in LaMars, IA, Vermillion, SD and NSC in Aberdeen, SD. During
his school years he helped on his father's farm and Rott Implement. In 1962 he
went into full-time farming.

Earl married Sylvia M. Weigel in 1966. They lived on the farm until the fall of
1969 when they moved to Mitchell, SD, where Earl was employed with Production
Credit Association. In the summer of 1971, they moved back to Leola and Earl
took over the family farm when Bennie retired.

Earl and Sylvia have six children: Shawna, Kalie, Tarri, Jamie, ReEtta and
Travis.

FRED and LENA ROTT

Fred, son of Jacob and Christina Rott, was born and raised at Fredonia, ND. In
1937 he married Lena Pfeifle of Venturia, ND. They made their home in Ashley,
ND. In April of 1942 they bought the George Witte farm and moved to Leola, SD.
Fred spent his spare time buying livestock and feeding cattle.

        Lena, Gerald and Fred Rott.

One son was born to them, Gerald, in November of 1944. After serving in the
Vietnam conflict, he returned to Leola and married Shirley Hayes of Leola. They
have one daughter, Shirlee, born in 1974. They reside on the family farm, which
Gerald has operated since his father passed away on September 10, 1974. Lena
also makes her home on the family farm.

CHRISTOPH and PAULINE RUEB

Christoph Rueb was born April 10, 1887 in McPherson County, Arena Township. His
father Fredrick, and mother Barbara were married in Russia before they came to
the United States. Christoph had four brothers and eight sisters. Christoph was
a farmer all his life. Christoph remembers the hard times the pioneers that
settled in South Dakota had. Along with a limited supply of food, they had to
endure the cold winters with snow and blizzards followed by hot summers. He
vividly remembers when Leola almost burned down. He was very young but still
remembers when his father came home with the news. He showed the family some of
the goods and clothing he rescued from the flaming store.

        The Christoph Rueb Family. Back: Leona, Ernest and Luella. Front:
        Freda, Christoph, Paulina and Melvin.

Christoph married Paulina Feiock November 12, 1912. Her parents lived east of
Eureka. Paulina and Christoph were parents of seven children: Freda married Ray
Kelley and they had one daughter, Judith (Kanfield) and one son, Vernon. They
each have two children. Luella married Clarence Blake. They had two daughters,
Mavis (Fowler) and Barbara (Searcy). Mavis has two children and Barbara has
one. Leona married Arnold Eichelberg. They have one son, Dwight, who has three
children. Ernest married Irene Binder. They have one daughter, Marjorie
(Baumann) and she has two sons. Melvin was a twin to Erna. Erna passed away at
six months of age. Melvin married Lylla Maisch and they have two sons, Chris
and Craig. There was another child, a boy, that passed away shortly after he
was born.

Paulina passed away May 14, 1983. They celebrated their 70th wedding
anniversary on November 12, 1982. Christoph is now living in Glendale, AZ.

JACOB F. and MAGDALENA RUEB

Jacob F. Rueb, son of Frederick and Barbara (Rueb) Rueb, born on October 30,
1882, came to the United States with his parents at the age of two, from
Kassel, Russia. They first settled at Tyndall, SD, living there for one year,
before moving northwest of Ipswich, SD. There they unloaded their belongings
from the railroad cars, and came by wagon to establish a home in Arena
Township, McPherson County. On November 22, 1907, Jacob was united in marriage
to Magdalena Lechner, daughter of Nickolas and Barbara Lechner. They made their
home on a farm 12 miles west of Leola.

        Jacob & Magdalena Rueb.

They were blessed with 13 children. Three children died in infancy. Living were
Edward, Frieda, Walter, Lavina, Harold, Florence, Adeline, Erline, Wesley,
Willis. They lived on that farm until retirement and then moved to Leola in
October 1944. Jacob died on November 25, 1949, due to a stroke. Magdalena then
married Gottlieb Eiseman of Wishek, ND on October 2, 1959. Gottlieb passed
away, leaving Magdalena a widow again. Magdalena died on May 31, 1967, after
having surgery.

Three children have passed away; Edward, Harold, Walter.

Jacob and Magdalena attended the Baptist Church. Jacob was a longtime Sunday
School teacher.

WALTER and VIVIAN RUEB

Walter Rueb, son of Jacob F. Rueb and Magdelena (Lechner) Rueb, was barn on
January 23, 1914 in McPherson County 15 miles west of Leola, where he grew up
on the farm. He married Vivian Albrecht on October 25 1942. Vivian was born
April 30, 1923. After their marriage they established their home in the city of
Leola.

In his early years he helped on the farm operated by his father and other
family members. He later spent some time in the beet fields and railroads in
the Yakima and Monroe, WA area. In 1938 he returned home and then started his
career as a salesman for the J. R. Watkins Co. of Winona, MN. Walter served
this farm community and city selling household and farm products. Later he also
sold vitamins and minerals for cattle. He served this community for 43 years
before his passing on November 5, 1981. He also served as deacon for many
years, and as Sunday School teacher for more than 30 years in the First Baptist
Church, where they were members. He also served in local community services.
Vivian has operated her beauty salon for the past 41 years and is still
operating the shop at the present time.

        Walter, Vivian, Karen, Gwen and Sandra Rueb.

To this union three daughters were born: Sandra, born August 13, 1943, married
Lee Ehlers. They have two sons, Jason and Travis, and live in Sioux Falls, SD.
Gwen, born October 21, 1947, married Jeff Smith. They live in Grand Junction,
CO. Gwen is employed with community services as a vocational trainer for
developmental service. Karen, born March 25, 1956, lives in Stamford, CT with
her daughter Sonja. She is employed as a buyer for Waldenbooks Inc. Co.
Sandra, Gwen, and Karen are LHS graduates.

WESLEY and VERNA RUEB

Wesley Rueb was born May 5, 1928 to Jacob and Magdalena (Lechner) Rueb at
Leola, SD. He married Verna Ernst June 19, 1949.

Verna was born December 10, 1927 at Hosmer, SD. Her parents are Eugene and Mary
(Schick) Ernst.

Verna and Wesley made their home in Leola, SD for many years. They are former
owners of the Jack and Jill Store.

Three children were born to the Ruebs. They are as follows: Glenda Rae, who
graduated from LHS and is now married to John Shepela; Gary Dean, graduated
from LHS, and is married to Sandra Hoffman; and Gavin, who lives with his
parents in Aberdeen, SD, where he is attending school.

JACOB and CHRISTINE RUEDE

Jacob and Christine (Glaser) Ruede came to Howard Township, McPherson County in
1907 from Freeman, SD, where Christine had been born. Jacob had come from south
Russia at the age of seven, with an older brother. Three children, Ramona,
Reuben and Noneta were born in Freeman. Hugo and Eckbert were born in McPherson
County.

The family lived on the Glaser homestead and Jacob did masonry work and helped
area farmers. He passed away in 1910. Christine moved to a house on her
brother's farm, living there until the fall of 1914, when she moved the family
into Leola.

She did housework and occasionally acted as midwife in the area. The children
did odd jobs when they became old enough.

Christine married Fred Hoff in 1918. They had one child, Viola. Fred passed
away in the 1930s. During the depression Christine worked on relief projects
(sewing, etc.).

Christine died October 1, 1955.

Ramona (Mrs. Art Weishaar) is the only one of the children living in Leola at
present. Hugo has lived in California since the 1930s, presently living in
Redding. Reuben has lived in Washington since the 1940s and presently resides
near Washougal. Eckbert, who also made his home in California for many years,
died in 1973. Noneta, (Mrs. Paul Krambeal), lived in the Ipswich area before
moving to Oregon. Her husband died in 1963 and she died about five years ago.
Viola Hoff married Richard Hammerich. They moved to Washington in the 1940s.
Richard died about five years ago and Viola presently makes her home in
Washougal.

Ramona, Eckbert, and Viola all graduated from Leola High School. Ramona taught
country school for six years before her marriage to Arthur Weishaar.

ENOCH and VIOLET SCHAFFER

Enoch E. Schaffer was born at Ashley, ND to Gottlieb and Sarah (Herman)
Schaffer, on January 18, 1920.

Violet L. Schaffer is the daughter of Otto J. and Paulina (Harter) Walz. She
was born at Ashley, ND on May 27, 1922.

        Enoch & Violet Schaffer.

After Enoch and Violet's marriage on April 12, 1942, they both taught schools
at Ashley, ND. In 1944 they moved to Leola, where Enoch started work for Mr.
Kulm at the Ford Garage. Violet taught country schools in Washington and Spring
townships for four years. Since then she has been employed with Agricultural
Stabilization and Conservation Service. Enoch worked several years for Kulms
until he and Oscar Maier purchased the Chrysler-Plymouth and John Deere Garage
from Jim Ferkin. Enoch sold his share to Oscar Maier when he was appointed
Director of Equalization in 1957, serving the county five years. Since then he
has been a representative for Northwestern National and Continental General
Insurance Companies.

Enoch has been active with the Leola Fire Department and has served as mayor of
Leola. The Schaffers are members of the St. James Lutheran Church.

They have two children: Jim, married to Mary Spitzer of Leola (has two
children); and Colin Schaffer, who lives in Lafeyette, CO.

JAMES R. and MARY LOU SCHAFFER

Jim is the oldest son of Enoch and Violet Schaffer of Leola, SD, born in
Waverly, IA. He has one brother, Colin. Jim was united in marriage to Mary Lou
Spitzer on August 11, 1968 in the St. James Lutheran Church at Leola. Mary is
the youngest daughter of Alfard and Lydia Spitzer of Leola and was born in
Eureka, SD. Mary has two sisters and one brother: Violet (Mrs. Arthur Bertsch)
of Aberdeen, SD; Roy Spitzer of Rapid City, SD; and Linda (Mrs. W. P. Schmit)
of Flushing, MI. Jim and Mary are both graduates of Leola High School. They
have two children, Jay and Jan. Jim has been employed by the USDA Soil
Conservation Service since 1964 and Mary has been employed by the Leola School
District since 1969.

        The James Schaffer Family. Back: Jay, Mary and James. Front: Jan.

PHILIP and CHRISTINA SCHAEFFER

Philip was born to John and Louise (Wills) Schaeffer on August 26, 1866 in
Neudorf, South Russia. He was married in the Vineche Lutheran Church on
February 14, 1894 in Russia. He married Christina, the daughter of Christian
and Carolina (Schwartzwalder) Wagemann. Christina was born in Neudorf, South
Russia on July 12, 1867.

Philip's mother died at about 26 years of age. The father then put the children
into an orphanage. Philip was about seven years old at the time. There were
three brothers: August, who made it out of Russia and then into Canada, from
there to California. He was killed and robbed while mining for gold, (newspaper
accounts). John, who came to America, settled in Nebraska. Gottlieb--there is
no record of his coming to America.

        Christina & Philip Schaeffer.

On September 12, 1906 Philip and Christina came to America on a ship called the
Barbarossa. They docked at the harbor in New York. They went to North Dakota
and lived for a time with Christina's brother, Daniel. They later settled on a
homestead in Wacker Township, SW Section 15, Township 128, Range 68, in
McPherson County.

Philip and Christina were the parents of 11 children: Jacob, Christ and
Christina died in Russia.

John, born May 20, 1892, died December 28, 1926 and is buried at Leola, SD. He
married Pauline Bollinger of Forbes, ND.

Phillip, born April 7, 1895, died November 11, 1963 and is buried at Leola. He
married Mathilda Merkel of Forbes, ND and then Mary Marie Schwartz of Napoleon,
ND.

August, born May 24, 1897, died June 20, 1982 and is buried at Eureka, SD. He
married Martha Zelmer of Long Lake, SD.

Magdalena, born July 12, 1904, died April 9, 1962 and is buried at Leola. She
married Wilhelm Rohrbach of Long Lake.

Fredrick, born October 9, 1906, died May 11, 1980 and is buried at Spokane, WA.
He married Ellatine R. Freund.

Lydia, born October 12, 1908, died in 1942 in a house fire and is buried at
Glasgow, MT. She married Martin Kappes of Long Lake.

Theophila, born May 28, 1910 and married Martin Lux (deceased) of North Dakota.

Pauline, born October 12, 1911, died January 3, 1980 and is buried at Ashley,
ND. She married Christ Lux of North Dakota.

On October 28, 1928 Philip and Louise moved to Leola. Wilhelm and Magdalena
Rohrbach took over the family homestead. They had a family of 20 children, of
which 14 grew to adulthood.

Philip died December 16, 1932 and Christina died September 12, 1939. They are
both buried in Green Mound Cemetery, near Leola. They spent a total of 33 years
in the Leola area.

PHILLIP and MATHILDA SCHAFFER

Phillip Schaffer was born to Philip Schaffer and Christina Wagemann on April 7,
1895 in Neudorf, South Russia. He came to the U.S. with his parents and other
children. They came on the ship "Barbarossa" entering New York harbor September
12, 1906. He lived with his parents on SW-Section 15, Township 128, Range 68 in
Wacker Township. On the 27th of July, 1926 in Leola, SD he married Mathilda
Merkel, daughter of Phillip Merkel and Carolina Heinrich of Forbes, ND.

The following children were born to this marriage: Raymond Phillip, born
September 23, 1927, died December 1950 in the Korean War. He is buried in Green
Mound Cemetery, Leola. Priscilla Lillian, born December 25, 1928, married
Donald Grohnke of Warner, SD. Mabel Florence, born March 20, 1930, married
Gailen Jackson of Spokane, WA. Marvin Paul, born August 26, 1932, married
Jeanette Yeske of Barnard, SD.

On the 4th of December, 1935, their mother, Mathilda died at home. Phillip had
to care for four small children and then realized he couldn't stay single very
long. April 2, 1937, he married Mary Marie Schwartz in Leola. She was the
daughter of Paul Schwartz and Katherine Knell of Napoleon, ND. She was born on
a farm at Napoleon, ND on the 14th of February, 1909. She had one daughter,
Adeline, born March 28, 1928. Adeline is married to Eagle Voight of Aberdeen,
SD.

        The Phillip Schaffer Family.

The following children are of this marriage: Sarah Martha, born February 22,
1938, married Allen Lechner of Leola, SD. Betty Lou, born May 12, 1939, married
Leon Nelson of Texas. Theophil Joseph "Bud", born June 21, 1940, married Jean
Marie Harding of Garden City, SD. Phillip Junior, born July 3, 1942, married
Beverly Hershman of Morgantown, WV. Ronald Lee, born August 26, 1943, married
Faye Krokel of Mound City, SD. Dennis Dwayne, born September 22, 1945, married
Linda Durheim of Ellendale, ND. LaVonne Kay, born January 11, 1949.

Phillip lived in Leola for 57 years. He was employed for about 30 years for the
State Highway Department until he retired in 1963. He became ill and died in
November of 1963. Mary then moved to Aberdeen where she lived until her death
in February of 1979. Both are buried in Green Mound Cemetery, Leola.

THEOPHIL and JEAN SCHAFFER

Theophil Joseph "Bud" was born to Phillip and Mary Marie (Schwartz) Schaffer on
June 21, 1940 at their home in Leola. He graduated from Leola High School in
1959. He served four years in the US Navy. He then spent considerable time
working out of state. On January 1, 1967, he went to work for the Aberdeen
Police Department. He is a Detective Sergeant, (Juvenile Officer). This has
kept him active with the youth by serving on the board of directors of several
agencies and also becoming a Boy Scout leader.

He is very active in genealogy (family history). He has been working with
genealogy for about 25 years. He started the South Dakota Genealogy Society in
Pierre, SD in 1982.

        The Theophil (Bud) Schaffer Family.

Bud met his wife, Jean Marie, in 1967 while attending Aberdeen School of
Commerce. They were married August 17, 1968 and made their home in Aberdeen.
Jean Marie is the daughter of Merle Wayne and Mabel Josephine (Erickson)
Harding of Garden City, SD. She was born March 30, 1949 in Watertown, SD. Her
family has been traced back to 1024 on her father's side of the family. She is
a collateral descendant of several famous people. Among them, George
Washington's mother; Presidents Adams, Harding and Hayes; signer of the
Declaration of Independence, George Walton. Bud has his family traced back to
the 1750's.

Bud is still employed with the Aberdeen Police Department. Jean is a secretary
for Aman Collection Agency.

Three children were born to this union, all born at Aberdeen, SD. Troy James
was born July 21, 1970. Todd Merle was born August 30, 1972. Amber Jean was
born April 30, 1977.

ANDREW and MARY ANN SCHAFFNER

Church.

Twelve children were born to this union: Regina was married to Felix Weber

MIKE and DELLA SCHAFFNER

Mike and Della Schaffner have lived in Leola for 38 years. They are members of
the Catholic Church. Mike is a member of the American Legion and Della is
active with the Legion Auxiliary.

Mike, a son of Andrew and Mary Ann Schaffner, was a farmer in Koto Township
before entering the Army. He was discharged in 1946.

On November 18, 1945 he was married to Della Neuharth of rural Leola. Mike
bought the Mobil Service Station. He later sold the business to the Schilling
brothers and worked for various garages. In 1954 Mike was hired as manager of
the Leola Equity Oil Department, serving in this capacity until 1970, when he
started a shop of his own. The business was sold to Curt Walz in 1979.

Mike was employed as custodian with the Leola school system until December 1982
when he retired.

Della grew up on a farm in Arena Township, graduated from Leola High School and
attended NSC. She taught rural schools for several years. She did bookkeeping
and direct selling for a number of years. At present she is employed at 3M
Company of Aberdeen.

Mike and Della are the parents of five children. All attended Leola school and
graduated from Leola High School.

Michael Allen, born August 11, 1946, is employed with the McPherson County

ADOLPH and OLIVIA SCHAIBLE

Adolph, son of John and Magdalena (Schmitt) Schaible, was the youngest son of a
family of 12 children. He had ten brothers and one sister. Adolph was born in
McPherson County, Leola, SD, on September 23, 1915. He grew up on the family
farm and attended country school.

In 1933, his father lost his life in a car accident. Adolph then had to be on
his own. He worked at the Eureka Experiment Farm, for about four years.

In July 1941, Adolph was drafted to serve in the U.S. Army. He received his
discharge in 1944. On September 10, 1944, Adolph was united in marriage to
Olivia Steiger, at Leola, SD. Olivia was born on September 10, 1918, in
McPherson County, Leola, SD, the daughter of Albert and Christina (Stoecker)
Steiger. She attended school in Leola.

        Olivia & Adolph Schaible.

Adolph and Olivia started farming for themselves on a farm located 5 1/2 miles
southeast of Leola. In 1956, they moved to Leola, where they had built a new
home.

Olivia worked in the Gerhardt Breitag store and then as deputy in the Office of
Director of Equalization, for a number of years.

They have one daughter, Carol. Three grandchildren, Jeffrey, James and Jessica
Becker, give them many hours of enjoyment.

Adolph and Olivia are members of St. James Lutheran Church, where Olivia is a
member of the ALCW. They are active members of the American Legion and Legion
Auxiliary.

BENJAMIN and LORRAINE SCHAIBLE

Ben Schaible was born August 22, 1914, on a farm southwest of Long Lake, SD, to

CHRIST J. and BEATRICE SCHANZENBACH

"I have but one lamp by which my feet are guided, that is the lamp of
experience. I know of no way of judging of the future but by the past."
                                                        Patrick Henry

Just what is there that can be said of the pioneers in and around Leola? None
had education advantages like our youth of today, yet they made as much or more
of the opportunities afforded them.

C. J. Schanzanbach was a man who always loved school. Along with his faithful
dog, Christ trotted three or more miles every day to get an education. He, like
many others, had to spend at least one night in the schoolhouse with his
teacher and schoolmates due to a severe blizzard which came up suddenly during
the day.

Christ was born on a farm northeast of Eureka, SD, to John J. and Magdalena
(Lippert) Schanzenbach in 1895. He had four brothers and two sisters. Christ
and his brother, Dan, are the only survivors of their family. One sister died
in infancy.

After going through grade school, Christ went to Congregation College for one
more year. He became a self-educated man by seizing every opportunity to read
and learn throughout his 88 years.

Christ joined the Army in 1918 and spent two years on the front lines in France
and six months in the Army of Occupation in Germany. At one time he spent five
weeks on the front lines, with nothing off except his shoes. He loaded every
shell into the cannon where they were fighting. Christ says he would not
exchange any money for the experience, but would not like to experience it
again.

In 1920, Christ returned home and married the girl he left behind, Beatrice
Berg. To this union were born seven children: Lillian (Winter) of Hacienda
Heights, CA; Raymond (Bud) of Norwalk, CA; Othelia (Weare) of Glenallen, AK;
Lorina (Paulson) of Brainerd, MN; Leo of Hacienda Heights, CA; Wanda (Duffy),
deceased; and Gordon of Athens, OH.

Due to drought conditions the family moved from Akaska, SD to the Leola area in
1936. Christ's brother, Dan, had moved here a year earlier. Two years later
Beatrice contracted tuberculosis and although she was sent to Custer to the
State Sanitarium she was unable to get well. In a short while the drought
conditions improved and farmers were able to buy livestock and make a decent
living once more.

Christ married Virginia Lindley in 1941. She is the daughter of William and
Leslie (Moulton) Lindley (see Lindley history) of Leola. Virginia was a
telephone operator in Leola and continued working until the dial system went
into effect. They had two children: Cathleen (Schwahn) of Hacienda, CA and a
son, William Chris of Anchorage, AK. Virginia and Christ raised nine children
and now have 18 grandchildren and 14 great-grandchildren.

        The Christ J. Schanzenbach Family.

Christ has been an active participant in the community, serving on school
boards, township boards, county ASC board, FHA committees and as county
commissioner. He served in most capacities in his church and has been a member
of the American Legion for 49 years. He was given a life membership several
years ago.

Virginia has been active in church work, and she and Chris have been singing
for funerals for years. She has been American Legion Auxiliary president,
twice. She also worked in the Leola Community Hospital as a nurses aid until
the hospital closed. The training helped her care for her aging mother, Leslie,
during the last years of her life.

Both Chris and Virginia have been willing helpers in the society in which they
have lived for 42 years as man and wife. They are still living and serving
their community in Leola, SD.

DAN and MARY SCHANZENBACH

Daniel Schanzenbach was born January 3, 1903, to John J. and Magdalene
(Lippert) Schanzenbach, Sr. of Eureka, SD. In 1905 they moved five miles north
of Akaska, where Dan grew up. In 1916, when Dan was 13, his folks moved to
town. Dan stayed on the farm and helped his brothers and sisters, staying
mostly with Jake. In 1927 Dan married Mary Weiszhaar of Lowry, and they moved
to a farm six miles north of Akaska. Here Mearl was born in 1929. Then the
family moved 13 1/2 miles southwest of Mobridge, and it was here that Ramona
and Melvin were born. In 1934 the Dan Schanzenbachs and Jake Liedles picked up
their belongings and moved east of Leola, because they had no water for cattle
due to the drought. It took one week to move by horse and wagon from Mobridge
to east of Leola, 115 miles. Dan brought with them 34 horses, nine cows, one
bull and a few sheep and chickens. They rented the farm where Anthony Kessler
now lives. Three more children were born while there: Harvey, Wanita and
LaVina. Then in October 1941, Dan bought three quarters of land with buildings
for $2,400. This is the home place where Gary now lives. Darlys and Gary were
born there.

July 7, 1949, Melvin was bringing in the milkcows while on horseback, and was
struck and killed by lightning.

        The Dan Schanzenbach Family.

Dan and Mary celebrated their golden wedding anniversary in 1977 and that same
year they retired from the farm and moved into Leola, SD. Dan and Mary have
seven children as follows: Mearl married Gail Heagley and had two sons, Melvin
and Tod. In 1980 he married Zona (Habeck-Olson) who has two children, Heather
and Chad. Ramona married LeRoy Rath and lives in Daly City, CA. They have four
sons, Daniel, Kevin, Travis, and Brian. Harvey married Joanne Heagley and
presently lives in Jamestown, ND, with their two sons, Stewart and Max. LaVina
married Dr. James Kauth and lives in San Francisco, CA. They have two sons,
Mark and Tom and one daughter, Kim. Wanita lives and works at Walnut Creek, CA,
and has a son, Paul. Darlys is married to Phil Dennert and lives in Overland
Park, KS. They have a daughter, Leigh Ann, and a son, Michael. Gary farms on
the home place and is married to Diane (Rohl-Schaible), who has two sons, Revi
and Brett.

Linda graduated in 1964 from North St. Paul High School. She attended the

CHARLEY and FRANCES SCHMALZ

Charley Schmalz came to Leola in 1921, where he became manager of the recently
purchased Mitchel Lumber Yard by the Atlas Lumber Company, of Minnesota (now
Peavey). Charley was chosen for Leola because of his ability to speak German
very fluently. He came to Leola from Gettysburg where he had worked in the
Atlas Lumber Yard.

Charley and Frances (Morse) Schmalz were married in September of 1921 at
Ipswich, SD, and moved into an apartment over the hardware store.

During the years that they lived in Leola (1921-1950) both were active in
social activities. Charley was Mayor (house mutter as he was called by
acquaintances) of Leola, from 1930 to 1938. He was a member of the American
Legion, the Masons and Shrine organizations, served as chief of the Fire
Department, and enjoyed many of their annual fishing trips.

Frances was an active member of the Disco Club, Legion Auxiliary, Ladies Aid of
the Methodist Church, and Eastern Star. She also was employed at Atlas. In
1927, they built a home two blocks west of the lumberyard.

In 1949, Charley became a full-time superintendent for Peavey Lumber Co. and
they moved to Worthington, MN. In 1958, they returned to Brookings, SD. Charley
retired from Peavey in 1963. They have been traveling, enjoying grandchildren,
friends and church. Charley and Frances celebrated their 60th wedding
anniversary in 1981.

They have an abiding interest in activities at USD, where they have established
a scholarship program in the Medical School at Vermillion.

Lois Schmalz Najacht was born in Aberdeen, SD, in 1922. She graduted from high
school in 1940. Lois was a member of the very first girls 4-H Club in Leola.
Gifted with musical ability, her interest in music has continued throughout her
adult life. She has been active in church, school groups, organizations, bands
and orchestras.

Lois entered nurses' training at SDSU and St. Luke's Hospital. After
graduation, she moved to Wisconsin in 1953, living in Sheboygan, Rhinelander
and Altoona, before returning to South Dakota, in 1973. Her family consists of
two stepsons. Charles and his wife, Norma, and sons Jason, Jonathan and Joshua
live in Hot Springs, SD.

Tom is a graduate of the University of Milwaukee, WI. He and his wife, Kris,
and children Elizabeth and Luke, live in Spearfish, SD.

A daughter, Jane, is a senior at SDSU, majoring in advertising journalism. She
lives in Brookings.

ELDON (SMITTY) and MARGARET SCHMIDT

Eldon M. Schmidt was born July 24, 1914, at Turton, SD. His parents, Martin and
Lucille Schmidt, came to Leola in 1928. Eldon attended grade school in Leola
(1928-1931) and three years of high school. He was student manager of athletics
in 1933 and 1934. He received the purple and gold letter, which he still has.

On July 21, 1936, he enlisted in the Military Service. After returning from
overseas in 1945, Eldon was assigned to the War Department Personnel Center at
Fort Lewis. If anyone from Leola came through this center, they may find his
signature on their discharge papers and orders. He retired in March 1959. After
retirement he was employed by, and the last six years was manager of, the
largest auto parts store in the city and vicinity of Olympia, WA.

        Jack Frost (Eldon's friend) and Eldon M. Schmidt.

Eldon's sisters were: Mrs. Vivian Gentle; Mrs. Lois Hallet; Mrs. Elaine Hallock
(the Hallock family owned the Blue Ribbon Bakery in Leola); Mrs. Marilyn
Schlendler; and Mrs. Shirley Hamilton, born in Leola. Brothers were: Cecil R.
and Richard N. Eldon's father was a barber; his mother was a cook in a Leola
restaurant. They are both deceased. The Schmidt family were not pioneers of
Leola, but are proud that they were from here. The family moved to Okanogan,
WA, in 1940.

Eldon and his wife Margaret reside at Olympia, WA. Their religious preference
is Catholic. No children were born to this union.

PETER and IDA SCHMIDT

Peter P. Schmidt, who is presently the clerk of courts and clerk magistrate, is
serving his 26th year in that capacity. Prior to this he had served four years
in the office of register of deeds.

Pete, his six sisters and one brother, children of Peter S. and Eva (Fuehrer)
Schmidt, were all born on the family farm, rural Artas, SD. Their first house
had been built of clay and straw (adobe) brick. While not attractive in
appearance, the sod shanties were cool in summer and warm in winter and were
not drafty. Their house was an improvement over some for it had wood floors. In
1926, it was replaced with a modern frame building.

Pete attended country school through the eighth grade. High school graduates
were hired to teach school. One teacher, teaching grades one through eight and
as many as 18 children in a one-room school.

Raising grain, livestock and dairying was the family's livelihood. Farming was
done with horses. With the use of horses, came buggies, surreys and phaetons.
There was as keen a rivalry among farmers to buy the best looking vehicle as
there is today with new autos. In 1927, a 15-30 tractor and a three bottom plow
were bought. This brought about a great speed-up in farming.

During the '30s there were hard times, low prices, drought, dust storms and
grasshopper plagues. There wasn't enough feed for the livestock. The government
bought the cattle and sheep, shot and buried them. There was no market for
cattle.

Most of the jobs available were farm related. Wages, 50 cents to $1 per day
were low, but then, so were the prices paid for goods.

On October 23, 1940, Pete lost his right arm in a corn shredder accident. In
spite of the misfortune which had befallen him, he kept up his courage and
tried to make the best of existing conditions. He entered Capitol Commercial
College at Bismarck, ND, graduating in 1942, in business administration.

        Ida & Peter P. Schmidt.

On June 28, 1946, at Leola, Pete was united in marriage with Ida, the daughter
of Fred F. and Rosina (Schlepp) Obenauer. Ida was born on the Obenauer
homestead, rural Java, SD. She moved to Eureka with her parents in 1927, where
she attended school. She grew up with five sisters and two brothers.

Ida presently is a part-time deputy court clerk. She also serves as FS CSHR of
the Food Stamp Program.

Twin daughters, Karyn Jean and Karyl Jane, were born June 14, 1951, at
Mobridge, SD. Pete and Ida's grandchildren are Lynne Marie and Lanna Beth Dais.

They have been living in Leola since 1952 and are members of St. James Lutheran
Church.

CARL K. SR. and ELIZABETH SCHOCK

Carl K. Schock, Sr., born in Russia on January 8 1870, came to the United
States in April 1890, and settled in North Dakota for a short time. He was
united in marriage to Elizabeth Gehring, who was born November 27, 1873. They
moved to South Dakota to set up a homestead on Section 1 in Highland Township,
McPherson County, where Carl purchased 160 acres of land. Later he purchased an
adjoining 480 acres, which was later divided among their children. The
homestead is now occupied by LeRoy and Eileen Schock.

        Carl K. & Elizabeth Schock.

Carl and Elizabeth were blessed with five children: Frieda (Mrs. Christ
Schutz), resides in Eureka, SD; Karl (deceased); John, resides at Long Lake,
SD; Jacob (deceased); and Christoph, resides in Leola, SD.

In 1928, Carl and his wife retired and moved to Leola. The homestead was then
operated by Christoph and his wife. Carl died on October 20, 1954 and Elizabeth
died on December 14, 1956.

ELMER and NORMA SCHOCK

JOHN E. and BARBARA SCHOCK

John E. Schock was born a twin with sister Katie on a farm near Long Lake, SD,
on June 16, 1888. His sister, Katie, is still living and resides at La Moure,
ND. John was the son of John Schock and Margurita Rath.

John's wife, Barbara, was also born a twin in a sod house near Long Lake, SD,
on April 3, 1890. They were married on the 27th of November in 1911. They spent
their entire lifetime working hard on a farm, first at Long Lake, SD, then at
Ashley, ND, and then seven miles south of Leola. Before their demise, they
resided for a few years in Leola.

        The John E. Schock Family.

The John Schocks had ten children. One died during the flu epidemic of WWI. The
remaining nine children are still living. By name they are: Freida Payne of
Aberdeen; John J. Schock, Leola; Wilbert, Sioux Falls; Florentina, Arizona; Al
and Ozzie, Sioux Falls; Della, Arizona; Hilda, Arizona; and Lavina, Arizona.

John and Barbara were highly respected in the rural farm community. They were
known as honest, hardworking people. John was known for his outgoing
personality and Barbara for her generosity.

As was typical of so many of the early pioneers that settled in McPherson
County in the Leola-Long Lake areas, they lived through relatively few periods
of prosperity. The most prosperous periods were in the mid '20's and during the
period of WWII. In 1928 John bought 640 acres of land near Leola, SD. During
the depression of the early '30's the insurance company foreclosed on this
land, and at one time the total assets of the John Schocks were reduced to
under $2,000. Bankruptcy might have been the way out, but John would not
consider it. John and Barbara were always proud of the accomplishments of their
children. John was, however, concerned about Al and Ozzie's dairy operation in
Sioux Falls. He always thought they might be growing too large. Al and Ozzie
founded Terrace Park Dairy in Sioux Falls, which is one of the largest regional
dairy companies in the upper Midwest. They also founded Nordica International
which sells media and cultures to the entire dairy industry all over the world.

Barbara suffered a stroke in 1954 and was in ill health until her death in the
Eureka Nursing Home in Eureka on December 24, 1957.

John lived by himself in Leola after Barbara's death. He died on September 14,
1960, at the age of 72.

After Barbara's death, son Al said he heard the rumor that his dad was thinking
about getting remarried. John said to Al, "Me think about getting remarried,
with 77 widows in Leola."

John's total assets at the time of his death were $3,664.64.  Each of the
children received an inheritance of $407.19.

JOHN J. and FLORENCE SCHOCK

John J. Schock's parents were Mr. and Mrs. John E. Schock. He was born near
Long Lake, SD on December 24, 1913. John's wife, Florence, was born near
Hillsview, SD to Mr. and Mrs. Henry Mehlhaff. Later she moved with her parents
to a farm near Hosmer, SD. They were married October 28, 1944. To this union
there were born two sons, Stanley and Arnie of Leola, and a daughter, Gwen, of
White Bear Lake, MN.

They spent their entire life living in the town of Leola. John was a farmer and
part-time salesman. His wife was a housewife until the children were grown,
then worked as a nurse's aid at the Leola Community Hospital until it closed.
Afterwards she worked as a clerk in the Gamble Store for 11 years. Both retired
about five years ago. Their children attended their first 12 years of school in
Leola. Stanley became a farmer, Arnie a teacher and Gwen is a housewife.

John and Florence remember well the "dirty thirties" and all the hardships it
caused their parents while they were growing up. John worked for 25 cents to $1
a day for room and board during that time. Later he was in a C.C. Camp at Hill
City, SD. When he returned, he farmed with his father.

They have six grandchildren, including a set of twin girls, which bring great
joy to John and Florence. They try to see them whenever they can. Their hobbies
include gardening for John, quilt-making and sewing for Florence. Sight-seeing
is another pleasure of theirs.

They are members of various organizations and belong to St. Paul's Lutheran
Church.
