FREDERICK and ANNA SCHOENFELDER

Frederick Carl Schoenfelder was born May 15, 1864 in Buffalo, NY and Anna
Rosetta (Leonard) Schoenfelder was born December 25, 1875 in Renville County,
MN. The parents of both Fred and Anna immigrated from Germany during the period
from 1845 to 1867. Fred's parents arrived in America about ten years before the
Civil War; Anna's parents arrived just after the conclusion of the Civil War,
during the " Reconstruction" period. The parents on both sides met each other
after immigrating to America. Fred's parents were married in 1849 at Buffalo,
NY and Anna's parents married in 1870 at St. Paul, MN. Fred and Anna were
married March 17, 1896 at Belview, MN.

Fred and Anna came to Leola in 1909 from Hoven, SD. Several years earlier, Fred
had been employed by the Central Lumber Company (headquartered in Minneapolis)
to manage and build up the business of lumber yards which that company was
establishing at various locations along the trackage of the Minneapolis and St.
Louis Railroad. In 1909, when Fred was transferred to take over as manager of
the Leola Yard, the company business was already established in the town. He
and Anna brought with them a family of four children: a daughter, Viola, and
three sons, Robert, Adolph and Otto. Shortly before their departure from Hoven,
they lost a 10-year-old daughter, Helen, from diphtheria. Upon arrival in Leola
and until 1922, they made their home in the substantial second-floor apartment
at the Central Lumber Company premises, next door to the McPherson County
Abstract Co. (now owned by Floyd Meidinger, attorney). At this home, in the
earlier years of their residency, two additional children were born: a son,
Walter, born in 1910 and their last child, Frederick Carl Jr., born in 1912,
whose accidental death in infancy occurred July 14, 1914.

        The Schoenfelder Family. Back: Adolph, Otto, Robert, Walter and Orrin
        Berridge. Front: Emma, Margaret, Ruth, Eugenie and Viola.

The Schoenfelder family participated actively in the Leola Community. The
children received their education in the Leola Public Schools. They were
members of the Methodist Episcopal Church. Fred was a member of the Masonic
Order, as was his son, Robert. Anna was a member of Eastern Star (as was her
daughter, Viola) and was also a Royal Neighbor. Robert, the eldest son,
enlisted in the U.S. Navy and served during WWI.

During Fred's management of the Central Lumber Co., the business enlarged and
sold all types of construction lumber and building materials, paints, household
hardwares, stoves and heating equipment, leather goods, saddles and harnesses,
guns and other sporting goods. They added a storage warehouse to store heavy
freight such as coal, cement, lime, sand, lath and other bulky building
supplies.

In early 1921, Anna acquired an illness that required surgery. During her
convalescence, complications developed, resulting in her death on March 27,
1921, ten days after she and Fred had celebrated their 25th wedding
anniversary. At the time of their mother's death, three children remained at
home. After her death, Fred sought to establish himself in his own retail
lumber business and in 1922 he and his family moved to Minneapolis, MN where he
and his older sons operated a retail market. However, this venture was not to
his liking, and early the following year he disposed of his interest in the
store and returned to the lumber business. His sons did likewise. Robert was
employed at Waconia, MN to manage a lumberyard; Adolph managed a yard in
Bowdle, SD. Fred managed the Dolliff Lumber Co. at Wheaton, MN. Viola, Otto and
Walter remained with him, and it was at their Wheaton home that Viola and Orrin
L. Berridge were married on June 2, 1923. Shortly after their marriage, Orrin
and Viola returned to Leola to make their home.

In the fall of 1923, Fred took over the manager's job of the Saltz Lumber Co.
at Forbes, ND and continued in this capacity until ill health forced him to
retire in 1926. His health continued to deteriorate and his last months were
spent in the home of his son Adolph, Bowdle, SD, where he died August 15, 1926.
He is buried beside his wife, Anna and their son, Frederick Carl, Jr. in Green
Mound Cemetery, Leola.

GORDON and ARDIS SIEH

The Gordon Sieh family came to McPherson County in February 1963, settling in
Dewey Township, where they had purchased 1,600 acres of ranch land. In 1964 the
land was exchanged for the "Strudle Ranch" located in Howard Township.

Steve Strudle came to America from Austria when he was 19 years old. He lived
in Pittsburgh, PA, where he worked on the railroad until he moved to South
Dakota and homesteaded land in Howard Township in 1909. The house was built in
1911. Steve and his wife Margaret had three children: Marie (Strudle)
Dutenhofer, Joe and Leonard. Steve used to say, "I bought the land and the
seller threw in the rocks." Steve died in 1960. Steve's brother homesteaded the
land now owned by Chris Jakober. His parents homesteaded the north end of Dewey
Township which is in Ordway Prairie Conservancy now.

In June 1964 most of the buildings on the Strudle Ranch were destroyed in a
wind-rain storm, leaving the house and bottom half of the barn. The barn was
repaired and a new house was built in '67. The land was incorporated as C
Cattle Company in '78. They buy and raise yearling calves, pasturing them and
selling the calves in the fall.

        The Gordon Sieh Family. Back: Danny, Gordon and Susan. Front: Carolyn,
        Ardis, Mary and Arden.

Gordon Francis Sieh was born May 3, 1928 near Aberdeen, where his grandparents
had homesteaded in 1881. He attended SDSU, where he studied Animal Science.

Ardis Colleen (Gulsvig) Sieh was born December 2, 1927 at Pinewood, MN. She
grew up in Havana, ND. She attended Presentation School of Nursing and is an
RN.

Gordon and Ardis were married February 13, 1950 at Aberdeen, SD. They have five
children, all born in Aberdeen, SD. Arden Michael was born December 14, 1950.

Mary Kathleen was born June 4, 1952. Kathleen and Wayne Morrill were married
December 19, 1970 at Ipswich, SD. They are the parents of two children. Nicole
Lee was born June 16, 1971 and Travis Wayne, July 11, 1980. They live at

ALFRED (A. J.) and BERTHA SHAFER

Alfred Jacob, the son of Philip and Catherine (Weber) Shafer, was born May 6,
1886 on a farm at Sutter, IL.

Bertha Marie Ruhs was born July 12, 1888 to William and Hanna (Schachtsick)
Ruhs at Hamilton, IL.

In the fall of 1908, Alfred moved west where the land was cheaper and the
opportunity brighter in the Dakotas. He looked around and gathered much
information from other folks who had come to this territory earlier to
homestead.

After returning to Illinois, he pondered about his adventure, and through the
mail bought a quarter of land in Section 3 of Leola Township in McPherson
County.

On December 30, 1908, Alfred and Bertha were married in a little country church
(where both had attended church and Sunday school as children) at Sutter, IL.
They lived with Alfred's parents until March 1909. Then John Mullering and
Alfred, with their belongings, headed west to their new land of promise. Their
families joined them later in the spring.

Alfred and Bertha stayed with the Otto Hauffe family the first summer, as they
had nothing on their land for shelter. In the fall of 1909 they returned to
Hamilton, IL and stayed with Bertha's family. They returned again in the spring
and again made their home with the Otto Hauffe family, until Alfred had erected
a granary. This was their new home. While living in the Leola community, Alfred
farmed and did carpenter work. In the fall of 1917, Alfred took his family and
moved to a farm near Roscoe, SD. Seven years later the family returned to the
Leola area, locating on the farm known as "Leola Ranch." In 1941 they purchased
a small place on the southeast edge of Leola. The two younger boys took care of
the farming. Alfred slowly drifted into a larger scale of carpenter trade,
something he pursued through the years. Alfred built a house in town across
from the Methodist Church. They bought the Porter Hotel in 1952. Alfred passed
away on December 5, 1959. Bertha later moved to a smaller home. She passed away
July 22, 1970.

        The Alred Shafer Family. Back: Lucille, Lela, Maie, Florence, Edna,
        Verna, Vida and Esther. Front: Harold, Alfred, Bertha, Alfred, Warren
        and Lloyd.

Alfred and Bertha were the parents of 13 children.

Maie was born in Hamilton, IL on January 5, 1910. She married Edwin Haberman.
They had two boys. Edwin passed away in 1973, Maie on August 7, 1979. They were
living in Lodi, CA.

Five children were born in McPherson County.

Esther was born June 29, 1911. She married Henning Hakanson. They had three
children. She is presently living in Aberdeen.

Alfred was born February 13, 1913. He married Hazel Osborn. They had two
children. Alfred passed away January 5, 1974, Hazel on April 6, 1977. They had
lived at West Concord, MN.

Lela was born September 26, 1914. She married Edward Harrison. Edward died
April 8, 1978. Lela is living in Ellendale, ND. They had two children.

Lucille was born May 3, 1916. She married Reinhold Kolb. They are living in
Aberdeen, SD. They have ten children.

Floyd was born March 31, 1917. He is married to Virginia Lanzine. They are
living in Divile, LA. They have three children.

Five children were born in Edmunds County, SD.

Edna was born March 3, 1918. She is married to Joe Lippert. They live in Eau
Claire, WI. They have seven children.

The twins, Verna and Viola, were born April 13, 1919. Viola is married to
Raymond Sumpton. They are living at Frederick, SD. They have seven children.

Verna was married to Emil Joireman. He passed away. They had three children. In
1970 Verna married John McCrow. They are living at Battleground, WA.

Warren--(refer to Warren Shafer history).

Florence was born on June 1, 1925. She is married to Edwin Diede. They are
living in Lebanon, SD. They have five children.

Harold--(refer to Harold Shafer history).

KENNETH WARREN and DIANNA SHAFER

Kenneth was born August 2, 1949 in Leola, SD, to Warren Harry and Margaret June
(Crouch) Shafer. Ken graduated from the Leola High School in 1968 and moved to
Denver, CO, where he enrolled in Metro State College courses and a vocational
computer school.

Ken married Dianna Lynn Van Dorin on June 12, 1971. They made their home in
Brighton, CO. They have two children, Brian James and June Rene.

Ken was employed as a senior electronics technician for five years and changed
employment to operations manager for a trucking firm for 11 years. At that time
he decided to return to South Dakota and farm the Warren Shafer farm, located
eight miles north of Leola in McPherson County.

WARREN HARRY and MARGARET SHAFER

Warren was born July 29, 1920, at Roscoe, SD, to Alfred J. and Bertha (Ruhs)
Shafer. When he was five years old his family moved to a farm four miles north,
one mile east, and three-fourths of a mile north of Leola.

On October 6, 1944 Warren married Margaret June Crouch at Leola. They lived at
the edge of Leola until 1950 when they moved to their present farm eight miles
north of Leola.

        The Warren Shafer Family. Back: Peggy, Karen, June and Warren. Front:

EMIL and MARY SMOLNISKY

Emil was born July 7, 1890 in McPherson County near Eureka, to Nickalaus and
Christine (Renchler) Smolnisky. He had five brothers: John, William, George,
Carl and Gustav, and two sisters, Christine and Anna. He grew up on the family
farm and attended school through the eighth grade.

On February 2, 1914 he married Mary Lammle and they lived on the farm with his
parents. Emil was appointed postmaster of the Martell Post Office which was
moved to the family farmhouse in 1919. He later resigned this position, as this
became a star route between Leola and Eureka.

        Emil & Mary Smolnisky.

Unable to farm as a result of a farm accident in 1924, Emil moved to Leola,
where he was elected as the Register of Deeds from 1928 to 1932. After his term
in office they returned to the farm, and with the help of his sons, farmed
until 1945, when they moved to Vanport, OR for three years. They moved back to
Leola in 1948, where he was bookkeeper for Kulm's Garage, Maier's Garage and
Leo's Garage.

After Mary died, December 2, 1973, Emil spent some time with his children. He
then made his home at the Aberdeen Nursing Center until his death on May 24,
1980.

Emil and Mary had eight children: Leo, married Viola Heupel, lives in Leola and
has three children; Elmer, married Lilas Wipf, was killed in Germany during
World War II; Ralph, married Erma Rall, lives in Lodi, CA and has three
children; Ruth and her husband, Christ Schumacher, have one son and live near
Eureka, SD; John married Delores Schumacher, lives in Eugene, OR and has two
children; Mary and her husband, Julius Peters, have two children and live in
Sioux Falls, SD; Kathleen Robinson lives in Denver, CO and has five children;
Eveyln Ringsley has two children and lives in Denver, CO.

LEO and VIOLA SMOLNISKY

Leo Smolnisky was born January 31, 1916 to Mary (Lammle) and Emil Smolnisky at
the farm home south of Long Lake. He enlisted in the Army in 1941 and was
discharged after five years of service. On December 5, 1943 he was united in
marriage to Viola Heupel, born November 3, 1922, daughter of Mary (Klooz) and
August G. Heupel of Leola.

Leo worked for Rueb's Chevrolet. In 1955 he purchased the Standard Service
Station from Art and Rueben Kiesz. In 1958 he leased the gas operation to James
Geffre, keeping the back part of the station for glass installation, body and
fender work, car painting and general mechanics. He purchased the Rueb's
Chevrolet upon Ed's death, and had dealerships for Oliver, Farmhand, Dual and
Melroe. He sold Leo's Garage to Bill and Walter Hoffman in September of 1981.

        The Leo Smolnisky Family. Back: Sheilah, Elmer and Imogene. Front:
        Leo and Viola.

Vi and Leo became the parents of three children. Imogene was born February 21,
1947 and married Robert Kaul. They have two girls, Melissa and Lynnette, and
live in Aberdeen. Sheilah was born January 24, 1950 and married Edward
Rubenstein. They have two children, Brian and Brooke. Elmer was born December
25, 1951, married Joy Schlagel, and lives in Chicago, IL.

Vi and Leo enjoy their retirement. They are avid duplicate bridge players, love
to golf, bowl, and have a home by the Missouri River where they spend time
fishing.

They are members of St. James Lutheran Church in Leola.

FRED and KATHERINA SPITZER

Fred Spitzer was born December 1, 1892 to Fred and Barbara (Kramlich) Spitzer
near Long Lake, SD. He had ten brothers and sisters: Alfard, Edward, Leo,
Barbara, Anna, Hulda, Tina, Lea, Pauline and Ida.

On November 15, 1914 Fred married Katherina Heyd, daughter of Adam and
Magdalena (Rath) Heyd, born December 2, 1894. Their parents all immigrated from
Russia.

Fred and Katherina made their first home on a farm southwest of Long Lake. Here
they lived for 35 years and raised nine children: Ida (Mrs. Lloyd McKittrich),
born August 8, 1915, lives in Seattle, WA; Alvin, born January 2, 1917, lives
on his grandfather's farm at Long Lake; Harold, born May 9, 1918, lives at
Mathis, TX; Edna (Mrs. Eugene Kurtz) was born June 25, 1920 and lives in
Aberdeen, SD; Erwin, born January 7, 1922, lives at Kent, WA; Henry, born April
26, 1923, died in 1967 at Seattle, WA; August, born November 12, 1925, lives at
Minneapolis, MN; Reinhold, born November 30, 1930, lives at Parkers Prairie,
MN; and Wilma (Mrs. Ray Schnabel), born June 29, 1936, lives in Aberdeen, SD.

In 1950 Fred and Katherina moved to a farm east of Leola, in Brown County,
until 1960 when they purchased a home and moved to Leola. Fred passed away in
1967 but Katherina continued to make her home here until 1980 when she moved to
the Senior Housing in Leola.

While living at Long Lake, Fred served on the school board and as deacon of
Salem Emmanuel Lutheran Church. In Leola they became members of the St. James
Lutheran Church.

Fred and Katherina were blessed with 40 grandchildren, over 80
great-grandchildren, and a few great-great-grandchildren.

JOHANN and ELIZABETH SPITZER

Johann and Elizabeth (Streyle) Spitzer and their four children left Kassel,
South Russia in 1890 and came to America. They homesteaded northwest of Leola.
The four children were: Christina, later Mrs. Fred Feickert; Christian, who
died at the age of 13; Katherine, later married Gotthilf Pfeifle; and Jacob
Spitzer, who had married Elizabeth Schock. Three more children were born to
them in America: Elizabeth, who married Fred F. Hoffman; and twins Adam and
Eva. Eva married Fred Wolff of Eureka, SD. Adam died at the age of three.

In 1916 the Spitzers retired, moving to Leola where they had purchased the
Valentine Lehr home. Their son Jacob took over the farm.

Johann died in 1923 and Elizabeth in 1930. All of the children are deceased.

GOTTHILF and BARBARA STICKEL

Among the early pioneers were Gotthilf and Barbara (Glaser) Stickel, married
April 10, 1904. Both Mr. and Mrs. Stickel were born in Tripp, SD in the 1880's.
They both moved with their parents to the Eureka area as children, where they
grew up and were married. They moved to a farm one mile south of Leola. Five
years later they moved to the Stickel homestead, four miles west and one-half
mile south of Leola. Mr. and Mrs. Stickel lived on the farm until their deaths.
Mrs. Stickel died in a farm accident in September of 1939, Mr. Stickel died in
May 1947.

        Gotthilf & Barbara Stickel.

Mr. Stickel was a charter member of St. Paul Lutheran Church. He was
instrumental in organizing, planning and building of the present church. He
served as an officer of the church board. His wife, Barbara, was a member of
the Ladies Aid. Both were lifelong members of the church.

Five children were born to this union: Hedwig, died in infancy; Sigmund, died
in 1968; Mrs. Wilma Ryan, of Denver, CO; Mrs. Sylvia Feickert, of St. Paul, MN;
Mrs. Meta Bain, Aberdeen, SD . There are also 13 grand-children, 20
great-grandchildren and five great-great-grandchildren.

EDWIN and NORMA STOECKER

Edwin W. Stoecker, the son of Fred and Christina (Lehr) Stoecker, was born
October 13, 1917, rural McPherson County, northeast of Hosmer, SD. He attended
rural school near the family farm, through the eighth grade. He lived with his

On September 18, 1949 at Hoffnungsfeld Congregational Church, rural Newton, SD,
Edwin was united in marriage to Norma Pietz. Norma, the daughter of John and

of Hosmer, SD. She attended rural school through the eighth grade and helped

After their marriage they farmed in Blaine and Moscow townships until 1958. Due

their local school boards for several years.

In October 1958 they moved to Leola, SD, where Edwin was employed at the
McPherson County Courthouse. Edwin was register of deeds when poor health
forced his retirement in 1962.

Edwin passed away July 22, 1981. He is buried at Sunset Memorial Gardens,
Aberdeen, SD.

Norma was employed at the Leola Bakery from 1958 to 1975.

        Edwin, Norma and Keenan Stoecker.

Leola school, graduating from high school in 1971. He attended Northern State
College and is presently employed at 3M Company at Aberdeen, SD.

Norma resides in Leola and is a member of St. James Lutheran Church.

JOHN and ELIZABETH STOLLER

John Stoller was born near Odessa, Russia on June 24, 1862. He was a son of
Dominick Stoller, who was born and reared in the same locality.

John received his education in the schools of his native land and was a lad of
ten years at the time of his immigration to America.

In 1872 the Stollers, in company with about 40 other families from the same
district, came to America. They proceeded west from New York and temporarily
located at Sandusky, OH. Dominick Stoller and three other men of the company of
immigrants set forth in search of a location, making an investigation tour
through various states. They finally decided to colonize in what is now the
state of South Dakota. The entire company moved forward to the new home on the
frontier, arriving in Yankton on April 22, 1872. Previous to coming to America,
Dominick Stoller had been engaged in farming and raising sheep. He continued in
the same line of industry after coming to South Dakota.

On January 9, 1883, John Stoller was united in marriage with Elizabeth Kost.
She was born in Odessa, Russia and accompanied her parents on their immigration
to America when a child. The family came to South Dakota in 1874, thus being
numbered among the early pioneers of the present state.

In 1885, John came to McPherson County, taking up a quarter section of land in
the center of the county, and there remained for two years, engaged in farming
and stock raising. They then moved to Eureka, being one of the first settlers
in the town. They stayed three years and seven months. He was employed on
salary in a mercantile store. He then engaged in the hardware business in
Eureka, forming at the time a partnership with C. J. Hezel, manager of the
Golden Rule mercantile house in Aberdeen. This association continued until
1893, when Frederick Hepperle purchased Mr. Hezel's interest in the enterprise.
In 1902 they opened a second store in Eureka, where they also carried a full
line of merchandise, running the two stores in conjunction.

Mr. Stoller took active part in public life, serving as school commissioner and
justice of the peace. In 1902 he elected to represent his district in the state
senate.

        John & Elizabeth Stoller.

John and Elizabeth had five children: Magdalena Lortcher, now residing in
Winona, MN; Hildegarde Meidinger, resides in Leola; and Amelia, Rosetta and
John F. Stoller are deceased.

The Stoller family moved to Leola in 1919. They built the building that now
houses an auto body shop and a preschool nursery, where they had a Ford
dealership for many years.

Elizabeth died April 2, 1927 and John died December 16, 1929.

JOSEPH and VERONICA STEPHAN

Joseph Stephan was born in South Russia on December 11, 1861. He came to
America on the steamship Ellie in October, 1886. He arrived in Ipswich, SD,
where some of his friends from Russia were already living. He got a job as a
farm laborer, learned the language and the American way of life. The Sears
Roebuck catalog was his textbook, where he learned the language by pictures and
associations.

He then acquired a quarter of land as a homestead in Howard Township 7 1/2
miles southwest of Leola. He walked along guiding a hand plow drawn by a pair
of oxen, breaking up a few acres of prairie. A prairie fire in the fall burned
his home and all his possessions. He had no money and no place to go; with the
help of his neighbors he started up again.

        The Joseph Stephan Family.

On May 5, 1890, he married Veronica Zahn at Ipswich, SD. She had also come from
Russia and worked as a maid in the Sherman Hotel in Aberdeen. An ox team
provided the transportation for their honeymoon from Ipswich to the farm. It
was a hot day in May and the ox team was getting tired. When they were half way
home, the oxen spotted a pond of water near the road and took off for that.
There sat Joe and his bride in a borrowed wagon in the middle of the pond,
waiting for the oxen to cool off and continue on the homeward journey.

Three daughters were born to this union: Anna, Magdalena and Elizabeth, all
born and raised on the family homestead southwest of Leola. Anna was born April
17, 1892. She attended rural school in Howard Township and later taught rural
school for many years in the Leola area. During the summer she attended
Northern State College in Aberdeen to improve her teaching career.

Anna helped her father in the field, plowing with four horses and also, walking
along behind a horse drawn drag.

In 1927 she and her parents moved to Leola, where she took care of them and
furnished room and board for high school girls before there was bus service.
She had been active in church affairs all her life. She was a member of Our
Lady of Perpetual Help Catholic Church, St. Ann's Altar Society, Ave Maria
Study Club and was a leader of the Holy Rosary Confraternity. She had great
pride in her home and yard.

Mrs. Stephan died July 30, 1944; Joseph died June 15, 1945.

Anna died September 11, 1983, age 91 years, 5 months, 24 days. Anna was active
up to a short time of her passing away, out early in the morning tending her
business and visiting with friends.

Magdalena (Lena) attended grade school and two years of high school; taught
school and in June of 1917 married John Kessler. They had two children.
Celestine lives in Brookings, is the co-manager of the Sexauer Grain Company,
and has five children. Mrs. Oscar (Angela) Schilling, lives in Leola and works
in the Leola State Bank. They have two sons. John died February 1, 1961;
Magdalena (Lena) died November 3, 1980.

Elizabeth went to rural school, graduated from Leola High School and attended
Northern State College, two years. She taught rural school for four years in
Edmunds County. She married Walter Kline on June 29, 1926. They moved on the
Stephan homestead in 1927, where they lived until they retired and moved to
Leola in 1961. They had six children: one daughter died in infancy; Loretta
(Mrs. Ray Dylla), Webster, has four children; Leo, lives near Warner, and has
nine children; Juliann (Mrs. Wilbur Haiar), Alexandria, SD, has four children;
Leonard, of Aberdeen, has two children; and Rita (Mrs. Elmer Zulk), Leola, has
five children.

SIDNEY JOHN SR. and IRENE SWANSON

Sidney John Swanson, Sr. was one of eight children born to Andrew Swanson, a
baker's apprentice from Sweden, and Anna (Rundberg) Swanson, a minister's
daughter, on January 15, 1904. His parents moved to Devils Lake, ND and then to
Moorhead, MN, where he grew up and attended school until he finished his
freshman year. He started to work with his father in the bakery and learned the
trade.

Irene Ivonna Eloise Hall was one of six children born to Emil Hall and Anna
(Olson) Hall on February 1, 1905. They farmed near Hawley, MN. They moved into
Hawley following her father's death. Her mother, Anna, provided a living by
being a nurse and midwife. Irene attended school, graduating from Hawley High
School. She attended college at Moorhead, MN and taught school at Black Duck,
MN.

        Sidney, Sr. & Irene Swanson.

Irene met Sid Sr. in Hawley, MN and they were married on November 28, 1924 in
Moorhead, MN. He worked in bakeries at Hawley, Lake Park, Ada and Moorhead.
They moved to La Moure, ND and operated the bakery for two years. It was in
1942 that they appeared on the Leola scene. They owned and operated the bakery
in Leola for six years until their son, Sid Jr. bought and took over in 1948.
Sid and Irene started bakeries in Ashley, ND, Hoven, Faulkton, and Ipswich, SD,
where they stayed until they retired in 1970, after 55 years in the bakery
business. Their son, Earl, took over the Ipswich bakery for several more years.
They have always maintained their home in Leola. All of the seven children
graduated from Leola High School.

Bonita Ann (Gill) was born in Moorhead, MN March 18, 1926. She attended schools
in Minnesota and North Dakota and graduated from LHS in 1944. She married L. D.
(Bud) Gill in 1947 (see Gill history).

Sidney John Swanson, Jr. is still operating the bakery that his father started.
(See Sid Swanson, Jr. history.)

Earl Hubert was born in Hawley, MN on May 21, 1929. He attended schools in
Minnesota and North Dakota and graduated from LHS in 1947. He has four
children: Earl Hubert, Jr., Alan Jay, Valerie Ann, and Dirk Steven. Earl is now
residing in Milford, IA, and is employed by the American Legion Club.

Shirley Irene was born in Hawley, MN on April 13, 1931. She attended schools in
Minnesota and North Dakota and graduated from LHS in 1949. She married Jack
Britcliffe (now deceased). She has three children: Michael Jon, Mark Edward and
Robin Irene. Shirley is now married to Joe Zrelak. They reside in Barstow, CA
where she owns a dress shop and Joe is in the carpet business.

James Edmund was born August 8, 1936 in Moorhead, MN. He attended school in
Leola and graduated in 1954. He married Maxine Hansen. They have two children:
Signe Olene and Kjersten Irene. They live in Madison, SD, where Jim is the
professor of English at Dakota State College.

Jerome Allen was born April 30, 1938 at Ada, MN. He attended school in Leola
and graduated in 1956. He married Diane Bessler and they have seven children:
Cheryl Virginia, Ann Jean Carol, Sara Jane, Kari Linn, Kelly Lee, Rebecca
Irene, and Jerome Allen. They now reside in Osnabrock, ND where Jerry is the
director of the Good Samaritan Nursing Home.

Diane Marie was born May 27, 1940. She attended school in Leola and graduated
in 1958. She married James Sitter and they have three children: Andrew John,
Angela Michele, and Daniel James. They reside in Aberdeen, SD. Sid and Irene
had 29 grandchildren and 16 great-grandchildren.

Irene passed away August 31, 1979 and Sid passed away October 19, 1983.

SIDNEY JOHN JR. and AGNES SWANSON

Sidney John Swanson, Jr., better known as "Tubby," was born in Moorhead, MN on
May 3, 1927, to Sid, Sr., a baker, and Irene Swanson, a teacher, both of
Swedish descent. He moved with his parents to several towns in Minnesota,
including Hawley, Lake Park and Ada, and then to La Moure, ND; but always in
the bakery business. He came to Leola with his father in November of 1942 to
take over the Leola Bakery, the family following in a few weeks. He graduated
from LHS in 1945. He served two years in the U.S. Army.

Agnes Arlene Jundt was born to Fred and Rose Jundt in McPherson County, SD, on
May 24, 1926. She grew up on the farm and graduated from LHS in 1944. She
attended NSC in Aberdeen and taught in rural schools for three years.

Agnes accompanied her parents on a trip to California in 1946 and decided to
stay in San Diego and go to business college. She worked for the Veterans
Administration in San Diego until Tubby was discharged from the army. He
stopped in San Diego to visit Agnes and they decided to come back to Leola.
They were married December 31 1947, in Aberdeen, SD.

They started their married life in the bakery that they bought from Tubby's
father. They bought the building that occupied the bakery and Gamble store from
Pete Sherman. Al Rudes rented the Gamble store section which helped their
finances. Tubby and Agnes did some remodeling, and installed a new revolving
tray oven replacing the old coke burning oven. They lived in the Swanson home
until they remodeled the second floor of the bakery into an apartment. On
February 11, 1959, a fire destroyed the bakery and apartment and they lost
everything they owned. They saved only what was most precious to them, their
two living children, Susan and John. Tubby and Agnes rebuilt the bakery and
were in business in August of that same year. They have been in the bakery for

GRANT and ELIZABETH TOOKER

Rev. Grant Tooker, born in Kankakee, IL in 1872 came to Dakota Territory with
his parents. They traveled by oxen and a covered wagon. His only memory of the
trip was a pet kitten he was allowed to bring along. When they reached their
destination (in Willow Township), they built a sod house and lived in it until
a new and better home was built. The new home was one mile from the present
Brown County line. He lived there nearly all his life.

The new house served as an area Post Office and the address was Delhi, SD. It
was operated by Grant's mother, Josephine Tooker. The house was a large house
for its day and was moved from Wetonka by a 40-horse team.

Grant's father, James, was a Civil War veteran who died at an early age,
leaving Grant to support his mother and three sisters, Eva, Jennie and Olive.
He accomplished this by farming and teaching school.

Elizabeth Thompson was born in Indiana in 1883. She came to Dakota Territory
with her parents, six sisters and one brother. Their first home was a log cabin
on the Elm River where her father worked for Earl Webster. Later they worked on
the Agar Ranch, six miles north of Wetonka, where they raised several thousand
sheep. Elizabeth and her brother Tom herded the sheep in every kind of weather.
While living on the Agar Ranch, the family had a typhoid epidemic where the
entire family was very ill. Two teenage sisters, Dora and Ada, died within two
weeks of each other.

Elizabeth attended country school where Grant Tooker was the teacher. Student
and teacher fell in love and were married in 1905. They lived on the Tooker
homestead until 1936.

Grant was ordained (1902) in the Church of the Brethern and served that church
until 1933. A minister did not get a salary in those days, consequently he
depended on the farm to support his family. He had many interests and served
the public well. He was a McPherson County Commissioner for several years and
used his influence towards securing a nine months term for county schools. He
was vitally interested in education and worked hard to further the interests
and benefits of education.

Grant remembered early pioneer life very well. He used to tell about the times
they were very poor. One difficult winter, having no flour for bread, James
Tooker walked 15 miles to Westport to ask for flour. He had no money with which
to pay, but the kind grocery man let him take a 50 pound sack of flour. James
carried the 50 pound sack on his back and walked every mile of the way home.

Grant and Elizabeth had five children. They were, Marion, Lester, Olive, Dora
and Calvin. The children attended rural school Willow No. 4. Lester and Marion
graduated from Barnard High School, Olive from Leola, and Dora and Calvin
finished their education in California. All of the Tooker family moved to
California in 1936 except Olive (Hayenga), who lives at Andover. The others
reside in the Modesto, CA area.

The only thing that remains of the Tooker homestead are the trees that were
planted in the 1920's. They are across the road from the building site. They
remain a monument to beauty and conservation these 63 years later.

FRED and NELLIE TSCHAPPAT

Fred Tschappat, son of Julius and Adele Tschappat was born May 6, 1877 in
Convert, Switzerland. In the year of 1885, he came to the United States with
his parents, a brother and sister. They settled for a short time in Orville,
OH, then moved to Hickory County, MO, where they lived about 20 years. During
this time nine more children were born to Julius and Adele Tschappat. The
family consisted of five girls and seven boys.

While in Missouri Fred mentioned many different places he worked in Missouri.

In 1909 Fred's parents moved to a farm northeast of Hecla, and later when
Adele's husband died, she moved into Hecla and remained there until the time of
her death in 1931.

Fred also worked at various places in Iowa, around Storm Lake and in
southeastern Iowa, around Swedesburg. In Swedesburg is where he met his future
wife, Nellie Turnwall.

Nellie Turnwall was born at Swedesburg, IA, May 10, 1887. She was baptized and
confirmed in the Lutheran faith at Swedesburg, IA.

In 1909 Fred came by immigrant train with Carl, Herman and Nellie Turnwall from
Swedesburg, IA to Frederick, SD. He worked with Carl Turnwall on his steam
engine, breaking ground and threshing. They threshed for many farmers around
Frederick and Leola. Fred dearly loved steam engines, and mentioned how he
would have liked to have been a railroad engineer but it never materialized.

Nellie Turnwall, Carl, and Herman's sister, cooked for the threshing crew in a
cook car and kept house for her brothers. She then became employed in Leola,
working for several different families before her marriage.

On April 11, 1912 Nellie was married to Fred Tschappat. They moved to a farm
three miles south of Leola and later bought the farm.

They then began farming for a number of years. They farmed with horses; he had
some good horses of which he was very proud. Gradually he changed from horses
to tractors. His first tractor was a one cylinder Titan, he then got a Rumely
Oil pull, with a six bottom plow. In later years he bought a Hart Parr and an
International tractor. He also milked many cows and specialized in hog raising.
He went through both good and hard times as did many others.

        The Fred Tschappat Family. Back: Gladys, Clihon and Ethyle. Front:
        Nellie, June and Fred.

Four children were born to Fred and Nellie. Gladys was born January 5, 1916,
married Albert Berreth on January 1, 1940. Ethyle was born November 27, 1918,
married Otto Kapp on October 17, 1947. June was born June 5, 1920, married
Victor Kamm on June 25, 1941. Clifton was born September 5, 1923 and married
Clara Gienger September 10, 1944.

Fred remained on his farm until his passing at the age of 74 on January 18,
1952, from coronary thrombosis. Shortly after his death Nellie turned the farm
over to her son, Clifton. Her son and sons-in-law built her a home in Leola,
where she lived until her death, July 25, 1960. She was a member of St. Paul's
Lutheran Church.

CHARLES and CEDORA TURNER

Charles Turner was the son of John and Margaret (Jehu) Turner, natives of
England and Wales, respectively. They came to America in 1838 and established
their home on a Wisconsin farm, where Charles was born January 13, 1853. He
left home at the age of 17. Graduating from the State Normal School at
Whitewater, WI, he was a well-educated man who did much to advance the cause of
education in the localities in which he taught.

In the spring of 1881 he came to Lake County, Dakota Territory, where he was
involved in the field of banking. In 1884 he came to Leola where he was
responsible for organizing the McPherson County Bank, later known as the Bank
of Leola--also known as the Turner Bank--of which he was the president
continuously for 31 years. He was engaged in other business ventures,
particularly in ranching. In fact, the Turner Ranch was well known throughout
the area.

Charles and Delphy were members of the Methodist Episcopal Church. Charles was
a charter member of Leola Lodge No. 154, A.F. & A.M., serving as secretary; the
Odd Fellows Lodge, the Scottish Rite and the Mystic Shrine. He served on the
Leola school board and as register of deeds of McPherson County. Delphy was a
past matron of the Order of Eastern Star. The Turners contributed much to the
political, civic and cultural growth of this area.

        Les, George and Lyle Turner.

In 1880 Charles married Cedora Johnson, daughter of Isaiah and Nancy Jane
Johnson. To them was born a son, Worth Charles, (see Worth Turner history).
Cedora passed away in February 1887 at Leola.

On August 8, 1888, Charles Turner married Delphy Johnson, sister of his first
wife, at Leola. Charles and Delphy had five children: Leslie, Lyle, George,
Madge and Gerald. All grew up in Leola and attended school there. All are
deceased except Lyle, who is living with his daughter, Joan Jacobson, in
Cascade, CO.

GEORGE and LILY TURNER

The parents of Lily Valentine Turner (1900-1961) and George Turner (1891-1958)
were instrumental in the settling and developing of the Leola area. George's
father, Charles Turner (1863-1915) was a pioneer rancher and businessman. (See
Charles Turner family history.)

Lilly's father, Robert Valentine (1862-1917) owned and operated two oil rigs
and operated the first machine and implement business. Before his death, he
sold this business to Frank Kohlhoff. Lilly's mother was Wilhelmina Glaesman
Valentine (1888-1958). The Valentine children were Clara, Albert, Richard and
Lilly.

        George & Lily Turner.

George and Lilly were married in 1928. During the years they lived in Leola,
George was a banker, sold insurance and was a cattle buyer. He was a charter
member of the Eastern Star, Commander of the American Legion, and Mayor. Their
child, Viva, was born in 1932. She married Orley Rath and lives in Sioux Falls,
SD at the present time. Their three children are Laurel, Steven and Nancy.

WORTH and JOHANNA TURNER

Worth Charles Turner was born December 7, 1884, at Leola, Dakota Territory; to
Charles and Cedora (Johnson) Turner, natives of Wisconsin. Worth was the first
child born in Leola, where he lived most of his life. After attending school in
Leola, he furthered his education at Dakota Wesleyan University at Mitchell.

Worth, like other members of his family, was involved in the field of banking
(serving as vice president of the Bank of Leola) and in the cattle business. In
1918, he was elected president of the board of trustees of the village of
Leola. Then after Leola was incorporated as a city, he was again elected to the
same capacity in 1925, which now carried the title of mayor.

Worth married Johanna Frostad on November 16, 1910, in Leola, SD. The Turners
were active in church and community affairs, belonging to the Methodist church.
Worth was a member of the Masonic Lodge and Jennie (as she was called) was a
charter member of the Past Matrons Association of Leola, Chapter 124, Order of
the Eastern Star, serving as vice president when it was organized in 1928.

Worth and Jennie had two children; Charles Vernon, born August 21, 1911, and
Mildred Delphy, born October 14, 1914, who grew up and attended school in
Leola. Vernon met and married Lillian Ouimet (pronounced Wemet) of Minneapolis.
They had two children, Robert and Judith. Delphy married Walter Hepperle and
they had one child, Duane Richard. Delphy died February 13, 1970. In their
later years, Worth and Jennie moved to Costa Mesa. CA. There they operated a
Western Auto dealer store. Vernon was a partner in Turner Cut Rate Drug Store
in Newport Beach, CA.

Mrs. Turner died October 13, 1967 and Mr. Turner died shortly after on November
19, 1967, at Costa Mesa.

CARL and CARMEL TURNWALL

Carl Oscar Turnwall was born January 21, 1884 in Malmo, Sweden. His family
immigrated to America when Carl was six weeks old. They settled in Swedesburg,
IA where Carl later attended school. (The building with some additions is now
being used as a town hall.)

Carl helped his father on the farm and later began farming for himself. When he
wasn't working his farm, he laid tile (for drainage) for neighbors. His sister
Nellie kept house for him. In 1909, Carl, with his brother Herman and sister
Nellie, moved by immigrant car to Frederick, SD. Here, Carl with his steam rig
broke 500 acres of sod for neighbors and put in a crop of his own. In 1910,
they moved to Leola where Carl broke more land for cultivation purposes.

Shortly after moving to Leola, Carl met his future wife, Carmel Ellen Mahoney.
Carmel was born December 23, 1893, in Dubuque County, IA. Later the Mahoney
family moved to Forbes, ND. Carmel attended school in Dubuque and graduated
from the eighth grade at Forbes. In 1910, her family moved to Leola where she
lived until her death, April 29, 1941, at the early age of 47. Carmel was a
member of the Catholic Church, a good and loving wife and mother, and friendly,
helpful neighbor.

Carl and Carmel were married February 23, 1912 and moved on a rented farm two
miles north and three-fourths of a mile east of Leola where they lived for 16
years.

        Carl & Carmel Turnwall.

During the fall and winter of 1928-1929, they remodeled the house and built a
barn on a farm they had owned for sometime. This farm was located one mile
north and 1 1/4 miles east of Leola. They moved into the house during the
winter.

For many years, Carl farmed around a thousand acres. His early farming was done
with horses but as soon as they were available he converted to tractors. His
first tractor was a Fordson followed by one John Deere after another. For a
number of years he threshed with his steam engine both for himself and his
neighbors. Later he bought a combine to harvest his grain and at 85, he still
ran the combine.

Later Carl moved to town with his daughter-in-law where he lived for a few
years. He then lived for a time with his son John and his wife. When he got so
he needed constant care, he went to live at the Colonial Manor in Ipswich,
where he spent his last couple of years. On January 25, 1979, he passed away in
the hospital in Ipswich.

Carl was confirmed in the Swedesburg Lutheran Church and was a member of the
St. Paul's Lutheran Church in Leola. He served on the board of directors for
the Coop, served as Leola township clerk for over 20 years, served on the board
of education at Leola from 1938-1950, and served on the McPherson County
Selective Service Board from 1954-1968. He was very supportive of worthy
causes, helping many with work and financial support.

The family consisted of seven children: Hannah, was born December 25, 1912 and
died in infancy. Florence (Thompson) was born January 2, 1914. She spent 33
years in education, teaching and counseling. She and her husband, Dick, have
two children, five grandchildren and two great grandchildren. They live in
Gettysburg, SD; Mary (Mack) was born May 15, 1915. She spent 35 1/2 years as a
federal employee. She married Ralph Mack and they had one daughter and three
grandchildren. Mary passed away October 28, 1978; Oliver (refer to Oliver
Turnwall history); John J. (see John J. Turnwall history); Stewart A. was born
October 19, 1918. He was prominently identified with high school and college
sports. Sgt. Stewart Turnwall was killed in action on Luzon in the Philippines
on February 6, 1945. He was awarded the Silver Star, posthumously, for
gallantry and bravery in action; Dr. Lloyd W. (refer to Lloyd Turnwall
history).

JOHN and CAROLINE TURNWALL

Johan Oscar Carlson was born near the church parish of Tornfall, Farramling,
Sweden, June 27, 1854. His future wife, Caroline Josephine Peterson was born
August 22, 1860 at Malmo, Sweden. Here she grew to young womanhood and on June
25, 1880 was united in marriage to Johan O. Carlson.

        John & Caroline Turnwall.

Four years later they immigrated to America bringing with them their daughter,
Annie Marie; son, Carl Oscar; and nephew, Carl, son of Johan's brother Gustof.
The nephew, Carl, had remained in Sweden with his grandparents when his parents
came to America a year earlier.

Gustof and Johan Carlson changed their family name to Turnwall when they
settled at Swedesburg, IA. Apparently the name change was necessary because of
confusion over the common name of Carlson in the Swedish community. It is
believed the name Turnwall was derived from the Swedish name, Tornfall, a
church parish in Sweden.

While living in Swedesburg, IA, John farmed and laid tile (for drainage
purposes) for other farmers. In 1911, the John O. Turnwall family moved to
Leola settling one-half mile north of town. They had bought this land and other
quarters of land in 1908. In 1911, they built a large two-story house (still
standing) now owned and occupied by the grandson, John J. Turnwall's widow,
Bernice Turnwall.

John O. Turnwall was killed on July 8, 1914 when lightning struck and burned
the family barn. He had entered the barn to remove a prize team of mules from
the burning building.

Caroline continued to make her home on the farm, aided by her sons who took
care of the farm duties. In 1925 she joined the St. Paul's Lutheran Church and
kept up her membership until her death. In 1944, she gave up her home and went
to live with her children. At the time of her death, February 12, 1949,
Caroline was living with her daughter, Annie Anderson in Storm Lake, IA.
Caroline was married 34 years and a widow for 34 years.

John and Caroline's family consisted of 14 children of which three are still
living: Algot Turnwall, born October 6, 1880, died in infancy; Annie Marie
Anderson, October 23, 1881, died November 13, 1964; Carl Oscar Turnwall,
January 21, 1884, died January 25, 1979; Joseph Herman Turnwall, March 20,
1886, died June 4, 1960; Nellie Josephine Tschappat, May 10, 1887, died July
25, 1960; Ellen Sophie Durheim, July 29, 1889, died July 7, 1980; Victoria
Amalie Turnwall, December 22, 1891, died November 29, 1903; Axel Hjalmer
Turnwall, May 20, 1893, died April 2, 1972; Edith Elvera Durheim, September 6,
1895, now living in Deer Park, WA; Ernest Fabin Turnwall, September 8, 1897,
died May 25, 1970; George William Turnwall, October 8, 1899, now living in Deer
Park, WA; Walter Paul Turnwall, April 12, 1902, died December 25, 1909; Esther
Alverda Jeske, December 17, 1904, now living in Eldora, IA; Albert Theodore
Turnwall, December 9, 1906, died May 17, 1931.

JOHN and BERNICE TURNWALL

John, son of Carl and Carmel Turnwall, was born September 14, 1917. John
attended school in Leola and lived here all his life except for the years he
served in the Army (1942-1945). John saw service in the Philippines. Sgt. John
Turnwall was the recipient of the Bronze Star and received his discharge from
the Army on October 18, 1945. On November 1, 1946, he and Bernice Kamm were
married and moved on his grandfather's homestead where they farmed for a number
of years. Later he rented out his land and worked in construction and ranch
work.

Bernice was born April 20, 1924 to Mr. and Mrs. Fred Kamm, Leola, SD. She has
been a teacher for 34 years. She graduated from Leola High School, and Northern
State College and is presently teaching in the Leola grade school.

John and Bernice were blessed with four sons: Stewart, married to Julie
Nickleson November 5, 1978. They have six children. Dick lives in Ohio and has
one daughter, Ginny. He is a careerman in the Navy. Patrick is married to Cindy
L. Mock of Forbes, ND. They have two daughters. John Jr. is married to Terri
Lake. They have three children. All the Turnwall boys graduated from Leola High
School.

John passed away in March of 1983. Bernice still resides in Leola.

LLOYD (LEFTY) and HARRIET TURNWELL

One of the finer athletes to come out of Leola High School was Lloyd (Lefty)
Turnwall, youngest of the six children of Carl and Carmel Turnwall. Lefty
graduated in 1938 as a three-sport letterman. During those years, the Leola
Pirates dominated the North Central Conference. The Pirates won the Conference
Crown in football during the 1936, 1937 and 1938 seasons. The Pirates also won
the basketball title in 1937 and 1938.

Upon graduation in 1938, Lefty enrolled at Dakota Wesleyan University, where he
became a three-sport letterman, lettering in football, basketball and track.

Finishing his Bachelor's degree in the spring of 1942, Lefty was called into
the U.S. Air Force for 4 1/2 years, with 26 months in the Pacific Theatre.

Discharged from the Air Force in 1946, Lefty married his college sweetheart,
Harriet Long of Armour, SD. They were hired to teach in Leola. Harriet taught
the third and fourth grades for two years, having taught previously in Wagner
and Sturgis. Lefty taught in high school and coached all sports. He stayed 11
1/2 years as a teacher, coach, principal, and the last four years was
superintendent of schools.

        Harriet & Lloyd Turnwall.

During those years Lefty played baseball for the Leola Town Team, with several
appearances in the State Amateur Tournament. He also led the Leola Indee
Basketball Team into numerous State Tournaments. In the first State Indee
Tourney, Aberdeen defeated Leola in the finals, 43-41, with Lefty selected as a
unanimous choice for the all-tournament team. In 1948, the Leola Indee
Basketball team won the championship of the State Legion Tournament, by
defeating Rapid City 52-50, with Turnwall leading the Leola team. In 1947, this
same team was defeated in the semi-finals of the Legion Tournament.
Undoubtedly, the greatest game played in the All-Dakota Basketball Tournament
was the double-overtime finals in 1948, in which Henry defeated Ipswich-Leola,
led by Lefty Turnwall, who scored 29 points.

While teaching and coaching the Pirates, Lefty earned his Master's degree at
Northern. He resigned his Leola job in 1957, to become superintendent of
schools at Lemmon, thereby leaving the coaching ranks. Staying in Lemmon for
six years, he resigned in 1963 to become president of an Omaha Business
College. After one year in Omaha, Lefty became superintendent of schools in
Huron and remained there for 17 years. While in the Huron position, he took
time to earn his Doctorate degree at the University of South Dakota.

In July 1981, he retired and moved to Rapid City. During his educational career
Lefty earned many honors and awards with various educational boards and
commissions.

Peggy, the oldest of three children, is married and has two children, living in
Kansas City. Mike is married and lives in Chamberlain. Robert is single, living
in Minneapolis.

OLIVER and MILDRED TURNWALL

Oliver Turnwall was the oldest son born to Carl and Carmel (Mahoney) Turnwall
on September 13, 1916. He was raised on a farm one mile east, one mile north,
and one-fourth mile east of Leola.

Oliver married Mildred Muhlbeier on October 11, 1943, at Leola. They lived on
the family farm until Oliver died of a heart attack on June 7, 1970. Mildred
continued living on the farm for several years before moving into Leola.

Mildred married Arden Vietmeier on October 18, 1975, at Leola. They live on a
small farm seven miles west and two miles south of Leola.

Oliver and Mildred have two daughters. Carmel was born on October 23, 1945, and
Susan was born on December 29, 1949. A son, Thomas, died at birth.

Carmel married Ronald Heyd on June 24, 1967. They live in Aberdeen, where
Carmel is a loan officer at United Federal Savings and Loan, and Ron is
employed at Hub City Feed and Seed.

Susan married Donald Hoffman on September 15, 1968. They live in Leola. Donald
is the oil department manager of the Ipswich Coop. They were blessed with one
daughter, Kristi, who was born on September 22, 1975.

ALBERT L. and FLOSSIE VALENTINE

Albert Louis Valentine was born September 22, 1891 to Robert and Wilhelmiena
Valentine. He and his brother Richard and two sisters, Clara and Lily, grew up
on the family farm seven miles southeast of Leola. They walked to school
located three miles north of their farm at that time. They and all the children
attending school spoke German at home. They tell of having to stay all day and
all night at school when a raging blizzard came up, preventing their return
home.

        Flossie & Albert Valentine.

In 1916 Albert married Flossie Mae McLaughlin. Their wedding trip by train to
Yellowstone National Park was interrupted at Miles City, MT by an urgent call
back to the farm. Albert's father passed away the following year, 1917.

Albert and Flossie remained on the farm where they raised a family of four
girls. The girls attended rural school, Willow No. 3, then located 80 rods east
of the family farm, built in 1925. It was a very modern school for the times,
with coal burning furnace and indoor chemical toilets. Because of the many
Valentine families settled in that area it was known as the "Valentine School."

The family later lived in Leola where the girls all graduated from Leola High
School. Albert worked as a machinist for many years and in Minneapolis at a
Defense Plant during WWII. They spent their retirement years in California
where they helped manage a trailer court until Flossie's death in March of
1965. Albert died in July of 1975.

The Valentine girls are as follows. Olive is the widow of Henry McElhone. She
lives at Clear Lake, MN. They have seven children.

Beverly is married to Clemens Crace. They are retired and live at Isle, MN.

Vera is married to Eugene Kulm. They are retired and live at Stockton, CA. They
have three children.

Eva is married to William Hilgemann. They have three children and are presently
living in Leola.

ELYARD and LEONA VILHAUER

Elyard Vilhauer is a lifelong McPherson County resident. He was born September
19, 1921 to August (1890-1977) and Anna (1893-1983) Jundt Vilhauer. Elyard is
one of a family of four brothers and seven sisters. He married Leona Brandner
June 11, 1944.

Leona was born June 5, 1925 to Albert and Pauline (Walker) Brandner. After
marriage, she and Elyard farmed in the Hosmer area until 1950 when they bought
the former Fred Leicht farm. This farm has been occupied by the Vilhauers ever
since.

        Leona & Elyard Vilhauer.

Children in the Vilhauer family are as follows: Leo was born July 7, 1945 at
Eureka, SD and married Ruthie Rueb of Ashley, ND. They have two children,
Debbie and Deon. They live two miles south of Elyard and Leona's farm.

Arlene was born December 9, 1948. She is married to Gary Webb (1968) and they
have five children, Mike, Jeff, Greg, Dan and Amber. The Webb family lives in
Aberdeen, SD.

Paul was born November 29, 1950. He married Hazel Rath in 1978 and they live in
Longmont, CO. Paul has two children, Tracy and Troy.

The Vilhauers are members of the Assembly of God Church in Ashley, ND.

JACOB and MAGDALENA VILHAUER

Jacob Vilhauer was born June 14, 1886, to Fred and Katherine (Hieb) Vilhauer,
in McPherson County. He lived with his parents until he married Magdalena Hieb,
near Hosmer, SD, on November 24, 1908.

They lived on a farm 15 miles northwest of Leola until 1944 when they retired
and moved to Aberdeen, SD. Two years later they moved to Leola. In 1968, they
became residents of the Lutheran Home at Eureka, SD. In 1969, Jacob moved to
the Hosmer Senior Citizens Home, for skilled nursing care. Jacob died June 11,
1971, at the Holy Infant Hospital, Hoven, SD.

Magdalena, the daughter of Jacob and his wife (Helm) Hieb, was born at Odessa,
South Russia on February 7, 1888. She came to the United States with her
parents in 1895. They settled on a farm northeast of Hosmer, SD. She died
November 26, 1972 at the Eureka Hospital.

Jacob and Magdalena were the parents of ten children, seven are still living;
August, Raymond E., Clarence, and Emil, and three daughters, Irmgard, Erna Lea
and Dina E. Three sons, Samuel, Jacob E. and Harold are deceased.

The Vilhauers were members of the Leola St. James Lutheran Church.

IRMGARD (IRMA) VILHAUER

Irma Vilhauer was born November 11, 1913, to Jacob and Magdalena Vilhauer. She
was 14 years of age when the McPherson County Courthouse was dedicated.

        Irmgard Vilhauer.

She went to work in Aberdeen during the depression years. In 1944, she went to
Minneapolis, MN. She worked as a seamstress for 30 years. During WWII, she made
hammocks for the Army.

In 1964, Irma moved to California, where she continued to sew until retirement.
Irma presently resides in Los Angeles, CA.

LEO and RUTHIE VILHAUER

Leo Vilhauer, a graduate of LHS, was born July 7, 1945 to Elyard and Leona
Brandner Vilhauer at Eureka. On March 12, he married Ruthie Rueb, an Ashley
High School graduate, who was born July 6, 1944 at Streeter, ND to George H.
and Alma Sayler Rueb.

        The Leo Vilhauer Family. Deon, Ruthie, Leo, and Deb.

The Vilhauers have two children: Debbie, born May 24, 1967; and Deon, born
August 27, 1970. Both attend Leola Public Schools.

The Vilhauers live on a farm about 14 miles northwest of Leola and attend the
Bethel Assembly of God Church in Ashley, ND.

JOHN I and FREDRICKA VOEGELE

John Voegele I was born in Germany and married Fredricka Martz. Several
children were born in Germany and some in America.

        The John I. Voegele Family.

The family lived in Russia for a short time. Searching for a better life, the
family migrated to America in 1884. They settled 18 miles southwest of Leola.
They raised eight children: Kate (Martz), Fredricka (Mohr), John Jr., Fred,
Christian, Eva (Jesser), Rose (Hegel), and Christina Voegele.

John died in the year of the flu epidemic (1918).

JOHN II and CAROLINA VOEGELE

John Voegele, Jr. was born in 1876, in Germany. He married Carolina Becker in
1897. They lived on a farm 12 miles west of Leola. Four children were born. The
first, a daughter, died in infancy. There were three sons: Emil, Julius and
John.

        John II & Carolina Voegele.

Carolina was an invalid for nine years. She died in March, 1940. John, Jr. died
in April, 1941.

JOHN III and LILLIAN VOEGELE

John was born November 14, 1907, 12 miles west of Leola. He grew up tending to
duties of the farm. He married a neighbor girl, Lillian Binder. Lillian is one
of six children born to Daniel and Magdalena (Zumbaum) Binder.

John and Lillian continued to live on the farm. Three children were born. The
first-born died an infant; Myron, born in March 1931; and Violet, born in
February of 1934.

        John III, Lillian, Viola and Myron Voegele.

In 1964 John and Lillian moved to Leola where John started a shoe shop located
in the old Central Lumber Company building. In November of 1965 the building
burned, forcing him to locate elsewhere. John worked in the Sherman Shoe Shop
in Aberdeen for six years. He has a shop in his home at the present time. John
has an interesting hobby, he enjoys watching and working with bees.

John and Lillian's son, Myron, started farming after he married Beatrice Suter
in August 1951. A few years later they moved to Lincoln, NE, where Myron took
up theology and is now a minister of the Seventh-Day Adventist Church. He has
served in Nebraska, North Dakota, Michigan and Austin, TX. Myron and Beatrice
have five children: Warren, Bruce, Nancy, Bryan and Amber.

Viola Voegele took her nurse's training in Boulder and Denver, CO. She married
Loren Heiser from Rush Center, KS in February of 1958. She continued nursing
for seven years. In 1965 they adopted a baby, Ronnie, and Viola gave up nursing
to be home with him. In 1968 a girl, Janet was born and in 1970, a boy, Ricky
was born. Viola finds time to help with immunization clinics now and then but
does not work full-time. Loren is a wheat and livestock farmer.

ARTHUR and EMMA WACKER

Arthur Wacker was born March 26, 1904 on a farm that was homesteaded by his
parents, 12 miles northeast of Long Lake, SD. Arthur's father, Jacob Wacker,
was born in Russia in 1870. His mother, Margaret (Nuss) Wacker was born in 1867
in Russia also. They were married in Menno, SD. Jacob died in a farm accident
at the age of 45. At the time, Arthur was 11 years old. He was one of five
children.

Arthur married Emma Dockter February 23, 1928 at St. Peter's Lutheran Church in
Dickey County, ND. Emma was born September 13, 1908 on a farm 13 miles
northeast of Long Lake in McIntosh County, ND. Her parents were Jacob and
Magdalena (Wagemann) Dockter. They came from South Russia in approximately 1900
and were married in McPherson County, SD in 1907. Emma has three brothers and
four sisters.

        The Arthur Wacker Family.

Arthur and Emma have two children, Alvin and Lualla. Alvin was born January 23,
1930 and he married Alma Bender, daughter of Arthur and Eva (Helfenstein)
Bender April 30, 1961.

Lualla was born September 9, 1936. She married Irvin M. Hauck and they have
made their home in Coeur D'Alene, ID. They have three children: Renee, Dwight
and Farren.

The Wackers are members of the Leola Reformed Church

KARL and BARBARA WACKER

Karl Wacker was born in South Russia in 1855. He was educated while he lived in
Russia. Karl came to America with two brothers in October of 1874. Wagon
building and carpentry was his trade. Although wagons weren't built by manual
labor in America, carpentry became his livelihood the first few years in this
country.

Karl and his brothers came as far as Yankton, SD, which was the end of the
railroad at that time. Karl earned $10 a month building homes and furniture for
the many settlers who were moving into the area. On November 14, 1875 he
married Barbara Neuhardt.

        Karl & Barbara Wacker.

When the railroad reached Eureka, Karl and Barbara traveled there by train,
then headed northeast and homesteaded in Wacker Township. They raised their 12
children there.

Karl was very active in the community. He taught school, and was elder and
deacon for the early Reformed Church. In 1900, he was appointed commissioner in
the first district, replacing John Schock, who had died while in office. He
finished John's term of office. From 1899 to 1915, he was county and township
assessor. While township assessor, he assessed Wacker, Weber, Hoffman, Koto,
Carl, Highland, Long Lake, Harrison, Bergdorf, Leola and Spring townships,
which entailed a lot of traveling.

Barhara died in 1933 and Karl died in 1944.

RUDOLF and CHRISTENA WAGENMANN

Life for Rudolf Wagenmann in the U.S. began in the year 1910, when he arrived
here from Russia. Rudolf chose to leave Russia due to political problems in the
country. He worked on a freighter to compensate for his trip to the U.S.

Rudolf was born in Neudorf, South Russia, January 2, 1890 to Peter and
Carolina (Pleines) Wagenmann, Germans who had migrated to Russia. He spent his
early youth helping his parents on the farm until their death. He left Russia
at age 20. He came to the U.S., semi-settling northeast of Leola with friends,
working wherever employment was available. It was during this time that he met
Christena Kranzler. He married her December 10, 1912. She was the daughter of
Bernard and Emelia (Schlickenmeyer) Kranzler, who also had migrated to Russia
from Germany. Christena was born January 1, 1891 in Gluckstal, Russia and came
to America with her parents when she was nine years of age. Her early years
were spent helping her parents on the farm and working for several families in
the community. After their marriage, Rudolf and Christena moved to Leola where
Rudolf operated a creamery for a short time, before moving northwest of Leola
(1918) to take up farming.

Rudolf had great concern for a younger brother, Jacob, living in Russia. He
managed, midst struggle and strife, to save enough to sponsor him to come to
America.

Rudolf and Christena moved to Leola in the early 1950's. Their son, Reinhold,
remained on the farm for several years thereafter. While living in Leola,
Rudolf farmed the Bell farm for several years, but due to his health he
semi-retired. He worked for the International Harvester Co. of Leola until he
passed away January 21, 1958.

        The Rudolf Wagenmann Family.

The Wagenmann family consisted of seven children. Two sons, Leonard and Gideon,
died in infancy, and daughter Lea died August 31, 1979. The eldest, Reinhold,
married Alma Burrer November 20, 1938. They live in Aberdeen, SD. Daughter
Elsie married Edwin Walker November 13, 1938 and now lives in Aberdeen, SD.
Another daughter, Leona, married Edmund Schaffer June 6, 1946 and moved to
Sacramento, CA. The youngest in the family is Rudy, who married Agnes Jakober
August 16, 1959. They lived briefly in South Dakota, Arizona, and Minnesota and
now live in Portland, OR.

Christena remarried in May of 1961 to Eugene Huber, moving to Aberdeen where
they remained until September of 1972, when the Hubers entered the Hosmer
Senior Citizens Nursing Home. Eugene died in 1973 and Christena in June of
1983.

DELMAR and DELORES WAHL

Delmar Wahl was born September 5, 1930, to Johanna (Neiffer) and Carl Wahl at
Java, SD. Delmar attended rural school in Spring Township and farmed with his
parents until their retirement. Delmar well remembers going to school by horse
and buggy and attending classes in a one-room schoolhouse. Delmar continues to
live on the home place.

Delores Aman was born in Roscoe, SD on February 7, 1931. Her parents were Emil
and Ottelia (Geist) Aman of Roscoe, SD. When Delores was 12 years of age, the
family moved to Aberdeen, SD. Delores was married to Elmer Sandmeier October
16, 1949 at Aberdeen, SD. They were the parents of five children.

Sandra, born April 22, 1950, married Rodney Ulrich. They have two daughters.

Pamela, born March 25, 1952, married Ronnie Stoecker. They have one daughter.

Connie, born April 27, 1955, married Robert Stewart Jr. They have one daughter
and two sons.

Donald was born April 27, 1957. Donald is not married and is currently working
in Sidney, MT.

Troy was born January 13, 1968. He is attending Leola High School.

Elmer passed away May 9, 1971 and Delores continued to live in Aberdeen until
she married Delmar, May 31, 1975. Delores and Troy moved to the Wahl farm west
of Leola, where they now reside.

GOTTFRIED and LILY WALTH

Gottfried Walth, born July 7, 1901 was the son of Jacob Walth (born November
19, 1851) and Katherine (Eisenbeisz) Walth (born January 22, 1859). Both of his
parents attended school and then married in Gluckstal, South Russia. Four of
their ten children were born in Gluckstal before they migrated to a farm near
Hosmer, SD. Gottfried was ninth of the ten children. After maturity, Gottfried
became an excellent mechanic. He married Lily Sayler May 1, 1932 at Bowdle, SD.

Lily Sayler was born April 5, 1908 to Emanuel and Marie (Schumacker) Sayler at
Underwood, ND. Both of her parents were born in the Menno-Tripp area in South
Dakota. Lily had two brothers and one sister, Lily being the eldest. She lost
her mother at age ten. Consequently she spent a lot of time with her
grandmother Sayler, who taught her many useful things. One of them was sewing
(her favorite). Lily made all of her own clothes at a very early age and
continued using her talents in Leola for many years.

Gottfried and Lily lived in Bowdle until 1936, when they moved to Leola, where
Gottfried began mechanic work at the John Kulm Ford garage. His starting wage
was $40 per month. His highest salary was $400 in the 35 years he was employed
there. Many days he worked 12 hours and saw many new cars handled in the
garage. He owned one new car during his lifetime, a Model T. Gottfried resigned
from Kulms in 1970 and worked for Vincent Geffre at his station until he became
ill. Gottfried died in September 1971.

Lily and Gottfried enjoyed traveling in their last years together. Their
favorite vacation spot was the Black Hills, although they spent many enjoyable
visits with their daughter, Jeanette, and her family in Washington, DC and
later in Oklahoma City, OK. After Gottfried died, Lily traveled to Texas to
visit the Conahans several times. She is a resident in the Aberdeen Nursing
Home at the present time.

        Gottfried & Lily Walth.

The Walths had three children and six grandchildren. Jeanette, born May 23,
1933, married Lee Conahan in 1955 (see Conahan history); Harley, born October
6, 1935, died in July of 1938; and Carol, born September 14, 1940, married
Harvey Rott September 24, 1961. They have two children, Julie, born in 1962 and
Dean, born in 1963. Carol now resides in Aberdeen, SD.

JOHN and MAGDALENA WALTH

Among the immigrants who came to America on the crest of the tide which swept
in from Russia was Gottlieb Walth and his wife Christina. They came to
McPherson County in 1889 and homesteaded at the junction of Dewey, Arena and
Blaine townships.

Their early home was the usual house built of sod.

This union was blessed with nine children, five of whom died during an epidemic
in Russia. Four more were born to them in this country. Fred farmed near
Eureka. He later moved to Glenham, SD. Rosina married Gottlieb Gienger.
Christina married Carl Hoffman. John Walth broke horses and fixed horses' teeth
along with working on his father's farm. Helping with the field work, he walked
along guiding a hand plow drawn by two horses.

        John & Magdalena Walth.

John took over the family farm after his marriage to Magdalena Walth.
Magdalena's parents, George and Elizabeth Walth, of Fairfax, SD, were both born
in Russia; however, they met and were married in America.

John was active in the community as a committeeman and range inspector. As
range inspector he surveyed land, and staked out contour farming, reservoirs
and dams. He designed a "Ditcher." This was used by farmers in building dams.

They continued on the farm until October 16, 1945, when they had a farm sale.
They moved to Aberdeen, SD, where John was employed at the Western Union
Building. In 1965, they sold their Aberdeen home and moved to Leola, SD.

On December 20, 1964, John and Magdalena celebrated their 50th wedding
anniversary with family and friends at the St. James Lutheran Church in Leola.
They had been members of the Leola Church.

John died on August 9, 1976; Magdalena on August 4, 1979.

They were the parents of four children. Gertrude married Adolph Mohr. They have
three children, Sharon Kay (Hieb), Imogene (Schmahl), and Jerome; and nine
grandchildren.

Alma married Milbert Koerner. They have a daughter, Sharlene (Hoffman) and a
son Lynn; and nine grandchildren. Alma and Milbert are retired after having
farmed near Leola for many years. They spend the winter months in Harlingen,
TX. During the summer, Milbert works part time at the Miller Funeral Home in
Aberdeen, SD.

Viola married Otto Mohr. They have two sons, Merle and Harley, and three
grandchildren.

Oscar married Mary Timmerman. Dr. Walth graduated from Leola High School in
1944. Dr. Walth practices optometry in Waterloo, IA.

Oscar and his dad were gifted with musical ability, a circumstance which
provided much to the happiness and the enjoyment of the family circle.

MARLIN and COLLEEN WANGSNESS

The Rev. Marlin Wangsness was installed as the new pastor of St. James Lutheran
Church in Leola on Sunday, January 8, 1978. Rev. Wangsness came to Leola from
Canova, SD, where he had served his first parish, the Immanuel Lutheran Church.
1973 to 1978.

        Marlin, Colleen, Eric, Ryan and Michael Wangsness.

Marlin, the son of Otto and Florence Wangsness, was born August 10, 1946 at
Grafton, ND. He moved with his parents to Faribault, MN, where he attended
school, graduating from high school in 1964 and Luther College in Decorah, IA
in 1968. He moved to Thomson, IL, where he taught social studies and served as
